**NITI Aayog** (**1 January 2015**) came much later and put cooperative federalism into practice through its **bottom-up** approach; it did not first recommend the idea.
xa: The **Inter-State Council** (**Art. 263**) was set up in **1990** on **Sarkaria's** recommendation; its chairman is the **PM**.
NITI's version of cooperative federalism is called **"marble-cake federalism"**.
⚠ **Competitive federalism** = States compete; **competitive sub-federalism** = **local bodies** compete.

59.s: Under NITI Aayog's approach to cooperative federalism, planning is meant to proceed by:
o: Allocating plan funds from the Centre to States through a single national Five Year Plan
Leaving all planning to the Union Ministries with States only implementing schemes
Assigning planning exclusively to State Finance Commissions
Formulating credible plans at the village level and aggregating them progressively upwards
59.x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach in which credible village-level plans are formulated and aggregated at higher levels of government, unlike the top-down Planning Commission model.
59.tq: NITI plans grow from the village up, not from Delhi down.
xs: Under NITI's cooperative federalism, planning proceeds by **formulating credible plans at the village level and aggregating them upwards** — option **(4)**, a **bottom-up** approach.
A single national plan with Central allocation of plan funds belongs to the old **Planning Commission** model; NITI has **no financial powers** (no plan grants).
xa: NITI's version of cooperative federalism brings states together on a **single platform** — **"marble-cake federalism"**.
**NITI Aayog** replaced the **Planning Commission** by a **Union Cabinet resolution** of **1 January 2015**.
With NITI giving no plan grants, the **Finance Commission's** domain was restored.

59.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NITI Aayog:
1. It replaced the Planning Commission.
2. It follows a bottom-up approach.
3. It possesses powers to allocate plan grants to the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission and follows a bottom-up approach. It has no financial powers and does not allocate plan grants, making statement 3 incorrect.
59.tq: Identify the false statement by distinguishing NITI Aayog's advisory role from the former Planning Commission's financial role.
xs: Statement 1 correct: NITI Aayog **replaced the Planning Commission** (**1 January 2015**).
Statement 2 correct: it follows a **bottom-up approach** — village-level plans aggregated upwards.
Statement 3 wrong: NITI has **no financial powers** and gives **no plan grants**. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: Legal status: **non-constitutional, non-statutory**, created by **Union Cabinet resolution**.
Its lack of financial powers is a common **criticism**: advice is **not binding**.
The **Finance Commission's** domain over grants was restored once plan grants ended.

59.s: The State Support Mission of NITI Aayog is intended to help States
o: replace their elected local bodies with nominated bodies
obtain constitutional status for their planning departments
receive plan grants directly from NITI Aayog
59.x: The State Support Mission helps States build State Institutions for Transformation. GRIT in Gujarat and MITRA in Maharashtra are examples.
59.tq: Link the mission name to its institutional capacity-building function and reject the financial-power trap.
xs: The **State Support Mission** helps States build **State Institutions for Transformation** — option **(3)**.
Examples: **GRIT** (Gujarat) and **MITRA** (Maharashtra).
NITI cannot give **plan grants** — it has **no financial powers**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: The Mission falls under NITI's mandate area "**NITI for States**" (cooperative and competitive federalism).
**Team India Hub** leads the States' engagement with the Centre (APPSC-GS **2018**).
**Regional Councils** handle issues spanning States, jointly headed by a **CM (by rotation)** and a **Union Minister**.

59.s:
Match the institution with its establishment and status:

List-I (Institution)
 a. Planning Commission
 b. National Development Council
 c. NITI Aayog

List-II (Establishment and status)
 i. Union Cabinet resolution, 1 January 2015; non-constitutional, non-statutory and advisory
 ii. Executive resolution, 1952; extra-constitutional
 iii. Cabinet resolution, 1950; extra-constitutional
59.x: The Planning Commission was created by a Cabinet resolution in 1950; the National Development Council by an executive resolution in 1952; and NITI Aayog by a Union Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015 with advisory status.
59.tq: Begin with the distinctive NITI Aayog date and status, then distinguish the 1950 and 1952 resolutions.
xs: **Planning Commission** – **Cabinet resolution, 1950**; **NDC** – **executive resolution, 1952**; **NITI Aayog** – **Union Cabinet resolution, 1 January 2015**, advisory — option **(2)**: a–iii, b–ii, c–i.
The first two are **extra-constitutional**; NITI is **non-constitutional, non-statutory**.
xa: The Planning Commission was **abolished** and replaced by NITI.
The **NDC** is now **inactive**; its role is taken by NITI's **Governing Council**.
The Governing Council was first constituted in **February 2015**, reconstituted **February 2021**.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about the structure of NITI Aayog:
1. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson and appoints the Vice-Chairperson.
2. It can have at most two part-time members, on a rotational basis.
3. It can have at most four Union Ministers as ex-officio members.
4. Its CEO is a Union Cabinet Minister with no fixed tenure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: the PM chairs NITI Aayog and appoints the Vice-Chairperson. Statement 2 is correct: at most two part-time members, by rotation. Statement 3 is correct: at most four ex-officio Union Ministers. Statement 4 is wrong: the CEO is a Secretary-rank officer with a fixed tenure. So '1, 2 and 3 only'; '1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, and options with 4 are wrong.
59.tq: NITI numbers: max 2 part-time, max 4 ex-officio; CEO = Secretary rank, fixed tenure.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the **PM** is **Chairperson** and **appoints the Vice-Chairperson**.
Statement 2 correct: **max 2 part-time** members, rotational. Statement 3 correct: **max 4 ex-officio Union ministers**.
Statement 4 wrong: the **CEO** is of **Secretary rank** with a **fixed tenure**. So **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: Current Vice-Chairperson: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** (**April 2026**), replacing **Suman K. Bery**.
Full-time members: **K.V. Raju**, **M. Srinivas**, **Abhay Karandikar**, **Gobardhan Das**, **Rajiv Gauba**.
The **Governing Council** (PM chairs) includes **CMs of all States** and of UTs with legislatures.

59.s: Regional Councils of NITI Aayog are constituted primarily to deal with:
o: Allocation of funds to individual districts
Issues affecting more than one State
59.x: Regional Councils address issues that affect more than one State.
59.tq: Match the council type with the geographical scope of the issues it handles.
xs: **Regional Councils** deal with **issues affecting more than one State** — option **(4)**.
They are **jointly headed** by a **CM (by rotation)** and a **Union Minister**.
xa: ⚠ **Governing Council** = **PM** chairs; Regional Councils = CM by rotation + Union Minister.
NITI's two hubs: **Team India Hub** and **Knowledge and Innovation Hub**.
**DMEO** handles NITI's monitoring and evaluation mandate.

59.s: Which of the two hubs at the core of NITI Aayog leads the engagement of the States with the Centre?
59.x: NITI Aayog has two hubs: the Team India Hub, which leads State engagement with the Centre (APPSC-GS 2018), and the Knowledge and Innovation Hub, its think-tank arm. DMEO is the monitoring and evaluation office, and there is no 'Regional Council Hub'; Regional Councils are separate forums for issues spanning States.
59.tq: States' engagement = Team India Hub.
xs: The **Team India Hub** leads the **States' engagement with the Centre** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS **2018**).
The **Knowledge and Innovation Hub** is the other hub; **DMEO** is the monitoring and evaluation office, not a hub.
There is no "Regional Council Hub"; **Regional Councils** are forums for issues spanning States.
xa: NITI's four mandate areas: knowledge and innovation, **NITI for States**, transformational change, monitoring and evaluation (**DMEO**).
**State Support Mission** → **State Institutions for Transformation** (e.g., **GRIT**, **MITRA**).
NITI is called a "**directional and policy dynamo**".

59.s: The Chief Ministers of which Union Territories are members of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
o: Puducherry, Lakshadweep, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry
Delhi, Chandigarh, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
59.x: The Governing Council includes the Chief Ministers of Union Territories having legislatures: Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry.
59.tq: Use the legislature-based classification to distinguish Union Territories represented by Chief Ministers.
xs: CMs of **UTs with legislatures** — **Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry** — sit on the Governing Council — option **(3)**.
Other UTs (like **Chandigarh**, **Lakshadweep**, **Ladakh**) are represented by their **Lt Governors**, not CMs.
xa: The Council is chaired by the **PM** and includes **CMs of all States**.
Also members: **ex-officio members**, the **Vice-Chairperson**, **full-time members** and **special invitees**.
It took over the role of the **NDC**, now inactive.

59.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes — Shivraj Singh Chouhan
b. Skill Development — Parkash Singh Badal
c. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan — N. Chandrababu Naidu
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
59.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Parkash Singh Badal and N. Chandrababu Naidu convened the respective sub-groups.
59.tq: Start from the sure subject–convener pairs and verify all three matches.
xs: All three pairs are correct: **CSS rationalisation – Shivraj Singh Chouhan**, **Skill Development – Parkash Singh Badal**, **Swachh Bharat – N. Chandrababu Naidu** — option **(4)**: a, b and c.
These were the three **2015** sub-groups of Chief Ministers constituted by **NITI Aayog**.
xa: **Digital payments** was not a 2015 sub-group; a separate CM **committee on digital payments** came in **2016**, also convened by **Naidu**.
The 2015 sub-group classified CSS into **core of the core**, **core** and **optional**.
AP angle: Naidu also presented **Swarna Andhra @2047** to NITI.

59.s:
With reference to the separate committee of Chief Ministers on digital payments, consider the following statements:
1. It was set up in 2016.
2. It was convened by N. Chandrababu Naidu.
3. It was one of the three NITI Aayog sub-groups constituted in 2015.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
59.x: The digital-payments committee was set up in 2016 and was convened by N. Chandrababu Naidu. It was separate from the three 2015 sub-groups and therefore statement 3 is false.
59.tq: Separate the later committee from the original 2015 sub-groups and identify the false time-linked statement.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the CM **committee on digital payments** was set up in **2016**.
Statement 2 correct: it was convened by **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.
Statement 3 wrong: digital payments was **not** one of the **2015** sub-groups. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: The three 2015 sub-groups: **CSS rationalisation** (Chouhan), **Skill Development** (Badal), **Swachh Bharat** (Naidu).
Exam angle: **Digital payments** is the **odd one out** among CM sub-groups (APPSC-G1 **2017**).

59.s: The 2015 sub-group of Chief Ministers classified Centrally Sponsored Schemes into which categories?
o: Core of the core, core and optional
59.x: The 2015 sub-group divided CSS into core of the core, core and optional schemes.
59.tq: Recall the exact three-part classification.
xs: The **2015 CM sub-group** classified CSS into **core of the core, core and optional** schemes — option **(3)**.
This sub-group on **Rationalisation of CSS** was convened by **Shivraj Singh Chouhan** (MP).
xa: Core schemes funding: **60:40** usually; **90:10** for **North-Eastern & Himalayan States**.
CSS need **matching State contributions**, with parameters set by the Centre.
Suggested fixes: **revisit CSS**, greater State say in **GST design**, regular **ISC meetings**.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about the funding pattern of core Centrally Sponsored Schemes:
1. The usual Centre-State sharing ratio is 60:40.
2. For the North-Eastern and Himalayan States, the ratio is 75:25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: the usual ratio for core schemes is 60:40. Statement 2 is wrong: for North-Eastern and Himalayan States it is 90:10. So '1 only'; '2 only' and 'Both' wrongly accept 75:25, and 'Neither' wrongly rejects statement 1.
59.tq: Core CSS: 60:40 normally, 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the usual sharing ratio for core CSS is **60:40**.
Statement 2 wrong: for **North-Eastern & Himalayan States** it is **90:10**, not 75:25. So **1 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: CSS form a **large part of Centre-State transfers** and need **matching State contributions**.
Debate: CSS **squeeze State priorities** since the Centre decides parameters.
2015 classification: **core of the core**, **core**, **optional**.

59.s: Which of the following has been advanced as a criticism of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: They eliminate all State contributions to development programmes
They make State Governments responsible for designing all national schemes
They can squeeze State priorities because programme parameters are decided by the Centre
They prevent the Centre from transferring funds to States
59.x: A major criticism is that CSS may squeeze State priorities because the Centre determines important programme parameters and States must provide matching contributions.
59.tq: Apply the financing structure to the federal-priorities debate.
xs: A key criticism: CSS can **squeeze State priorities** because **programme parameters are decided by the Centre** — option **(3)**.
CSS actually **require matching State contributions** and are a **large part of Centre-State transfers**, so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Suggested fixes: **revisit CSS**, **greater State say in GST design**, **regular ISC meetings**.
Funding pattern: **60:40**; **90:10** for North-Eastern & Himalayan States.
**GST critique**: curtailed States' taxation powers, plus **compensation disputes**.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about the GST Council:
1. It is provided for in Article 279A of the Constitution.
2. In its voting, the Centre has two-thirds of the votes and the States together one-third.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 279A provides for the GST Council, where the Centre and States decide jointly. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the reverse - the Centre has one-third of the votes and the States two-thirds. So '1 only'; '2 only' and 'Both' wrongly accept statement 2, and 'Neither' wrongly rejects statement 1.
59.tq: GST Council voting: Centre 1/3, States 2/3 - the States hold the larger share.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the **GST Council** is under **Art. 279A**; Centre and States decide jointly.
Statement 2 wrong: it is the reverse — **Centre one-third of votes, States two-thirds**. So **1 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: The GST Council is the usual example of **cooperative federalism**.
GST critique: **curtailed States' taxation powers** (many local taxes subsumed) and **compensation disputes**.
Fix suggested: **greater State say in GST design**.

59.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the usual relationship between the institution or mechanism and the type of federalism?
o: GST Council — Cooperative federalism; NITI Aayog rankings — Competitive federalism
GST Council — Competitive federalism; NITI Aayog rankings — Cooperative federalism
Both GST Council and NITI Aayog rankings — Competitive federalism
Both GST Council and NITI Aayog rankings — Cooperative federalism
59.x: The GST Council is generally cited as a model of cooperative federalism, whereas NITI Aayog rankings encourage competitive federalism.
59.tq: Use the contrast between joint decision-making and performance-based comparison.
xs: The usual pairing: **GST Council — cooperative federalism**; **NITI Aayog rankings — competitive federalism** — option **(1)**.
In the GST Council the Centre and States **decide jointly** (**Art. 279A**); rankings make States **compete**.
xa: Competitive federalism is driven by NITI's **performance rankings** — **SDG**, **Health**, **Fiscal Health**.
Cooperative federalism was **first recommended by** the **Sarkaria Commission**.
⚠ Competitive **sub-federalism** = local bodies compete, e.g. ADP **"Champions of Change"** district rankings.

59.s: The proposal for establishing Zonal Councils is associated with:
59.x: The proposal for Zonal Councils was made by Jawaharlal Nehru.
59.tq: Match the institutional proposal with its associated statesman.
xs: The **Zonal Councils** were **proposed by Jawaharlal Nehru** — option **(1)**.
They were set up under **Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, as **statutory** bodies.
xa: Chair of **all five**: the **Union Home Minister**.
Each State: **CM + 2 ministers**; councils are **advisory only**.
**Inter-State Council** (**Art. 263**, **1990**) is chaired by the **PM**.

59.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Inter-State Council under Article 263 was set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation and is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. All five Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister.
3. River boards are set up under the Inter-State Council Order, 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: the ISC (Art 263) came in 1990 on Sarkaria's advice, with the PM as chairman. Statement 2 is correct: the Union Home Minister chairs all five Zonal Councils, which are statutory and advisory. Statement 3 is wrong: river boards are set up under the River Boards Act, 1956. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the Zonal Council chair, and options with 3 are wrong.
59.tq: ISC chair PM; Zonal Councils chair Home Minister.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the **Inter-State Council** (**Art. 263**) came in **1990** on **Sarkaria's** recommendation; chaired by the **PM**.
Statement 2 correct: the **Union Home Minister** chairs **all five Zonal Councils**.
Statement 3 wrong: river boards come under the **River Boards Act, 1956**. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: Zonal Councils are **statutory** under **Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, proposed by **Nehru**.
The Inter-State Council is **recommendatory**; Zonal Councils are **advisory only**.
**GST Council** rests on **Art. 279A**.

59.s: Competitive federalism refers to competition
o: among States, and between States and the Centre in policy, to attract investment and improve outcomes
only between the two Houses of Parliament over financial legislation
among courts over the interpretation of federal provisions
only among municipalities for constitutional status
59.x: Competitive federalism involves States competing with one another and with the Centre through policy initiatives to attract investment and improve outcomes.
59.tq: Distinguish the level of competition and its policy objective instead of treating all inter-governmental relations as federal competition.
xs: **Competitive federalism** = competition **among States** (and between States and the Centre in policy) **to attract investment** and **improve outcomes** — option **(1)**.
Its tool is **better policies and services**; its driver is NITI's **performance rankings**.
xa: ⚠ **Competitive sub-federalism** = competition **among local bodies**.
**Cooperative federalism** = Centre and States on a **common platform**, first recommended by **Sarkaria**.
Usual pairing: **NITI rankings = competitive**; **GST Council = cooperative**.

59.s: A competition among district administrations or other local bodies to improve performance is best described as
59.x: Competitive sub-federalism means competition among local bodies. District rankings under the Aspirational Districts Programme provide an example.
59.tq: Identify the governmental level first: competition below the State level indicates sub-federalism.
xs: Competition **among local bodies** (e.g., districts) is **competitive sub-federalism** — option **(3)** (APPSC-G1 **2017** key).
**Cooperative federalism** is Centre and States working together; competitive federalism is competition **among States**.
xa: Example: **district rankings** on the ADP **"Champions of Change"** dashboard.
AP angle: **Alluri Sitharama Raju** district ranked **1st** in India in ADP **Basic Infrastructure** (March **2026**).
⚠ Competitive federalism = **States** compete; competitive sub-federalism = **local bodies** compete.

59.s:
Consider the following statements about State-ranking indices:
1. The SDG India Index, released by NITI Aayog, was built to encourage competitive federalism and is now localised to districts.
2. The Export Preparedness Index is prepared by NITI Aayog with the Institute for Competitiveness, with pillars including export policy, business environment, export infrastructure and export performance.
3. Swachh Survekshan is released by NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
59.x: Statement 1 is correct: the SDG India Index is NITI Aayog's and is now localised to districts. Statement 2 is correct: NITI Aayog prepares the EPI with the Institute for Competitiveness, on those four pillars. Statement 3 is wrong: Swachh Survekshan is released by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the EPI, and options with 3 are wrong.
59.tq: Swachh Survekshan is the odd one out: MoHUA, not NITI Aayog.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the **SDG India Index** (NITI) was built for **competitive federalism** and is **localised to districts**.
Statement 2 correct: **EPI** is by **NITI Aayog with the Institute for Competitiveness**, with those four pillars.
Statement 3 wrong: **Swachh Survekshan** is by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **Ease of Doing Business (BRAP)** = **DPIIT**, not NITI.
**State Health Index** = NITI with **MoHFW and World Bank**; **SEQI** = NITI with **MHRD**.
AP has **~70% of India's shrimp exports** → helps its EPI rank.

59.s: The Ease of Doing Business State Business Reform Action Plan is published by
59.x: The State Business Reform Action Plan rankings are associated with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
59.tq: Match the index with its exact publishing institution and avoid substituting NITI Aayog.
xs: The **Ease of Doing Business** (**State Business Reform Action Plan**) is published by **DPIIT** — option **(3)**.
It is **not a NITI Aayog** index; **MoHFW** partners NITI on the State Health Index.
xa: ⚠ **Swachh Survekshan** = **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** — also not NITI.
NITI indices: **SDG India Index**, **EPI**, **State Health Index**, **SEQI**, **Fiscal Health Index**.
AP in the **Fiscal Health Index 2023-24**: **17th**.

59.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s position in the SDG India Index 2023–24?
o: It scored 100 out of 100 and was classified as a Front Runner State.
It ranked seventeenth and was classified as a Performer.
It scored 74 out of 100 and was classified as a Frontrunner.
It scored 57 out of 100 and was classified as an Aspirant.
59.x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74 out of 100 in the SDG India Index 2023–24 and was classified as a “Frontrunner”.
59.tq: Read the score and category together; do not substitute a rank for a classification.
xs: In the **SDG India Index 2023-24**, AP scored **74/100** and was a "**Frontrunner**" — option **(3)**.
**17th** is AP's rank in the **Fiscal Health Index 2023-24**, not the SDG Index.
xa: The SDG India Index is by **NITI Aayog**, built to encourage **competitive federalism**, and now **localised to districts**.
AP won **5 National Panchayat Awards 2025**, second after **Karnataka (6)**.
**ASR district** ranked **1st** in ADP **Basic Infrastructure** (March **2026**).

59.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: School Education Quality Index — Institute for Competitiveness alone
Swachh Survekshan — Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
59.x: The School Education Quality Index is associated with NITI Aayog with MHRD, not with the Institute for Competitiveness alone. The other pairs are correctly matched.
59.tq: Look for the altered institutional partner in an otherwise familiar index–publisher pair.
xs: **SEQI — Institute for Competitiveness alone** is wrong: **SEQI** is by **NITI Aayog with MHRD** — option **(1)**.
The others are correct: **Swachh Survekshan – Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**; **Health Index** and **SDG India Index – NITI Aayog**.
xa: The **Institute for Competitiveness** partners NITI on the **Export Preparedness Index**.
State Health Index: NITI with **MoHFW and World Bank**.
⚠ **Ease of Doing Business** = **DPIIT**.

59.s: The State Health Index is also known by the title:
o: Progressive Health and Human Capital Index
59.x: NITI Aayog’s State Health Index is titled “Healthy States, Progressive India.”
59.tq: Discriminate between a formal title and a plausible reversal of its words.
xs: The **State Health Index** is titled "**Healthy States, Progressive India**" — option **(3)**.
Option (4) reverses the words — a trap.
xa: It is prepared by **NITI Aayog with MoHFW and World Bank**.
Health rankings are part of NITI's **competitive federalism** tools with **SDG** and **Fiscal Health** rankings.
**SEQI** = NITI with **MHRD**.

59.s: Andhra Pradesh was showcased in the context of which of the following?
o: Exclusive control over the GST Council Secretariat
The creation of the North Eastern Council
Real Time Governance and AI-enabled tools such as AWARE
The chairmanship of all Zonal Councils
59.x: Andhra Pradesh was showcased for Real Time Governance and AI-enabled tools such as AWARE.
59.tq: Identify the correct State-specific governance initiative.
xs: AP was showcased for **Real Time Governance** and **AI-enabled tools** such as **AWARE** — option **(3)**.
Zonal Councils are all chaired by the **Union Home Minister**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: AP angle: **ASR district 1st** in ADP **Basic Infrastructure** (March **2026**).
**Naidu** convened the **Swachh Bharat** sub-group and presented **Swarna Andhra @2047** to NITI.
AP has **~70% of India's shrimp exports** → helps its **EPI** rank.

59.s: Approximately what share of India’s shrimp exports is contributed by Andhra Pradesh?
59.x: Andhra Pradesh contributes approximately 70 percent of India’s shrimp exports, a factor associated with its EPI ranking.
59.tq: Recall the approximate percentage rather than confusing it with a rounded half or majority figure.
xs: Andhra Pradesh contributes **~70% of India's shrimp exports** — option **(2)**, about 70 percent.
This export strength **helps AP's rank** in the **Export Preparedness Index (EPI)**.
xa: The **EPI** is prepared by **NITI Aayog** with the **Institute for Competitiveness**.
EPI pillars: **export policy**, **business environment**, **export infrastructure**, **export performance**.
Other AP angles: **ASR district 1st** in ADP **Basic Infrastructure** (March **2026**); showcased for **Real Time Governance** and **AWARE**.

59.s: Which of the following best defines a Constitutional Body?
o: A body created exclusively by a State Legislature
A body constituted periodically by an executive order
An authority directly established and anchored within the Constitution of India
A body created only by an Executive Order
59.x: A constitutional body is one set up and empowered by the Constitution itself, such as the ECI or the CAG. A body created by law is statutory, and one created by executive order is extra-constitutional.
59.tq: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.
n: A constitutional body is an authority or institution directly established within the text of the Constitution of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
A constitutional body is empowered within the text of the Constitution of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
A constitutional body is anchored within the text of the Constitution of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xs: A **Constitutional Body** is **directly established and anchored within the Constitution of India** — option **(3)**.
Bodies created by an **Act** are **statutory**; those created by an **executive order** are **extra-constitutional**.
xa: Constitutional examples: **Election Commission**, **Finance Commission**, **CAG**, **Attorney General**, Public Service Commissions.
Statutory examples: **NHRC**, **Lokpal**, **NGT**.
Extra-constitutional: **NITI Aayog**, **Planning Commission**, **NDC**.

59.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: NITI Aayog was established through a Cabinet Resolution in 2015.
The National Development Council was established through an Executive Order in 1952.
The Planning Commission is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
The Planning Commission was established through a Cabinet Resolution in 1950.
59.x: Option C is incorrect: the Planning Commission (1950) was set up by a Cabinet resolution, so it was extra-constitutional and non-statutory. NITI Aayog (2015) and the NDC (1952) were also set up by executive action.
59.tq: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.
n: The Planning Commission was established in 1950. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is an extra-constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is not a constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is not a statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog was established in 2015. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog was established through a Cabinet Resolution dated 1 January 2015. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission was established through a Cabinet Resolution dated 15 March 1950. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Development Council was established through an Executive Order dated 6 August 1952. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
An extra-constitutional or non-statutory body is established through an executive order or cabinet resolution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is an example of an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is an example of an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is not a constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is not a statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the **Planning Commission** is a **statutory** body — option **(3)**.
It was set up by a **Cabinet resolution** in **1950**, so it was **extra-constitutional**.
**NITI Aayog** (Cabinet resolution, **1 January 2015**) and the **NDC** (executive resolution, **1952**) were also set up by executive action.
xa: NITI Aayog is **non-constitutional, non-statutory**, with **no financial powers**.
NDC is now **inactive**; its role is taken by NITI's **Governing Council**.
The Planning Commission was **abolished** and replaced by NITI.

59.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A Statutory Body is created by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature.
Statement B: NHRC, Lokpal and NGT are examples of Statutory Bodies.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
59.x: Both are true: a statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament or a State Legislature, and the NHRC, Lokpal and NGT are examples.
59.tq: Recall examples of statutory bodies.
n: A statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament or a State Legislature. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Human Rights Commission is an example of a statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Lokpal is an example of a statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Green Tribunal is an example of a statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)** is correct.
A: a **statutory body** is created by an **Act of Parliament** or a **State Legislature**.
B: **NHRC**, **Lokpal** and **National Green Tribunal** are statutory bodies.
xa: **Constitutional** bodies are anchored in the **Constitution** (e.g. **Election Commission**, **CAG**).
**Extra-constitutional** bodies come from an **executive order** or **cabinet resolution** (e.g. **NITI Aayog**).
NITI Aayog was created on **1 January 2015**.

60.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Democratic decentralisation transfers power to elected local bodies.
2. Administrative delegation or deconcentration transfers work to field officers within the bureaucracy.
3. Democratic decentralisation and administrative deconcentration are identical in meaning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Democratic decentralisation involves elected local bodies, whereas delegation or deconcentration keeps functions within the administrative bureaucracy; therefore, statement 3 is false.
60.tq: Separate elected political authority from bureaucratic transfer of work.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **democratic decentralisation** moves power to **elected local bodies** (Balwant Rai Mehta's term).
Statement 2 correct: **administrative delegation or deconcentration** moves work to **field officers** who stay **inside the bureaucracy**.
Statement 3 wrong: the two are different — one transfers power to elected bodies, the other only work to officials. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(4)**.
xa: Order of depth: **deconcentration → delegation → devolution**.
Three dimensions: **political** (decide), **administrative** (implement), **fiscal** (raise and spend).
**Vertical devolution** = States' share of the **divisible pool**; **horizontal** = allocation **among States** by formula.

60.s: Which of the following represents the increasing order of depth of decentralisation?
60.x: The order of increasing depth is deconcentration, delegation and devolution. Devolution transfers the greatest degree of authority to the receiving institution.
60.tq: Arrange concepts by depth rather than by alphabetical order.
xs: The increasing order of depth is **deconcentration → delegation → devolution** — option **(3)**.
**Devolution** is the deepest: power moves to **elected** local bodies; deconcentration only shifts work to **field officers** within the bureaucracy.
xa: **Democratic decentralisation** is **Balwant Rai Mehta's** term.
Three dimensions of decentralisation: **political**, **administrative**, **fiscal**.
The **73rd Amendment** gave panchayats **constitutional status**, but **no independent taxing power**.

60.s:
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment made which of the following mandatory for Panchayati Raj institutions?
1. Constitutional status
2. Three-tier structure
3. Direct elections
4. Five-year term
5. Reservation
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
60.x: The 73rd Amendment provided constitutional status, a three-tier structure, direct elections, a five-year term and reservation for Panchayati Raj institutions. It also provided for State Election Commissions and State Finance Commissions.
60.tq: Treat a constitutional-amendment list as a completeness question and check every element.
xs: The **73rd Amendment** made all five mandatory: **constitutional status**, **three tiers**, **direct elections**, **5-year term**, **reservation** — option **(4)**.
It also mandated the **State Election Commission (243K)** and the **SFC (243I)**.
xa: ⚠ The **29 subjects** of the **Eleventh Schedule** are **not mandatory** — Art. **243G** says "may".
Panchayats have **no independent taxing power** under the Constitution; they tax only if the State Legislature authorises (**243H**).
Union FC grants to local bodies flow under **Art. 280**, routed through States.

60.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal position of the Eleventh Schedule after the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
o: It contains subjects exclusively reserved for municipalities.
It automatically transferred all 29 subjects to Panchayats.
It provides a menu of 29 subjects that may be entrusted under Article 243G.
It abolished the discretionary role of the States in Panchayat functions.
60.x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects that may be entrusted to Panchayats under Article 243G. It is a menu of possible functions and does not itself automatically transfer every subject.
60.tq: Distinguish a constitutional enabling provision from an automatic transfer of powers.
xs: The **Eleventh Schedule** (**29 subjects**) is **only a menu** that **may** be entrusted to panchayats under **Art. 243G** — option **(3)**.
It does **not automatically transfer** all 29 subjects; the word in 243G is "**may**", so States keep discretion.
xa: Mandatory features of the 73rd Amendment: constitutional status, **three tiers**, direct elections, **5-year term**, reservation, **SEC (243K)**, **SFC (243I)**.
**Art. 243H**: own taxes, duties, tolls, fees only if the **State Legislature authorises**.
**Art. 243X** is the **municipal equivalent** of 243H.

60.s: Under Part IX of the Constitution, the State Finance Commission and the State Election Commission for Panchayats are provided for, respectively, in:
60.x: Article 243I provides for the State Finance Commission and Article 243K for the State Election Commission, both mandatory under the 73rd Amendment. The reverse pairing is wrong; 243H (taxing powers) and 243G (powers and functions) deal with other matters; Articles 280 and 324 concern the Union Finance Commission and the Election Commission of India.
60.tq: SFC = 243I (I for finance-Inquiry); SEC = 243K.
xs: The **SFC** is in **Article 243I** and the **State Election Commission** in **Article 243K** — option **(1)**.
**243H** covers panchayat taxing powers and **243G** the Eleventh Schedule menu; **Art. 280** is the **Union Finance Commission**.
xa: Under **243I**, grants-in-aid come from the **State Consolidated Fund** on **SFC** advice.
Comparative note: **Union FC (Art. 280, President)** vs **SFC (Art. 243I, Governor)**.
**243J / 243Z**: State legislature provides for maintenance and **audit** of LB accounts.

60.s:
Consider the following statements about Panchayat revenue:
1. Property tax is a major source of own revenue.
2. Panchayats may levy their own taxes, duties, tolls and fees only when authorised by the State Legislature.
3. The Constitution gives Panchayats an independent and unrestricted taxing power.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: Property tax is a major own-source revenue of Panchayats, and their power to levy taxes, duties, tolls and fees depends on authorisation by the State Legislature under Article 243H. The Constitution does not confer an independent and unrestricted taxing power on them.
60.tq: Reject the absolute claim in statement 3 and distinguish constitutional authorisation from independent taxing power.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **property (house) tax** is the major own revenue (APPSC-GS **2018** key).
Statement 2 correct: own taxes, duties, tolls and fees only if the **State Legislature authorises** (**Art. 243H**, "may").
Statement 3 wrong: panchayats have **no independent taxing power** under the Constitution. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: Other own revenue: **markets, fairs, water, lighting**.
**Assigned taxes** = State-levied taxes handed over to panchayats; **shared taxes** = share of State taxes as per SFC.
**SVAMITVA** drone maps create a **rural property-tax baseline**.

60.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Source)
 a. Assigned taxes
 b. Shared taxes
 c. Grants-in-aid from the State Consolidated Fund
 d. Union Finance Commission grants

List-II (Basis)
 i. Article 280
 ii. Share of State taxes as recommended by the State Finance Commission
 iii. State-levied taxes handed over to Panchayats
 iv. Article 243H and State Finance Commission recommendations

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
60.x: Assigned taxes are State-levied taxes handed over to Panchayats; shared taxes are shared according to the State Finance Commission; State Consolidated Fund grants relate to Article 243H and SFC recommendations; Union Finance Commission grants arise under Article 280.
60.tq: Start from the sure Article 280 pair and then separate assigned taxes from shared taxes.
xs: **Assigned taxes – State-levied taxes handed over**; **shared taxes – share of State taxes per SFC**; **State Consolidated Fund grants – 243H / SFC**; **Union FC grants – Art. 280** — option **(1)**: a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i.
Union FC grants are **routed through States**.
xa: **Scheme funds** come from **Centrally Sponsored Schemes**.
Major own revenue: **property (house) tax**.
Own taxes need **State Legislature** authorisation under **Art. 243H**.

60.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes vertical and horizontal devolution?
o: Vertical devolution is between Union and States; horizontal devolution is among the States
Vertical devolution concerns taxes; horizontal devolution concerns borrowing alone
Vertical devolution is among States; horizontal devolution is between Union and States
Both terms refer only to grants to local bodies
60.x: Vertical devolution divides the divisible pool between the Union and States, while horizontal devolution distributes the States' share among the States.
60.tq: Discriminate between two closely related fiscal terms by their direction of distribution.
xs: **Vertical devolution** = share of the **divisible pool** going from the **Union to States**; **horizontal devolution** = allocation of that share **among States** by a formula — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the two terms.
xa: ⚠ The divisible pool (**Art. 270** taxes) **excludes cesses and surcharges**.
Vertical shares: **13th FC 32%**, **14th FC 42%**, **15th FC 41%**.
Highest horizontal weight in every FC: **income distance**.

60.s: Vertical fiscal imbalance in India primarily reflects the fact that
o: The Union has the more buoyant taxes while States carry heavier spending duties
States have the more buoyant taxes and the Union has the heavier spending duties
Local bodies collect most buoyant taxes and undertake no major spending duties
Both Union and States have identical tax bases and spending responsibilities
60.x: Vertical fiscal imbalance arises because the Centre controls more buoyant taxes, while States bear major expenditure responsibilities such as health, education, agriculture and police.
60.tq: Match the direction of tax buoyancy with the direction of expenditure responsibility.
xs: **Vertical fiscal imbalance**: the **Centre has the more buoyant taxes** while **States carry heavier spending duties** — option **(1)**.
State duties include **health, education, agriculture, police**.
xa: Vertical devolution of the **divisible pool** corrects this imbalance.
⚠ Divisible pool **excludes cesses and surcharges** — a "shrinking divisible pool" is a criticism.
**18 states** had sought **50%** (Aug **2026**).

60.s:
With reference to the vertical devolution of the divisible pool of Central taxes to the States, consider the following statements:
1. The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended 42 per cent.
2. The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended 41 per cent.
3. The Sixteenth Finance Commission retained the share at 41 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended 42 per cent, while the Fifteenth and Sixteenth Finance Commissions recommended 41 per cent. The Fifteenth Finance Commission reduced the share from 42 per cent because Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory.
60.tq: Combine successive percentages and use a near-date comparison to test vertical devolution.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **14th FC — 42%** (the largest-ever rise).
Statement 2 correct: **15th FC — 41%**, cut because **J&K became a UT**.
Statement 3 correct: the **16th FC** award (**2026-31**) **retained 41%**. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: Chairs: **14th Y.V. Reddy**, **15th N.K. Singh**, **16th Dr Arvind Panagariya**.
**18 states** had sought **50%**.

60.s: Which one of the following is excluded from the divisible pool of Central taxes?
60.x: Cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool. The divisible pool was approximately 81 per cent of gross tax revenue in 2025-26.
60.tq: Test the exact composition of a fiscal pool through exclusion.
xs: **Cesses and surcharges** are **excluded** from the divisible pool — option **(1)**.
The divisible pool is made up of **Art. 270** taxes, excluding cesses and surcharges.
xa: Vertical devolution = States' share of this pool; horizontal = its allocation **among States**.
Criticism: a **shrinking divisible pool**.
16th FC kept the States' share at **41%**.

60.s: Who among the following chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
60.x: Dr Arvind Panagariya chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission. Y.V. Reddy and N.K. Singh chaired the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commissions respectively.
60.tq: Use a chairperson-to-Commission association instead of relying on the numerical order alone.
xs: The **16th FC** was chaired by **Dr Arvind Panagariya** — option **(2)**.
**Y.V. Reddy** chaired the **14th FC** and **N.K. Singh** the **15th FC**.
xa: 16th FC constituted **31 Dec 2023**; report tabled **1 Feb 2026**; award **1 Apr 2026 – 31 Mar 2031**.
The 14th FC was constituted on **2 Jan 2013**.
16th FC added **contribution to GDP** (**10**) and dropped **revenue deficit grants**.

60.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the criteria used by the Fourteenth Finance Commission.

List-I (Criterion)
a. Income distance
b. Population, 1971
c. Area
d. Forest cover

List-II (Weight)
i. 7.5
 ii. 15
 iii. 17.5
 iv. 50

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
60.x: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, income distance carried 50 per cent, population 1971 carried 17.5 per cent, area carried 15 per cent and forest cover carried 7.5 per cent.
60.tq: Start from the distinctive 50 per cent income-distance pair and eliminate incompatible codes.
xs: 14th FC weights: **income distance 50**, **population 1971 17.5**, **area 15**, **forest cover 7.5** — option **(1)**: a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
The 14th FC also gave **population 2011** a weight of **10**.
xa: Income distance carried the highest weight in **every FC** (13th FC: **47.5**, called fiscal capacity distance).
The 14th FC used **1971** population plus the change since; FC-15 used **2011**.
14th FC chair: **Y.V. Reddy**; vertical share **42%**.

60.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Fifteenth Finance Commission's criteria for tax devolution:
1. Population, 2011 carried a weight of 15 per cent.
2. Demographic performance carried a weight of 12.5 per cent.
3. Tax and fiscal effort carried a weight of 2.5 per cent.
4. Contribution to GDP was included as a criterion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission assigned 15 per cent to population 2011, 12.5 per cent to demographic performance and 2.5 per cent to tax and fiscal effort. Contribution to GDP was introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission, not the Fifteenth.
60.tq: Identify the later-added criterion as the swapped statement in a multi-criterion question.
xs: Statements 1–3 correct: 15th FC gave **population 2011 – 15**, **demographic performance – 12.5**, **tax and fiscal effort – 2.5**.
Statement 4 wrong: **contribution to GDP** is **new in the 16th FC**. So **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: 15th FC: **income distance 45**, **area 15**, **forest and ecology 10**.
The 16th FC's **GDP contribution replaces tax effort**.
15th FC demographic performance used **change in TFR**.

60.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Demographic performance was measured by total fertility rate alone.
Income distance was calculated from the average of the three largest States.
Forest cover excluded open forests from consideration.
Tax and fiscal effort replaced contribution to GDP.
60.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission calculated income distance from the average of the top three large States. Its demographic-performance measure was population growth from 1971 to 2011; forest included open forests; and contribution to GDP replaced tax effort.
60.tq: Discriminate between closely related criteria by matching each change with the correct Commission.
xs: The **16th FC** measured **income distance** from the **average of the top three large States'** per capita GSDP — option **(2)**.
Others are wrong: demographic performance = **population growth 1971-2011** (not TFR); forest **includes open forests**; **GDP contribution replaced tax effort**, not the reverse.
xa: 16th FC weights: income distance **42.5**, population 2011 **17.5**, area **10**, forest **10**, demographic performance **10**, GDP **10**.
Forest also counts the **increase in forest area (2015-2023)**.
GDP criterion = **square root of State GSDP** over the sum of square roots.

60.s:
With reference to the Sixteenth Finance Commission for 2026–31, consider the following statements:
1. Income distance has a weight of 42.5%.
2. Population 2011 has a weight of 17.5%.
3. Contribution to GDP has been introduced with a weight of 10%.
4. Tax and fiscal effort has been retained with a weight of 2.5%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
60.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: the Sixteenth Finance Commission dropped the 2.5% criterion for tax and fiscal effort.
60.tq: Find the dropped criterion before selecting the coded combination of retained weights.
xs: Statements 1–3 correct: 16th FC — **income distance 42.5%**, **population 2011 17.5%**, **contribution to GDP 10%** (new).
Statement 4 wrong: **tax and fiscal effort** (**2.5** in 15th FC) was **dropped** — **GDP contribution replaces tax effort**. So **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: Area and forest each carry **10** under the 16th FC; demographic performance **10**.
16th FC award period: **1 Apr 2026 – 31 Mar 2031**.
The GDP criterion **helped AP's share** rise to **4.217%**.

60.s: With reference to the horizontal devolution criteria of the Thirteenth Finance Commission, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
60.x: The Thirteenth Finance Commission assigned 47.5 per cent to income distance, termed fiscal capacity distance by that Commission. Population (1971), area and fiscal discipline were assigned 25 per cent, 10 per cent and 17.5 per cent respectively.
60.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate the swapped weights.
xs: The **13th FC** gave **income distance** (which it called **fiscal capacity distance**) **47.5** — option **(1)**.
Its **population 1971** weight was **25**, not 17.5; **17.5** was the 14th FC's population 1971 weight.
xa: Area **15** was the weight in the **14th** and **15th** FCs.
Income distance was the **highest weight in every FC**: 47.5 → **50** → **45** → **42.5**.
13th FC vertical share: **32%**.

60.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission assigned the highest weight among the following to which criterion?
60.x: Income distance received the highest weight under the Fifteenth Finance Commission, at 45 per cent. Demographic performance, forest and ecology, and Population (2011) received 12.5 per cent, 10 per cent and 15 per cent respectively.
60.tq: Compare the principal weight with the three moderately weighted criteria.
xs: **Income distance** got the highest weight under the 15th FC, at **45** — option **(1)**.
Others: **population 2011 – 15**, **demographic performance – 12.5**, **forest and ecology – 10**.
xa: Income distance was the highest weight in **every FC** (16th: **42.5**).
15th FC also used **area 15** and **tax and fiscal effort 2.5**.
15th FC chair: **N.K. Singh**; vertical share **41%**.

60.s: Why does Andhra Pradesh face a 'prosperity paradox' under the income-distance criterion?
o: Its forest area is excluded from the formula.
Its above-average per capita income works against it in income-distance allocation.
Its tax effort is automatically assigned zero weight under every Finance Commission.
Its low population prevents it from receiving any tax devolution.
60.x: Andhra Pradesh's above-average per capita income works against it because the income-distance criterion gives greater weight to States with lower per capita GSDP.
60.tq: Apply the direction of the income-distance formula to Andhra Pradesh's relative prosperity.
xs: AP's **above-average per capita income** works against it under income distance — the **prosperity paradox** — option **(2)**.
Income distance gives **lower GSDP = higher share**, and it carries the **highest weight** in every FC.
xa: The 16th FC measures income distance from the **average of the top three large States**.
The new **GDP-contribution** criterion helped AP's share rise.
AP's 16th FC share: **4.217%**; tax share in **AP Budget 2026-27**: **4.22%**.

60.s: The introduction of the contribution-to-GDP criterion under the 16th Finance Commission helped Andhra Pradesh's share because it
o: recognised the State's contribution to economic output
increased the weight of tax and fiscal effort to 10%
excluded all States with above-average per capita income
removed the divisible pool from the devolution formula
60.x: The new contribution-to-GDP criterion carried a 10% weight and helped Andhra Pradesh's share rise by recognising its economic contribution.
60.tq: Link the newly introduced criterion with its stated effect on Andhra Pradesh's share.
xs: The **contribution-to-GDP** criterion **recognised AP's contribution to economic output**, helping its share rise — option **(1)**.
It did not raise tax effort to **10%** — tax effort was **dropped**; GDP contribution itself carries **10**.
xa: AP's share rose to **4.217%** from **4.05%**; Karnataka **4.131%**, TN **4.097%**.
Formula: **square root of State GSDP** over the sum of square roots.
⚠ **Prosperity paradox**: AP's above-average PCI hurts it under income distance.

60.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Gram Panchayats — Basic: performance grant ratio of 90:10
2. Municipalities — Basic: performance grant ratio of 80:20
3. Fourteenth Finance Commission grants — Distribution according to 2011 population and area in the ratio of 90:10
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
60.x: All three pairs are correct. The Fourteenth Finance Commission used a 90:10 basic-performance ratio for Gram Panchayats, 80:20 for Municipalities, and distributed grants using 2011 population and area in a 90:10 ratio.
60.tq: Check each numerical pairing separately, especially the easily confusable 90:10 and 80:20 ratios.
xs: Pair 1 correct: **Gram Panchayats – basic:performance 90:10** (APPSC-G2 **2017**).
Pair 2 correct: **Municipalities – 80:20** (APPSC-GS **2019** key).
Pair 3 correct: grants distributed by **2011 population (90%)** and **area (10%)**. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ PYQ trap: do **not mix** the 90:10 and 80:20 ratios.
14th FC panchayat total: **Rs 2,00,292 crore**; overall **Rs 2,87,436 crore**.

60.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Fifteenth Finance Commission provision for rural local bodies during 2021–26?
o: ₹2.36 lakh crore, with tied and untied components in a 60:40 ratio for rural bodies
₹4.40 lakh crore, with the urban share fixed at 45 per cent
₹2.00 lakh crore, with no conditions relating to accounts or property tax
60.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission provided ₹2.36 lakh crore for rural local bodies, with tied and untied components in a 60:40 ratio. Performance-linked conditions included audited accounts and property-tax floor rates.
60.tq: Match the Commission period with its amount and distinguish its tied-untied structure from the Fourteenth and Sixteenth Commissions.
xs: The **15th FC** (**2021-26**) gave rural local bodies **₹2.36 lakh crore**, with **tied and untied** components in **60:40** — option **(2)**.
**₹1.18 lakh crore** was the 14th FC comparison figure; **45% urban share** belongs to the **16th FC**.
xa: Part of the tied grant goes to **drinking water and sanitation**.
Performance conditions: **audited accounts** and **property-tax floor rates**.
Urban LBs got roughly **Rs 1.2-1.3 lakh crore**.

60.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants-in-aid framework?
o: Limitation of grants-in-aid to local bodies and disaster management
An overall grants-in-aid figure of ₹9.47 lakh crore for the specified categories
Continuation of revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants
60.x: Under the stated Sixteenth Finance Commission framework, revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants were dropped. Grants-in-aid were limited to local bodies and disaster management, with total grants-in-aid of ₹9.47 lakh crore.
60.tq: Spot the reversed policy change: the discontinued grant categories are presented as if they continued.
xs: **Continuation of revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants** is NOT a feature — the 16th FC **dropped** them — option **(4)**.
Its grants-in-aid total **₹9.47 lakh crore**, limited to **local bodies + disaster management**, with **basic and performance-linked** components.
xa: Grants-in-aid share fell from **19.4% to 8.3%** of FC transfers.
Criticism: "**tyranny of the base year**" after RDGs ended.
Local bodies get **₹7.91 lakh crore**; urban share raised to **45%**.

60.s: Which one of the following statements about the commonly cited figures for Finance Commission local-body grants is INCORRECT?
o: The ₹1.18 lakh crore figure is the correct Fourteenth Finance Commission grant to Panchayats.
The Fourteenth Finance Commission's total local-body grant was ₹2,87,436 crore.
The Fourteenth Finance Commission gave ₹2,00,292 crore to Panchayats.
The 41 per cent figure refers to the States' share, not the Rural Local Bodies' share of the divisible pool.
60.x: The ₹1.18 lakh crore figure is incorrect for the Fourteenth Finance Commission's Panchayat grant; the stated amount was ₹2,00,292 crore. The 41 per cent figure refers to the States' share.
60.tq: Identify the numerical misinformation by comparing the often-confused rural grant figure with the actual Panchayat allocation.
xs: The INCORRECT statement: "**₹1.18 lakh crore** is the 14th FC panchayat grant" — the correct figure is **₹2,00,292 crore** — option **(1)**.
The others are correct: 14th FC total **₹2,87,436 crore**; **41%** is the **States' share**, not the rural local bodies' share.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "15th FC raised RLB share from **40% to 41%**" is wrong.
**₹1.18 lakh crore** appears only as the 14th FC comparison for the **15th FC's ₹2.36 lakh crore** rural grant.
14th FC basic:performance: GPs **90:10**, municipalities **80:20**.

60.s: Which of the following statements regarding the 16th Finance Commission and Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Revenue deficit grants were increased and Andhra Pradesh's devolution share fell to 4.05%
Revenue deficit grants ended, while Andhra Pradesh's devolution share fell to 3%
Revenue deficit grants ended, while Andhra Pradesh's devolution share rose to 4.217%
The 16th Finance Commission restored the distinction between special and general category States
60.x: The 16th Finance Commission for 2026-31 ended revenue deficit grants, while Andhra Pradesh's devolution share rose to 4.217%, from the earlier 4.05%.
60.tq: Track both the direction of change and the exact revised percentage.
xs: The 16th FC **ended revenue deficit grants**, while **AP's share rose to 4.217%** (from **4.05%**) — option **(3)**.
AP's share did not fall; **4.05%** was its earlier share.
xa: The **GDP-contribution** criterion helped AP's share rise.
AP gets **₹28,785 crore** local body grants over **2026-31**.
Only **duly constituted LBs** qualify → **Rs 12,150 crore** at stake for AP's local polls.

60.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission (2026-31), local body grants of about ₹7.91 lakh crore were recommended. What share of these grants goes to urban local bodies?
60.x: The 16th FC raised the urban share of local body grants to 45% (about ₹3.6 lakh crore urban against about ₹4.4 lakh crore rural). 36% was the earlier urban share, 41% is the States' share of the divisible pool, and 60 per cent is not the urban share.
60.tq: 16th FC: ₹7.91 lakh crore to local bodies, urban share 45%.
xs: The 16th FC raised the **urban share** of local body grants to **about 45 per cent** — option **(3)**.
Of **₹7.91 lakh crore**: rural about **Rs 4.4 lakh crore**, urban about **Rs 3.6 lakh crore**.
**41%** is the **States' share** of the divisible pool, not the urban share.
xa: Some notes give urban as **~Rs 3.56 lakh crore**.
**Revenue-deficit grants** were discontinued.
AP: **₹28,785 crore** local body grants over **2026-31**.

60.s:
Which of the following are sub-schemes or components associated with the revamped RGSA?
1. Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program
2. Training of Trainers on own-source revenue
3. Urban GST Devolution Programme
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
60.x: The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program and Training of Trainers on own-source revenue are associated with RGSA. Urban GST devolution is not identified as an RGSA sub-scheme.
60.tq: Separate genuine scheme components from a thematically related but unrelated fiscal programme.
xs: **RGSA (revamped 2022)** sub-schemes include the **Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program** and **ToT on own-source revenue** — option **(2)**: 1 and 2 only.
An "Urban GST Devolution Programme" is not an RGSA component — RGSA is a panchayat scheme.
xa: RGSA trained **35 lakh+** participants in **FY25**.
**AMRUT 2.0 (2021)** rewards **property-tax reform** and **municipal bonds**.
**SVAMITVA** drone maps create a **rural property-tax baseline**.

60.s: Which reform is specifically rewarded under AMRUT 2.0?
o: Only privatisation of municipal water supply
Abolition of municipal property tax and bank loans
Replacement of municipal accounts by cash accounting
60.x: AMRUT 2.0 rewards progress in property-tax reform and the mobilisation of resources through municipal bonds.
60.tq: Identify the paired reforms associated with the named urban programme.
xs: **AMRUT 2.0 (2021)** rewards **property-tax reform** and **municipal bonds** — option **(2)**.
It rewards building up property tax and bond finance — not abolishing property tax.
xa: ⚠ Barrier: **weak accrual accounting** and **missing credit ratings** keep most LBs out of the bond market.
**Property tax** is the major own revenue of ULBs and panchayats.
15th FC performance conditions included **property-tax floor rates**.

60.s: The SVAMITVA scheme contributes to the strengthening of rural local finance primarily by:
o: Providing unconditional grants to Gram Panchayats
Transferring urban property taxes to rural bodies
Using drone maps to create a rural property-tax baseline
Issuing municipal bonds for village councils
60.x: SVAMITVA drone mapping helps create a baseline for rural properties, which can support the development of rural property-tax systems.
60.tq: Link the institutional tool to its practical fiscal application.
xs: **SVAMITVA** uses **drone maps** to create a **rural property-tax baseline** — option **(3)**.
It does not give grants or issue bonds; **municipal bonds** are rewarded under **AMRUT 2.0**.
xa: **Property (house) tax** is the main own revenue of Gram Panchayats (APPSC-GS **2018**).
**RGSA** runs **ToT on own-source revenue**.
Own taxes need **State Legislature** authorisation (**Art. 243H**).

60.s: The Technical Guidance and Support provided by the Comptroller and Auditor General over the audit of local bodies was recommended by which Finance Commission?
60.x: CAG Technical Guidance and Support over local-body audits was recommended by the Eleventh Finance Commission.
60.tq: Discriminate between closely related Finance Commission numbers.
xs: **CAG's Technical Guidance and Support (TGS)** over local body audit was recommended by the **11th FC** — option **(3)**, the Eleventh Finance Commission.
The 14th and 16th FCs are known for other things: **42%** share and the **GDP criterion** respectively.
xa: Audit of LB accounts is provided by State law under **Art. 243J / 243Z**.
15th FC performance conditions: **audited accounts** and **property-tax floor rates**.
**Weak accrual accounting** keeps most LBs out of the bond market.

60.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Institution)
a. Union Finance Commission
b. State Finance Commission

List-II (Constitutional provision and authority)
i. Article 243I — Governor
 ii. Article 280 — President

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
60.x: The Union Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 by the President, whereas the State Finance Commission is constituted under Article 243I by the Governor.
60.tq: Start from the sure article-authority pair and eliminate the reversed combination.
xs: **Union FC – Art. 280, President**; **SFC – Art. 243I, Governor** — option **(2)**: a–ii, b–i.
Option (1) swaps the two.
xa: Under **243I**, grants-in-aid come from the **State Consolidated Fund** on **SFC** advice.
Union FC grants to LBs are **routed through States**.
**SFC (243I)** and **SEC (243K)** are mandatory under the **73rd Amendment**.

60.s: Which one of the following changes is associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission award for 2026–31?
o: The GDP criterion was added and revenue-deficit grants were dropped.
The divisible pool was abolished and all grants became untied.
State Finance Commissions were replaced by the Union Finance Commission.
The GDP criterion was dropped and revenue-deficit grants were doubled.
60.x: The award adds a GDP criterion and drops revenue-deficit grants. It does not abolish the divisible pool or replace State Finance Commissions.
60.tq: Find the option containing both distinctive changes rather than a sweeping institutional claim.
xs: The **16th FC award (2026-31)** **added the GDP criterion** and **dropped revenue-deficit grants** — option **(1)**.
It also **retained 41%** as the States' share; the divisible pool and SFCs remain.
xa: GDP contribution (weight **10**) **replaces tax effort**.
Grants-in-aid of **₹9.47 lakh crore** are limited to **local bodies + disaster management**.
16th FC chair: **Dr Arvind Panagariya**.

60.s: Why are local elections being held in Andhra Pradesh in the context of the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants?
o: Local elections determine the State's share in Central taxes.
The Constitution requires all local elections to be held by the Union Government.
Only elected and duly constituted local bodies qualify for the grants.
The grants are available only to municipalities and not to Panchayats.
60.x: Only duly constituted local bodies qualify for the relevant Sixteenth Finance Commission grants, making local elections important; approximately ₹12,150 crore is at stake.
60.tq: Identify the eligibility condition that connects an administrative event with fiscal transfers.
xs: **Only duly constituted local bodies qualify** for 16th FC grants — option **(3)**; so AP is holding local polls.
About **Rs 12,150 crore** is at stake for AP.
Grants go to both rural and urban bodies: rural about **Rs 4.4 lakh crore**, urban about **Rs 3.6 lakh crore**.
xa: AP's total local body grants over **2026-31**: **₹28,785 crore**.
**Direct elections** and a **5-year term** are mandatory under the **73rd Amendment**, conducted by the **SEC (243K)**.

61.s: Which of the following pairs correctly states the number of subjects in the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules, respectively?
61.x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects relating to Panchayats, while the Twelfth Schedule contains 18 subjects relating to municipalities.
61.tq: Keep the Panchayat and municipal Schedule counts in their constitutional order.
xs: The **Eleventh Schedule** has **29** subjects (panchayats) and the **Twelfth Schedule** **18** (municipalities) — option **(2)**: 29 and 18.
Option (1) reverses them — the classic trap.
xa: **Neither Schedule transfers anything by itself**; Art. **243G/243W** say the State "**may**" devolve.
Panchayat taxing powers: **243H**; municipal equivalent: **243X**.
The 3Fs: **Functions**, **Funds**, **Functionaries**.

61.s:
Consider the following statements about constitutional devolution to local bodies:
1. The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules transfer subjects automatically without legislative action.
2. Article 243G relates to Panchayats.
3. Article 243W relates to municipalities.
4. The relevant Articles state that the State legislature may devolve powers and responsibilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. The Schedules do not themselves transfer subjects automatically; Articles 243G and 243W use the discretionary expression 'may' for devolution.
61.tq: Spot the absolute claim that the Schedules themselves transfer functions automatically.
xs: Statement 1 wrong: **neither Schedule transfers anything by itself** — devolution is **discretionary**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: **Art. 243G** is for **panchayats**, **Art. 243W** for **municipalities**.
Statement 4 correct: they say the State "**may**" devolve. So **2, 3 and 4 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: Likewise **243H/243X** (taxing powers) use "**may**".
This discretion is the **root cause** of weak devolution.
**DPC (243ZD)** and **MPC (243ZE)** are meant to **integrate plans**.

61.s: Which one of the following best describes the standard condition of 3F devolution in practice?
o: Staff are answerable to local bodies, while functions and funds are retained by the Union.
Functions, funds and functionaries are fully transferred to local bodies in an untied form.
Funds are untied, but functions remain exclusively with State departments.
Functions are devolved on paper, funds arrive tied to schemes, and staff report to State line departments.
61.x: The standard finding is that functions exist on paper, funds are commonly tied to schemes, and functionaries continue to report to State line departments.
61.tq: Compare the formal position with the operational reality across all three Fs.
xs: In practice, **functions are devolved on paper**, **funds arrive tied to schemes**, and **staff report to State line departments** — option **(4)**.
The ideal — **untied** funds and staff answerable to the local body — is what is missing, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: Result: PRIs are **reduced to implementing agencies**.
ULBs **depend on tied grants**; own revenue only **~0.3% of GDP**.
**Roadmap for Panchayati Raj** lists weak 3F devolution, **bureaucratic control**, **tied funds**, **dependence on grants**, **reluctance to tax**.

61.s: Which one of the following is the single most important source of own revenue for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)?
61.x: Property tax is the main own-source revenue of ULBs, although it remains under-assessed and under-collected.
61.tq: Directly identify the principal own-source revenue item.
xs: **Property tax** is the **single most important own revenue** of ULBs — option **(3)**.
It is **under-assessed** and **under-collected**, and property registers are **outdated**.
xa: ULB own revenue is only **~0.3% of GDP**.
**GST** cost ULBs ~**19%** of own revenue (**octroi**, **entry tax**).
**SVAMITVA** gives a **property-tax baseline** for rural homes.

61.s:
With reference to the finances of Urban Local Bodies, consider the following statements:
1. Their own-source revenue is only about 0.3% of GDP.
2. Cities produce about 67% of GDP.
3. Cities receive more than half of the country’s tax revenue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because cities receive less than 1% of tax revenue, despite producing about two-thirds of GDP.
61.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the revenue-share statement.
xs: Statement 1 correct: ULB own revenue is only **~0.3% of GDP**.
Statement 2 correct: cities produce **~2/3 (about 67%) of GDP**.
Statement 3 wrong: cities get **<1%** of tax revenue. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: **GST** cost ULBs ~**19%** of own revenue (octroi, entry tax).
ULBs **depend on tied grants**; property registers outdated.
**Weak balance sheets** keep most bodies out of the bond market.

61.s:
With reference to the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants for 2026–31, consider the following statements:
1. The urban share increased from 36% to 45%.
2. The grants are divided into 80% basic and 20% performance components.
3. Half of the basic grants are tied to sanitation and water.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: All three statements are correct: the urban share rises to 45%, the division is 80% basic and 20% performance, and 50% of basic grants are tied to sanitation and water.
61.tq: Check each numerical component before selecting the comprehensive option.
xs: Statement 1 correct: 16th FC urban share rose **36% → 45%**.
Statement 2 correct: **80% basic / 20% performance**.
Statement 3 correct: **basic grants 50% tied** (sanitation, water). So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: 16th FC (**2026-31**): rural **₹4.4 lakh crore**, urban **₹3.6 lakh crore** (~**₹75,000 crore** a year).
15th FC urban: about **₹1.2-1.3 lakh crore** (about **0.12-0.13%** of GDP).
Grant conditions: **properly constituted** LBs, **audited accounts**, **timely SFCs**.

61.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of bodies or arrangements identified as bypassing elected local bodies?
o: State Legislatures, Finance Commissions, DPCs and MPCs
DPCs, MPCs, Gram Sabhas and Zila Panchayats
DRDAs, user groups, SHGs and MPLADS/MLA LADS
61.x: DRDAs, user groups, SHGs and MPLADS/MLA LADS were identified as arrangements that bypass elected local bodies. DPCs and MPCs are constitutional planning bodies intended to integrate plans.
61.tq: Separate parallel or scheme-based bodies from constitutional planning and capacity-building institutions.
xs: **DRDAs**, **user groups**, **SHGs** and **MPLADS/MLA LADS** all bypass elected local bodies — option **(4)**.
**DPCs (243ZD)** and **MPCs (243ZE)** are constitutional bodies for **integration of plans**, not parallel bodies; **SIRDs**, **NIRDPR**, **eGramSwaraj** support PRIs.
xa: Under **MPLADS/MLA LADS**, **legislators pick the works**.
**Parastatals** and **SPVs** also bypass elected bodies and citizen participation.
The proposed **District Development Council** was criticised as a **parallel executive**.

61.s: Which of the following correctly matches the Andhra Pradesh-specific arrangements with the period in which they were associated?
o: Janmabhoomi committees—2014-19; village and ward secretariats and volunteers—2019
Janmabhoomi committees—2007-12; village and ward secretariats—2014
Janmabhoomi committees—2019; village and ward secretariats—2014-19
Janmabhoomi committees—2022-26; village and ward secretariats—2018-19
61.x: Janmabhoomi committees operated during 2014-19, while village and ward secretariats and volunteers were introduced in 2019; both were criticised as parallel to gram panchayats and wards.
61.tq: Match each AP-specific body with its correct period before judging the comparison.
xs: **Janmabhoomi committees – 2014-19**; **village/ward secretariats and volunteers – 2019** — option **(1)**.
Both were **criticised as parallel** to gram panchayats and wards.
xa: When terms lapse, AP local bodies are run by **Special Officers**.
AP gives **50%** women's reservation (Art. **243D** floor is **one-third**).
AP was showing a **local-body poll push** with **direct Mayor elections**.

61.s: The constitutional planning bodies intended to integrate plans at the district and metropolitan levels are, respectively:
o: DPC under Article 243ZD and MPC under Article 243ZE
MPC under Article 243ZD and DPC under Article 243ZE
DPC under Article 243G and MPC under Article 243W
DPC under Article 280 and MPC under Article 281
61.x: The District Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZD, while the Metropolitan Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZE.
61.tq: Match the planning body, territorial level and Article number in sequence.
xs: **DPC under Article 243ZD** (district) and **MPC under Article 243ZE** (metropolitan) — option **(1)** is correct; both exist for **integration of plans**.
Option 2 swaps them; **243G/243W** cover devolution of functions, not planning committees.
xa: **243K / 243ZA**: **SEC** for panchayats / municipalities.
**243E/243U**: **5-year term**; elections within **6 months** of dissolution.
**243D**: women's reservation floor of **one-third**.

61.s: With reference to MPLADS, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Gram Panchayat recommends works and the Election Commission executes them through eSAKSHI.
The Member of Parliament executes the works directly, and RTI does not apply.
The Member of Parliament recommends works, while the Implementing District Authority executes them; RTI applies and the eSAKSHI portal is associated with the scheme.
The State Finance Commission recommends works and the District Planning Committee executes them without any transparency law.
61.x: Under MPLADS, the MP recommends works and the Implementing District Authority executes them. RTI applies, and eSAKSHI is the associated portal.
61.tq: Ask who recommends and who executes; this separates legislative recommendation from administrative implementation.
xs: Under **MPLADS**, the **MP recommends** works and the **Implementing District Authority executes** them; **RTI applies**; **eSAKSHI** is the portal — option **(3)**.
The MP does not execute works directly, and RTI does apply, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: MPLADS/MLA LADS are criticised as bypassing PRIs because **legislators pick the works**.
Other parallel bodies: **DRDAs**, user groups, **SHGs**, **parastatals/SPVs**.

61.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the role of the Collector in Panchayati Raj administration?
o: Balwantrai Mehta — made the Collector the Zilla Parishad chairman
Hanumantha Rao — recommended complete abolition of the Collector’s role
Ashok Mehta — made the Collector the Zilla Parishad chairman
G.V.K. Rao — kept the Collector central without modification
61.x: Balwantrai Mehta made the Collector the chairman of the Zilla Parishad. Later committees split on the Collector's role, and none of them (Ashok Mehta, Hanumantha Rao or G.V.K. Rao) is correctly paired with the statement shown, so only A is correctly matched.
61.tq: Avoid swapping committee recommendations concerning the Collector.
