**Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)** = **State funding of elections**, partial funding **in kind**.
⚠ **Vohra (1993)** = **crime–politics nexus**.

64.s: The nationwide rollout of Electors Photo Identity Cards was initiated in 1993 under the leadership of:
64.x: The nationwide rollout of voter ID cards (EPIC) began in 1993 under CEC T.N. Seshan.
64.tq: Recall Seshan's 1993 reform.
n: Electors Photo Identity Cards (EPICs) had their nationwide rollout initiated in 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The nationwide rollout of EPICs was initiated under Chief Election Commissioner T. N. Seshan. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xs: The nationwide rollout of **EPIC** began in **1993** under CEC **T.N. Seshan** — option **(3)**.
**A.C. Jose** is linked to the case on the first EVM use (**A.C. Jose v. Sivan Pillai**), not EPIC.
xa: EPIC was introduced to prevent **bogus voting** and **impersonation**.
An EPIC number, once issued, is **valid for life**.
PYQ order: **EVM → photo ID → VVPAT → NOTA** (UPPSC 2025).

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. EVM first experimental use
 b. EPIC nationwide rollout initiated
 c. VVPAT first introduction
 d. NOTA implementation

List-II
 i. 1993
 ii. 27 September 2013

64.x: EVMs were first used on 19 May 1982, EPIC rolled out in 1993, VVPAT on 4 September 2013 and NOTA on 27 September 2013. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
64.tq: Recall the order: EVM 1982, EPIC 1993, VVPAT and NOTA 2013.
n: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) were first used experimentally on 19 May 1982. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
Electors Photo Identity Cards (EPICs) had their nationwide rollout initiated in 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) was first used on 4 September 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
None of the Above (NOTA) was implemented on 27 September 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
VVPAT was introduced before NOTA in 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
NOTA was mandated later in September 2013 than VVPAT was introduced. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xs: The correct code is **a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii** — option **(4)**.
**EVM** first experimental use = **19 May 1982**; **EPIC** rollout = **1993**.
**VVPAT** first introduced = **4 September 2013**; **NOTA** = **27 September 2013**.
xa: ⚠ **VVPAT** came **before NOTA** in **2013**.
**Section 61A** (RPA 1951) gave EVMs statutory backing in **1989**.
**2004** = first all-EVM Lok Sabha election.

64.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Parur Assembly Constituency
 b. Noksen Assembly Constituency
 c. Goa
 d. 14th Lok Sabha General Election

List-II
 i. First state-wide General Assembly election using EVMs
 ii. First nationwide general election entirely using EVMs

64.x: Parur saw the first EVM, Noksen the first VVPAT, Goa the first all-EVM State poll (1999), and the 14th Lok Sabha poll (2004) the first all-EVM general election. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
64.tq: Recall each EVM and VVPAT first.
n: The first experimental use of EVMs occurred in the Parur Assembly Constituency in Kerala. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The first VVPAT use occurred in the Noksen Assembly Constituency in Nagaland. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
Goa was the first State to conduct an entire General Assembly election using EVMs across all constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The 14th Lok Sabha General Election in 2004 was the first nationwide general election conducted entirely using EVMs. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xs: The correct code is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(2)**.
**Parur** (Kerala) = first **EVM** use; **Noksen** (Nagaland) = first **VVPAT**.
**Goa** = first state-wide Assembly election using EVMs (**1999**); **14th Lok Sabha** (**2004**) = first all-EVM general election.
xa: ⚠ **Gujarat** was **not** the first State to use EVMs in an Assembly election.
Noksen VVPAT use was a **by-election** on **4 September 2013**.
EVM makers: **BEL** (Bengaluru) and **ECIL** (Hyderabad).

64.s: Section 61A was inserted into the Representation of the People Act, 1951, in which year to provide statutory backing to Electronic Voting Machines?
64.x: Section 61A was added to the RPA, 1951 in 1989 to give EVMs legal backing, after the 1982 trial was challenged.
64.tq: Recall the 1989 Section 61A.
n: EVMs were later backed by statutory amendments to the Representation of the People Act, 1951. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
Section 61A was added to the Representation of the People Act, 1951, in 1989. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xs: **Section 61A** was added to the RPA 1951 in **1989** — option **(3)** — giving EVMs **statutory** backing.
**1982** was the first experimental use (Parur); **1993** = EPIC; **2013** = VVPAT and NOTA.
xa: First experimental use: **19 May 1982**, **Parur**, **Kerala** — **A.C. Jose v. Sivan Pillai**.
**1998:** wider trial in **16** Assembly seats.
M3 EVM records up to **2,000 votes**; one control unit takes up to **24 ballot units**.

64.s:

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

64.tq: Ask whether a date and place explain a court case.
n: The first experimental use of EVMs was associated with the A.C. Jose v. Sivan Pillai case. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A: the first EVM use is associated with **A.C. Jose v. Sivan Pillai**.
R: it took place on **19 May 1982** in **Parur**, **Kerala** — the date and place do not explain the case link.

**2004** = universal EVM use in the Lok Sabha election.

65.s: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
65.x: A.O. Hume is identified as the founder of the Indian National Congress, which was established in 1885.
65.tq: Use direct founder identification while distinguishing the founder from the first president.
xs: The **Indian National Congress** was founded by **A.O. Hume** in **1885** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**W.C. Bonnerjee** was the INC's **first president** (**1885**), not its founder.
xa: FIRST presidents: **INC** - **W.C. Bonnerjee**; **Jana Sangh** - **S.P. Mookerjee**; **BJP** - **A.B. Vajpayee**.

65.s: The Communist Party of India formally took shape at which conference?
65.x: Although the CPI dates its initial association with M.N. Roy and others at Tashkent in 1920, it was formally established at the Kanpur conference in 1925.
65.tq: Separate the preliminary formation at Tashkent from the formal establishment at Kanpur.
xs: The CPI formally took shape at the **Kanpur** conference in **1925** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Tashkent** (**1920**) was where **M.N. Roy** and others first formed it, but the exam year is **1925** (Kanpur).
xa: ⚠ **CPI**: **Tashkent (1920)** vs **Kanpur (1925)**.
The **CPI(M)** broke away from the CPI in **1964**.
The CPI marked its **100th foundation day** on **26 Dec 2025**.
**Puchalapalli Sundarayya** was secretary of the **Andhra Communist Party** (**Kakinada, 1936**).

65.s:
Match List-I (Party) with List-II (Founder):
List-I
A. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
B. Bharatiya Jana Sangh
C. Swatantra Party

List-II
1. C. Rajagopalachari

65.x: The DMK was founded by C.N. Annadurai (1949), the Bharatiya Jana Sangh by Syama Prasad Mookerjee (1951) and the Swatantra Party by C. Rajagopalachari (1959), so A-3, B-2, C-1. 65.s: In 1969, the Indian National Congress split into
65.x: The Congress split of 1969 produced Congress (Organisation) and Congress (Requisitionists), commonly abbreviated as Congress (O) and Congress (R).

65.s: Which of the following groups merged to form the Janata Party in 1977?

Congress for Democracy, NCP, BLD and Socialists

o: Congress(R), Janata Party, CPI and Lok Dal

65.s:

Statement 2 is wrong: the **AIADMK** split from the DMK after **Annadurai's** death.

65.s: With reference to the split in the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) in 2023, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Sharad Pawar faction retained the NCP name, and the Ajit Pawar faction formed the NCP-SP
The Ajit Pawar faction retained the NCP name, upheld by the top court, and the Sharad Pawar group formed the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar)
Both factions merged into the Indian National Congress
The Election Commission froze the NCP name and neither faction could use it
65.x: In the 2023 split the Ajit Pawar faction kept the NCP name, which the top court upheld, while Sharad Pawar's group became the NCP-SP (Sharadchandra Pawar). Option A reverses the factions; there was no merger with the INC and the name was not frozen.

xs: After the **2023** split the **Ajit Pawar** faction kept the **NCP** name (upheld by the top court); **Sharad Pawar**'s group formed the **NCP-SP** (**Sharadchandra Pawar**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the factions; there was no merger with the INC and the name was not frozen.
xa: ⚠ After **2023**: **Ajit Pawar** = **NCP** (name kept); **Sharad Pawar** = **NCP-SP**.
**Sharad Pawar and Supriya Sule** lead the **NCP-SP**.
The **NCP** was formed in **1999** by **Sharad Pawar**, out of the INC.

65.s: India is described as a multi-party system primarily because political divisions occur along the lines of

65.s:

Statement 3 is wrong: parties **seldom hold real internal elections** — weak **inner-party democracy**.

**Defections** are handled by the **Tenth Schedule** (**52nd Amendment, 1985**).
Parties must **disclose donors above ₹20,000** every year.

65.s:

Statement 2 is wrong: **parties seek power**; **pressure groups seek influence**.

65.s: Which one of the following statements regarding election symbols is correct?
o: Recognised parties receive reserved symbols, whereas registered unrecognised parties and independents choose from the free symbols list.
Only national parties are allotted reserved symbols.
Registered unrecognised parties cannot contest elections using any symbol.
Recognised parties and independents must choose symbols from the same reserved-symbol list.
65.x: Recognised parties receive reserved symbols. Registered unrecognised parties and independents choose symbols from the free symbols list.
65.tq: Use the contrast between reserved symbols and the free-symbol list to eliminate reversed comparisons.
xs: **Recognised parties** get **reserved symbols**; **RUPPs and independents** choose from the **free symbols list** — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: The free symbols list had **184** symbols in **May 2025**.
Recognition is under the **Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968**.
The satirical "**Cockroach Janta Party**" put the **Symbols Order** back in the news (**11 Jun 2026**).
**RUPPs**: **2,800+** registered, only about **750** contested **2024**.

65.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated route for recognition as a State party?

Securing 10 per cent of votes alone
Securing 6 per cent of votes and two Assembly seats
Securing 6 per cent of votes in a Lok Sabha election and one Lok Sabha seat

xs: **10 per cent of votes alone** is not a route to State-party status — so option **(2)** is the answer.
The vote-only route is **8% of votes** alone.
Valid routes also include **6% of votes + 2 Assembly seats** and **6% in a Lok Sabha poll + 1 LS seat**.

Meeting **any one** of these criteria suffices.
**National status**: **AAP** in **2023**; **NPP** was the first from the **North-East**.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the registration of a political party under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951:
1. The party's constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to socialism, secularism and democracy.
2. The party must apply within 90 days of its formation.

65.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the application must be made within 30 days of formation, not 90. Statement 1 is correct: the party constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to socialism, secularism, democracy and national integrity. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' each misjudge one statement.
65.tq: Section 29A: 30 days + allegiance to socialism, secularism, democracy.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(2)** "**1 only**".
1: the party constitution must pledge allegiance to the **Constitution** and to **socialism, secularism and democracy** (and national integrity).
2 is wrong: the party must apply within **30 days** of formation, not 90.
xa: Registration is under **Section 29A, RPA 1951**; recognition under the **Election Symbols Order, 1968**.
**INC v. Institute of Social Welfare (2002):** ECI **cannot deregister** a party except for fraud, loss of allegiance, or unlawful declaration.
Parties must **disclose donors above ₹20,000**; cash only up to **₹2,000**.

65.s: Political parties were not mentioned in the original Constitution. They entered the constitutional framework through the:

Eleventh Schedule, inserted by the 73rd Amendment
Fourth Schedule, inserted by the 42nd Amendment
Eighth Schedule, inserted by the 44th Amendment

xs: Parties entered the Constitution via the **Tenth Schedule**, inserted by the **52nd Amendment in 1985** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Parties had **no mention in the original Constitution**.

65.s:
Consider the following statements regarding INC v. Institute of Social Welfare (2002):

2. Deregistration may be possible in cases of fraud.
3. Deregistration may be possible where a party loses allegiance to the Constitution or is declared unlawful.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
65.x: The decision restricted the Election Commission's deregistration power, while recognising exceptions involving fraud, loss of allegiance and a party being declared unlawful.
65.tq: Combine the general rule with its listed exceptions instead of treating deregistration as wholly impossible.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**INC v. Institute of Social Welfare (2002)**: the ECI **cannot deregister** a party, except for **fraud**, **loss of allegiance**, or the party being **declared unlawful**.
xa: **Registration** is under **Sec. 29A** of the RPA, applied for **within 30 days** of formation.
Non-compliant **RUPPs** are now **delisted** after State CEOs verify them.
**2,800+** RUPPs are registered; only about **750** contested **2024**.

65.s:
Consider the following statements about the funding of political parties:
1. Parties must disclose every year the donors who give more than Rs 20,000.
2. Cash donations are permitted up to Rs 20,000; only larger donations need a cheque or bank transfer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: Statement 1 is correct: donors above Rs 20,000 must be disclosed annually. Statement 2 is wrong: donations above Rs 2,000 must be by cheque or bank transfer; Rs 20,000 is the disclosure threshold, not the cash cap. So '1 only'.
65.tq: Two numbers, two rules: 20,000 = disclosure, 2,000 = cash cap.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: parties must **disclose donors above ₹20,000** every year.
Statement 2 is wrong: donations above **₹2,000** must be by **cheque or bank transfer**.
xa: ⚠ **₹20,000** = disclosure limit; **₹2,000** = cash limit.
Parties are **tax-exempt** under **Sec. 12 of the Income-tax Act, 2025**.
Electoral bonds were struck down in **ADR v. Union of India** (**15 Feb 2024**).

xs: Electoral bonds were struck down in **ADR v. Union of India** on **15 Feb 2024** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**INC v. Institute of Social Welfare** (**2002**) is about **deregistration**, not bonds.

Tax exemption now under **Sec. 12 of the Income-tax Act, 2025**.
The **Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)** backed partial **State funding in kind**.

xs: The correct order is **B, D, C, A** — option **(3)**.
xa: ⚠ CPI: **Tashkent** (**1920**) vs **Kanpur** conference (**1925**) — exam year is **1925**.
**CPI(M)** came from the **1964** split of the CPI.
Other dates: **DMK 1949**, **Swatantra 1959**, **BJP 1980**.

65.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
 a. Indian National Congress
 b. Bharatiya Jana Sangh
 c. Bharatiya Janata Party
 d. Nationalist Congress Party

List-II
 i. First President: Atal Bihari Vajpayee

 iii. First President: W.C. Banerjee
 iv. Split from INC by Sharad Pawar, P.A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar
65.x: W.C. Banerjee was the Congress's first president, Syama Prasad Mookerjee founded the Jana Sangh, Vajpayee was the BJP's first president, and Pawar, Sangma and Anwar formed the NCP. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
65.tq: Match each party to its founder.
n: W.C. Banerjee was the first president of the Indian National Congress. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee founded the Bharatiya Jana Sangh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the first president of the Bharatiya Janata Party. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Nationalist Congress Party split from the Indian National Congress. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]

Tariq Anwar was associated with the split that formed the Nationalist Congress Party. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
xs: The correct code is **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**INC** first president = **W.C. Banerjee**; **Jana Sangh** founder = **Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee**.
**BJP** first president = **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**; **NCP** = split from INC by **Sharad Pawar, P.A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar**.
xa: ⚠ Other notes spell the first INC president **W.C. Bonnerjee**.
**NCP** formed in **1999**; split in **2023** — **Ajit Pawar** faction kept the name; Sharad Pawar = **NCP-SP**.

65.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The BJP was formed in 1980 and succeeded the BJS.
II. The BSP was formed in 1984.
III. The Samajwadi Party was formed in 1998.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
65.x: I and II are correct: the BJP was formed in 1980 as the Jana Sangh's successor, and the BSP in 1984. III is false because the Samajwadi Party was formed in 1992; 1998 is the Trinamool Congress.
65.tq: Recall the years parties were founded.
n: The Bharatiya Janata Party was formed in 1980. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Bharatiya Janata Party succeeded the Bharatiya Jana Sangh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Bahujan Samaj Party was formed in 1984. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Samajwadi Party was formed in 1992. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
xs: Statements **I and II only** are correct — option **(4)**.
I: **BJP** formed in **1980**, succeeding the **Bharatiya Jana Sangh**; II: **BSP** formed in **1984** by **Kanshi Ram**.
III is wrong: the **Samajwadi Party** was formed in **1992**; **1998** is the **Trinamool Congress**.
xa: **AAP** = **2012** (Arvind Kejriwal).
**Republican Party of India** was planned by **Dr B.R. Ambedkar** (APPSC-GS 2025).

65.s:
How many of the following parties were formed in 1980 or later?

65.x: Five were formed in 1980 or later: BJP (1980), BSP (1984), SP (1992), TMC (1998) and NCP (1999). The CPI dates from 1925.
65.tq: Check each party's year against 1980.
n: The Communist Party of India was formed in 1925. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Bharatiya Janata Party was formed in 1980. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Bahujan Samaj Party was formed in 1984. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]

xs: **Only five** were formed in 1980 or later — option **(3)**.
The **Communist Party of India** dates from **1925**.
xa: **AITC** is also known as **TMC**.
**Janata Dal** formed on **11 Oct 1988**.
**CPI** marked its **100th foundation day** on **26 Dec 2025**.

66.s: Which one of the following statements regarding political parties and the Constitution of India, as originally adopted, is correct?
o: The Constitution recognised only national parties.
The Constitution contained no specific provision regarding political parties.
The Constitution made coalition government compulsory.
The Constitution prescribed a two-party system.
66.x: The Constitution, as adopted, said nothing specifically about political parties.
66.tq: Test the constitutional omission directly and avoid importing later political developments.
xs: The Constitution as adopted **said nothing about political parties** — it **contained no specific provision** on them — so option **(2)** is correct.
It neither recognised only national parties nor prescribed a two-party or coalition system.
xa: Parties first entered the Constitution via the **anti-defection law** (**Tenth Schedule**, **52nd Amendment, 1985**).
India has a **multi-party system**, unlike the two-party **UK** and **USA**.
Parties are classed by ECI status as **national**, **state** and **registered-unrecognised**.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the classification of political parties in India:
1. On the basis of Election Commission status, parties are classified as national parties, State parties and coalition parties.
2. On the basis of organisational character, parties are classified as cadre parties and mass parties.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statement 2 is correct: by organisation, parties are cadre or mass parties. Statement 1 is wrong: by ECI status the categories are national, State and registered-unrecognised parties; 'coalition party' is not an ECI category. So '2 only' is right and the other options misjudge one statement.
66.tq: ECI status: national / State / registered-unrecognised.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(1)** "**2 only**".
2: by organisation, parties are **cadre** or **mass** parties.
1 is wrong: by ECI status, parties are **national, state** and **registered-unrecognised** — "coalition party" is not an ECI category.
xa: India has a **multi-party system** as society divides along **region, language, caste, religion and class**.
The Constitution as adopted **said nothing about political parties**.
Over **2,800** RUPPs, only about **750** contested the 2024 election.

66.s:
Consider the following statements regarding registered-unrecognised political parties:
1. They constitute a very large segment of India’s registered political parties.
2. Their number is over 2,800.
3. All such parties contested the 2024 general election.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: There were over 2,800 registered-unrecognised parties, but only about 750 contested the 2024 general election; hence statement 3 is false.
66.tq: Use the numerical contrast to reject the extreme claim that all registered parties contested the election.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: there are **over 2,800 registered unrecognised parties** — a very large segment.
Statement 3 is wrong: only about **750** of them contested the **2024** general election.
xa: Classification by ECI status: **national, state, registered-unrecognised**.
Classification by organisation: **cadre vs mass**.
⚠ **2,800+** registered vs ~**750** contested.

66.s: Which election is associated with the beginning of the coalition era in the States, rather than with the end of the Congress system at the national level?
66.x: The 1967 election led to the loss of Congress power in several States and marked the beginning of the coalition era in the States.
66.tq: Separate closely related election milestones by identifying the level of government involved.
xs: The **fourth general election of 1967** began the **coalition era in the States** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Congress lost power in several States; **Samyukta Vidhayak Dal** governments followed.
**1971** = end of Congress dominance (**APPSC 2007** key); **1977** = first non-Congress government at the Centre; **1989** = end of the 'Congress system'.
xa: After **1967**, rich and middle peasants defected from Congress; **Jana Sangh** and **Swatantra** formed fronts.
Exception: **Tamil Nadu** (**DMK** alone).
⚠ Match: **1967** (States), **1971** (APPSC key), **1977** (Centre), **1989** (multi-party era).

66.s:
Match List-I (Term/work) with List-II (Scholar):
A. 'Congress system'
B. 'One-party dominance'
C. Party Building in a New Nation
1. Myron Weiner
2. W.H. Morris-Jones
3. Rajni Kothari
66.x: Rajni Kothari coined 'Congress system' (1964); W.H. Morris-Jones described 'one-party dominance' (dominance co-existing with competition); Myron Weiner wrote Party Building in a New Nation on Congress as a party-building organisation. So A-3, B-2, C-1; the other codes swap these scholars.
66.tq: Kothari = Congress system; Morris-Jones = one-party dominance; Weiner = party building.
xs: The correct match is **A-3, B-2, C-1** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**'Congress system'** → **Rajni Kothari** (**1964**).
**'One-party dominance'** → **W.H. Morris-Jones** (dominance co-existing with competition).
**Party Building in a New Nation** → **Myron Weiner**.
xa: The Congress system phase ran **1952-1977**, with Congress as an **umbrella** party.
It gave way after the **1969** split to **Indira Gandhi's personalised politics** (**1971**).

66.s: As per the APPSC (2007) answer key, which general election is regarded as marking the end of Congress dominance, when the umbrella 'Congress system' gave way to Indira Gandhi's personalised politics after the 1969 split?
66.x: The APPSC 2007 key gives the fifth general election (1971): after the 1969 split, the umbrella Congress system gave way to Indira Gandhi's personalised politics. 1967 ended Congress rule in several States, 1977 brought the first non-Congress government at the Centre, and 1989 is cited (e.g. RPSC 2023) as the end of the Congress system in the multi-party era.
66.tq: 1967 States; 1971 APPSC key; 1977 Centre; 1989 end of Congress system.
xs: The **APPSC 2007** key gives the **Fifth general election, 1971** — so option **(2)** is correct.
After the **1969** split, the umbrella "Congress system" gave way to **Indira Gandhi's personalised politics**.
**1967** ended Congress rule in several **States**; **1977** brought the first non-Congress government at the **Centre**; **1989** is cited (**RPSC 2023**) as the end of the Congress system.
xa: ⚠ "End of Congress dominance" (APPSC) = **1971**; "end of Congress system" (RPSC) = **1989**.
"Congress system" — **Rajni Kothari**; "one-party dominance" — **W.H. Morris-Jones**.
**1967** → **Samyukta Vidhayak Dal** governments in the States.

66.s: The first non-Congress government at the Centre was formed in which year under the leadership of which Prime Minister?
66.x: The Janata Party formed the first non-Congress government at the Centre in 1977, with Morarji Desai as Prime Minister.
66.tq: Use the first-and-year association to distinguish 1977 from the later coalition milestones.
xs: The first non-Congress government at the Centre came in **1977** under **Morarji Desai** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1989** (V.P. Singh) was the first non-Congress **coalition of the multi-party era**, not the first non-Congress government.
**1996** (Deve Gowda) was the **United Front**; **1967** saw coalitions only in the **States**.
xa: The **Janata Party** defeated the INC after the **Emergency** — Congress's first general-election loss since independence.
It was also the **first coalition-type government** at the Centre, yet had a **Lok Sabha majority**.
Congress returned in **1980**.

66.s: The return of the Congress Party to power at the Centre after the Janata government occurred in:
66.x: Congress returned to power at the Centre in 1980 after the Janata government period.
66.tq: Test a precise year through close chronological distractors.
xs: Congress returned to power at the Centre in **1980** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Janata Party** government of **Morarji Desai** ran **1977-79**.
xa: The Janata win of **1977** came after the **Emergency**.
Next Congress defeat: **1989**, when it stayed the **single largest party** (INC **197**) but sat in opposition.
**16th Lok Sabha (2014)**: BJP **282 of 543** — first single-party majority since **1984**.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Front government of 1989-90:
1. It was headed by V.P. Singh.
2. It was a majority government of the Janata Dal alone.
3. It survived on outside support from the BJP and the Left.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statement 1 is correct: V.P. Singh headed the National Front (Janata Dal + regional parties). Statement 2 is wrong: it was a minority government of a front, not a Janata Dal majority. Statement 3 is correct: the BJP and the Left supported it from outside. So '1 and 3 only'.
66.tq: 'Front' and 'outside support' both signal a minority coalition - reject statement 2.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **V.P. Singh** headed the **National Front** (**1989-90**).
Statement 2 is wrong: it was a **minority** government of the **Janata Dal + regional parties**.
Statement 3 is correct: it had outside support of the **BJP and Left**.
xa: The **Janata Dal** was created on **11 October 1988** from **Jan Morcha, Congress(S), Janata and Lok Dal**.
The **National Front** was formed in **August 1988**.
**1989**: Janata Dal won **143** seats, BJP **85**.

66.s: Which Prime Minister headed the minority Congress government that completed a full term from 1991 to 1996?
66.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao headed the minority Congress government from 1991 to 1996, and it completed a full term.
66.tq: Focus on the unusual combination of a minority government and completion of a full term.
xs: **P.V. Narasimha Rao** headed the minority Congress government that completed a **full term** (**1991-96**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Manmohan Singh** led the **UPA** (**2004-14**).
xa: **APPSC 2007** key: "only minority government to continue under two PMs" = Congress government led by **P.V. Narasimha Rao**.
⚠ Doubt: the **United Front** (**Deve Gowda** then **Gujral**) is the obvious two-PM minority government; learn the key, know the doubt.
Rao's government followed **Chandra Shekhar** (**1990-91**).

66.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the United Front governments:
1. H.D. Deve Gowda and I.K. Gujral successively served as Prime Ministers.
2. The governments were formed during 1996–98.
3. Congress provided outside support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All three statements are correct. The United Front governments during 1996–98 were headed successively by Deve Gowda and Gujral and received outside support from Congress.
66.tq: Check the leadership, period and support arrangement separately in a coalition sequence.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **United Front** (**1996-98**) had **H.D. Deve Gowda** then **I.K. Gujral** as PMs.
It was a **minority** government with **Congress outside support**.
xa: Its coordinating document was a **Common Minimum Programme** (**1996**).
⚠ The **APPSC 2007** key still names **P.V. Narasimha Rao**'s government as the "only minority government under two PMs".
**1996** began with Vajpayee's **13-day** BJP government.

66.s: Which of the following correctly describes the NDA government led by A.B. Vajpayee?
o: It governed from 1998 to 2004 and was a coalition of parties with no previous experience of working together.
It governed from 1989 to 1990 as a minority government supported by the Left.
It governed from 1991 to 1996 as a minority Congress government.
It governed from 2004 to 2014 under the leadership of Manmohan Singh.
66.x: The NDA government led by A.B. Vajpayee governed from 1998 to 2004 and involved parties that had no prior experience of working together; it governed for about six years.
66.tq: Use the government’s period, leader and coalition character together to reject swapped descriptions.
xs: The **NDA** under **A.B. Vajpayee** governed **1998 to 2004** as a coalition of parties with **no experience of working together** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1989-90** was the **National Front**; **1991-96** was **Rao**'s Congress; **2004-14** was **Manmohan Singh**'s **UPA**.
xa: The NDA governed for **~six years**.
Its document was the "**National Agenda for Governance**" (**1998**).

66.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding coalition arrangements in India.
List-I (Coalition arrangement)
 a. United Front
 b. National Democratic Alliance
 c. United Progressive Alliance

List-II (Programme and year)
 i. National Common Minimum Programme — 2004
 ii. National Agenda for Governance — 1998
 iii. Common Minimum Programme — 1996

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
66.x: The United Front adopted its Common Minimum Programme in 1996, the NDA its National Agenda for Governance in 1998, and the UPA its National Common Minimum Programme in 2004.
66.tq: Start from the sure programme-year pair and eliminate codes with a misplaced pairing.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–ii, c–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**United Front** → **CMP (1996)**.
**NDA** → "**National Agenda for Governance**" (**1998**).
**UPA** → "**National Common Minimum Programme**" (**2004**).
xa: Coalitions coordinate through a **Common Minimum Programme** + **coordination committee** of constituents.
The UPA (**2004-14**) was a coalition led by **Congress** under **Manmohan Singh**.

66.s:
Match List-I (Lok Sabha) with List-II (Seats of major parties):
List-I
A. 9th Lok Sabha (1989)
B. 11th Lok Sabha (1996)
C. 13th Lok Sabha (1999)

List-II
1. BJP 182, INC 114
2. INC 197, Janata Dal 143, BJP 85
3. BJP 161, INC 140

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: 1989: INC 197 (largest), Janata Dal 143, BJP 85; 1996: BJP 161 (largest), INC 140; 1999: BJP 182, INC 114. So A-2, B-3, C-1. The other codes put the BJP ahead in 1989 or mix up the 1996 and 1999 BJP figures.
66.tq: Only 1989 has the Janata Dal; BJP rises 161 -> 182 from 1996 to 1999.
xs: The correct match is **A-2, B-3, C-1** — so option **(2)** is correct.
xa: **16th (2014)**: BJP **282 of 543** — first single-party majority since **1984**.
⚠ In **1989** Congress was the **largest party** yet sat in opposition.

66.s: Which statement correctly describes the 2014 Lok Sabha election?
o: BJP won 282 of 543 seats, securing the first single-party majority since 1984.
BJP and Congress together won exactly 282 seats.
Congress won 282 of 543 seats, securing the first single-party majority since 1984.
BJP won 182 of 543 seats and formed a minority government.
66.x: In 2014, BJP won 282 of the 543 Lok Sabha seats, marking the first single-party majority since 1984.
66.tq: Combine the seat count, total strength and historical comparison to identify the precise statement.
xs: In **2014** the **BJP** won **282 of 543** seats — the **first single-party majority since 1984** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**182** was the BJP's tally in **1999**, not **2014**.
xa: The BJP's majority in **2014** ended the **1989-2014** multi-party era.
BJP now rules alone in **11 States** (**12 Aug 2026**).

66.s:
Consider the following statements about coalition governments in the States after the 1967 elections:
1. Tamil Nadu, too, was ruled by a coalition of opposition parties.
2. They were commonly known as Samyukta Vidhayak Dal governments.
3. Rich and middle peasants defecting from the Congress contributed to their rise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the post-1967 State coalitions were Samyukta Vidhayak Dal governments, helped by rich and middle peasants defecting from the Congress (Jana Sangh and Swatantra also formed fronts). Statement 1 is wrong: Tamil Nadu was the exception, where the DMK ruled alone. So '2 and 3 only'.
66.tq: 1967 = SVD governments; Tamil Nadu (DMK alone) is the exception.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
2: post-**1967** State coalitions were **Samyukta Vidhayak Dal** governments.
3: **rich and middle peasants** defecting from the Congress helped their rise.
1 is wrong: **Tamil Nadu** was the exception — the **DMK** ruled alone.
xa: **Jana Sangh** and **Swatantra** also formed fronts.
**Kerala** is a bipolar coalition State: **UDF** vs **LDF**.
**AP:** Congress dominance until **1983**, then Congress v **TDP**; since **2014** **TDP v YSRCP**.

66.s: Which one of the following State-level party systems is correctly matched?
o: Kerala — United Democratic Front and Left Democratic Front
Kerala — Congress and Telugu Desam Party
Andhra Pradesh — Bharatiya Janata Party and Left Democratic Front
Andhra Pradesh — United Democratic Front and Left Democratic Front
66.x: Kerala is characterised by a bipolar contest between the United Democratic Front and the Left Democratic Front.
66.tq: Find the correctly matched State-party combination and reject cross-state substitutions.
xs: **Kerala — UDF and LDF** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
Kerala: **UDF** (Congress-led) vs **LDF** (CPI-M-led); the leading party's legislature leader becomes CM.
**Andhra Pradesh** is bipolar too, but between **Congress v TDP** and later **TDP v YSRCP** — not UDF/LDF or BJP/LDF.
xa: AP: **Congress dominance until 1983**; since **2014**: **TDP v YSRCP**.
AP now: a coalition where a **regional party** is dominant and the **BJP supports** it.

66.s:
Arrange the following phases of the Andhra Pradesh party system in chronological order:
A. Congress dominance
B. Congress–Telugu Desam Party competition
C. Telugu Desam Party–YSR Congress Party competition

Select the correct sequence.
66.x: Congress dominance continued until 1983; thereafter the principal contest was between Congress and the Telugu Desam Party, and since 2014 it has been between the Telugu Desam Party and the YSR Congress Party.
66.tq: Use the dated transition points to establish the first, middle and latest phases.
xs: The order is **A, B, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Congress dominance** until **1983**; then **Congress v TDP**; since **2014**: **TDP v YSRCP**.
xa: AP now: coalition with a **regional party** dominant and **BJP supporting** (also **Meghalaya, Nagaland, Puducherry**).
**Kerala** is the other **bipolar** State: **UDF** vs **LDF**.
The **Justice Party**-era awakening of **non-Brahmin agrarian castes** laid the base for regional parties in Andhra.

66.s: The political arrangement described for Andhra Pradesh in the current context is best characterised as one in which:
o: A coalition is led by the Congress Party with no regional party.
Two national parties share power equally without regional participation.
A regional party is the dominant coalition partner and the Bharatiya Janata Party provides support.
A national party is the sole governing party.
66.x: The arrangement is a coalition in which a regional party is the dominant partner and the Bharatiya Janata Party supports it.
66.tq: Identify the dominant partner and supporting partner instead of treating every coalition as an equal alliance.
xs: AP has a coalition where a **regional party is the dominant partner** and the **BJP supports** it — so option **(3)** is correct.
The same pattern holds in **Meghalaya, Nagaland, Puducherry**.
xa: AP history: **Congress dominance until 1983** → **Congress v TDP** → **TDP v YSRCP** since **2014**.
Coalitions now govern **10** States (**12 Aug 2026**).
Major consequence of coalitions: **increased role of regional and small parties**.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about coalition politics:
1. It encourages consensus building.
2. It may slow decision-making and lead to policy reversals or delays.
3. Compromises can dilute strong policy measures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Coalition politics may promote consensus, but the need for compromise can slow decisions, cause policy reversals or delays, and dilute strong measures.
66.tq: Balance the positive and negative consequences instead of treating coalition politics as wholly stable or unstable.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Coalitions bring **consensus building** but **slow decisions**, **policy reversals/delays**.
**Compromises dilute strong measures**.
xa: Checks and balances: **no single party holds absolute power**; **regional representation** in national policy.
**Federalism** became more **bargained** after **1989**.
Major consequence (APPSC key): **increased role of regional and small parties**.

66.s: Defections and horse-trading in coalition politics led directly to which constitutional measure?
o: The Ninth Schedule through the First Amendment
The Tenth Schedule through the 52nd Amendment in 1985
The Eleventh Schedule through the 73rd Amendment
The Twelfth Schedule through the 74th Amendment
66.x: Defections and horse-trading led to the anti-defection law, introduced through the Tenth Schedule by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
66.tq: Match the political problem with the correct Schedule, Amendment and year.
xs: Defections and horse-trading led to the **anti-defection law** — the **Tenth Schedule** through the **52nd Amendment in 1985** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **first time parties entered the Constitution**.
xa: The Constitution as adopted **said nothing about political parties**.
Other coalition effects: **slow decisions**, **regional representation**, **bargained federalism**.
Coalition coordination: **Common Minimum Programme** + **coordination committee**.

66.s: Federalism in India became more bargained after:
66.x: The bargaining character of federalism became more pronounced after 1989 in the context of coalition politics.
66.tq: Test the turning-point year through a sequence of major party-system changes.
xs: Federalism became more **bargained** after **1989** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**1989** began the **multi-party coalition era** at the Centre, lasting to **2014**.
**1967** began coalitions in the **States**; **1977** gave the first non-Congress Centre government.
xa: Coalition effect: **regional representation** in national policy.
Major consequence (APPSC key): **increased role of regional and small parties**.
**1989**: the end of the 'Congress system' (**RPSC 2023**).

66.s: Which one of the following is regarded as a major consequence of coalition politics in India?
o: Increased role of regional and small parties
66.x: The APPSC key identifies the increased role of regional and small parties as the major consequence of coalition politics. India did not become a two-party system; coalition politics ended one-party dominance rather than strengthening it; and defections led to the anti-defection law (52nd Amendment, 1985), not its abolition.
66.tq: Coalition era = regional and small parties gain weight.
xs: The APPSC key's major consequence of coalition politics is the **increased role of regional and small parties** — so option **(1)** is correct.
India did not become a **two-party** system; coalitions ended **one-party dominance**.
Defections led to the **anti-defection law** (**52nd Amendment, 1985**), not its abolition.
xa: Coalitions bring **consensus building** but **slow decisions**.
No single party holds **absolute power**.
**Federalism** became more **bargained** after **1989**.

66.s: Which development marked the end of the multi-party era that extended from 1989 to 2014?
o: The creation of the INDIA bloc in 2026
Formation of the United Front in 1996
The BJP winning a majority on its own in 2014
66.x: The multi-party era of 1989–2014 ended when the BJP won a majority on its own in the 2014 general election.
66.tq: Link the era-ending event with the correct year rather than with an earlier coalition formation.
xs: The **1989-2014** multi-party era ended when the **BJP won a majority on its own in 2014** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **United Front** (**1996**) and **NDA** (**1998**) were coalitions within that era.
xa: **2014**: BJP **282 of 543** — first single-party majority since **1984**.
BJP now rules alone in **11 States**.
The **INDIA bloc** met on **8 June 2026**.

66.s: The awakening of which social group during the Justice Party era is regarded as having laid the base for regional parties in Andhra?
66.x: The Justice Party-era awakening of non-Brahmin agrarian castes laid the social base for regional parties in Andhra.
66.tq: Identify the specific social base and avoid replacing it with a broader but unsupported group.
xs: The **Justice Party**-era awakening of **non-Brahmin agrarian castes** laid the base for regional parties in Andhra — so option **(3)** is correct.
The notes tie this base to agrarian **non-Brahmin** castes, not tribal groups, labour unions or Brahmin professionals.
xa: AP party system: **Congress dominance until 1983**, then **Congress v TDP**.
Since **2014**: **TDP v YSRCP**.
AP now: regional party dominant, **BJP supporting**.

66.s: At the INDIA bloc meeting referred to, which party was described as the only party present in all States?
66.x: The Congress was described as the only party present in all States.
66.tq: Match the organisational reach claim with the party identified in the political context.
xs: At the **INDIA bloc** meeting (**8 June 2026**), the **Indian National Congress** was called the **only party present in all States** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **TDP** and **YSRCP** are Andhra regional parties, contesting each other since **2014**.
xa: Congress rules alone in **3** States; the **BJP** in **11**.
In **1989** Congress was still the **single largest party** (**197**) but sat in opposition.
The INC led the **UPA** (**2004-14**) under **Manmohan Singh**.

66.s: Who coined the term “One-Party Dominant System” or “Congress System”?
66.x: Political scientist Rajni Kothari coined 'one-party dominant system', or 'Congress system', for the post-independence pattern.
66.tq: Recall Rajni Kothari.
n: Rajni Kothari coined the term “One-Party Dominant System.” [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
Rajni Kothari coined the term “Congress System.” [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
xs: **Rajni Kothari** coined "**One-Party Dominant System**" and "**Congress System**" — option **(2)**.
It describes Congress dominating a **democratic, multi-party** landscape after independence.
xa: ⚠ Other notes credit "**one-party dominance**" to **W.H. Morris-Jones**, Kothari only with "Congress system".
**Myron Weiner** = Congress as a party-building organisation.
Phase 1 (**1952-1977**) = Congress as an **umbrella** of many interests.

66.s:
Assertion (A): The “Congress System” referred to a one-party dominant system in India.
Reason (R): It characterized a democratic, multi-party electoral landscape dominated by the Congress party after independence.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
66.x: Both are true: the 'Congress system' meant one party dominating a competitive, multi-party democracy. R gives that meaning, so R explains A.
66.tq: Recall Kothari's idea of the Congress system.
n: Rajni Kothari coined the term “Congress System.” [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Congress System characterized India’s democratic, multi-party electoral landscape after independence. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Congress party dominated India’s democratic, multi-party electoral landscape after independence. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
The "**Congress System**" meant a **one-party dominant** system: Congress **dominated** a **democratic, multi-party** electoral landscape after **independence**.
xa: Coined by **Rajni Kothari**.
It ended with the **1989** general election.
⚠ **Kothari** = "Congress system"; **Morris-Jones** = "one-party dominance"; **Weiner** = party building.

66.s: Which election marked the end of the “Congress System”?
66.x: The 1989 general election ended the Congress system and began the era of minority and coalition governments.
66.tq: Recall the 1989 turning point.
n: The 1989 General Election marked the end of the Congress System. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The 1989 General Election ushered in an era of minority governments. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The 1989 General Election ushered in an era of coalition governments. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
xs: The **1989 General Election** ended the "Congress System" — option **(2)**.
It ushered in an era of **minority** and **coalition** governments.
xa: Congress lost but remained the **single largest party** (**197** seats).
**1967** = Congress lost power in several States; **1977** = first non-Congress government at the Centre.
**APPSC 2007 key:** **1971** (fifth election) as end of Congress dominance.

66.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: V.P. Singh led the National Front after the 1989 General Election.
Statement B: The National Front received outside support from the BJP and the Left.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
66.x: Both are true: after 1989, V.P. Singh led the National Front government, supported from outside by the BJP and the Left.
66.tq: Recall the National Front's outside support.
n: V.P. Singh led the National Front after the 1989 General Election. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The National Front received outside support from the Bharatiya Janata Party. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The National Front received outside support from the Left. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)** is correct.
After **1989**, **V.P. Singh** led the **National Front**, with **outside support** from the **BJP** and the **Left**.
xa: **National Front** formed in **August 1988**; **Janata Dal** on **11 October 1988**.
Next: **Chandra Shekhar** (**1990-91**) with Congress outside support.
**P.V. Narasimha Rao** (**1991-96**) led a minority government that completed a full term.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the rise of regional parties in India:
1. Linguistic and cultural identity and regional economic neglect are among its causes.
2. After 1989, coalition arithmetic increased the weight of regional parties.
3. Uniform economic development across all regions is among its causes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: identity, regional neglect and the failure of national parties to accommodate State leaders, plus post-1989 coalition arithmetic, explain their rise. Statement 3 is wrong: regional economic neglect, not uniform development, fuels regional parties. So '1 and 2 only'.
67.tq: Regional parties grow from grievance and identity; 'uniform development' is the opposite.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: causes include **linguistic and cultural identity** and **regional economic neglect**.
Statement 2 is correct: after **1989**, **coalition arithmetic** raised regional parties' weight.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is **regional economic neglect**, not uniform development, that fuels them.
xa: Another cause: **national parties' failure** to accommodate State leaders.
Roots of regionalism: **historical, geographical, linguistic** (**22** scheduled languages), **religious, ethnic**.
Impact: regional parties became **kingmakers** in coalitions.

67.s: The politically awakened non-Brahmin agrarian castes in Andhra during the Justice Party era included
67.x: The Andhra non-Brahmin agrarian castes identified as becoming politically awakened during the Justice Party era were Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas.
67.tq: Recall the complete caste grouping rather than selecting a partly familiar list.
xs: The Andhra non-Brahmin agrarian castes were **Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They **awakened politically** in the **Justice Party** era.
xa: This caste base later supported regional parties such as the **TDP** (**NTR, 1982**).
Roots of regionalism: **historical, geographical, linguistic, religious, ethnic**.
The TDP's plank was **Telugu atma gauravam** (Telugu self-respect).

67.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: DMK — Tamil Nadu — C. N. Annadurai — 1949
Shiv Sena — Maharashtra — M. G. Ramachandran — 1966
Biju Janata Dal — Bihar — Naveen Patnaik — 1997
67.x: The DMK was founded in Tamil Nadu by C. N. Annadurai in 1949. The other options interchange founders or States.
67.tq: Start with the complete party-State-founder-year combination and reject swapped pairs.
xs: **DMK — Tamil Nadu — C.N. Annadurai — 1949** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **AIADMK** was founded by **M.G. Ramachandran**, and the **Shiv Sena** by **Bal Thackeray** — options (2) and (3) swap them.
The **BJD** belongs to **Odisha**, not Bihar.
xa: AIADMK: **1972**; Shiv Sena: **1966** (Maharashtra).
**RJD** (Bihar) — **Lalu Prasad Yadav**, **1997**.
DMK origin: **anti-Brahmin, anti-North, anti-Hindi**; demanded **Dravidanadu**.

67.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rashtriya Janata Dal — Bihar — Lalu Prasad Yadav — 1997
Biju Janata Dal — Odisha — Naveen Patnaik — 1997
67.x: The Shiromani Akali Dal was founded in Punjab in 1920, not 1985. Asom Gana Parishad was founded in Assam in 1985.
67.tq: Spot the altered year while retaining the correct party and State.
xs: **Shiromani Akali Dal — Punjab — 1985** is wrong: it dates to **1920** — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**1985** is the founding year of the **Asom Gana Parishad** (Assam).
**RJD** (Bihar, **Lalu Prasad Yadav**) and **BJD** (Odisha, **Naveen Patnaik**) both date to **1997**.
xa: **JJP** (Haryana) — **Dushyant Chautala**, **2018**.
The BJP defeated the **BJD** in **Odisha** in **2024**.

67.s: The DMK originally demanded which of the following and later formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under C. N. Annadurai?
67.x: The DMK began with anti-Brahmin, anti-North and anti-Hindi positions and demanded Dravidanadu; it later scaled back these demands and formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under Annadurai.
67.tq: Connect the original demand with the party’s later electoral transition.
xs: The DMK originally demanded **Dravidanadu** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its origin was **anti-Brahmin, anti-North, anti-Hindi**; it scaled back and formed the Tamil Nadu government in **1967** under **Annadurai**.
"**Bombay for Maharashtrians**" was the **Shiv Sena**'s slogan, not the DMK's.
xa: The DMK was founded by **C.N. Annadurai** in **1949**.
The **AIADMK** (**M.G. Ramachandran**, **1972**) is the other Tamil Nadu regional party.
APPSC-G2 **2025** keyed order: **DMK, TDP, BSP, SP**.

67.s: The slogan associated with Shiv Sena’s regional mobilisation was
o: Autonomy for West Bengal through Centre-State memoranda
Bombay for Maharashtrians, along with jobs for sons of the soil
Telugu atma gauravam and welfare populism
67.x: Shiv Sena mobilised around the idea of “Bombay for Maharashtrians” and the demand for jobs for the sons of the soil.
67.tq: Discriminate between the distinctive regional slogans of different parties.
xs: **Shiv Sena** mobilised on "**Bombay for Maharashtrians**" + **jobs for sons of the soil** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dravidanadu** and anti-Hindi = **DMK**; **Telugu atma gauravam** = **TDP**.
xa: Shiv Sena was founded by **Bal Thackeray** in **1966** (Maharashtra).
It comes between the **DMK (1949)** and the **TDP (1982)** in founding order.
TDP had **no specific ideology** beyond Telugu pride + **welfare populism**.

67.s:
Arrange the following political parties in chronological order of their founding:
A. Bahujan Samaj Party
B. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
C. Telugu Desam Party
D. Shiv Sena
67.x: The correct order is DMK (1949), Shiv Sena (1966), TDP (1982) and BSP (1984).
67.tq: Fix the earliest and latest parties first, then place the middle entries by year.
xs: The order is **B, D, C, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025** keyed order: **DMK, TDP, BSP, SP**.
The TDP won power **within nine months** (Jan **1983**).

67.s: Which of the following is the correct list of the six National Parties referred to in the current classification?
o: BJP, INC, CPI, NCP, AITC and AAP
BJP, INC, CPI(M), NCP, AITC and NPP
BJP, INC, DMK, BSP, NPP and AAP
BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP and AAP
67.x: The six listed National Parties are the BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP and AAP.
67.tq: Direct list recall with nearby recognised and derecognised parties as distractors.
xs: The six national parties are **BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP and AAP** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**CPI, NCP, AITC** and **DMK** are not in the list; **DMK** and **AITC** are State parties in the IYB list.
xa: All others in the IYB **2026** list — **TDP, YSRCP, JSP, DMK, AITC, BJD, SP, SS, BRS** — are State or unrecognised parties.
The **BSP** was founded in **1984**.
The BJP defeated **AAP** in **Delhi** in **2025**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telugu Desam Party:
1. N.T. Rama Rao founded it in 1982 on the plank of Telugu atma gauravam (Telugu self-respect).
2. It won power in the January 1983 Assembly election, about nine months after its founding.
3. It was built on a clearly defined Marxist ideology.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NTR founded the TDP in 1982 on Telugu self-respect and it won power within nine months (January 1983). Statement 3 is wrong: the TDP had no specific ideology beyond Telugu pride and welfare populism. So '1 and 2 only'.
67.tq: TDP = identity + welfare populism, not a defined ideology.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **NTR** founded the TDP in **1982** on **Telugu atma gauravam**.
Statement 2 is correct: it won power **within nine months** (Jan **1983**) — one of the fastest ascents by any party.
Statement 3 is wrong: the TDP had **no specific ideology** beyond Telugu pride + **welfare populism**.
xa: The **1983** win ended Congress's unbroken rule in AP since the State's formation (**1956**).
In **1984**, the TDP (**30** seats) became the **main opposition party** in the **8th Lok Sabha**.

67.s: Which regional party became the main opposition party in the Eighth Lok Sabha in 1984?
67.x: With 30 seats in 1984, the TDP became the main opposition party in the Eighth Lok Sabha and was the first regional party to attain that position.
67.tq: Link the party, election year, seat figure and parliamentary status.
xs: The **Telugu Desam Party**, with **30** seats, was the **main opposition party in the 8th Lok Sabha** (**1984**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was the **first regional party** to do so.
xa: The TDP was founded by **NTR** in **1982**.
NTR chaired the **National Front** (**1988**).
The TDP left the **NDA** in **2018** over **special category status**.

67.s: Who was the chairman of the National Front in 1988, which formed the V. P. Singh government in 1989?
67.x: N. T. Rama Rao was chairman of the National Front in 1988; the National Front formed the V. P. Singh government in 1989.
67.tq: Distinguish the coalition’s chairman from the Prime Minister it subsequently supported.
xs: **N.T. Rama Rao** was **chairman of the National Front** (**1988**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**V.P. Singh** headed the government the Front formed in **1989**; he was not its chairman.
xa: NTR's TDP was the **main opposition** in the **8th Lok Sabha** (**1984**).
Federalism became **more genuinely bargained** after **1989**.

67.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Praja Rajyam Party — K. Chandrashekar Rao — 2008
Telangana Rashtra Samithi — Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy — 2001
67.x: The Lok Satta Party was founded by Jayaprakash Narayan in 2006. Praja Rajyam was founded by Chiranjeevi, Jana Sena by Pawan Kalyan, and TRS by K. Chandrashekar Rao.
67.tq: Start from the sure founder-year pair and eliminate swapped identities.
xs: **Lok Satta Party — Jayaprakash Narayan — 2006** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jana Sena** was founded by **Pawan Kalyan** (**2014**), not Chiranjeevi.
**TRS** was founded by **K. Chandrashekar Rao** (**2001**), not Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
xa: **YSRCP**: **Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy**, **March 2011** (split from Congress).
**Mahajana Socialist Party**: **Manda Krishna Madiga** (**MRPS** leader).
**Praja Shanti Party**: **K.A. Paul**.

67.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Praja Shanti Party — Y. S. Sharmila
YSR Congress Party — Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy
Praja Shanti Party — K. A. Paul
Mahajana Socialist Party — Manda Krishna Madiga
67.x: Praja Shanti Party was founded by K. A. Paul. Y. S. Sharmila founded the YSR Telangana Party, not the Praja Shanti Party.
67.tq: Find the swapped founder in a closely related party pair.
xs: **Praja Shanti Party — Y.S. Sharmila** is wrong — so option **(1)** is the answer.
The Praja Shanti Party was founded by **K.A. Paul**; **Sharmila** founded the **YSR Telangana Party**.
⚠ This was the **incorrect** pair in **APPSC 2021**.
xa: **YSRCP** — **Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy**; **Mahajana Socialist Party** — **Manda Krishna Madiga**.
YSRCP Rajya Sabha strength: **9** as of July **2023** (**APPSC 2023**).
YSRCP full name: **Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party**.

67.s: Which of the following is a consequence of the rise of regional parties in coalition politics?
o: They transferred all legislative powers to local bodies.
They prevented all coalition governments after 1989.
They have sometimes acted as kingmakers and supplied Speakers, Union Ministers and survival votes.
They eliminated the need for bargaining between the Centre and the States.
67.x: Regional parties have acted as coalition kingmakers, supplied Speakers and Union Ministers, and provided votes necessary for government survival.
67.tq: Identify the practical parliamentary consequences of coalition dependence.
xs: Regional parties have acted as **kingmakers**, supplying **Speakers**, **Union Ministers** and **survival votes** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They did not end coalitions or bargaining; federalism became **more genuinely bargained** after **1989**.
xa: Positive: **backward-region representation**, **balanced development**.
Negative: **parochialism**, **instability**.
The TDP left the **NDA** in **2018** over **special category status**.

67.s: Which of the following correctly states both a positive and a negative impact of regional parties?
o: End of coalition politics; strengthening of one-party rule
Reduced representation and slower development; political permanence
Centralisation and uniformity; elimination of regional demands
Backward-region representation and balanced development; parochialism and instability
67.x: Regional parties can improve representation of backward regions and promote balanced development, but may also encourage parochialism and instability.
67.tq: Match the positive and negative columns without reversing their direction.
xs: Positive: **backward-region representation** and **balanced development**; negative: **parochialism** and **instability** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The other options invert the effects — regional parties did not end coalitions or centralise power.
xa: Coalition role: **kingmakers**.
Federalism: **more genuinely bargained** after **1989**.
"**One Nation, One Election**" is feared to **weaken regional parties**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Special Category Status was demanded for the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after 2014.
2. The TDP left the NDA over this demand in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statement 1 is correct: the demand concerned the residuary Andhra Pradesh after 2014. Statement 2 is wrong: the TDP left the NDA over it in 2018, not 2014. So '1 only'.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **special category status** was demanded for **residuary AP** after **2014**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **TDP left the NDA** over it in **2018**, not 2014.
xa: Today the **TDP** leads AP's ruling coalition with **BJP** support.
Regional parties have acted as **kingmakers** at the Centre.
YSRCP Rajya Sabha strength: **9** (July **2023**).

67.s: In assessing the strength of a regional party, analysts caution that which of the following is a more meaningful indicator than seats alone?
o: The number of defections from other parties
Number of Rajya Sabha Members only
Whether the party supports the Union Government
67.x: Vote share is considered an important indicator of the extent of regional support, whereas seats alone may not fully reflect that support.
67.tq: Distinguish the substantive electoral indicator from related but incomplete political measures.
xs: Analysts say **vote share**, not seats, shows regional support — so option **(1)** is correct.
The remark followed **Trinamool's 2026 West Bengal defeat** and defections (**AITC**, **AAP** Rajya Sabha MPs, **NCP-SP**).
xa: A BJD MP: the **BJD** won **182 Lok Sabha seats between 1999 and 2024**.
The BJP defeated the **BJD** (**Odisha, 2024**), **AAP** (**Delhi, 2025**) and **Trinamool** (**West Bengal, 2026**).
⚠ Seats can mislead; **vote share** measures support.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political position of the Telugu Desam Party in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It is outside the ruling coalition and is supported by the BJD.
It leads the ruling coalition with support from the Trinamool Congress.
It leads the ruling coalition with support from the Bharatiya Janata Party.
It leads the ruling coalition without support from any other party.
67.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the Telugu Desam Party leads the ruling coalition with support from the Bharatiya Janata Party.
67.tq: Test the party–coalition relationship by identifying both the leading party and its supporting ally.
xs: The **TDP** leads AP's ruling coalition with support from the **Bharatiya Janata Party** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is neither outside the coalition nor backed by the **BJD** or **Trinamool**.
xa: The TDP left the **NDA** in **2018** over **special category status**.
The TDP was founded by **NTR** in **1982** on **Telugu atma gauravam**.
A regional party can hold power alone or **dominate a coalition**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about 'One Nation, One Election':
1. It is feared that it would weaken regional parties.
2. India's first general elections were held simultaneously for the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies.
3. It is expected to automatically increase the number of regional parties.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statement 1 is correct: critics fear it would weaken regional parties. Statement 2 is correct: the early general elections were simultaneous. Statement 3 is wrong: nothing suggests it would increase regional parties; the fear is the opposite. So '1 and 2 only'.
67.tq: Statement 3 contradicts statement 1 - both cannot be the criticism.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: "**One Nation, One Election**" is feared to **weaken regional parties**.
Statement 2 is correct: the first four general elections (**1951-52, 1957, 1962, 1967**) were **simultaneous**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the fear is the opposite — weakening, not multiplying, regional parties.
xa: After **1989**, coalition arithmetic raised regional parties' weight.
The **DMK** formed the Tamil Nadu government in **1967**, one of those simultaneous elections.
Regional parties' negatives: **parochialism**, **instability**.

68.s: Which authority is responsible for registration of a political party under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and for recognition under the Symbols Order, respectively?
o: Election Commission of India and Parliament
Election Commission of India and Election Commission of India
President of India and Governor of the concerned State
Ministry of Law and Justice and Election Commission of India
68.x: The Election Commission handles both processes: registration under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951, and recognition under the Election Symbols Order, 1968.
68.tq: Compare the two legal steps while keeping the authority constant.
xs: The **Election Commission of India** does both: it registers and it recognises — so option **(2)** is correct.

**Registration** is under **Section 29A, RPA 1951**; **recognition** (National/State) is under the **Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968** — the authority for both is the **ECI**.
**Parliament**, the **President**, the **Governor** and the **Ministry of Law** play no part in either step.
xa: The **1968 Order** is a **statutory order of the ECI** under **RPA 1951** and **Article 324**.
In recognition and symbol disputes the ECI acts as a **court**.
Three states of a party: **Unregistered** → **registered but unrecognised (RUPP)** → **recognised**.

68.s: The Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 is best described as:
o: An Act of Parliament dealing exclusively with National Parties
An executive notification issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs
A constitutional provision contained in the Election Commission chapter
A statutory order of the Election Commission issued under the RPA, 1951 and Article 324
68.x: The 1968 Order is a statutory order of the Election Commission under the RPA, 1951 and Article 324. It is neither an Act of Parliament nor a constitutional provision.
68.tq: Use the legal-status distinction to reject the familiar but incorrect labels.
xs: The 1968 Order is a **statutory order of the Election Commission** issued under the **RPA, 1951** and **Article 324** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **not an Act of Parliament** and **not a constitutional provision**.
It is the ECI's own order, not a notification of the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, and it covers both National and State parties.
xa: **Para 15** of the Order: the ECI decides split disputes using the **Sadiq Ali (1971)** majority test.
**Para 16A**: the ECI may **suspend or withdraw recognition** for defying the **Model Code of Conduct**.
**Para 6B** lays down the **National party** criteria.

68.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three statuses through which a political party may be classified?
68.x: The three relevant states are unregistered, registered but unrecognised—commonly referred to as an RUPP—and recognised.
68.tq: Direct classification recall using the legally distinct middle category.
xs: A party is **unregistered**, **registered but unrecognised (RUPP)**, or **recognised** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Registration** comes under **Section 29A, RPA 1951**; **recognition** under the **Symbols Order, 1968**.
**Reserved** and **free** are kinds of **symbols**, not statuses of a party.
xa: Registration: apply within **30 days** of formation.
The party constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to **socialism, secularism, democracy** and national integrity.
Only about **750 of 2,800+ RUPPs** contested **2024**.

68.s:
Consider the following statements regarding deregistration of political parties:
1. The Election Commission's power to deregister a party is limited.
2. Fraud may form a basis for deregistration.
3. Ceasing to uphold the required allegiance may form a basis for deregistration.
4. The Law Commission's 255th Report recommended a limited power of deregistration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: The ECI's deregistration power is limited and may arise in cases such as fraud, ceasing allegiance or an unlawful declaration. The Law Commission's 255th Report favoured a limited deregistration power.
68.tq: Check whether the apparently broad deregistration power is carefully qualified.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Statement 1** correct: **INC v Institute of Social Welfare (2002)** held the ECI's power to **deregister** is **limited**.
**Statements 2 and 3** correct: grounds are **fraud**, **ceasing allegiance** and an **unlawful declaration**.
**Statement 4** correct: the **Law Commission's 255th report** wants a **limited deregistration power**.
xa: Registration is under **Section 29A, RPA 1951**, by the **ECI**.
RUPPs must contest at least once in **six years** or face **delisting**.
⚠ **Para 16A** (suspend/withdraw **recognition** for defying the MCC) is different from **deregistration**.

68.s:
With reference to registration of a political party under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951, consider the following statements:
1. The application must be made within 30 days of the party's formation.
2. The party's constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to socialism, secularism and democracy.
3. Registration automatically entitles the party to a reserved symbol.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: Statement 1 is correct: the application is made within 30 days of formation. Statement 2 is correct: the party constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to socialism, secularism, democracy and national integrity. Statement 3 is wrong: a reserved symbol comes only with recognition under the 1968 Order; a registered unrecognised party gets free or common symbols. So '1 and 2 only'.
68.tq: Registration = 29A RPA (30 days, socialism-secularism-democracy pledge); reserved symbol needs recognition.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** **1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: apply within **30 days** of formation.
**Statement 2** correct: the constitution must pledge allegiance to the **Constitution** and to **socialism, secularism, democracy**, national integrity.
**Statement 3** wrong: **reserved symbols** go only to **recognised** parties; an RUPP gets **free symbols** or a **common symbol** on conditions.
xa: Common symbol for RUPPs: if they contest **2 Lok Sabha seats** or **5% of Assembly seats**.
Latest free symbols list: **May 2025 - 184 symbols**.
Recognition is a separate step under the **Election Symbols Order, 1968**.

68.s: Which one of the following is NOT a valid criterion for recognition as a National Party under paragraph 6B of the Symbols Order?
o: Recognition as a State party in four or more States
At least 2% of Lok Sabha seats, won from not fewer than three States
At least 6% of valid votes in four or more States and four Lok Sabha seats
At least 15% of valid votes in two States, without any Lok Sabha seat
68.x: The 15%-in-two-States route is not a National Party criterion. The valid alternatives are the four-State recognition route, the 6% plus four-seat route, and the 2% Lok Sabha-seat route.
68.tq: Find the one percentage-and-seat combination absent from the recognised alternatives.
xs: **15% of valid votes in two States without any seat** is not a criterion — so option **(4)** is correct.
The three valid routes: **State party in four or more States**; **6% votes in four States + 4 Lok Sabha seats**; **2% of Lok Sabha seats** from **three States**.
The notes flag "**2 or more States**" and "**4% / 10% / 15%** of votes" as standard wrong distractors.
xa: **2%** of Lok Sabha seats = **11 of 543**.
⚠ The vote-only (no seat) route — **8%** of valid votes — exists only for a **State party**, not a National party.
**APPSC-G2 2025**: all listed conditions were valid, so the key was "**None of the above**".

68.s: Which one of the following changes was associated with the Election Commission's April 2023 review of National Party status?
o: DMK, RSP and AIFB were recognised as National Parties
CPI, NCP and AITC were derecognised and AAP was recognised
BSP, NPP and AAP were derecognised and CPI was recognised
INC and BJP were derecognised and AAP was recognised
68.x: The April 2023 review derecognised CPI, NCP and AITC and recognised AAP as a National Party.
68.tq: Use the date and separate recognition from derecognition.
xs: The **April 2023** review **derecognised CPI, NCP and AITC** and **recognised AAP** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**DMK, RSP and AIFB** are not National parties; **INC** and **BJP** were not derecognised.
xa: AAP got national status in **2023**.
In **May 2020** there were **eight** national parties.
**NPP (Meghalaya)** was the **first North-East party** with national status.
⚠ The ECI reviews status after each general election — always quote the list with a date.

68.s: Which party was the first party from the North-Eastern region to obtain National Party status?
68.x: The National People's Party (NPP), based in Meghalaya, was the first North-Eastern party to obtain National Party status.
68.tq: Direct identity recall based on region and status.
xs: The **NPP (Meghalaya)** was the **first North-East party** with national status — so option **(4)** is correct.
**AAP** won national status in **2023**; **AITC** lost it in the **April 2023** review.
xa: April 2023: **CPI, NCP and AITC** derecognised; **AAP** recognised.
**Eight** national parties as of **May 2020** (APPSC 2019 key).
National status needs any one of: **State party in 4 States**, **6% in 4 States + 4 LS seats**, or **2% LS seats from 3 States**.

68.s: Which of the following combinations consists entirely of parties that are not National Parties?
o: DMK, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Bloc and Peasants and Workers Party
68.x: DMK, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Bloc and Peasants and Workers Party are not National Parties in the classification referred to here.
68.tq: Separate the complete non-National group from the recognised list.
xs: **DMK, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Bloc and Peasants and Workers Party** are not National parties — so option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC 2018**).
**NPP** and **AAP** hold national status; **BJP** and **INC** are national parties.
xa: **AAP** was recognised in **April 2023**; **CPI, NCP, AITC** were derecognised then.
**NPP** = first **North-East** national party.
AP angle: **TDP** and **YSRCP** are recognised **State parties**; neither is National.

68.s:
Which of the following are routes to recognition as a State party?
1. At least 6% of valid votes in the Assembly election and 2 Assembly seats
2. At least 6% of valid votes in the Lok Sabha election in the State and 1 Lok Sabha seat from the State
3. At least 6% of valid votes in the Assembly election and 4 Lok Sabha seats
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: Routes 1 (6% + 2 Assembly seats) and 2 (6% in the Lok Sabha poll + 1 Lok Sabha seat) are valid. Route 3 is wrong: '6% + 4 Lok Sabha seats' mixes in the National-party criterion (6% in four States + 4 Lok Sabha seats). So '1 and 2 only'.
68.tq: 4 Lok Sabha seats belongs to the National-party test, not the State-party test.
xs: Routes 1 and 2 are valid — option **(1)** **1 and 2 only**.
**Route 1** valid: **6%** valid votes in the Assembly election **+ 2 Assembly seats**.
**Route 2** valid: **6%** valid votes in the Lok Sabha election **+ 1 Lok Sabha seat** from the State.
**Route 3** wrong: "6% + 4 Lok Sabha seats" borrows from the **National party** route (6% in **four States** + **4** LS seats).
xa: Other State routes: **3% of Assembly seats or 3 seats**, whichever is more; **1 Lok Sabha seat for every 25** allotted.
