75.x: Sweden’s first ombudsman dates to 1809, the first Lokpal Bill to 1968, Maharashtra’s first Lokayukta to 1971, and India’s first Lokpal appointment to 2019.
75.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two middle events by year.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
B: Sweden's first ombudsman, **1809**; A: first Lokpal Bill, **1968**.
C: Maharashtra's first Lokayukta, **1971**; D: first Lokpal appointed, **2019**.
xa: The term Lokpal was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** in **1963**.
Odisha passed the first Lokayukta law in **1970**.
Present Lokpal chair: **A.M. Khanwilkar** (**2024**).

75.s: Which of the following correctly states the distinction between the Central Vigilance Commission and the Lokpal in relation to the Central Bureau of Investigation?
o: The CVC has superintendence over the CBI generally in Prevention of Corruption Act cases, whereas the Lokpal has it only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has general superintendence, while the CVC acts only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has superintendence over the CBI in every Prevention of Corruption Act case.
Neither the CVC nor the Lokpal has any relationship with the CBI.
75.x: The CVC Act, 2003 gives the CVC superintendence over the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases generally. The Lokpal exercises such a role only in cases referred by it.
75.tq: Compare the scope words ‘generally’ and ‘only in cases it refers’.
xs: The **CVC** has superintendence over the **CBI** in **PCA cases generally**; the **Lokpal** only in **cases it refers** — option **(1)**.
The CVC's power comes from the **CVC Act 2003**.
So options 2-4 misstate the split.
xa: The **Santhanam Committee (1962-64)** recommended the **CVC** and **CBI**.
**Group C and D** complaints go from the Lokpal to the **CVC**, which reports back.
The 2013 Act amended the **DSPE Act** (CBI Director's committee; Directorate of Prosecution).

75.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: State Vigilance Commission — Set up from 1964 on the CVC pattern
75.x: Section 17A belongs to the Prevention of Corruption Act and concerns prior approval before investigation. The Lokpal Inquiry Wing is associated with Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act.
75.tq: Check the statute before accepting a section-number match.
xs: **Section 17A — Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
**Section 17A** belongs to the **Prevention of Corruption Act** (prior approval before investigation).
The others are right: Inquiry Wing — **Section 11**; **CVC Act 2003**; State Vigilance Commission — from **1964** on the CVC pattern.
xa: SC **split verdict** on Section 17A on **22 Jan 2026**.
**Section 63** of the 2013 Act mandates State Lokayuktas.
The AP Lokayukta appointment was under **Section 3(1)**, term under **Section 5**.

75.s: Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act is associated with the issue of:
o: Publication of the Corruption Perceptions Index
Appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner
General consent of States for all CBI investigations
Prior approval before investigating certain decisions or recommendations by public servants
75.x: Section 17A concerns prior approval for investigation in specified circumstances involving decisions or recommendations of public servants. Its interpretation has been the subject of a Supreme Court split verdict and debate over 'sanction paralysis'.
75.tq: Distinguish prior approval under the PCA from State general consent under the DSPE Act.
xs: **Section 17A** of the PC Act concerns **prior approval before investigation** of public servants — option **(4)**.
It was the subject of an SC **split verdict** (**22 Jan 2026**).
Justice **K.V. Viswanathan** upheld it only with a **binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta**.
xa: Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** held 17A unconstitutional.
The Lokpal's **Inquiry Wing** handles preliminary inquiries into **PCA** offences.
Criticism: the Lokpal has **no power of prior sanction**.

75.s: In the January 2026 split verdict of the Supreme Court on Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which judge held Section 17A unconstitutional?
75.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna held Section 17A unconstitutional. Justice K.V. Viswanathan upheld prior approval only if based on a binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta. Khanwilkar is the Lokpal Chairperson and Surya Kant the CJI; neither was part of the split.
75.tq: 17A split: Nagarathna struck it; Viswanathan read it down via Lokpal opinion.
xs: Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** held **Section 17A** unconstitutional — option **(2)**.
Justice **K.V. Viswanathan** upheld prior approval only on a **binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta**.
**A.M. Khanwilkar** is the Lokpal chair, not on this bench.
xa: The verdict came on **22 Jan 2026**.
Section 17A is in the **Prevention of Corruption Act**.
The **Mahua Moitra** matter also raised the sanction procedure; the SC agreed to clarify it (**14 Mar 2026**).

75.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Lokpal Selection Committee:

List-I
 a. Prime Minister
 b. Speaker of the Lok Sabha
 c. Chief Justice of India
 d. Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

List-II
 i. Member
 ii. Chairperson
 iii. Member who may nominate a Supreme Court judge instead
 iv. Not a member
75.x: The Prime Minister chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee; the Lok Sabha Speaker is a member; the CJI is a member who may nominate a Supreme Court judge in his place; the Rajya Sabha Chairman is not a member — the usual trap.
75.tq: Recall the committee's five seats and note who is left out.
n: The Prime Minister is the Chair of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court nominee is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Rajya Sabha Chairman is not a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xs: Correct match: **a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
The **Prime Minister** is the **Chairperson** of the Lokpal **Selection Committee**; the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** is a **Member**.
The **Chief Justice of India** is a member who may nominate a **Supreme Court judge** instead.
⚠ The **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** is **NOT a member** (UKPSC 2025 key).
xa: The other members: the **Leader of the Opposition** in the Lok Sabha and **one eminent jurist**.
The **President** appoints the Lokpal on the **Selection Committee**'s recommendation.
The Selection Committee sets up a **Search Committee** of at least **seven** persons, at least **half** from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women.

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act:

I. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee.
II. An eminent jurist is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee.
III. The minimum age under the Act is 45 years.
IV. The Act covers public servants outside India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
75.x: All four are correct: the Leader of the Opposition (or leader of the largest opposition party) and an eminent jurist sit on the Selection Committee, the minimum age is 45 years, and the Act covers public servants outside India too.
75.tq: Check each Lokpal provision separately.
n: The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
An eminent jurist is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The minimum age for the Lokpal is 45 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Lokpal Act covers public servants outside India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(1)**, **I, II, III and IV**.
I and II: the **Leader of the Opposition** in the Lok Sabha and an **eminent jurist** are both members of the **Selection Committee**.
III: the **minimum age** of the Lokpal is **45** years.
IV: the Act covers public servants **inside and outside India** (UKPSC 2025 key).
xa: Selection Committee chair: the **Prime Minister**; the **Rajya Sabha Chairman** is **not** a member.
Lokpal strength: **Chairperson + not more than 8 members**; **50%** judicial and at least **50%** from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women.
Term: **5 years or age 70**, whichever earlier; no reappointment.
A Chairperson or Member cannot be an **MP or MLA**.

75.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The institution of Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809.
II. The First Administrative Reforms Commission was established in 1966.
III. The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas.
IV. Morarji Desai submitted the interim report of the First Administrative Reforms Commission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
75.x: All four are correct: the Ombudsman began in Sweden (1809); the First ARC (1966) recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas, and Morarji Desai submitted its interim report on them.
75.tq: Verify the origin year and the ARC's recommendation and author.
n: The institution of Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The First Administrative Reforms Commission was established in 1966. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended the establishment of Lokpal and Lokayuktas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Morarji Desai submitted the interim report of the First Administrative Reforms Commission on Lokpal and Lokayuktas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(2)**, **I, II, III and IV**.
I: the **Ombudsman** was first created in **Sweden**, **1809**.
II and III: the **First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966)** recommended **Lokpal and Lokayuktas**.
IV: its interim report "**Problems of Redressal of Citizens' Grievances**" (**1966**) was submitted by **Morarji Desai**.
xa: The First ARC proposed **two tiers**: **Lokpal** for the Union and a **Lokayukta in every State**.
Desai was later replaced by **K. Hanumanthaiya** after he joined the Cabinet.
⚠ **Santhanam Committee (1962-64)** → **CVC** and **CBI**; **First ARC** → Lokpal + Lokayukta.
The **Second ARC (2007)** strongly reiterated the recommendation.
⚠ **1809** Sweden ombudsman ≠ **1766** Sweden RTI law.

75.s:
Assertion (A): The first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968.
Reason (R): Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was the first Lokpal of India.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
75.x: Both are true but unrelated: the first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968, while Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became the first Lokpal only in 2019 under the 2013 Act.
75.tq: A later appointment cannot explain an earlier Bill.
n: The first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was the first Lokpal of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xs: Both statements are true but unrelated — option **(2)**: R is **not** the correct explanation of A.
A: the **first Lokpal Bill** was introduced in **1968**, in the **Lok Sabha** (4th Lok Sabha).
R: **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose** became the **first Lokpal** only in **2019**, under the **2013** Act.
xa: The 1968 Bill was **passed by the Lok Sabha** in **1969** but **lapsed** when that House was dissolved.
⚠ Read the verb: **1968** = first introduced; **1969** = first passed by the Lok Sabha.
The term **Lokpal** was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** in **1963**.
Present Lokpal: **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar**, since **10 March 2024**.

75.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Maharashtra
(b) Year Maharashtra enacted its Lokayukta law
(c) Odisha

List-II
(i) 1971
(ii) First state to pass a Lokayukta Act
(iii) First state to set up a working Lokayukta
(iv) 1968
75.x: Odisha passed the first Lokayukta Act (1970), but Maharashtra, with its 1971 Act, was the first State to set up a working Lokayukta (1972). 1968 is the year of the first Lokpal Bill, the distractor.
75.tq: Separate passing an Act (Odisha) from setting up the institution (Maharashtra).
n: Maharashtra was the first state to introduce a Lokayukta in 1971 or 1972. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Odisha was the first state to pass a Lokayukta Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xs: Correct match: **a-iii, b-i, c-ii** — option **(4)**.
**Maharashtra** was the **first state to set up a working Lokayukta** (**1971**, BPSC 2021 key); its Lokayukta law is dated **1971**.
**Odisha** was the **first state to pass a Lokayukta Act** (**1970**), though the institution came only in **1983**.
**1968** is the year of the **first Lokpal Bill** — the distractor.
xa: ⚠ **1970** Odisha law ≠ **1971** Maharashtra institution.
Other Lokayukta Acts: Rajasthan **1973**, Bihar **1974**, UP **1975**, **Andhra Pradesh 1983**, Karnataka **1984**.
By **2013**, **21 States and 1 UT (Delhi)** had Lokayuktas.
The **2013 Act** (**Section 63**) asks every State to set up a Lokayukta within **one year** by its own law.

76.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Central Information Commission:
1. It consists of the Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.
2. It is a statutory body.
3. It possesses powers of a civil court.
4. It is the only body that can declare an organisation to be a public authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: All four statements are correct as stated: the CIC has the specified composition, is statutory, has civil-court powers and alone can declare an organisation a public authority.
76.tq: Test a cluster of institutional characteristics and use the all-inclusive option only when every statement fits.
xs: All four statements **1, 2, 3 and 4** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: Chief IC + **up to 10 ICs**; statement 2: a **statutory body**.
Statement 3: **civil-court powers**; statement 4: the only body that can declare an organisation a **"public authority"**.
xa: Constituted **2005** (**12 Oct 2005**) under **Section 12**.
The **RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019** lets the **Centre fix tenure and salaries** of CIC/SIC members.
Under the **2019** Rules the term is **3 years**.

76.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Information framework:
1. The RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 empowered the Centre to fix the tenure and salaries of the CIC and SIC members.
2. Under the Rules of 2019, the term of an Information Commissioner is five years.
3. Earlier, the pay of the Chief Information Commissioner was equal to that of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2019 Amendment lets the Centre fix tenure and salaries. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2019 Rules fixed the term at three years, not five. Statement 3 is correct: the CIC's pay earlier equalled the CEC's (and a State Chief IC's equalled an Election Commissioner's). So '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 are wrong.
76.tq: 2019 = Centre fixes tenure and pay; Rules term = 3 years; old pay link = CEC/EC.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the **RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019** lets the **Centre fix tenure and salaries** of CIC/SIC members.
Statement 2 wrong: the **2019** Rules fixed the term at **3 years**, not five.
Statement 3: earlier the CIC's pay equalled the **CEC**'s.
xa: Earlier, a State Chief IC's pay equalled an **Election Commissioner**'s.
The CIC has Chief IC + **up to 10 ICs**.
State ICs are appointed by the **Governor** on the recommendation of the **CM**, **LoP in the Assembly** and a CM-nominated minister.

76.s: An RTI application concerns a person’s life or liberty. The information should ordinarily be provided within
76.x: When the application concerns life or liberty, information must be provided within 48 hours. The ordinary time limit is 30 days.
76.tq: Apply the special exception to the ordinary statutory time limit.
xs: Information concerning **life or liberty** must be given within **48 hours** — option **(2)**.
This is **Section 7** of the RTI Act.
The normal reply period is **30 days**.
xa: **BPL applicants** get information free.
**Public Information Officers** are designated by each public authority (**Section 5**).
The CIC was constituted under **Section 12**.

76.s: Which of the following best describes the amendment made to Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information Act by the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023?
o: It transferred RTI appeals involving personal data to the CVC
It restricted exemption only to information held by private companies
It made all personal information mandatorily disclosable
It exempted personal information outright and removed the public-interest override
76.x: The DPDP Act, 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act to exempt personal information outright, thereby removing the earlier public-interest override.
76.tq: Distinguish an outright exemption from the earlier balancing approach involving public interest.
xs: The **DPDP Act 2023** made **Section 8(1)(j)** exempt **personal information outright**, removing the **public-interest override** — option **(4)**.
It did not make personal information disclosable or move appeals to the CVC.
The Congress president said it "**diluted** the RTI Act's public interest clause" (**31 Jan 2026**).
xa: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** called for a **"re-examination"** of the RTI Act.
It floated a possible **"ministerial veto"**.
Criticism of RTI: **backlogs and vacancies**, misuse of **Section 8**, attacks on RTI activists (**100+ killed**).

76.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 is associated with which of the following in relation to the RTI Act?
o: A call for its 're-examination', including a possible 'ministerial veto'
A proposal to extend RTI to all private companies
Restoration of the public-interest override in Section 8(1)(j)
Making the CIC a constitutional body
76.x: The Survey called for a re-examination of the RTI Act, suggesting exemptions for confidential service records and draft policy discussions and floating a possible ministerial veto. It did not propose extension to private companies, restoration of the override (removed by the DPDP Act) or constitutional status.
76.tq: ES 2025-26: re-examine RTI + ministerial veto.
xs: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** called for a **'re-examination'** of the RTI Act, including a possible **'ministerial veto'** — option **(1)**.
It suggested exemptions for **confidential service records** and **draft policy discussions**.
The public-interest override was **removed** by the **DPDP Act 2023**, not restored.
xa: The DPDP change was to **Section 8(1)(j)**.
The CIC is a **statutory**, not constitutional, body.
The **RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019** let the Centre fix tenure and salaries.

76.s:
With reference to the Central Bureau of Investigation, consider the following statements:
1. It is a constitutional body.
2. It is an attached office under the Department of Personnel and Training.
3. It was initially set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
4. It derives its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: The CBI is not a constitutional body. It is an attached office under DoPT, was set up by a Ministry of Home Affairs resolution, and derives its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946.
76.tq: Use the constitutional-versus-executive body distinction and check each institutional description separately.
xs: Statements **2, 3 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 wrong: the CBI is **neither constitutional nor statutory**.
Statement 2: it is an **attached office** under the **Ministry of Personnel** (DoPT).
Statements 3 and 4: set up by a **Ministry of Home Affairs resolution** (**1 April 1963**); powers from the **DSPE Act, 1946**.
xa: Precursor: the **Special Police Establishment (1941)**.
Founder Director: **D.P. Kohli** (APPSC **2018** key).
Critics call it a **"caged parrot"** over executive control.

76.s: The Central Bureau of Investigation was set up in 1963 on the recommendation of the
o: Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption
76.x: The CBI was set up in 1963 following the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption, constituted during 1962–64.
76.tq: Link an executive agency to the committee whose recommendation led to its creation.
xs: The CBI was set up in **1963** on the **Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption** recommendation — option **(3)**.
The committee sat in **1962-64** (APPCA says **1962-63**).
The **Second ARC (2007)** proposed a new law to replace the DSPE Act; the **Vohra Committee (1993)** looked at the criminal-politician nexus.
xa: The **CVC** was also set up on Santhanam's recommendation, in **1964**.
⚠ **CBI = 1963**, executive resolution, still non-statutory; **CVC = 1964**, statutory only in **2003**.
The CBI was set up on **1 April 1963**.

76.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their establishment or enactment:
A. Special Police Establishment
B. Delhi Special Police Establishment Act
C. Central Bureau of Investigation
D. Central Vigilance Commission
76.x: The Special Police Establishment originated in 1941, the DSPE Act was enacted in 1946, the CBI was set up in 1963, and the CVC was set up in 1964.
76.tq: Fix the earliest institutional origin first, then place the legal framework and later bodies.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
A: **Special Police Establishment**, **1941**; B: **DSPE Act**, **1946**.
xa: The CVC became statutory under the **CVC Act, 2003**.
The SPE probed bribery and corruption in **war-time supplies**.
The **Vineet Narain** case (**1997**) led to the **2003** DSPE revision.

76.s: Who was the founder Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation?
76.x: D.P. Kohli was the founder Director of the CBI (APPSC 2018 key); an annual memorial lecture is held in his name. K. Santhanam headed the committee that recommended the CBI; Vineet Narain was the petitioner in the 1997 case; Vohra headed the 1993 committee on the criminal-politician nexus.
76.tq: CBI founder Director = D.P. Kohli.
xs: **D.P. Kohli** was the founder Director of the CBI (APPSC **2018** key) — option **(1)**.
**K. Santhanam** headed the committee that recommended the CBI; **Vineet Narain** was the **1997** petitioner.
**Vohra** headed the **1993** committee on the criminal-politician-bureaucrat nexus.
xa: The **22nd** D.P. Kohli Memorial Lecture was given by CJI **Surya Kant** (**22 Apr 2026**).
The CBI was set up by an **MHA resolution** in **1963**.
It is now an **attached office** under the **Ministry of Personnel**.

76.s: The Director of the CBI is appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a committee comprising the
o: Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Attorney General of India
Union Home Minister, Leader of the largest opposition party and CVC
Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and CVC
Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India or his nominee
76.x: The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha or leader of the largest opposition party, and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by the CJI.
76.tq: Split the options by identifying the required judicial member and the chairperson.
xs: The CBI Director is picked by the **PM**, the **Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha** and the **CJI or his nominee** — option **(4)**.
The appointment is made by the **Central Government**.
⚠ **CVC panel = Home Minister**; **CIC panel = PM-nominated Cabinet Minister**; **CBI panel = CJI or SC judge**.
xa: If there is no LoP, the **leader of the largest opposition party** sits.
Tenure: minimum **2 years**, extendable to **5 years** (**2021**).
In **May 2026** the LoP recorded **dissent** over the new Director's selection.

76.s: The present procedure for selection of the CBI Director through a committee headed by the Prime Minister was introduced through the
76.x: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 amended the DSPE framework and introduced the present three-member selection committee. Until 2014, the process operated under the DSPE Act alone.
76.tq: Use the legal-amendment trap by separating the original statute from the later reforming Act.
xs: The PM-led committee came through the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**, which amended the **DSPE Act** — option **(2)**.
Before **2014**, the Director was chosen on a committee headed by the **CVC**, under the DSPE Act alone.
The **CVC Act, 2003** gave the CVC superintendence, not this committee.
xa: Committee: **PM (chair)**, **LoP in Lok Sabha**, **CJI or an SC judge nominated by the CJI**.
Director's minimum tenure: **2 years**.
The **Vineet Narain** case had fixed a **two-year tenure** for the Director.

76.s: Which of the following statements regarding the tenure of the CBI Director is correct?
o: The minimum tenure is one year and it may be extended up to three years.
The tenure is coterminous with that of the Central Government.
The tenure is fixed at five years with no possibility of extension.
The minimum tenure is two years and it may be extended up to five years.
76.x: The CBI Director has a minimum tenure of two years, which was made extendable up to five years in 2021.
76.tq: Compare the minimum and maximum periods rather than selecting the familiar-looking fixed-term option.
xs: The CBI Director has a minimum tenure of **two years**, extendable up to **five years** — option **(4)**.
The extension came in **2021**: **one year at a time up to five years**.
The same **2021** rule applies to the **ED** Director.
xa: The **Vineet Narain** case (**1997**) first fixed the two-year tenure.
The **Director of Prosecution** also has a **2-year** term.
The Director is appointed by the **Central Government**.

76.s: Which one of the following statements about the Vineet Narain judgment is NOT correct?
o: It transferred the decision to investigate every case from the CBI to the CVC.
It led to revision of the DSPE framework and the statutory CVC.
76.x: The judgment did not transfer every investigation decision to the CVC; the CBI alone decides whether to investigate. The other statements correctly describe the judgment and its reported citation.
76.tq: Reject the option that reverses institutional autonomy between the CBI and CVC.
xs: The claim that it **transferred the decision to investigate every case from the CBI to the CVC** is NOT correct — option **(1)**.
The judgment said the **CBI alone decides** whether to investigate; the CVC got only **superintendence**.
The other statements are true: **1997**, **(1998) 1 SCC 226**, and the **2003** DSPE revision and statutory CVC.
xa: It quashed the **"Single Directive"**.
It fixed a **two-year tenure** for the Director.
The **Second ARC (2007)** later proposed a new law to replace the DSPE Act.

76.s: The decision in Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1997) is associated with which of the following changes concerning the CBI?
o: Transfer of CBI control to the Ministry of Finance and a five-year tenure
Transfer of all CBI investigations to the Enforcement Directorate
Abolition of State consent and appointment of the Director by the Lokpal
Superintendence by the CVC and a fixed two-year tenure for the CBI Director
76.x: The 1997 Vineet Narain judgment gave the CVC superintendence over the CBI and prescribed a fixed two-year tenure for the CBI Director. The DSPE Act was revised accordingly in 2003.
76.tq: Match the landmark case with its specific institutional consequences rather than later reforms.
xs: **Vineet Narain (1997)** gave the **CVC superintendence** over the CBI and a **fixed two-year tenure** for the Director — option **(4)**.
It also quashed the **"Single Directive"**.
The DSPE Act was revised accordingly in **2003**.
xa: The CBI stays under the **Ministry of Personnel**, not Finance.
The CVC became statutory under the **CVC Act, 2003**.
The **2021** amendments let the tenure run up to **five years**.

76.s:
With reference to the institutions connected with CBI supervision, consider the following statements:
1. The Lokpal has superintendence and direction over the CBI in cases referred to it by the Lokpal.
2. The Directorate of Prosecution in the CBI is headed by a person not below the rank of Joint Secretary.
3. The Director of Prosecution is appointed on the recommendation of the CVC for a two-year term.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: All three statements correctly describe the special supervisory and prosecutorial arrangements associated with the CBI. The Director of Prosecution is appointed on the CVC's recommendation for two years and must not be below Joint Secretary rank.
76.tq: Check each institutional relationship separately, especially the authority responsible for appointment.
xs: All three statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the **Lokpal** has **superintendence and direction** over the CBI in cases it refers.
Statement 2: the **Directorate of Prosecution** is headed by a Director not below **Joint Secretary** rank.
Statement 3: he is appointed on **CVC** recommendation for **2 years**.
xa: CBI officers of **SP rank and above** are chosen by a committee led by the **CVC**.
The CVC has superintendence over the CBI for **Prevention of Corruption Act** cases.
Issue: friction and overlap among **Lokpal, CBI and CVC**.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about the BHARATPOL portal:
1. It was developed by the CBI.
2. It was launched in January 2025.
3. It provides a platform for real-time Interpol assistance requests by central and State agencies.
4. It is exclusively a portal for RTI appeals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. BHARATPOL is related to international police cooperation, not RTI appeals.
76.tq: Eliminate the statement that assigns a neighbouring subject to the platform.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statements 1 and 2: **BHARATPOL** was developed by the **CBI** and launched in **January 2025**.
Statement 3: it lets central and state agencies make **real-time Interpol** assistance requests.
Statement 4 wrong: it has nothing to do with **RTI appeals**.
xa: It puts State and central police on **one platform**.
It uses **Big Data and AI** for fugitive tracking.
The CBI is India's **National Central Bureau** for Interpol.
