90.x: Pair 1 is correct: Section 11 deals with third-party information. Pair 2 is wrong: Section 15 constitutes the State Information Commission; the CIC is under Section 12. Pair 3 is correct: Section 19 deals with appeals. Pair 4 is wrong: Section 22 gives the RTI Act overriding effect over the OSA, it does not repeal it. Hence only 1 and 3 (A); B wrongly includes 2, C picks the two wrong pairs, D assumes all are right.
90.tq: Section 12 = CIC, 15 = SIC; Section 22 overrides, never repeals, the OSA.
xs: Pairs **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Pair 1 correct: **Section 11** = **third-party information**; pair 3 correct: **Section 19** = **appeals**.
Pair 2 wrong: **Section 15** constitutes the **SIC**; the CIC is under **Section 12**.
Pair 4 wrong: **Section 22** **overrides** the OSA 1923; it does not repeal it.
xa: Third-party information has a time limit of **40 days**.
**Section 20** = penalties on PIOs.

90.s:
With reference to the Right to Information Act, 2005, consider the following statements:
1. A body substantially financed or controlled by the government may be a public authority.
2. A body established by a government notification may be a public authority.
3. Only bodies created directly by the Constitution can be public authorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct under Section 2(h). Statement 3 is false because public authorities also include bodies established by law or government notification and substantially financed or controlled by government.
90.tq: Split the definition into its alternative categories and reject the word “only”.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Under **Section 2(h)**, public authorities include bodies set up by the Constitution, a law or a **government notification**, and bodies **substantially financed or controlled** by government.
Statement 3 wrong: bodies created by law or notification also qualify, not only constitutional ones.
xa: NGOs **substantially financed** by government are public authorities (**DAV College Trust, 2019**).
⚠ The CIC held **BCCI is not a public authority** (May 2026).

90.s:
Under Section 6 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, an application for information may be made in which of the following ways and languages?
1. By post, in person or through e-mail
2. In Hindi, English or the official language of the area
3. Only after stating the reasons for seeking the information
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
90.x: Applications may be submitted by post, in person or electronically and may be made in Hindi, English or the local official language. Under Section 6(2), the applicant need not give reasons for seeking information, so statement 3 is false.
90.tq: Catch the reversed requirement that an applicant must disclose reasons.
xs: Only **1 and 2** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Requests go **by post, in person or e-mail**, in **Hindi, English or the local official language**.
Statement 3 wrong: under **Section 6(2)**, **no reason need be given**.
xa: ⚠ The **Madras High Court (2014)** remark that an applicant should state a reason was later **withdrawn**.
Normal reply time under **Section 7**: **30 days**.

90.s:
Match List-I with List-II relating to provisions of the Right to Information Act, 2005:

List-I (Section)
A. Section 5
B. Section 9
C. Section 12
D. Section 15

List-II (Subject)
1. Constitution of the Central Information Commission
2. Constitution of the State Information Commission
3. Designation of Public Information Officers and Assistant Public Information Officers
4. Rejection where disclosure would infringe copyright of a person other than the State

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
90.x: Section 5 concerns PIOs and APIOs; Section 9 concerns copyright belonging to a person other than the State; Sections 12 and 15 concern the CIC and SIC respectively.
90.tq: Start with the sure statutory pair and eliminate codes that disturb it.
xs: Correct matching is **A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Section 5** = designation of **PIOs/APIOs**; **Section 9** = rejection infringing **copyright of a person other than the State**.
**Section 12** = constitution of the **CIC**; **Section 15** = constitution of the **SIC**.
xa: PIOs are designated by each **public authority**, not by the President or Governor.
**Section 11** deals with third-party information.

90.s: Which of the following statements regarding Section 24 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 is correct?
o: Information relating to corruption and human-rights violations is not excluded from disclosure merely because it is held by a listed organisation.
It applies only to organisations created after 2005.
It excludes all information held by intelligence and security organisations without exception.
It removes the jurisdiction of the Information Commission in every case involving a security organisation.
90.x: Section 24 generally excludes listed intelligence and security organisations, but information concerning corruption and human-rights violations remains subject to disclosure under the specified conditions.
90.tq: Test the exception to a broad exclusion and reject absolute wording such as “all” and “without exception”.
xs: Under Section 24, information on **corruption and human-rights violations** is not excluded merely because a listed organisation holds it — option **(1)**.
The Act does not apply to **Second Schedule** bodies (e.g. **IB, RAW**) **except** for such allegations, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: Human-rights information from such bodies: **45 days**, with **Commission approval**.
The **CBI** was added to the Second Schedule in **2011**.

90.s: Under the Right to Information framework, information is provided free of cost to applicants belonging to which category?
o: All applicants below 25 years of age
All applicants belonging to rural areas
90.x: Applicants belonging to the below-poverty-line category are entitled to information without payment of the prescribed fee.
90.tq: Recall the specific beneficiary category attached to fee exemption.
xs: Information is free / fee waived for **BPL** applicants (**persons below the poverty line**), so option **(4)** is correct.
Only **citizens** can apply.
xa: Requests may be in **Hindi, English or the local official language**.
**Section 6(2)**: **no reason need be given**.

90.s: Under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, which of the following is included within the meaning of ‘information’?
o: Information personally generated by an applicant after filing a request
Only physical records maintained by public authorities
Material in any form, including records, e-mails, opinions, contracts, samples and electronic data
Only final judicial decisions published in the Gazette
90.x: Section 2(f) covers material in any form, including records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, contracts, samples, models and electronic data.
90.tq: Choose the option reflecting the broad statutory wording ‘material in any form’.
xs: Under **Section 2(f)**, information is **material in any form**, including **records, e-mails, opinions, contracts, samples and electronic data** — option **(3)**.
It is not limited to physical records or judicial decisions.
xa: The list also covers **advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, models**.
It includes information on a **private body accessible to a public authority under law**.
**CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)**: evaluated **answer sheets** are "information".

90.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the ‘right to information’ under Section 2(j)?
o: Compelling an authority to create a new explanation or opinion
Taking notes, extracts or certified copies
Inspection of works, documents and records
90.x: Section 2(j) includes inspection, notes, extracts, certified copies, certified samples and electronic information. It does not require an authority to create a new explanation or opinion.
90.tq: Find the option that demands creation of information rather than access to existing information.
xs: **Compelling an authority to create a new explanation or opinion** is not part of **Section 2(j)**, so option **(1)** is the answer.
2(j) covers **inspection** of work, documents, records; **notes, extracts or certified copies**; **certified samples**; and electronic information.
xa: ⚠ **2(f)** = "information"; **2(h)** = "public authority"; **2(j)** = "right to information".
**CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay** also warned that impractical demands should not **clog administration**.

90.s:
Consider the following time limits for replying to an RTI request:
1. Information concerning the life or liberty of a person — 48 hours
2. Application routed through an Assistant Public Information Officer — 35 days
3. Information involving a third party under Section 11 — 45 days
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
90.x: Pair 1 is correct: life or liberty cases must be answered within 48 hours. Pair 2 is correct: an APIO adds 5 days to the normal 30, giving 35 days. Pair 3 is wrong: third-party information carries 40 days, not 45 (45 days applies to human-rights allegations against Section 24 organisations). So B; A omits pair 2, C and D include the wrong pair 3.
90.tq: 30 normal, +5 via APIO, 40 third party, 48 hours life/liberty; 45 days is the standard wrong pair.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Life or liberty** → **48 hours**; via an **APIO** → 30 + **5 days** (**35 days**).
Pair 3 wrong: third-party information (**Section 11**) gets **40 days**, not 45.
xa: Normal reply by PIO: **30 days**.
⚠ "Reply in **45 days**" is the standard wrong pair (APPSC 2025).

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding appeals under the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. The first appeal is ordinarily filed within thirty days.
2. The First Appellate Authority may decide the first appeal within thirty days or, for recorded reasons, within an extended period not exceeding forty-five days.
3. A second appeal to the Central or State Information Commission is ordinarily filed within ninety days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: All three statements are correct. The first appeal is due within thirty days, its decision period may extend to forty-five days with reasons, and the second appeal is ordinarily filed within ninety days.
90.tq: Separate the filing period from the decision period and then identify the longer second-appeal limit.
xs: All three statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
First appeal within **30 days**; decided in **30 days**, extendable to **45**.
Second appeal to CIC/SIC within **90 days**.
xa: Appeals are under **Section 19**: First Appellate Authority, then Information Commission.
Life or liberty requests: **48 hours**.

90.s:
Consider the following pairs under the RTI Act, 2005:
1. Normal reply by the PIO - 45 days
2. Information concerning life or liberty - 48 hours
3. First appeal to the First Appellate Authority - within 30 days
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
90.x: B is correct (APPSC 2025 key). Pair 1 is wrong: the normal reply period under Section 7 is 30 days, not 45; 45 days applies only to human-rights allegations against Section 24 organisations. Pair 2 is correct: 48 hours. Pair 3 is correct: the first appeal lies within 30 days. A and C include the wrong pair 1; D includes all.
90.tq: Reply 30 days; life/liberty 48 hours; '45 days reply' is the trap.
xs: Pairs **2 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Pair 1 wrong: a normal PIO reply is due in **30 days**, not 45.
Pair 2 correct: **life or liberty** → **48 hours**; pair 3 correct: first appeal within **30 days**.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2025** key: "reply in 45 days" is the standard wrong pair.
Second appeal: within **90 days**.

90.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Section 8(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
o: Commercial confidence and trade secrets — Section 8(1)(a)
Information held in a fiduciary relationship — Section 8(1)(e)
Information from a foreign government in confidence — Section 8(1)(j)
90.x: Section 8(1)(e) covers information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship. Commercial confidence and trade secrets fall under clause (d), foreign-government information under clause (f), and personal information under clause (j).
90.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring clauses by matching each exemption with its exact letter.
xs: **Fiduciary relationship — Section 8(1)(e)** is correctly matched, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Personal information** is **8(1)(j)**, not (f); trade secrets are **8(1)(d)**, not (a); foreign government information is **8(1)(f)**, not (j).
xa: ⚠ **8(1)(e)** = fiduciary; **8(1)(i)** = cabinet papers; **8(1)(j)** = personal information.
The CIC rejected **CBSE's** fiduciary plea under 8(1)(e) on answer-book procurement data (Jun 2026).

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Section 8 of the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. Under Section 8(2), exempt information may be disclosed if the public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests, even if it is covered by the Official Secrets Act.
2. Under Section 8(3), exempt information becomes disclosable after 10 years.
3. Cabinet deliberations are excluded from the disclosure rule of Section 8(3).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: Section 8(2) is the public-interest override, which applies even to OSA-covered information. Statement 2 is wrong: the Section 8(3) rule is 20 years, not 10. Statement 3 is correct: cabinet deliberations (with security, strategic and economic interests, foreign relations and incitement) are excepted from the 20-year rule. So B; A and C include the wrong statement 2, and D includes it too.
90.tq: 8(2) = public-interest override; 8(3) = 20-year rule with exceptions.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Section 8(2)** allows disclosure when **public interest outweighs the harm**, even under the **OSA**.
Statement 2 wrong: Section 8(3) applies after **20 years**, not 10.
Statement 3 correct: **cabinet deliberations** are excepted from the 20-year rule.
xa: Other exceptions to 8(3): security/strategic/economic interests, foreign relations, incitement.
**Section 9**: copyright of a person other than the State.

90.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the organisations generally covered by the exemption under Section 24 and the Second Schedule of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
90.x: The IB, R&AW and CRPF are among the intelligence and security organisations covered by Section 24. The Central Information Commission is the appellate information body and is not a Section 24 exempt organisation.
90.tq: Identify the odd institutional category instead of confusing an exempt security body with the appellate authority.
xs: The **Central Information Commission** is not a Second Schedule body, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The Second Schedule lists **IB, R&AW**, DRI, ED, NCB, BSF, **CRPF**, NSG.
xa: The **CBI** was added in **2011**.
Exception: information on **corruption and human-rights violations** must still be given.

90.s:
Which of the following institutions or activities has been recognised as falling within the RTI framework in the stated manner?
1. Office of the Chief Justice of India — public authority
2. NGO substantially financed by Government — public authority
3. MPLADS works — covered by RTI
4. BCCI — public authority under Section 2(h)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
90.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the CIC ruled that BCCI is not a public authority under Section 2(h).
90.tq: Find the single reversed institutional classification among three covered categories.
xs: Items **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
**CJI's office** = public authority (**2019**); **substantially financed NGOs** = public authority; **MPLADS** works = covered.
Item 4 wrong: the CIC held **BCCI is not a "public authority"** (May 2026).
xa: BCCI is not **substantially financed** by government, per the CIC.
**Zee Telefilms v. UoI (2005)**: BCCI performs public functions but is not "State" under **Art. 12**.

90.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the six national political parties declared public authorities by the Central Information Commission in June 2013?
90.x: The six parties were INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP and BSP. The Aam Aadmi Party was not included in that CIC order.
90.tq: Find the odd name by recalling the complete six-party list.
xs: The **Aam Aadmi Party** was not among the six, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The six were **INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP, BSP**.
xa: The CIC declared them **public authorities** under **2(h)** in **June 2013**.
The parties **did not comply**; the issue is pending before the Supreme Court.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the demand to bring political parties under the Right to Information Act:
1. It is intended to help check corruption and crony capitalism.
2. It seeks greater scrutiny of illegal foreign contributions.
3. It is linked with the state privileges enjoyed by political parties, including free airtime on Doordarshan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: All three statements describe the reasons advanced by activists for bringing political parties under RTI.
90.tq: Test the cumulative rationale by checking each policy objective separately.
xs: All three statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
Activists want parties under RTI to prevent **corruption + crony capitalism** and check **illegal foreign contributions**.
Parties enjoy **state privileges**, such as **free airtime on DD**.
xa: The **CIC (June 2013)** cited indirect government funding: land, bungalows, free airtime.
**2026 demand**: a **transparent, auditable electoral-funding system**.

90.s:
With reference to political parties and the Right to Information Act, consider the following statements:
1. The RTI Act expressly named political parties as public authorities when it was enacted in 2005.
2. The six parties declared public authorities by the CIC did not comply with the order.
3. The issue was pending before the Supreme Court in the position described.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is false because the 2005 Act did not expressly name political parties. Statements 2 and 3 are correct in the stated position.
90.tq: Spot the wrong historical premise concerning the original wording of the Act.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 wrong: the **2005** Act **did not name** political parties.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: the six parties **did not comply**; the issue is **pending before the Supreme Court**.
xa: ⚠ No final **2018** SC ruling made parties disclose funding under RTI.
The RTI (Amendment) Bill **2013** to exclude parties **lapsed**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding eligibility for appointment as a State Information Commissioner:
1. The person must be one of eminence in public life.
2. Knowledge of law, science and technology, social service, management, journalism, mass media or administration is relevant.
3. The person may be a sitting Member of Parliament if otherwise qualified.
4. The person must not hold an office of profit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. A sitting Member of Parliament cannot be appointed as a State Information Commissioner.
90.tq: Separate the positive eligibility conditions from the disqualifications.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Commissioners must be persons of **eminence in public life** with experience in **law, science and technology, social service, management, journalism, mass media or administration**.
Statement 3 wrong: they **cannot be MP/MLA**; statement 4 correct: they cannot hold an **office of profit**.
xa: They also cannot be connected with a **political party** or carry on a business or profession.
Term now **3 years** under the **2019** Rules.

90.s: A State Information Commissioner is found guilty of proved misbehaviour. Which one of the following correctly describes the removal procedure?
o: The State Legislature must remove the Commissioner by a simple majority.
The High Court may directly remove the Commissioner on a complaint.
The Governor may remove the Commissioner only after a Supreme Court inquiry on a reference made by the Governor.
The Chief Minister may remove the Commissioner without inquiry.
90.x: For proved misbehaviour or incapacity, removal is by the Governor only after the Supreme Court conducts an inquiry on a reference made by the Governor.
90.tq: Ask which authority would perform the job and apply the prescribed safeguard.
xs: The **Governor** removes an SIC member only after a **Supreme Court inquiry** on the Governor's reference — option **(3)**.
This is under **Section 17**, for **proved misbehaviour or incapacity**.
xa: At the Centre, the **President** removes after a Supreme Court inquiry.
The **CVC** is also removed by the President after a **Supreme Court inquiry**.

90.s: Which of the following is NOT a permissible ground associated with removal of a State Information Commissioner?
o: Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude
Disagreement with a decision of the State Government
Proved incapacity after the prescribed inquiry
90.x: Disagreement with a State Government decision is not a stated ground for removal. Insolvency, conviction involving moral turpitude and proved incapacity are recognised grounds.
90.tq: Reject the plausible-sounding ground that is not a statutory basis.
xs: **Disagreement with a decision of the State Government** is not a removal ground, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Valid grounds: proved **misbehaviour/incapacity** (after SC inquiry), **insolvency**, **conviction (moral turpitude)**, **paid employment**, **infirmity**.
xa: Removal is by the **Governor** (Section **17**).
⚠ CIC/SIC = **up to 10** ICs; CVC = **two** Vigilance Commissioners, **4 years or age 65**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central and State Information Commissions:
1. Both are statutory bodies created under the Right to Information Act.
2. Both have powers of a civil court.
3. Both hear second appeals and complaints under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: The Central and State Information Commissions are statutory bodies. They exercise civil-court powers and deal with second appeals and complaints under the Act.
90.tq: Verify the common features before considering the Central-State distinction.
xs: All three statements are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
CIC and SICs are **statutory bodies** created by the RTI Act (not constitutional).
Both have **powers of a civil court** and hear **second appeals and complaints**.
xa: Composition: Chief IC + **up to 10** ICs at both levels.
The **2019 amendment** let the Centre fix tenure and salaries, raising **autonomy** concerns.

90.s: With reference to the composition of the Information Commissions, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Central and State Commissions may each consist of a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.
The State Commission has a Chief Information Commissioner and a maximum of five Information Commissioners.
Each Commission must consist of exactly ten Information Commissioners besides its Chief.
The Central Commission consists only of the Chief Information Commissioner, whereas the State Commission has up to ten members.
90.x: At both levels, the structure consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.
90.tq: Watch the difference between ‘up to’ and a compulsory fixed number.
xs: Both the Central and State Commissions consist of a **Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The cap is "**up to 10**" at both levels — not exactly ten, and not five for States.
xa: The **President** appoints the CIC (**Section 12**); the **Governor** appoints the SIC (**Section 15**).
⚠ CIC/SIC = **up to 10** members; CVC = **two** Vigilance Commissioners.
Both are **statutory bodies** with **powers of a civil court**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure of Information Commissioners:
1. Under the original RTI Act, the term was five years or until the age of 65, whichever was earlier.
2. Under the original RTI Act, a Commissioner could be reappointed for a second term.
3. After the 2019 amendment, the Central Government notifies the term, which the RTI Rules, 2019 fix at three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: the original term was 5 years or age 65. Statement 2 is wrong: the original Act allowed no reappointment. Statement 3 is correct: after 2019 the Centre notifies the term, three years under the RTI Rules, 2019. So B; A, C and D include the wrong statement 2.
90.tq: Before 2019: 5 years/65, no reappointment; after 2019: Centre decides (3 years).
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the original term was **5 years or age 65**.
Statement 2 wrong: there was **no reappointment**.
Statement 3 correct: after **2019**, the Centre notifies the term — **3 years** under the **RTI Rules, 2019**.
xa: The **2019 amendment** also let the Centre fix salaries.
Critics say this **weakens the Commissions' autonomy**.

90.s: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends appointment of the State Chief Information Commissioner?
o: Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly
A State Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister
Chief Justice of the High Court
90.x: D is correct: the Chief Justice of the High Court is not on the SIC selection committee (the trap in the G2 2025 key). The committee is the Chief Minister (chair) (A), the Leader of Opposition in the Assembly (B) and a State Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM (C). The Governor then appoints.
90.tq: SIC panel: CM + LoP + Minister; no judge.
xs: The **Chief Justice of the High Court** is **not** on the SIC selection committee, so option **(4)** is the answer.
The committee is the **Chief Minister (chair)**, the **Leader of Opposition** in the Assembly and a **State Cabinet Minister** nominated by the CM.
xa: This was a **G2 2025** key.
At the Centre: **PM (chair)**, **Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha**, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.
The **Governor** appoints the SIC (**Section 15**).

90.s: The penalty that may be imposed on a Public Information Officer under Section 20 is
90.x: Section 20 provides for a penalty of ₹250 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000, along with possible disciplinary action.
90.tq: Retain both parts of a statutory penalty: the daily rate and the maximum ceiling.
xs: Section 20 penalty is **₹250 per day**, **subject to** a maximum of **₹25,000**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It runs until the application is received or the information furnished.
xa: It is imposed by the **CIC/SIC** on the PIO.
The Commission can also recommend **disciplinary action**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding penalty proceedings under Section 20 of the RTI Act:
1. The Public Information Officer must be given an opportunity of being heard before a penalty is imposed.
2. The burden of proof lies on the applicant.
3. Besides the monetary penalty, the Commission may recommend disciplinary action against the PIO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: the PIO must be heard first. Statement 2 is wrong: the burden of proof is on the PIO, not the applicant. Statement 3 is correct: the Commission can recommend disciplinary action. So C; A, B and D include the wrong statement 2.
90.tq: Section 20: PIO heard first, burden on PIO, ₹250/day up to ₹25,000 plus disciplinary action.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **PIO must be heard first**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **burden of proof is on the PIO**, not the applicant.
Statement 3 correct: the Commission can also recommend **disciplinary action**.
xa: The applicant can get **compensation** under **Section 19(8)(b)**.
Penalty: **₹250 per day**, up to **₹25,000**.

90.s: Under Section 19(8)(b), the Information Commission may require the public authority to
o: provide lifetime employment to the applicant
compensate the applicant for loss suffered
pay a penalty directly to the Information Commissioner
90.x: Section 19(8)(b) enables the Commission to require the public authority to compensate the applicant for any loss or other detriment suffered.
90.tq: Distinguish compensation for the applicant from the separate penalty imposed on the PIO.
xs: Under **Section 19(8)(b)**, the Commission can require the public authority to **compensate the applicant for any loss**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Penalties are under **Section 20** and are levied on the **PIO**, not paid to the Commissioner.
xa: **Section 19** deals with **appeals** (two-tier).
⚠ Penalty = **Section 20**; compensation = **19(8)(b)**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019:
1. Before 2019, the salary of the Chief Information Commissioner was equal to that of the Chief Election Commissioner.
2. Before 2019, the salary of a State Information Commissioner was linked to that of the Chief Secretary.
3. After 2019, the term of State Information Commissioners continues to be fixed in the Act itself.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: the CIC's salary was equal to the CEC's. Statement 2 is correct: a State IC's salary was linked to the Chief Secretary's. Statement 3 is wrong: after 2019 the term and salary of State ICs are also decided by the Centre. So A; B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
90.tq: 2019 amendment moved term and pay of both central and state commissioners to the Centre.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: before 2019, CIC salary = **Chief Election Commissioner**.
Statement 2 correct: a State IC's salary was linked to the **Chief Secretary**.
Statement 3 wrong: after 2019, State ICs' terms are **also decided by the Centre**.
xa: After **2019**, salaries are fixed by the **Central Government**.
The term is now **3 years** under the **2019** Rules.

90.s: The principal criticism of the 2019 changes relating to the tenure and salaries of Information Commissions is that they
o: removed the power of the Commissions to impose penalties
weakened the autonomy of the Commissions by placing tenure and pay in executive hands
made all decisions of the Commissions subject to approval by political parties
90.x: The criticism is that executive control over tenure and remuneration may weaken the institutional autonomy of the Information Commissions.
90.tq: Connect the institutional design change with its governance consequence.
xs: The 2019 changes **weakened the Commissions' autonomy by placing tenure and pay in executive hands**, so option **(2)** is correct.
They did not remove penalty powers or abolish the CIC.
xa: Original term: **5 years** or age **65**; now **3 years** under the 2019 Rules.
"Weakened autonomy after **2019**" is listed among the Act's criticisms.

90.s: Section 44(3) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 altered Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by
o: making personal information a blanket exemption and dropping the earlier public-interest override
transferring all RTI appeals to the Data Protection Board
requiring every applicant to disclose the reason for seeking personal information
removing all exemptions relating to personal information
90.x: Section 44(3) rewrote Section 8(1)(j) to exempt personal information outright, dropping the earlier test concerning relationship to public activity, unwarranted invasion of privacy and the public-interest override.
90.tq: Contrast the original conditional privacy exemption with the amended blanket exemption.
xs: **Section 44(3)** of the DPDP Act **made personal information a blanket exemption** and **dropped the public-interest override** — option **(1)**.
It also dropped the "**no relationship to public activity**" test.
xa: The original 8(1)(j) withheld personal information only if unrelated to public activity or an **unwarranted invasion of privacy**.
The **Supreme Court** referred the challenge to a **Constitution Bench** (Feb 2026).

90.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the challenge to the DPDP amendment is correct?
1. The Centre notified the amendment in November 2025.
2. The Supreme Court referred the challenge to a Constitution Bench in February 2026.
3. On 7 August 2026, the Supreme Court agreed to examine whether the en-bloc embargo was repugnant to the RTI Act.
4. The Attorney-General opined that the amendment diluted the RTI Act.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
90.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: the Attorney-General opined in January 2026 that the amendment did not dilute the RTI Act.
90.tq: Use the dated sequence and reject the statement that reverses the Attorney-General’s opinion.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
The Centre notified the amendment in **Nov 2025**; the SC referred it to a **Constitution Bench** in **Feb 2026**.
On **7 Aug 2026** the SC agreed to examine whether the "**en bloc embargo**" is repugnant to RTI.
Statement 4 wrong: the **Attorney-General** opined it **does not dilute** RTI.
xa: The SC noted its "**constitutional sensitivity**".
The DPDP change dropped the **public-interest override** from **8(1)(j)**.

90.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
a. CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay
b. Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v. CIC
c. CPIO, Supreme Court v. Subhash Chandra Agarwal
d. Zee Telefilms v. Union of India

List-II (Decision)
i. BCCI is not ‘State’ under Article 12
 ii. Service records and tax returns of a public servant are personal information
 iii. Evaluated answer sheets are information accessible to examinees
 iv. Office of the Chief Justice of India is a public authority under the RTI Act

Which of the following is the correct match?
90.x: CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay recognised evaluated answer sheets as information; Girish Deshpande treated service records and tax returns as personal information; Subhash Chandra Agarwal covered the CJI’s office; and Zee Telefilms held that BCCI was not State under Article 12.
90.tq: Start from the sure case–holding pairs and eliminate codes with swapped judicial decisions.
xs: Correct matching is **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)**: answer sheets = information; **Girish Deshpande (2012)**: service records, tax returns = personal information.
**Subhash Chandra Agarwal (2019)**: **CJI's office** is a public authority; **Zee Telefilms (2005)**: BCCI not "State" under **Art. 12**.
xa: ⚠ Answer sheets **2011**; CJI's office **2019**; service record **2012**.
The CIC also held **BCCI is not a public authority** (May 2026).

90.s:
With reference to CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011), consider the following statements:
1. Evaluated answer sheets are information under the RTI Act.
2. Examinees can inspect their evaluated answer sheets.
3. An examining body holds evaluated answer sheets in a fiduciary capacity in every case.
4. Indiscriminate and impractical demands may clog administration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Supreme Court held that the examining body does not hold the evaluated answer sheets in a fiduciary capacity.
90.tq: Find the single overbroad statement containing ‘in every case’.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2 correct: evaluated **answer sheets are information**; examinees can **see/inspect** them.
Statement 3 wrong: the examining body does **not** hold them in a **fiduciary capacity**.
Statement 4 correct: the Court warned that impractical demands should not **clog administration**.
xa: In **Jun 2026** the CIC rejected CBSE's fiduciary plea on answer-book procurement data.
⚠ Answer sheets = information (**2011**); service record/tax returns = personal information (**2012**).

90.s: A Madras High Court observation in 2014 regarding an RTI application was later withdrawn. Which of the following correctly describes the issue?
o: An applicant could seek information only after exhausting departmental remedies.
An applicant could seek information only through a lawyer, as required by Section 6(2).
An applicant had to state the reason for seeking information, contrary to Section 6(2).
An applicant had to pay a special fee for information concerning public authorities.
90.x: The 2014 observation said that an applicant should state the reason for seeking information. It was later withdrawn because Section 6(2) provides that an applicant need not give any reason for requesting information.
90.tq: Identify the judicial observation that conflicts with the express statutory safeguard in Section 6(2).
xs: The **Madras High Court (2014)** said an applicant should **state the reason** for seeking information, contrary to **Section 6(2)** — option **(3)**.
The remark was **later withdrawn**, since Section 6(2) says **no reason need be given**.
xa: This was a **UPPSC 2014** key.
Requests may be by post, in person or e-mail, in **Hindi, English** or the local official language.

90.s: The violation identified during the Andhra Pradesh Information Commission’s statewide inspection primarily related to
o: Section 7 and payment of RTI fees
90.x: The inspection found violations of Section 4(1)(b), which concerns proactive or suo motu disclosure of information.
90.tq: Match the section number with its exact RTI subject.
xs: The AP inspection found **Section 4(1)(b)** (**proactive disclosure**) violations — option **(1)**.
It covered **258 offices in 18 districts** over two days.
xa: It was led by AP Chief Information Commissioner **Vajja Srinivasa Rao** (Jul 2026).
Police denied him entry at **Medikonduru** police station.

90.s: Section 4 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Imposition of penalty on every delayed applicant
Compulsory adjudication of all RTI appeals by courts
Exemption of personal information from disclosure
Suo motu disclosure by public authorities
90.x: Section 4 mandates proactive or suo motu disclosure by public authorities, reducing the need for citizens to file separate applications.
90.tq: Match the statutory section with its distinctive function.
xs: **Section 4** mandates **suo motu disclosure** by public authorities, so option **(4)** is correct.
Personal information exemption is **8(1)(j)**; penalties are **Section 20** and fall on PIOs, not applicants.
xa: **4(1)(b)** lists what must be published.
The **2nd ARC** wanted maximum information **automatically in the public domain**.

90.s:
The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended, in the context of RTI, that:
1. Maximum information should automatically be placed in the public domain.
2. Section 8 exemptions should be interpreted narrowly.
3. Citizens should be required to file applications even for routinely publishable information.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 reflect the recommendation. Statement 3 is contrary to proactive disclosure because routinely publishable information should be available without an application.
90.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the purpose of proactive disclosure.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
The **2nd ARC** wanted **maximum information automatically in the public domain** and a **narrow reading of Section 8**.
Statement 3 wrong: Section 4 is meant so that citizens **need not file applications**.
xa: It also asked to **protect activists** and link RTI with **whistle-blower protection law**.
AP's inspection of **258 offices** found **Section 4(1)(b)** violations (Jul 2026).

90.s:
Which of the following is the most appropriate description of the achievements attributed to the RTI Act?
1. It has helped break the culture of secrecy.
2. It has strengthened citizen participation and service delivery.
3. It has reduced corruption and misuse of public funds.
4. It has completely eliminated corruption in public administration.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
90.x: The Act has helped break secrecy, improve accountability, reduce corruption and misuse of public funds, and strengthen participation and service delivery. It has not completely eliminated corruption.
90.tq: Reject the extreme claim of complete elimination while retaining the qualified achievements.
xs: Items **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
RTI breaks the **culture of secrecy**, strengthens **participation and service delivery**, and **reduces corruption** and misuse of funds.
Item 4 wrong: it has not "completely eliminated" corruption; there are "**miles to go**".
xa: It has **raised the sense of responsibility in the bureaucracy**.
Officials are made **accountable** through Sections like **4** (disclosure) and **20** (penalties).

90.s:
Assertion (A): The RTI Act has been misused by both members of the public and public authorities.
Reason (R): Applicants may file frivolous or bulk requests, while authorities may delay replies or invoke Section 8 in bad faith.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
90.x: Both the assertion and reason are true. The reason identifies the two distinct forms of misuse by applicants and public authorities.
90.tq: Link the general conclusion to concrete examples supplied in the reason.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation** of A — option **(1)** (APPSC 2019 key).
Applicants file **frivolous or bulk** requests; authorities **delay** or misuse **Section 8**.
xa: The Act was enacted for **transparency and accountability**.
Exam angle: A-R pairs on "purpose" vs "misuse" are usually **both true**.

90.s:
Assertion (A): The RTI Act has raised the sense of responsibility in the bureaucracy.
Reason (R): There are still miles to go before the Act achieves its full purpose.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
90.x: B is correct (UPPSC 2010 key). Assertion A is true: the RTI Act has raised the sense of responsibility in the bureaucracy. Reason R is also true: there are still miles to go. But R does not explain why responsibility has risen, so option A (R explains A) is wrong; C and D each wrongly call one statement false.
90.tq: RTI A-R: usually both true; here R is not the explanation.
xs: **Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)** (UPPSC 2010 key).
The Act has **raised the sense of responsibility** in the bureaucracy, but there are "**miles to go**".
xa: Achievements: breaking the **culture of secrecy**; reducing corruption.
Problems: **backlog** of appeals and **vacancies** in Commissions.

90.s: As of July 2026, the approximate number of RTI appeals and complaints pending across Information Commissions was reported to be
90.x: More than 4 lakh RTI appeals and complaints were reported to be pending across Information Commissions as of July 2026.
90.tq: Use the exact numerical figure rather than being distracted by nearby order-of-magnitude options.
xs: Over **4 lakh** RTI appeals/complaints were pending across commissions (Jul 2026), so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Do not mix with **26,000** — the figure cited by the Congress president for 2025.
xa: The **massive backlog of appeals** causes long delays.
**Chronic vacancies** in CIC/SICs add to pendency.

90.s: Which of the following is identified as a major institutional reason for delays in the disposal of RTI matters?
o: Absence of judicial review over RTI orders
Compulsory prior approval of Parliament for every RTI application
Chronic vacancies in the Central and State Information Commissions
90.x: Chronic vacancies in the Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions, together with a large backlog of appeals, cause long delays.
90.tq: Identify the institutional cause directly linked to the stated administrative consequence.
xs: **Chronic vacancies in the Central and State Information Commissions** are a major reason for delays, so option **(4)** is correct.
They feed the **massive backlog of appeals**.
xa: Over **4 lakh** appeals/complaints pending (Jul 2026).
The **Satark Nagrik Sangathan 2025** report flagged gaps in Information Commissions.

90.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 suggested re-examination of the RTI framework mainly in the context of exempting which of the following categories of information?
o: Only information supplied by private bodies
All information held by local authorities
All records relating to public expenditure and contracts
Confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions
90.x: The Economic Survey suggested considering exemptions for confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions, along with a possible ministerial veto.
90.tq: Match the policy proposal with the specific categories named in it.
xs: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** sought to exempt **confidential service records and draft/exploratory policy discussions** — option **(4)**.
It floated a possible "**ministerial veto**".
xa: It called India's RTI regime "**uniquely broad**", with a **chilling effect** on honest decision-making.
The **Opposition** called it dilution of accountability.

90.s: More than how many RTI activists were reported to have been killed by July 2026?
90.x: Reports cited that more than 100 RTI activists had been killed by July 2026.
90.tq: Recall the reported threshold and avoid confusing it with lower estimates.
xs: **More than 100** RTI activists have been killed, so option **(4)** is correct.
Threats include **harassment, legal intimidation and physical attacks**.
xa: The **Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014** is not operationalised; a **2015** amendment bill sought to dilute it.
The call to implement the 2nd ARC whistle-blower recommendations was repeated on **30 Jul 2026**.

90.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended that the RTI framework should be linked firmly with
90.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended firmly linking RTI with whistle-blower protection to prevent victimisation of those who disclose information.
90.tq: Identify the protection mechanism that directly addresses victimisation of information-seekers.
xs: The 2nd ARC wanted RTI linked firmly with **whistle-blower protection law**, to prevent victimisation — option **(4)**.
It also asked to **narrow Section 8** and **maximise Section 4** disclosure.
xa: The **Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014** is not operationalised.
The call was repeated on **30 Jul 2026**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission:
1. It consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners.
2. Its members hold office for 5 years or till the age of 65.
3. A member can be removed by the President for misbehaviour or incapacity only after a Supreme Court inquiry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: C is correct. Statement 1 is correct: the Commission has a Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners. Statement 2 is wrong: the CVC term is 4 years or age 65; 5 years or 65 was the original Information Commission term. Statement 3 is correct: the President removes for misbehaviour or incapacity after a Supreme Court inquiry. A and B include the false statement 2; D includes all.
90.tq: CVC: 1 + 2 members, 4 yrs/65; Information Commission originally 5 yrs/65.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: a **Central Vigilance Commissioner** + up to **two Vigilance Commissioners**.
Statement 2 wrong: the CVC term is **4 years or age 65**, not 5.
Statement 3 correct: removal by the **President** after a **Supreme Court inquiry**.
xa: ⚠ CIC/SIC = **up to 10** ICs, term now **3 years**.
CVC members can also be removed on grounds like **insolvency**.

90.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the firsts associated with the Right to Information movement?
o: Sweden — first RTI law; Tamil Nadu — first Indian State RTI law; Wajahat Habibullah — first CIC
United Kingdom — first RTI law; Kerala — first Indian State RTI law; Wajahat Habibullah — first CIC
Sweden — first RTI law; Tamil Nadu — first Indian State RTI law; M. Veerappa Moily — first CIC
United States — first RTI law; Tamil Nadu — first Indian State RTI law; Wajahat Habibullah — first CIC
90.x: Sweden enacted the first RTI law in 1766, Tamil Nadu enacted the first Indian State RTI law in 1997, and Wajahat Habibullah was the first CIC.
90.tq: Use the three independent firsts to eliminate options with one substituted country, State or office-holder.
xs: **Sweden** — first RTI law; **Tamil Nadu** — first Indian state RTI law; **Wajahat Habibullah** — first CIC: option **(1)**.
Sweden's law dates to **1766**; Tamil Nadu's to **1997**.
**Veerappa Moily** chaired the 2nd ARC, not the CIC.
xa: **Goa** passed its law the same year as Tamil Nadu (**1997**).
Order: **Sweden → UN → FOI Act → RTI Act**.

90.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or institutional concern relating to the functioning of the RTI regime?
o: Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications
90.x: The identified concerns include appeal backlogs, vacancies, misuse of Section 8 and threats to activists. Excessive speed in disposal is not listed as a criticism.
90.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented governance problem.
xs: **Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications** is not a concern — the problem is delay — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The listed criticisms are **backlog of appeals/delays**, **vacancies in Commissions**, misuse of **Section 8** and **threats/attacks on activists**.
xa: Over **4 lakh** appeals/complaints were pending (Jul 2026).
Another criticism: **weakened autonomy** after **2019**.
The **Satark Nagrik Sangathan 2025** report flagged gaps as the Act turns **20**.

90.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the decisions concerning BCCI under the RTI Act and Article 12?
o: BCCI was held to be State under Article 12 but exempt from the RTI Act because it is a sports body.
BCCI was held to be a public authority under Section 2(h) and State under Article 12.
BCCI performs public functions but was held not to be State under Article 12 and was also ruled not to be a public authority under Section 2(h).
BCCI performs no public functions and is outside all forms of public accountability.
90.x: Zee Telefilms held that BCCI performs public functions but is not State under Article 12. A later CIC ruling also held that BCCI is not a public authority under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act.
90.tq: Separate the Article 12 question from the distinct Section 2(h) public-authority question.
xs: BCCI **performs public functions** but is **not State under Article 12**, and the CIC ruled it **not a public authority under Section 2(h)** — option **(3)**.
**Zee Telefilms v. UoI (2005)** held it is not "State"; the **CIC** (May 2026) held it is not a public authority.
The CIC's reason: BCCI is **not substantially financed** by government (**Section 2(h)(d)**).
xa: By contrast, NGOs **substantially financed** by government are public authorities (**DAV College Trust, 2019**).
The **CJI's office** is a public authority (**2019**).

91.s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Max Weber’s ideal-type bureaucracy based on legal-rational authority?
o: Personal patronage as the primary basis of appointment
91.x: Weber’s ideal-type bureaucracy is based on hierarchy, rules, impersonality, specialisation, merit and written files. Personal patronage is not its defining basis.
91.tq: Identify the option that belongs to a contrasting patronage system.
xs: **Personal patronage as the primary basis of appointment** is not a Weberian feature, so option **(1)** is the answer.
Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy rests on **legal-rational authority**: **hierarchy**, rules, **impersonality**, specialisation, **merit**, **written files**.
xa: **Patronage** bureaucracy is one of **F. Morstein Marx's** four types, with guardian, caste and merit.
Morstein Marx wrote **The Administrative State**.

91.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the types of bureaucracy identified by F. Morstein Marx?
91.x: F. Morstein Marx identified guardian, caste, patronage and merit bureaucracies in The Administrative State.
91.tq: Recall the exact four-part typology without confusing it with Weber’s authority types.
xs: **F. Morstein Marx** classified bureaucracies as **guardian, caste, patronage and merit**, so option **(2)** is correct.
"Legal, traditional, charismatic" are types of authority, not his bureaucracy types.
xa: His book: **The Administrative State**.
**Max Weber** gave the **ideal-type** bureaucracy based on **legal-rational authority**.

91.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Doctrine of Pleasure in relation to services?
91.x: Article 310 embodies the Doctrine of Pleasure.
91.tq: Test precise constitutional article mapping.
xs: The **Doctrine of Pleasure** is in **Article 310**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Article 311** = safeguards; **312** = All India Services; **309** = recruitment and conditions of service.
xa: ⚠ **310** = pleasure; **311** = safeguards; **312** = AIS.
Article 311: no dismissal by an authority **subordinate** to the appointing one; **inquiry and hearing** required.

91.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 309
B. Article 311
C. Article 312
D. Article 320

List-II (Subject)
1. Functions of Public Service Commissions
2. Safeguards in dismissal and disciplinary proceedings
3. All India Services
4. Recruitment and conditions of service

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
91.x: Article 309 concerns recruitment and conditions of service; Article 311 provides safeguards; Article 312 concerns All India Services; and Article 320 specifies PSC functions.
91.tq: Begin with the distinctive Article 312–All India Services pair and complete the mapping.
xs: Correct matching is **A-4, B-2, C-3, D-1**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**309** = recruitment and conditions of service; **311** = safeguards; **312** = **All India Services**; **320** = functions of PSCs.
xa: **Article 315** = PSCs for Union and States; **316** = appointment and term; **317** = removal and suspension.
**Article 323** = reports of PSCs.

91.s: A member of a Public Service Commission is proposed to be removed for misbehaviour. Which procedure is constitutionally relevant?
o: Removal by the Chief Minister after consultation with the State Cabinet
An inquiry by the Supreme Court before removal for misbehaviour
Removal by the Governor without any inquiry
Removal by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha after a simple majority vote
91.x: B is correct: a member of a Public Service Commission can be removed for misbehaviour only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court. A, C and D are wrong because neither the Chief Minister, nor the Governor without inquiry, nor the Lok Sabha Speaker by a vote can remove a PSC member.
91.tq: Apply the constitutional safeguard by asking which authority performs the inquiry.
xs: A PSC member can be removed for misbehaviour only after **an inquiry by the Supreme Court**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Removal and suspension of members is under **Article 317**.
xa: **Article 316** covers appointment and term of members.
UPSC began in **1950**, from the **Federal PSC** under the **GoI Act 1935**.

91.s: A member of the Union Public Service Commission holds office for:
o: 5 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
6 years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier
6 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
4 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
91.x: C is correct: a UPSC member serves 6 years or until 65. B is the limit for State and Joint PSC members (6 years or 62). A was the original Information Commissioner term; D is the CVC term.
91.tq: UPSC 6 yrs/65; SPSC 6 yrs/62.
xs: A UPSC member serves **6 years or until 65**, whichever earlier, so option **(3)** is correct.
**62** is the age limit for **SPSC/JSPSC** members.
xa: ⚠ UPSC **65** vs SPSC/JSPSC **62**.
The **JSPSC** is a **statutory** body.
UPSC came in **1950**, succeeding the Federal PSC of the **GoI Act 1935**.

91.s: The tenure system under the Central Staffing Scheme refers to:
o: Permanent transfer of every State officer to the Union Government
A fixed term of service at the Centre followed by return to the State cadre
Rotation only among district offices within a State
Appointment of Central officers exclusively to local governments
91.x: Under the tenure system, State-cadre officers serve a fixed term at the Centre and then return to their State cadre.
91.tq: Distinguish a fixed central deputation followed by return from permanent transfer.
xs: The tenure system means **a fixed term at the Centre followed by return to the State cadre**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It runs under DoPT's **Central Staffing Scheme**.
xa: The **split system** separates **policy** (Secretariat) from **implementation** (field agencies).
⚠ IAS cadre control = **DoPT**, not MHA.

91.s: The split system in civil administration refers to the separation of:
o: Policy formulation in the Secretariat from implementation through field agencies
91.x: The split system separates policy functions performed by the Secretariat from implementation carried out by field agencies.
91.tq: Discriminate between policy and implementation functions.
xs: The split system separates **policy formulation in the Secretariat** from **implementation through field agencies**, so option **(2)** is correct.
This was a **BPSC 2021** question.
xa: The **tenure system**: state-cadre officers serve a fixed term at the Centre, then return.
Civil servants act as **policy advisers, implementers and stabilisers**.

91.s:
Match the service with its cadre-controlling authority:

List-I (Service)
A. IAS
B. IPS
C. Indian Forest Service

List-II (Authority)
1. Ministry of Home Affairs
2. Department of Personnel and Training
3. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
91.x: DoPT controls the IAS cadre, the Ministry of Home Affairs controls the IPS cadre, and MoEFCC controls the Indian Forest Service cadre.
91.tq: Start with the familiar IPS–MHA pair and distinguish the two remaining departments.
xs: Correct matching is **A-2, B-1, C-3**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**IAS** → **DoPT**; **IPS** → **MHA**; **Indian Forest Service** → **MoEFCC**.
xa: ⚠ IAS = **DoPT**, not MHA.
All India Services are under **Article 312**.

91.s: Civil Services Day is observed on 21 April because on 21 April 1947:
o: The Federal Public Service Commission was renamed UPSC
Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi
The first All India Service was created
The UPSC was established in New Delhi
91.x: On 21 April 1947, Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House in Delhi and described civil servants as the “steel frame of India.”
91.tq: Link the observance date to its historical origin and speaker.
xs: On **21 Apr 1947**, **Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi**, so option **(2)** is correct.
He called them the **"steel frame of India"**.
xa: The **17th CSD** was held on **21 Apr 2025** at **Vigyan Bhawan**.
UPSC itself came in **1950**.

91.s: Which rules require political neutrality and integrity from the concerned civil servants?
o: Civil Services Examination Rules, 1968 and Election Rules, 1964
All India Services Act, 1935 and CCS Rules, 1947
91.x: The AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968 and CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 require political neutrality and integrity.
91.tq: Discriminate between conduct rules and recruitment or constitutional provisions.
xs: The **AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968** and **CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964** require political neutrality and integrity, so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ AIS Conduct Rules **1968**; CCS Conduct Rules **1964**; AP CCA Rules **1991**.
xa: An AP section officer was dismissed under **Rule 9, AP CCA Rules 1991** for campaigning in the **2024** elections.
A **Chhattisgarh** circular (**21 Apr 2026**) barring party membership was quickly withdrawn.

91.s:
Which measures are associated with insulating civil servants from undue political pressure?
1. Fixed tenure
2. Civil Services Boards
3. Recommendations in the T.S.R. Subramanian case
4. Recommendations of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
91.x: Fixed tenure and Civil Services Boards were associated with the T.S.R. Subramanian case and the Second Administrative Reforms Commission in the context of insulating civil servants.
91.tq: Recognise the common institutional safeguards across judicial and administrative reform recommendations.
xs: All four are linked to insulating civil servants, so option **(3)** is correct.
The **T.S.R. Subramanian case** and the **2nd ARC** called for **fixed tenure** and **Civil Services Boards**.
xa: Neutrality is required by the **AIS (Conduct) Rules 1968** and **CCS (Conduct) Rules 1964**.
The **Chhattisgarh** circular (**21 Apr 2026**) reopened the neutrality debate.

91.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding committees that reviewed the Civil Services Examination:

List-I (Committee)
a. D.S. Kothari Committee
b. Satish Chandra Committee
c. Y.K. Alagh Committee
d. P.C. Hota Committee

List-II (Theme)
i. Civil service reforms
ii. Review of the Kothari scheme and introduction of an essay paper
iii. Review of the Civil Services Examination system
iv. Introduction of the three-stage examination system

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
91.x: The D.S. Kothari Committee was associated with the three-stage examination system; Satish Chandra reviewed that scheme and introduced the essay paper; Y.K. Alagh reviewed the CSE system; and P.C. Hota dealt with civil service reforms.
91.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with swapped committee themes.
xs: Correct matching is **a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kothari** → three-stage CSE; **Satish Chandra** (**1989**) → essay paper; **Alagh** → review of CSE scheme; **Hota** (**2004**) → civil services reforms.
xa: The three-stage CSE ran from **1979**.
**B.S. Baswan** (**2016**): eligibility, age limit, attempts, syllabus.

91.s: The B.S. Baswan Committee, constituted in 2016, examined issues relating to:
o: The introduction of the essay paper alone
Age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern
The three-stage examination system introduced in 1979
91.x: The B.S. Baswan Committee examined the age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern for the Civil Services Examination.
91.tq: Beware of the word “only” and identify the option that captures all the stated areas of review.
xs: The **Baswan** Committee (**2016**) examined CSE **eligibility, age limit, attempts and syllabus**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The essay paper came from **Satish Chandra** (**1989**); the three-stage exam from **Kothari**.
xa: **P.C. Hota** (**2004**): domain expertise, **lateral entry**, appraisal.
Baswan is the latest in the list: Kothari → Satish Chandra → Alagh → Hota → Baswan.

91.s: The committee set up by the UPSC in July 2000 to review the Civil Services Examination scheme was headed by:
91.x: Standard sources identify the July 2000 committee set up by the UPSC with Y.K. Alagh. Sukhadeo Thorat is named in a conflicting examination key, but the standard identification is Alagh.
91.tq: Resolve a look-alike attribution by focusing on the standard committee-chairman association.
xs: The UPSC's **July 2000** committee is named after **Y.K. Alagh** in standard sources, so option **(1)** is correct.
It reviewed the **CSE scheme** (**2000-01**).
xa: ⚠ An **MPPSC 2023** key names **Sukhadeo Thorat** — the Thorat vs Alagh trap.
**Satish Chandra** (**1989**) and **Kothari** (**1976**) were earlier.

91.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Administrative Reforms Commission:
1. It was constituted in 2005 with M. Veerappa Moily as Chairman.
2. It submitted 12 reports.
3. Its First Report was titled 'Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2nd ARC was constituted on 31 August 2005 under M. Veerappa Moily. Statement 2 is wrong: it submitted 15 reports (2006-2009); the 12th Report was 'Citizen Centric Administration'. Statement 3 is correct: the First Report was on RTI as the 'Master Key to Good Governance'. So B; A, C and D include the wrong statement 2.
91.tq: 2nd ARC: 2005, Moily, 15 reports; 1st = RTI, 4th = Ethics, 10th = Personnel, 12th = Citizen Centric.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the 2nd ARC was constituted on **31 Aug 2005** under **M. Veerappa Moily**.
Statement 2 wrong: it submitted **15 reports** (**2006-2009**).
Statement 3 correct: the 1st report was "**Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance**".
xa: Moily was later succeeded by **V. Ramachandran**.
It is called the "**Bible**" of administrative reform.

91.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Report)
A. Fourth Report
B. Tenth Report
C. Eleventh Report
D. Fifteenth Report

List-II (Title)
1. State and District Administration
2. Ethics in Governance
3. Promoting e-Governance – The SMART Way Forward
4. Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
91.x: The Fourth Report concerned Ethics in Governance; the Tenth, Refurbishing of Personnel Administration; the Eleventh, Promoting e-Governance; and the Fifteenth, State and District Administration.
91.tq: Start from the sure report-title pairs and eliminate codes with a misplaced item.
xs: Correct matching is **A-2, B-4, C-3, D-1**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**4th** = **Ethics in Governance**; **10th** = **Refurbishing of Personnel Administration - Scaling New Heights**.
**11th** = **Promoting e-Governance - The SMART Way Forward**; **15th** = **State and District Administration**.
xa: **12th** = **Citizen Centric Administration - The Heart of Governance**.
The 10th report title was an **APPSC 2018** question.

91.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Lateral entry at the Joint Secretary level
Abolition of right to public services laws
91.x: The Commission recommended right to public services laws, not their abolition. It also supported lateral entry, performance-based appraisal and rotational postings.
91.tq: Find the option that reverses a recorded recommendation.
xs: **Abolition of right to public services laws** was not recommended — the 2nd ARC backed such laws — so option **(4)** is the answer.
It recommended **lateral entry** at Joint Secretary level, **performance-based appraisal** and **rotational postings**.
xa: Other recommendations: a **code of ethics** + a **Public Service Bill**, and a **Department of e-Governance**.
Chairman: **M. Veerappa Moily**; **15 reports**.

91.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position on lateral entry into civil services?
o: It is restricted to entry-level clerical posts.
It replaces the Civil Services Examination for all services.
It was opposed by both the Second ARC and the Hota Committee.
It was supported by the Second ARC and the Hota Committee; a UPSC-led, merit-based process has been suggested for domain experts.
91.x: Both the Second Administrative Reforms Commission and the P.C. Hota Committee supported lateral entry. A UPSC-led, merit-based process has been suggested for domain experts.
91.tq: Compare the positions of two reform bodies and separate lateral entry from total replacement of the CSE.
xs: Lateral entry **was supported by the 2nd ARC and the Hota Committee**, with a **UPSC-led, merit-based process** suggested for domain experts — option **(4)**.
The 2nd ARC proposed it at **Joint Secretary** level.
xa: **Hota** (**2004**) also covered domain expertise and appraisal.
There is a parallel case for **dedicated scientific cadres**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission Karmayogi:
1. It is the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building, launched in 2020.
2. It runs on the iGOT Karmayogi online platform.
3. The Union Public Service Commission is its custodian.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mission Karmayogi is the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (2020). Statement 2 is correct: its online platform is iGOT Karmayogi. Statement 3 is wrong: its custodian is the Capacity Building Commission (CBC), not the UPSC. So (a) misses statement 2, and (c) and (d) wrongly include statement 3.
91.tq: Karmayogi: 2020, iGOT platform, Capacity Building Commission as custodian.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2)**, **1 and 2 only**.
1: **Mission Karmayogi** is the **National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building** (**2020**).
2: it runs on the **iGOT Karmayogi** online platform.
3 is wrong: its custodian is the **Capacity Building Commission (CBC)**, not the UPSC.
xa: The CBC launched the **Global Digital Capacity Building Alliance** on **20 Feb 2026** at the India AI Impact Summit.
**Lateral entry** at Joint Secretary level was backed by the **2nd ARC** and **Hota** (**2004**).
2nd ARC **10th report**: "**Refurbishing of Personnel Administration**" (APPSC 2018).

91.s:
Civil servants perform which of the following roles in public administration?
1. Policy advisers
2. Implementers of public policy
3. Stabilisers of the administrative system
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
91.x: Civil servants serve as policy advisers, implementers and stabilisers in public administration; therefore, all three statements are correct.
91.tq: Recognise the complementary roles of civil servants instead of treating advice, implementation and stability as mutually exclusive.
xs: All three roles are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
Civil servants act as **policy advisers**, **implementers** and **stabilisers**.
xa: Sardar Patel called the civil services the **"steel frame of India"** (**1947**).
The **split system** separates policy (Secretariat) from implementation (field agencies).

92.s: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by:
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
92.x: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by Transparency International, headquartered in Berlin.
92.tq: Identify the publisher rather than confusing the index with a World Bank or United Nations product.
xs: The CPI is published by **Transparency International (Berlin)**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It has been published **yearly since 1995**.
xa: It measures **perceived public-sector corruption** (APPSC-G2 2017).
Scale: **0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean)**; covers about **180 countries**.

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Corruption Perceptions Index?
o: It ranks only developing countries according to reported cases of bribery
It measures perceived public-sector corruption on a scale of 0 to 100, with 0 representing highly corrupt conditions
It measures proved corruption convictions on a scale of 0 to 100, with 100 representing highly corrupt conditions
It measures private-sector tax evasion on a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 representing maximum corruption
92.x: The CPI measures the perceived level of public-sector corruption on a 0-100 scale. A score of 0 denotes highly corrupt conditions; the index covers about 180 countries.
92.tq: Separate perception from proved cases and public-sector corruption from private-sector conduct.
xs: The CPI measures **perceived public-sector corruption** on a scale of **0 to 100**, with **0** = **highly corrupt** — option **(2)**.
It is about **perception**, from expert and business surveys — not convictions or tax evasion.
xa: ⚠ **0** = highly corrupt; **100** = very clean.
Publisher: **Transparency International**, yearly since **1995**.

92.s:
Under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, the expression ‘public servant’ includes which of the following?
1. An employee of a local authority
2. A Judge
3. A person whose office requires performance of a public duty
4. Only a permanent employee of the Union Government
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: The definition in Section 2(c) covers government and local-authority employees, Judges and persons performing a public duty. It is not restricted to permanent Union Government employees.
92.tq: Reject the restrictive word ‘only’ and identify the statutory scope of a definition.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Under **Sec 2(c)**, a public servant includes any government or **local-authority employee**, **any Judge**, or anyone whose office requires a **public duty**.
Statement 4 wrong: the definition is not limited to permanent Union employees.
xa: PCA offences: **bribery**, **undue advantage**, **criminal misconduct**.
The **2018** amendment aligned the PCA with **UNCAC**.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Santhanam Committee — Committee on Prevention of Corruption
2. CBI — 1963
3. CVC — 1964
4. Prevention of Corruption Act — 1988
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: The Santhanam Committee was the Committee on Prevention of Corruption; the CBI emerged in 1963, the CVC in 1964, and the Prevention of Corruption Act was enacted in 1988.
92.tq: Track the institutional sequence from committee recommendation to statutory law.
xs: All four pairs are correctly matched, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Santhanam Committee** (**1962**) on prevention of corruption; **CBI** **1963**; **CVC** **1964**; **PCA** **1988**.
xa: The CVC is now statutory under the **CVC Act 2003**.
The CBI rests on the **DSPE Act 1946**.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act:
1. Bribe-giving was made a direct offence punishable with imprisonment up to seven years.
2. A coerced bribe-giver is protected only if the matter is reported within 30 days.
3. Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf, with the offence framed around 'undue advantage'.
4. It sought to align Indian law with the UN Convention against Corruption, which India ratified in 2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Statement 1 is correct: bribe-giving became a direct offence (up to 7 years). Statement 2 is wrong: the coerced giver must report within 7 days, not 30. Statement 3 is correct: commercial organisations are liable and 'undue advantage' frames the offence. Statement 4 is correct: the amendment aligns with UNCAC, ratified in 2011. So B; A omits the correct statement 4, C and D include the wrong statement 2.
92.tq: 2018 PCA: giver punished (7 yrs), coerced giver reports in 7 days, firms liable, UNCAC alignment.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **bribe-giving** is a direct offence, up to **7 years**.
Statement 2 wrong: a coerced bribe-giver is protected if they report within **7 days**, not 30.
Statements 3 and 4 correct: **commercial organisations** liable ("**undue advantage**"); aligned with **UNCAC**, ratified **2011**.
xa: **Sec 17A**: government approval before inquiry/investigation into official decisions.
Trial within **2 years**, extendable to a maximum of **4**.

92.s: A public servant is prosecuted for an offence of bribery under the amended Prevention of Corruption Act. Which of the following correctly states the punishment and trial framework mentioned?
o: Imprisonment of three to seven years and trial within two years, extendable up to a maximum of four years
Imprisonment of one to three years and trial within seven years without extension
Fine alone, with no prescribed time limit for trial
Imprisonment of seven to ten years and trial only after retirement
92.x: A bribed public servant may receive three to seven years’ imprisonment and a fine. Trials are intended to conclude within two years, with extension possible up to a maximum of four years.
92.tq: Combine punishment and procedural time limits without confusing the two periods.
xs: A bribed public servant gets **three to seven years** + fine; trial **within two years**, extendable to a **maximum of four** — option **(1)**.
These are features of the **2018** amendment.
xa: Bribe-giving: up to **7 years**.
Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf.

92.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the United Nations Convention against Corruption in chronological order:
A. India ratified the Convention.
B. The Convention was adopted.
C. India signed the Convention.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: The Convention was adopted in 2003, India signed it in 2005, and India ratified it in 2011.
92.tq: Fix the sequence by identifying the legal order of adoption, signature and ratification.
xs: The order is **B, C, A**, so option **(2)** is correct.
UNCAC was **adopted in 2003**, **signed by India in 2005** and **ratified in 2011**.
xa: The **PCA (Amendment) Act, 2018** aimed to align Indian law with UNCAC.
⚠ UNCAC **2003** adopted → **2005** signed → **2011** ratified.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the differing views in the split verdict concerning Section 17A?
o: Justice Nagarathna struck it down as violating Article 14, while Justice Viswanathan upheld it subject to a binding Lokpal or Lokayukta opinion.
Justice Nagarathna upheld it, while Justice Viswanathan struck it down as violating Article 19.
Both judges upheld it without attaching any condition to approval.
Both judges struck it down solely because it concerned retired public servants.
92.x: Justice Nagarathna held Section 17A unconstitutional as violating Article 14. Justice Viswanathan upheld it on the condition that approval rests on a binding Lokpal or Lokayukta opinion; the matter is pending before a larger Bench.
92.tq: Separate the contrasting judicial views instead of treating a split verdict as a unanimous ruling.
xs: **Justice Nagarathna** struck Sec 17A down (violates **Art. 14**); **Justice Viswanathan** upheld it if approval rests on a binding **Lokpal/Lokayukta** opinion — option **(1)**.
The case is **Centre for PIL v. UoI** (Jan **2026**), a **split verdict**.
