132.x: PMSMA provides free antenatal check-ups for all pregnant women on the ninth day of every month.
132.tq: Recall the fixed monthly date associated with PMSMA.
xs: **PMSMA** gives free antenatal check-ups on the **ninth day of every month** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC **2022** key).
It started in **2016**, for all pregnant women.
xa: ⚠ **PMSMA** = **9th** of every month check-up; **PMMVY** = cash for the first child.
**JSY** (**2005**) = **100%** centrally sponsored cash for institutional delivery under NHM.

132.s: Swadhar Greh is intended primarily for which target group?
132.x: Swadhar Greh is meant for women in difficult circumstances and has now been brought within Shakti Sadan.
132.tq: Identify the target group before considering the scheme’s institutional location.
xs: **Swadhar Greh** is for **women in difficult circumstances** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is now within **Shakti Sadan** (with **Ujjawala**).
Hostels for working women = **Working Women Hostel**/**Sakhi Niwas**; rural savings = **Mahila Samriddhi**; ICDS nutrition = **Kishori Shakti**.
xa: AP: **26 Shakti Sadans** sheltered **950** women; earlier figure **28**.
Shakti Sadan sits under **Samarthya**.

132.s: STEP, introduced during 1986–87, was designed to promote which of the following?
o: Fast-track trials of crimes against women
Skills for gainful employment of women
132.x: STEP, or Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women, was introduced in 1986–87 to develop skills for women’s gainful employment.
132.tq: Link the programme’s historical period with its employment-oriented purpose.
xs: **STEP** (**1986-87**) promotes **skills for gainful employment of women** — option **(4)** is correct.
Fast-track trials were the aim of AP's **Disha** Bill (**2019**); post-birth grants = **Balika Samriddhi**.
xa: **DWCRA** (**1982-83**): groups of rural BPL women, sub-scheme of IRDP.
**Working Women Hostel** (**1972-73**) → now **Sakhi Niwas**.
**NAVYA** gives vocational training to girls **16-18**.

132.s: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana, introduced in 1993, seeks to promote which one of the following among rural women?
132.x: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana was introduced in 1993 to encourage the savings habit among rural women.
132.tq: Use the beneficiary group and the single core objective to avoid scheme substitution.
xs: **Mahila Samriddhi Yojana** (**1993**) promotes the **habit of saving** among rural women — option **(2)** is correct.
Shelter = **Swadhar Greh**; ICDS nutrition = **Kishori Shakti**; PMKVY training = **NAVYA**.

xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(2)**.
1: **Rashtriya Mahila Kosh** lends to **intermediary NGOs/MFIs**, which on-lend **micro-credit** to poor women — correct.

Ministry of Women and Child Development

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 17:
1. Untouchability is expressly defined in the Constitution.
2. Article 17 operates against private persons also.
3. Article 17 belongs to the Right to Equality group.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: The Constitution does not define ‘untouchability’. Article 17 is a Fundamental Right within the Right to Equality group and can operate against private persons as well.
133.tq: Reject the precise-sounding but false claim that the Constitution defines untouchability.
xs: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **neither the Constitution nor any Act defines "untouchability"**.
Statement 2: Art. 17 binds **private persons** as well as the State (**PUDR v Union of India**, **1982**).
Statement 3: Art. 17 is in the **Right to Equality** group.
xa: Only **Parliament** can prescribe punishment for Art. 17 offences (**Art. 35(a)(ii)**).
**Mysore HC:** untouchability means the practice **as it developed historically**, not the literal sense.
First law enforcing Art. 17: **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955**, renamed **Protection of Civil Rights Act** in **1976**.

133.s: Who is associated with ensuring that Article 17 made untouchability a punishable offence?
133.x: B.R. Ambedkar ensured that Article 17 constitutionally treated untouchability as a punishable offence.
133.tq: Match the constitutional contribution with the principal figure associated with it.
xs: **B.R. Ambedkar** ensured Art. 17 made untouchability a **punishable offence** — option **(3)** is correct.
He called caste "**a division of labourers**" and preferred the term **Dalit** over 'Harijan'.
xa: ⚠ **Gandhi** coined **'Harijan'** and called untouchability "**a blot on Hinduism**".
Ambedkar led the **Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha** on **20 Mar 1927**.
Ambedkar wrote **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**).

133.s: Under Article 35(a)(ii) of the Constitution of India, the power to prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17 belongs to
o: Both Parliament and State Legislatures concurrently
133.x: Article 35(a)(ii) gives Parliament, and not the State Legislatures, the power to prescribe punishment for offences relating to Article 17.
133.tq: Ask which authority would do this job, while distinguishing Parliament from State Legislatures.
xs: Under **Art. 35(a)(ii)**, only **Parliament** — not State legislatures — can prescribe punishment for Art. 17 offences: option **(1) Parliament alone**.
So the power is not concurrent and not with the courts.
xa: Art. 17 abolishes untouchability; its practice in any form is **forbidden** and **punishable by law**.
Laws enforcing Art. 17: **PCR Act** (**1955**/**1976**) and **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989**.
Conviction for untouchability offences disqualifies from elections under **Sec. 8, RPA 1951**.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mysore High Court's interpretation of 'untouchability' under Article 17:
1. It covers the practice as it developed historically, not the literal sense of the word.
2. Social boycott of a few individuals falls within its scope.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Mysore HC read 'untouchability' as the historically developed practice, not its literal meaning. Statement 2 is wrong: the same reading excludes social boycott of a few individuals. Hence A; B and C wrongly accept statement 2, and D wrongly rejects statement 1.
133.tq: Historical practice - yes; boycott of a few individuals - excluded.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: the **Mysore HC** read untouchability as the practice **as it developed historically**, not the literal sense.
Statement 2 is wrong: **social boycott of a few individuals** is **excluded**.
xa: **Neither the Constitution nor any Act** defines "untouchability".
Critics: because it is undefined, **new indirect forms escape penalty** (**2 Sep 2026**).
Two angles: stigma of **ritual pollution** + practices society uses to "protect" itself from it.

133.s: Which one of the following does NOT represent a form of untouchability mentioned in the constitutional context?
o: The two-tumbler system in tea shops
Election of representatives through universal adult franchise
133.x: The two-tumbler system, denial of temple entry and residential segregation are listed forms of untouchability. Universal adult franchise is unrelated to such a practice.
133.tq: Identify the odd item by grouping concrete discriminatory practices together.
xs: **Universal adult franchise** is not a form of untouchability — option **(4)** is the answer.
Listed forms: denial of **temple entry**, separate **wells/water sources**, **two-tumbler system**, **residential segregation**, forced "polluting" work.
xa: **Manual scavenging** = "the **worst surviving symbol of untouchability**".
PCR offences include barring entry to places of **public worship** and **justifying untouchability**.
Insulting an SC member "on the ground of untouchability" = **Sec. 7(1)(d)** PCR Act.

133.s: The concept of “structural violence”, in the context of untouchability, refers to
o: violence caused exclusively by international conflict
violence committed only by armed forces
133.x: Structural violence is harm built into social structures. The concept is associated with Johan Galtung.
133.tq: Choose the precise conceptual definition rather than a literal or unrelated form of violence.
xs: **Structural violence** means **harm built into social structures** — option **(2)** is correct.
The concept is from **Johan Galtung**.
xa: UPPSC **2019** A-R: "Untouchability is the worst form of structural violence" (A) + "practised in the name of religious sanction" (R) → **both true, R explains A**.
Two angles of untouchability: **ritual pollution** + society's "protective" practices.
**Two-tumbler system** = separate tumblers in tea shops.

133.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Article — Subject
o: Article 46 — Educational and economic interests of SCs and STs
Article 342 — National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
133.x: Article 46 concerns the educational and economic interests of SCs and STs. Article 342 concerns notification of STs, Article 338A establishes the NCST, and Article 275(1) concerns grants-in-aid.
133.tq: Start with the sure Article–subject pair and eliminate swapped constitutional provisions.
xs: **Article 46** — **educational and economic interests** of SCs/STs is correctly matched: option **(1)**.
**Art. 339** is Union control over Scheduled Areas; STs are notified under **Art. 342**.
**NCST** is **Art. 338A**; grants-in-aid for ST welfare are **Art. 275(1)**.
xa: Exam angle: Art. 46 asked **three** times; Art. 17 twice.
⚠ "Untouchability abolished" = **Art. 17**.

133.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?

1. Article 15(4) and Article 16(4) — Special provisions and reservation in posts
2. Article 244(1) — Fifth Schedule administration
3. Article 244(2) — Sixth Schedule administration
4. Article 244A — Autonomous State within Assam
133.x: All four pairings are correct. Article 244A provides for an Autonomous State within Assam and was inserted by the 22nd Amendment in 1969.
133.tq: Test a sequence of closely numbered Articles by matching each with its subject.
xs: All four pairings are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**15(4)** = special provisions for SEBCs/SCs/STs; **16(4)** = reservation in posts.
**244(1)** = **Fifth Schedule** (Scheduled Areas); **244(2)** = **Sixth Schedule** (Tribal Areas).
**244A** = **Autonomous State within Assam** (**22nd Amendment, 1969**).
xa: Sixth Schedule States: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
**15(4)** was inserted by the **1st Amendment, 1951**; **16(4)** was in the original Constitution.
⚠ Scheduled Areas are declared under the **Fifth Schedule (para 6)**, not Art. 339.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Articles 15 and 16 of the Constitution:
1. Article 15(4) provides for special provisions for the advancement of SEBCs, SCs and STs.
2. Article 16(4) concerns reservation of appointments or posts for backward classes that are not adequately represented in State services.
3. Article 15(5) permits admission quotas in private educational institutions, including minority educational institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 15(5) excludes minority educational institutions from its scope.
133.tq: Separate the similar-looking reservation provisions by their beneficiaries and institutional coverage.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **15(4)** = special provisions for **SEBCs, SCs and STs** (**1st Amendment, 1951**).
Statement 2: **16(4)** = reservation for a backward class **not adequately represented** in State services.
Statement 3 is wrong: **15(5)** covers private institutions **except minority ones**.
xa: **16(4A)** = reservation in **promotion** (**77th**, **1995**).
**16(4B)** = carry-forward vacancies outside the **50% ceiling** (**81st**).
⚠ **16(4)** was in the original Constitution; **15(4)** was the first reservation clause added by amendment.

133.s:
With reference to Article 16(4B), consider the following statements:
1. It permits unfilled reserved vacancies of a year to be carried forward as a separate class.
2. Such carried-forward vacancies are not counted against the 50 per cent ceiling for that particular year.
3. It was introduced by the Eighty-First Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: All three statements are correct. Article 16(4B), introduced by the Eighty-First Amendment, deals with carry-forward reserved vacancies and their treatment outside the annual 50 per cent ceiling.
133.tq: Check the clause, its numerical effect and the amendment together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**16(4B)** treats unfilled reserved vacancies of a year as a **separate class** carried forward.
They are **not counted for the 50% ceiling** of that year; inserted by the **81st** Amendment.
xa: **Indra Sawhney (1992)** set the **50% ceiling** and confined 16(4) to initial appointment.
**M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the **77th, 81st, 82nd, 85th** Amendments but required **quantifiable data**.
⚠ **77th – 82nd – 85th** = promotion quota – relaxed marks – consequential seniority.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:
1. Article 330 relates to reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha.
2. Article 332 relates to reservation of seats in State Legislative Assemblies.
3. The Constitution provides reservation of SC/ST seats in the Rajya Sabha under Article 332.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 332 concerns State Legislative Assemblies, and there is no constitutional reservation of SC/ST seats in the Rajya Sabha.
133.tq: Reject the reversed chamber trap by comparing Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Rajya Sabha.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Art. 330** = SC/ST seats in the **Lok Sabha**; **Art. 332** = in **State Assemblies**.
Statement 3 is wrong: there is **no SC/ST reservation in the Rajya Sabha**.
xa: Seats are in proportion to population; **no separate electorates**.
**Art. 334**: time limit, now till **2030** (**104th Amendment**).
Lok Sabha SC/ST seats: **79/41** (**1971** Census) → **84/47** after the **2008** delimitation.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 334 of the Constitution:
1. It originally prescribed the reservation of seats for SCs and STs for a period of 10 years.
2. The 104th Constitutional Amendment (2019) extended this reservation up to 2035.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 334 originally fixed a 10-year time limit, later extended by amendments. Statement 2 is wrong: the 104th Amendment (2019) extended the reservation up to 2030, not 2035. Hence '1 only' (A); B, C and D all wrongly accept the 2035 date or reject the 10-year original period.
133.tq: Original period 10 years; latest extension (104th, 2019) runs to 2030.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **Art. 334** originally fixed **10 years**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **104th Amendment (2019)** extended it to **2030**, not 2035.
xa: The **104th** also ended **Anglo-Indian nomination**.
⚠ **106th (2023)** = **334A** women's reservation.

133.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Article 335 of the Constitution?
o: It provides grants-in-aid for Scheduled Areas from the Consolidated Fund of India.
It empowers State Legislatures to alter the list of Scheduled Castes.
It requires SC/ST claims in services to be considered consistently with administrative efficiency.
It establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.
133.x: Article 335 requires that the claims of SCs and STs in appointments and posts be considered consistently with the maintenance of efficiency of administration.
133.tq: Match the service-related article with its governing principle.
xs: **Art. 335**: SC/ST claims in services must be consistent with **efficiency of administration** — option **(3)** is correct.
Grants-in-aid = **275(1)**; altering the SC list = **Parliament** under **341**; NCSC = **338**.
xa: **82nd Amendment (2000)** proviso to Art. 335 allows **relaxed qualifying marks** in promotion.
Art. 335 sits in **Part XVI** (**Articles 330-342**).
⚠ G2 **2024** key said **89th** — wrong; the correct answer is the **82nd**.

133.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 339 provides for Union control over the administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes.
2. Article 339(1) provides for a Commission to report on such administration and welfare.
3. Scheduled Areas are declared under Article 339 rather than under the Fifth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: Scheduled Areas are declared under paragraph 6 of the Fifth Schedule, not under Article 339.
133.tq: Spot the wrong constitutional location while retaining the correct Union-control provision.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Art. 339** = **Union control** over Scheduled Areas and ST welfare.
Statement 2: **339(1)** = President's **Commission** to report on Scheduled Areas.
Statement 3 is wrong: Scheduled Areas are declared under the **Fifth Schedule (para 6)**, not Art. 339.
xa: Art. 339 also lets the Union give **directions to States** on ST schemes.
⚠ **NCST** is under **338A**, not 338.
**275(1)** funds ST welfare from the **Consolidated Fund of India**.

133.s: Which of the following constitutional provisions deals with reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in local bodies?
133.x: Articles 243D and 243T provide for reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in Panchayats and Municipalities, respectively.
133.tq: Distinguish local-body reservations from Parliament and State Assembly reservations.
xs: **Articles 243D and 243T** reserve SC/ST seats and chairperson posts in **Panchayats/Municipalities** — option **(3)** is correct.
**330/332** are Lok Sabha/Assemblies; **341/342** are the SC/ST lists; **244/275** concern Scheduled Areas and grants.
xa: **244** = Scheduled Areas (Fifth Schedule) and Tribal Areas (Sixth Schedule).
**275(1)** = grants-in-aid for ST welfare.
**Art. 334** time limit now till **2030**.

133.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional provisions concerning the lists of certain classes?
o: Articles 341 and 342 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342A concerns SEBC lists
Articles 338 and 338A concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342 concerns SEBC lists
Articles 339 and 340 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 341 concerns SEBC lists
Articles 330 and 332 concern SC and ST lists, while Article 342A concerns Anglo-Indian lists
133.x: Article 341 concerns the list of Scheduled Castes, Article 342 the list of Scheduled Tribes, and Article 342A concerns socially and educationally backward classes.
133.tq: Compare the neighbouring list-related articles and reject the commission and reservation provisions.
xs: **Articles 341 and 342** = SC and ST lists; **342A** = SEBC list — option **(1)** is correct.
**338/338A** are the **NCSC/NCST**; **339** is Union control; **340** is the backward classes commission; **330/332** are reserved seats.
xa: Part XVI runs from **Articles 330-342**.
**331, 333** = Anglo-Indian nomination (ended by the **104th Amendment**).
Only **Parliament by law** can include or exclude castes.

133.s: With reference to the specification of Scheduled Castes in a State or Union Territory, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Governor specifies them, subject to approval by the State Legislature.
The State Legislature specifies the Scheduled Castes by resolution.
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes specifies them by order.
The President specifies them by public notification after consulting the Governor, and Parliament alone can subsequently alter the list by law.
133.x: Under Article 341, the President specifies the Scheduled Castes for a State or Union Territory after consulting the Governor. Subsequent inclusion or exclusion can be made only by Parliament by law.
133.tq: Ask who would do this job and distinguish the initial authority from the authority competent to make later changes.
xs: The **President** specifies SCs by **public notification after consulting the Governor**; only **Parliament by law** can alter the list — option **(4)** is correct.
Neither the Governor, the State Legislature nor the NCSC specifies SCs.
xa: **SC (July 2024)** struck down **Bihar's 2015** resolution merging **Tanti-Tantwa** into the SC list.
First SC list after the Constitution: **Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950**.
⚠ "Article **344**" (CDX) is wrong — 344 is the Official Language Commission.

133.s: In Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court held that a person who has converted to Christianity from a Scheduled Caste community—
o: automatically retains Scheduled Caste status after conversion
can claim Scheduled Caste status on the recommendation of the State Government alone
can claim Scheduled Caste status only with proof of original status, bona fide reconversion and acceptance by the community
can claim Scheduled Caste status because religion is irrelevant to the SC list
133.x: The judgment held that a Christian convert cannot claim Scheduled Caste status merely on the basis of earlier caste identity. Reconversion requires proof of original SC status, bona fide reconversion and acceptance by the community.
133.tq: Use a legal scenario to test the exact conditions rather than relying on a broad generalisation.
xs: A convert can claim SC status only with **proof of original status**, **bona fide reconversion** and **community acceptance** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Chinthada Anand v State of AP (SC):** **Christian converts cannot claim SC status**.
So SC status is not automatically retained after conversion.
xa: ⚠ By contrast, **ST status is religion-neutral**.
**K.G. Balakrishnan Commission**: SC status for Dalit converts to **Christianity and Islam**, extended to **10 June 2026**.
The Chinthada Anand ruling was in the news in **Jun 2026**.

133.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the recognition of Scheduled Castes in chronological order:
A. The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used by the Simon Commission.
B. The Government of India Act, 1935 gave shape to the term.
C. The first official Scheduled Caste list was prepared.
D. The earlier expression 'Depressed Classes' was replaced in official usage.
133.x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, given statutory shape in the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first official SC list followed in 1936, after which 'Scheduled Castes' replaced the earlier 'Depressed Classes' in official usage. Hence A, B, C, D.
133.tq: Start with the earliest institutional reference and then place the statutory development and list in sequence.
xs: Correct order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
A: the **Simon Commission** first used "Scheduled Castes"; B: the **GoI Act 1935** gave it shape.
C: the **first official SC list** came in **1936**; D: "Scheduled Castes" then replaced the earlier "**Depressed Classes**".
xa: First SC list after the Constitution: **Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950**.
**Census 2011**: **1,241** caste groups notified as SCs.
⚠ The FIRSTs table credits the **GoI Act 1935** with first using the term.

133.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional position regarding Scheduled Tribes?
o: Scheduled Tribe status is decided exclusively by the State Legislature.
Scheduled Tribe status is religion-neutral and the list for a State or Union Territory is specified under Article 342.
Scheduled Tribe status is confined to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists.
Scheduled Tribe status is determined by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes without Presidential notification.
133.x: Article 342 concerns the specification of Scheduled Tribes, and ST status is not restricted by religion.
133.tq: Combine the correct Article with the key SC–ST distinction instead of choosing a familiar but misplaced authority.
xs: ST status is **religion-neutral** and the list is specified under **Article 342** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not decided by the State Legislature or the NCST; the **President** notifies and **Parliament** alone alters.
xa: ⚠ For SCs, **Christian converts cannot claim SC status** (**Chinthada Anand**).
**366(25)** defines Scheduled Tribes.

133.s: Which sequence correctly represents the successive extensions of SC/ST reservation in legislatures under Article 334?
133.x: The listed extensions were made through the 8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th and 104th Amendments; the 104th extended the reservation up to 2030.
133.tq: Track the reservation-extension series separately from promotion and service-related amendments.
xs: Correct sequence: **8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th, 104th Amendments** — option **(1)**.
xa: **95th (2009)** took it from **60 → 70 years**.
⚠ **104th** = **2030** + end of **Anglo-Indian nomination**; **106th** = women's reservation (**334A**).

133.s:
With reference to reservation of seats for SCs and STs in legislatures, consider the following statements:
1. The number of reserved seats is related to the population of the respective communities.
2. Separate electorates are provided for SC and ST voters.
3. All voters in the constituency elect the representative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Reserved seats are provided in proportion to population, but there are no separate electorates. All voters in the constituency participate in electing the representative.
133.tq: Trap the reversal between reserved seats and separate electorates.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: seats are reserved **in proportion to population**.
Statement 2 is wrong: there are **no separate electorates**.
Statement 3: **all voters** in the constituency elect the representative.
xa: **Art. 330** = Lok Sabha; **Art. 332** = Assemblies.
AP Assembly: **29 SC + 7 ST** of **175**.
AP SC Lok Sabha seats: **Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor, Tirupati**.

133.s: The number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha was refixed on the basis of the
o: 1971 Census and 1981 Census through the 42nd and 44th Amendments
1981 Census and 1991 Census through the 73rd and 74th Amendments
1991 Census and 2001 Census through the 84th and 87th Amendments
2001 Census and 2011 Census through the 87th and 91st Amendments
133.x: The 84th Amendment refixed the seat numbers on the basis of the 1991 Census, and the 87th Amendment did so on the basis of the 2001 Census.
133.tq: Match the Census years with the corresponding amendment numbers.
xs: Seats were refixed on the **1991 Census** (**84th**) and the **2001 Census** (**87th**) — option **(3)** is correct.
The **73rd/74th** are local-body amendments; the **42nd/44th** are not listed for seat refixing.
xa: Lok Sabha SC/ST seats: **79/41** (**1971** Census) → **84/47** after the **2008** delimitation on **Census 2001**.
**51st Amendment (1984)**: ST seats for **Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal, Mizoram**.
⚠ **85th** = consequential seniority, not seat refixing.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reserved seats in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Of AP's 25 Lok Sabha seats, 4 are reserved for SCs and 1 for STs.
2. Of AP's 175 Assembly seats, 7 are reserved for SCs and 29 for STs.
3. Araku is the ST-reserved Lok Sabha constituency of AP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statement 1 is correct: 4 SC + 1 ST of 25 Lok Sabha seats. Statement 2 is wrong: the Assembly has 29 SC and 7 ST seats of 175 (the numbers are reversed). Statement 3 is correct: Araku is the ST seat. Hence B; A omits statement 3, while C and D wrongly include statement 2.
133.tq: AP: Lok Sabha 4+1 (Araku); Assembly 29 SC + 7 ST - watch for reversed numbers.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: AP Lok Sabha = **4 SC + 1 ST** of **25**.
Statement 2 is wrong: AP Assembly has **29 SC + 7 ST** of **175** (numbers reversed).
Statement 3: **Araku** is the ST Lok Sabha seat.
xa: AP SC Lok Sabha seats: **Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor, Tirupati**.
AP SC population: **84.69 lakh** = **17.08%**.
National: **84 SC, 47 ST** Lok Sabha seats after the **2008** delimitation.

133.s: The 51st Constitutional Amendment, 1984, provided for ST seats in the Lok Sabha for
o: Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram
133.x: The 51st Amendment, 1984, provided ST representation in the Lok Sabha for Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.
133.tq: Test the exact four-State grouping and avoid substituting neighbouring north-eastern States.
xs: The **51st Amendment (1984)** gave ST Lok Sabha seats to **Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram** — option **(3)** is correct.
Assam, Tripura, Manipur, Sikkim and Goa are not in the 51st Amendment list.
xa: Sixth Schedule (**244(2)**) States: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
**244A** = Autonomous State within Assam (**22nd Amendment, 1969**).

133.s: The proviso to Article 335 relating to relaxation of qualifying marks in promotion was enabled by which Constitutional Amendment?
133.x: The Eighty-Second Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 inserted the proviso to Article 335 permitting relaxation of qualifying marks and standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
133.tq: Separate the closely placed reservation amendments by their precise subject.
xs: The **82nd Amendment (2000)** added the proviso to **Art. 335** allowing **relaxed qualifying marks** in promotion — option **(3) Eighty-Second** is correct.
**77th (1995)** = 16(4A) promotion quota; **81st** = 16(4B) carry-forward; **85th** = consequential seniority.
⚠ G2 **2024** circulated key said **89th** — that is the **NCSC-NCST bifurcation** amendment.
xa: **M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd, 85th but required **quantifiable data**.
⚠ **77th – 82nd – 85th** = promotion quota – relaxed marks – consequential seniority.

133.s: The 85th Constitutional Amendment is associated with
o: relaxation in qualifying marks under Article 335
backlog vacancies being treated as a separate class
consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995
reservation of seats for STs in the Lok Sabha
133.x: The 85th Amendment provided consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995.
133.tq: Use the effective date and the phrase “consequential seniority” as the decisive identifiers.
xs: The **85th Amendment** gave **consequential seniority** in promotion under **16(4A)**, w.e.f. **17 June 1995** — option **(3)** is correct.
Relaxed marks = **82nd**; backlog as a separate class = **81st** (16(4B)); ST Lok Sabha seats = **51st**.
xa: The 85th is dated **2001** (IYB lists **2002**).
**16(4A)** itself was inserted by the **77th (1995)**.
**M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the 85th with the **quantifiable data** condition.

133.s: Article 16(4A), permitting reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, was inserted by the 77th Amendment (1995) mainly in response to which judicial position?
o: Indra Sawhney (1992) confining reservation under Article 16(4) to initial appointment
E.V. Chinnaiah (2004) treating SCs as a homogeneous class
133.x: Indra Sawhney (1992) held that reservation under Article 16(4) applies only at initial appointment, not promotion; the 77th Amendment (1995) responded by inserting Article 16(4A). M. Nagaraj came later and upheld the 77th; Chinnaiah concerns SC sub-classification; Janhit Abhiyan concerns EWS.
133.tq: 77th = 16(4A) promotion, answer to Indra Sawhney.
xs: The **77th Amendment (1995)** responded to **Indra Sawhney (1992)**, which confined **Art. 16(4)** to **initial appointment** — option **(1)** is correct.
**M. Nagaraj (2006)** came later and upheld the 77th; **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)** concerns SC sub-classification.
xa: Indra Sawhney also set the **50% ceiling**.
**85th** added consequential seniority w.e.f. **17 June 1995**.
**Davinder Singh (2024)** overruled **Chinnaiah**.

133.s:
Consider the following statements about the Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi (MRPS):
1. It was founded in 1994 by Manda Krishna Madiga.
2. It was founded at Karamchedu in Guntur district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: Statement 1 is correct: Manda Krishna Madiga founded the MRPS in 1994. Statement 2 is wrong: it was founded at Eedumudi in Prakasam district, not Karamchedu. Hence A; B and C wrongly accept Karamchedu, and D wrongly rejects statement 1.
133.tq: MRPS: 1994, Manda Krishna Madiga, Eedumudi (Prakasam).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **MRPS** was founded in **1994** by **Manda Krishna Madiga**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was founded at **Eedumudi**, **Prakasam** district — not Karamchedu.
xa: ⚠ **Karamchedu** (**1985**) was a massacre of Madiga Dalits (then Prakasam, now Bapatla).
MRPS alleged **Mala** dominance of the **15%** SC quota.
**Tsundur** (**1991**) was in **Guntur**.

133.s: What was the principal demand of the Madiga Dandora movement?
o: Categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups
133.x: Madiga Dandora demanded categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups, or reservation within reservation.
133.tq: Distinguish reservation sub-categorisation from general reservation demands.
xs: **Madiga Dandora** demanded **A-B-C-D categorisation** of AP's SC reservation — option **(3)** is correct.
It was the **MRPS** movement (**1994**) led by **Manda Krishna Madiga**.
xa: **Ramachandra Raju Commission (1996)**: **A** (Relli), **B** (Madiga), **C** (Mala), **D** (Adi-Andhra).
**AP Act 2000** fell in **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)**; **Davinder Singh (2024)** allowed sub-classification.
**Telangana** first implemented SC sub-categorisation (**3** groups, **April 2025**).

133.s: The Madiga Dandora movement alleged that which community dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota?
133.x: The movement alleged that the Mala community disproportionately dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota, leading to the demand for a separate share.
133.tq: Discriminate between closely related communities in a reservation controversy.
xs: The movement alleged **Mala** dominance of the **15%** SC quota — option **(1)** is correct.
**Madiga** were the complainants; **Relli** and **Adi-Andhra** were groups **A** and **D**.
xa: ⚠ **A – B – C – D** = **Relli – Madiga – Mala – Adi-Andhra**.
**AP** was first to sub-categorise SCs **by law** (**2000**); **Punjab 1975** by circular.
**Usha Mehra Commission (2007-08)** recommended amending **Art. 341** to let States sub-categorise.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission:
1. It recommended grouping the Scheduled Castes of Andhra Pradesh into four categories.
2. The four categories were designated A, B, C and D.
3. It recommended grouping Madigas under Category B and Malas under Category C.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: All three statements are correct. The Commission recommended four groups: A comprising Relli and others, B Madiga, C Mala and D Adi-Andhra.
133.tq: Check the complete composition of a classification rather than recognising only its headline.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission (1996)** grouped AP's SCs into **four** categories, **A, B, C, D**.
**B = Madiga**, **C = Mala** (with **A = Relli** and others, **D = Adi-Andhra**).
xa: It was implemented by the **AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000**.
The Act fell in **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)**.
The demand came from **Madiga Dandora** (**MRPS, 1994**).

133.s: Which State was the first to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by legislation, after the Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission process?
133.x: Andhra Pradesh became the first State to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by statute, through the AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000 (Punjab had done so earlier, in 1975, only by an executive circular).
133.tq: Test a superlative linked to a specific legislative milestone.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** was first to sub-categorise SCs **by law** (**AP Act 2000**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Punjab** did so earlier (**1975**) only **by circular**.
**Telangana** was first to **implement** sub-categorisation after **Davinder Singh** (**April 2025**).
xa: The Act followed the **Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission** (**1996**).
It was struck down in **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)**.
⚠ **A – B – C – D** = **Relli – Madiga – Mala – Adi-Andhra**.

133.s:
With reference to E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court treated Scheduled Castes as a single homogeneous class under Article 341.
2. It struck down the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Caste (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000.
3. It held that sub-classification did not interfere with the Presidential list under Article 341.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Chinnaiah treated Scheduled Castes as a homogeneous class and struck down the State Act; it regarded sub-classification as interfering with the Article 341 list, so statement 3 is false.
133.tq: Find the statement that reverses the court’s holding.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Chinnaiah (2004)** held SCs a **single homogeneous class** under **Art. 341**.
Statement 2: it struck down the **AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it held sub-classification **interferes with the Art. 341 list** and violates **Art. 14**.
xa: Some notes date the Act **2005**.
**Davinder Singh (2024)**, **7-judge bench, 6:1**, overruled Chinnaiah.
**Usha Mehra Commission (2007-08)** recommended amending **Art. 341**.

133.s: The Usha Mehra Commission, constituted in 2007–08, recommended which of the following?
o: Amending Article 341 to enable States to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes
Including all Other Backward Classes in the Scheduled Caste list
133.x: The Usha Mehra Commission recommended amendment of Article 341 so that States could undertake sub-categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
133.tq: Match a commission with its specific recommendation.
xs: The **Usha Mehra Commission (2007-08)** recommended **amending Art. 341** to let **States sub-categorise SCs** — option **(1)** is correct.
It came after **Chinnaiah (2004)** blocked State sub-classification.
xa: **Davinder Singh (2024)** later held sub-classification **permissible** under **Arts. 14, 15, 16**.
Only **Parliament by law** can alter the SC list under **Art. 341**.
**Telangana** implemented **3** groups in **April 2025**.

133.s: In State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024), the seven-judge Bench held that sub-classification within Scheduled Castes is permissible when the class is not homogeneous. What was the majority ratio?
133.x: The seven-judge Bench permitted sub-classification by a majority of 6:1, overruling the position taken in E.V. Chinnaiah.
133.tq: Test the exact judicial majority using closely spaced numerical distractors.
xs: **Davinder Singh (2024)** was decided **6:1** by a **7-judge bench** — option **(1)** is correct.
It held sub-classification within SCs **permissible** under **Arts. 14, 15, 16** where the class is not homogeneous.
It **overruled Chinnaiah (2004)**.
xa: AP angle: **Madiga Dandora** and the **2000** AP Act started the debate that ended in Davinder Singh.
**Telangana became the first State** to implement it (**April 2025**).
The Centre opposed an **income-based creamy layer** in SC/ST quotas (**7 Aug 2026**).

133.s: Which case upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Constitutional Amendments, subject to the State showing quantifiable data on specified conditions?
o: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh
133.x: M. Nagaraj upheld the four constitutional amendments but required quantifiable data concerning backwardness, inadequate representation and administrative efficiency.
133.tq: Associate a cluster of constitutional amendments with the case that examined them.
xs: **M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the **77th, 81st, 82nd, 85th** Amendments — option **(3)** is correct.
But the State must show **quantifiable data** on **backwardness**, **inadequate representation** and **administrative efficiency**.
**Davinder Singh** and **Chinnaiah** concern **SC sub-classification**.
xa: ⚠ **77th – 82nd – 85th** = promotion quota – relaxed marks – consequential seniority.
**81st** = **16(4B)** carry-forward vacancies.
**Indra Sawhney (1992)** set the **50% ceiling**.

133.s: Which State became the first to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after the Davinder Singh judgment?
133.x: Telangana became the first State to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after Davinder Singh, with three groups in April 2025.
133.tq: Distinguish the State that enacted the earlier framework from the State that implemented the post-2024 classification.
xs: **Telangana** was first to implement SC sub-categorisation after **Davinder Singh** — option **(1)** is correct.
It made **3** groups in **April 2025**.
**AP** was first by law (**2000**), and **Punjab** first by circular (**1975**) — both before the judgment.
xa: **Davinder Singh (2024)** was decided **6:1**.
AP's **Ramachandra Raju Commission (1996)** made **four** groups.

133.s: The original form of Article 338 provided for—
o: a non-statutory multi-member commission appointed by the State Governments
a Special Officer designated as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
a Parliamentary committee for monitoring reservations
a separate National Commission for Scheduled Castes and a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
133.x: Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer, known as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, to investigate safeguards and report to the President.
133.tq: Track institutional evolution by identifying the original arrangement before later commissions were created.
xs: Original **Art. 338** provided a **Special Officer** (Commissioner for SCs and STs) — option **(2)** is correct.
He **investigated safeguards** and **reported to the President**.
Separate NCSC and NCST came only with the **89th Amendment (2003)**.
xa: **1978 Resolution**: non-statutory multi-member Commission for SCs and STs; modified in **1987**.
**1990**: the joint commission became **constitutional** (**Art. 338**).
**NCST** from **19 Feb 2004**.

133.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding the status of office-bearers of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
133.x: The Chairperson of the NCST has Cabinet rank, the Vice-Chairperson has Minister of State rank, and members have Secretary rank. Therefore, describing the Chairperson as having Minister of State rank is incorrect.
133.tq: Find the single reversed rank in a hierarchy-based matching question.
xs: **Chairperson — Minister of State rank** is NOT correct — option **(4)**; the NCST Chairperson has **Cabinet rank**.
**Vice-Chairperson** = **MoS rank**; **members** = **Secretary rank**.
xa: Composition: Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson + **three** members.
The **President** fixes tenure and service conditions.
The Commission has **civil-court powers** while inquiring.

133.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commissions for SCs and STs:
1. In 1990 the joint national commission for SCs and STs became a constitutional body under Article 338.
2. The 89th Amendment (2003) bifurcated it into the NCSC (Article 338) and the NCST (Article 338A).
3. The Commissions submit their reports to the Prime Minister, who lays them before Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the joint commission became constitutional in 1990, and the 89th Amendment (2003) split it into the NCSC under Article 338 and the NCST under new Article 338A. Statement 3 is wrong: the Commissions report to the President, and the reports are laid before Parliament. Hence A; B, C and D wrongly include statement 3 or drop statement 1.
133.tq: 89th = bifurcation; reports go to the President.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: in **1990** the joint commission became **constitutional** under **Art. 338**.
Statement 2: the **89th Amendment (2003)** split it into **NCSC (338)** and **NCST (338A)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: they report to the **President**, and reports are laid before Parliament.
xa: Functions: investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints, **advise on planning**.
Powers: **civil-court powers** while inquiring.
Original Art. 338 had a **Special Officer**.

133.s: What does Article 338(9) of the Constitution provide?
o: It empowers the President to create State Commissions for Scheduled Castes
It requires the Union and every State to consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on all major policy matters affecting SCs
It gives the NCSC power to amend the Scheduled Caste list
It provides grants-in-aid to State SC Commissions
133.x: Article 338(9) obliges the Union and State Governments to consult the NCSC on major policy matters affecting SCs. It does not empower the President to create State commissions (a trap in CDCA); State SC Commissions are created by State law. The SC list is altered only by Parliament under Article 341, and grants-in-aid are under Article 275(1) for ST welfare.
133.tq: 338(9) = duty to consult NCSC; State SC Commissions come from State law.
xs: **Art. 338(9)** requires the **Union and every State to consult the NCSC** on major policy matters — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ CDCA says 338(9) lets the President create State commissions — **wrong**; State SC Commissions are made by **State law**.
The SC list is altered only by **Parliament** (**Art. 341**); grants-in-aid are **Art. 275(1)**.
xa: NCSC and NCST have **civil-court powers** while inquiring.
AP has a statutory **State SC Commission** (chairman **K.S. Jawahar**).

133.s: Which of the following is NOT an offence covered by the Protection of Civil Rights law in relation to untouchability?
o: Providing reservation in public employment to an eligible Scheduled Caste candidate
Denying access to shops, hotels and places of entertainment
Barring entry to a place of public worship
Justifying untouchability on religious or traditional grounds
133.x: The Protection of Civil Rights law covers practices such as denial of temple entry, justification of untouchability and denial of access to public facilities. Providing reservation in public employment is not one of the listed offences.
133.tq: Find the item outside the statutory list rather than choosing a familiar Scheduled Caste-related provision.
xs: **Providing reservation** to an eligible SC candidate is not a PCR offence — option **(1)** is the answer.
PCR offences: barring entry to **public worship**, **justifying untouchability**, denying access to **shops, hotels, entertainment**.
xa: Insulting an SC member "on the ground of untouchability" = **Sec. 7(1)(d)**.
The PCR Act was the **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955**, renamed in **1976**.
Conviction disqualifies from elections under **Sec. 8, RPA 1951**.

133.s: A conviction for an offence relating to untouchability results in disqualification from contesting elections under
o: Section 7 of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1976
Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
133.x: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides disqualification from contesting elections upon conviction for untouchability offences.
133.tq: Match the consequence with the correct statutory source, not with the constitutional article governing reservation.
xs: Disqualification comes under **Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Sec. 7(1)(d)** of the PCR Act defines an offence (insulting an SC member), not disqualification.
**Art. 244** = Scheduled Areas; **Art. 330** = Lok Sabha seats.
xa: Only **Parliament** can prescribe punishment for Art. 17 offences (**Art. 35(a)(ii)**).
Only **24 cases** were registered under the PCR Act in **2023**; **97%** pendency.

133.s: Under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Rules, which one of the following is correctly stated?
o: Police investigations must ordinarily be completed within 60 days.
The Rules were framed in 1989 and the Act enacted in 1995.
Monitoring committees are constituted only at the national level.
Special courts are prohibited from hearing atrocity cases.
133.x: The PoA Act was enacted in 1989 and the Rules were framed in 1995; the framework includes special courts and State and district vigilance and monitoring committees, with a 60-day limit for police investigation.
133.tq: Check the statutory timeline and institutional provisions without reversing Act and Rules.
xs: Police investigation has a **60-day** limit — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Act** is of **1989** and the **Rules** of **1995** (option 2 reverses them).
The Rules set up **State and district vigilance and monitoring committees** and **special courts**.
xa: The **PCR** and **PoA** Acts are overseen by the **Dept of Social Justice**.
AP gives **enhanced monetary relief** and **free legal aid** to PoA victims.
Vigilance committees **meet irregularly** (enforcement gap).

133.s: Which combination contains the principal measures identified for abolishing untouchability?
133.x: Untouchability can be addressed through legislation, education and public awareness.
133.tq: Match the social problem with the three-part reform approach.
xs: Untouchability can be abolished through **laws, education and public awareness** — option **(2)** is correct (UPPSC **1992**).
The key marked **1, 2 and 3** — all three measures together.
xa: Laws: **PCR Act** and **PoA Act 1989**.
Economic measures: **NSFDC**, **NSKFDC**, **PM-DAKSH**, **VCF-SC**.
Undefined untouchability lets **new indirect forms escape penalty**.

133.s:
Which of the following institutions or programmes is correctly associated with economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities?
1. NSFDC — SCs below the poverty line
2. NSKFDC — Support related to sanitation workers
3. PM-DAKSH — Skill development
4. VCF-SC — Economic support for SCs
Select the correct answer using the code below.
133.x: NSFDC, NSKFDC, PM-DAKSH and VCF-SC are all listed among economic empowerment measures, with the associations stated in the question.
133.tq: Match each programme with its target or function before selecting the code.
xs: All four associations are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**NSFDC** = SCs below the poverty line; **NSKFDC** implements **NAMASTE** for sanitation workers.
**PM-DAKSH** and **VCF-SC** are also listed economic measures.
xa: **SRMS** (since **2007**) gave a one-time **₹40,000**.

133.s:
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 provides for which of the following?
1. Prohibition of employing manual scavengers
2. Prohibition of cleaning sewers and septic tanks without protective gear
3. Identification and rehabilitation of affected persons
4. Legalisation of dry latrines under regulated conditions
Select the correct answer using the code below.
133.x: The 2013 Act prohibits manual scavenging, unsafe cleaning of sewers and septic tanks, and requires identification and rehabilitation. It does not legalise dry latrines.
133.tq: Spot the false legalization claim among the Act’s prohibitory and rehabilitative provisions.
xs: Provisions 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
The **2013 Act** bans **manual scavengers** and **manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks** without protective gear.
It requires **identification and rehabilitation**.
Provision 4 is wrong: the earlier **1993** Act already prohibited **dry latrines**.
xa: **58,000** manual scavengers identified, but only **2,652** projects approved.
**498** sewer/septic deaths from **2019** to **June 2026**.

133.s: Manual scavenging has been described as the:
133.x: Manual scavenging is described as the “worst surviving symbol of untouchability.”
133.tq: Recall the precise evaluative phrase used for the practice.
xs: Manual scavenging is "the **worst surviving symbol of untouchability**" — option **(2)** is correct.
It is forced "polluting" work, one of the listed forms of untouchability.
xa: **Bezwada Wilson**'s **Safai Karmachari Andolan** campaigns against it (Magsaysay **2016**).
The **2013 Act** bans manual scavengers and unsafe sewer cleaning.
**NAMASTE** aims at **zero sanitation deaths**.

133.s:
Which of the following statements about NAMASTE is correct?
1. It is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
2. Its stated goal is zero sanitation deaths.
3. ₹349.70 crore was allocated for 2023–24 to 2025–26.
4. It provides a training stipend of ₹3,000 and Ayushman Bharat coverage.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
133.x: All four statements correctly describe NAMASTE: its two ministries, zero sanitation deaths goal, allocation of ₹349.70 crore, and the stated stipend and health coverage.
133.tq: Verify ministry, objective, financial allocation and beneficiary benefits as one scheme profile.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**MoSJE + MoHUA**; goal **zero sanitation deaths**.
**₹349.70 crore** for **2023-24 to 2025-26**; stipend **₹3,000** and **Ayushman Bharat** cover.
xa: Implemented by **NSKFDC**.
Profiling: **90,915** sewer/septic workers and **1.3 lakh** waste pickers.
**SRMS** (**2007**) is subsumed in NAMASTE.

133.s: According to reports associated with the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, which one of the following is NOT listed as a cause of caste atrocities?
133.x: Land alienation, bonded labour, indebtedness and non-payment of wages are listed causes. Religious causes are not included in the stated list.
133.tq: Find the excluded item in a familiar list rather than selecting a general social factor.
xs: **Religious causes** are NOT listed — option **(1)** (MPPSC **2015** trap).
The **National Commission for SCs & STs (1990)** listed **land alienation**, **bonded labour**, **indebtedness**, **non-payment of wages**.
xa: CDX factors: **caste hierarchy**, **upper-caste dominance**, **rising Dalit activism**, **political interference**.
NCRB (**2017**) added the head "forced to leave residence / facing **social boycott**".

133.s:
Which of the following factors has been identified as contributing to caste atrocities?
1. Caste hierarchy
2. Upper-caste dominance
3. Rising activism among Dalits
4. Political interference
Select the correct answer using the code below.
133.x: All four factors—caste hierarchy, upper-caste dominance, rising Dalit activism and political interference—are identified as contributing factors.
133.tq: Check whether all listed structural and political factors belong to the same causal group.
xs: All four factors are listed — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Caste hierarchy**, **upper-caste dominance**, **rising activism** among Dalits and **political interference** (CDX).
xa: The **1990** Commission listed land alienation, bonded labour, indebtedness, non-payment of wages.
Dalit labourers **hide complaints** for fear of boycott.
**UP** had **57** social-boycott cases in **2017**.

133.s: Karamchedu, Tsundur and Khairlanji are respectively associated with which States?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra
Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
133.x: Karamchedu and Tsundur occurred in Andhra Pradesh, while Khairlanji occurred in Maharashtra.
133.tq: Use location pairing to distinguish closely related atrocity incidents.
xs: **Karamchedu** — AP; **Tsundur** — AP; **Khairlanji** — **Maharashtra**: option **(1)** is correct.
**Karamchedu** (**17 Jul 1985**): then Prakasam, now Bapatla; **Tsundur** (**6 Aug 1991**): Guntur.
**Khairlanji** (**29 Sep 2006**): Bhandara district.
xa: Karamchedu **sparked the independent Dalit movement**.
**Hathras** (**2020**, UP): SC entrusted monitoring to the **Allahabad HC**.

133.s: Karamchedu incident is associated with which one of the following descriptions?
o: It resulted in monitoring by the Allahabad High Court.
It involved four members of a Dalit family in Bhandara district.
It led to the creation of the NCRB crime head for social boycott.
It sparked the independent Dalit movement.
133.x: The Karamchedu incident of 1985, in which Madiga Dalits were killed by dominant-caste landlords, sparked the independent Dalit movement.
133.tq: Identify the distinctive consequence attached to the incident.
xs: **Karamchedu** **sparked the independent Dalit movement** — option **(4)** is correct.
Madiga Dalits were killed by dominant-caste landlords (**17 Jul 1985**).
Allahabad HC monitoring = **Hathras**; Bhandara = **Khairlanji**.
xa: APP gives **1985**; CDX prints **1982**.
Then Prakasam district, now **Bapatla**.

133.s: In relation to the Hathras case, the Supreme Court entrusted monitoring to the:
133.x: In the Hathras case, the Supreme Court entrusted monitoring to the Allahabad High Court.
133.tq: Identify the authority entrusted with a specific monitoring responsibility.
xs: In **Hathras** (**2020**, UP), the SC entrusted monitoring to the **Allahabad High Court** — option **(3)** is correct.
The monitoring was not given to the NHRC or any other High Court.
xa: **Khairlanji** (**2006**) = Maharashtra.
**Karamchedu** (**1985**) and **Tsundur** (**1991**) = AP.
NCRB **2017** crime head: social boycott.

133.s: In 2017, the NCRB added a separate crime head for SCs relating to:
o: Being forced to leave residence or facing social boycott
Denial of reservation in educational institutions
133.x: The 2017 NCRB crime head covered persons forced to leave their residence or facing social boycott. Uttar Pradesh recorded 57 cases under this head that year.
133.tq: Recall the exact wording of a newly introduced crime category.
xs: The **2017** NCRB head: SCs **forced to leave residence / facing social boycott** — option **(1)** is correct.
**UP** recorded **57** cases that year.
xa: Dalit labourers depend on dominant-caste landowners and **hide complaints** for fear of boycott.
⚠ **Mysore HC**: social boycott of a few individuals is **not** untouchability under Art. 17.

133.s: The first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State was established by Bhagya Reddy Varma under the name
133.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma established Jagan Mitra Mandali in 1906, described as the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State.
133.tq: Match the organisation with its founder and year.
xs: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** founded **Jagan Mitra Mandali (1906)**, the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State — option **(2)** is correct.
His **Adi Hindu Social Service League** came later (originally **Manya Sangham**, **1911**).
**Harijan Sevak Sangh** was Gandhi's (**1932**), which Varma **criticised as paternalistic**.
xa: **Adi Andhra** (paper) = **Didla Pullaiah**; **Nava Jeevan** = **Undru Subbarao**.
The **Adi-Andhra movement** (**1910s-30s**) claimed Dalits were Andhra's original inhabitants.

133.s:
Consider the following statements about the Adi-Andhra movement:
1. Its adherents claimed that Dalits were the original inhabitants of Andhra.
2. It demanded access to education, temples and tanks.
3. It was active mainly between the 1950s and the 1970s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the movement claimed Dalits were Andhra's original inhabitants and demanded education, temple and tank access. Statement 3 is wrong: it was active in the 1910s-30s. Hence A; B, C and D all include the wrong period.
133.tq: Adi-Andhra = 1910s-30s, 'original inhabitants' claim.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: it claimed Dalits were the **original inhabitants of Andhra**.
Statement 2: it demanded **education, temple and tank access**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it was active in the **1910s-30s**.
xa: **Siddhantam Temple Entry** (**1933**, Krishna district) was one of the earliest in Andhra.
Andhra Dalit papers: **Adi Andhra** (Didla Pullaiah), **Nava Jeevan** (Undru Subbarao).

133.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gandhi used the term ‘Harijan’.
2. B.R. Ambedkar preferred the terms ‘Dalit’ and ‘Scheduled Caste’ and emphasised legal-constitutional remedies.
3. Bhagya Reddy Varma supported the Harijan Sevak Sangh without criticism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Bhagya Reddy Varma criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as paternalistic, making statement 3 incorrect.
133.tq: Use the contrasting approaches of major reformers and identify the reversed statement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Gandhi** used "**Harijan**" (moral persuasion, reform from within).
Statement 2: **Ambedkar** preferred "**Dalit**"/SC and **legal-constitutional remedies**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** **criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh** as paternalistic.
xa: Ambedkar sought **annihilation of caste**.
Gandhi called untouchability "**a blot on Hinduism**".
**Periyar**: political freedom is meaningless without social equality.

133.s: Which one of the following combinations relating to Vaikom Satyagraha is correct?
o: Travancore — T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon — 1924–25
133.x: Vaikom Satyagraha took place in Travancore in 1924–25 and was organised by T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon, with K. Kelappan also associated with it.
133.tq: Start with the sure location and verify the corresponding leaders and date.
xs: **Travancore — T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon — 1924-25** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mahad** was Ambedkar's (**1927**); **Nashik** = Kalaram (**1930**); **Krishna district** = Siddhantam (**1933**).
xa: **K. Kelappan** also took part; **Sree Narayana Guru** supported it.
**Periyar** was jailed in it.
⚠ **Mahad** = water (**20 Mar 1927**); **Kalaram** = temple (**1930**).

133.s: The Mahad Chavdar Tank Satyagraha was led by B.R. Ambedkar to assert the right of Dalits to
o: Draw water from a public tank
Use roads around the Vaikom temple
133.x: The Mahad Satyagraha, held at Mahad in Maharashtra on 20 March 1927, asserted Dalits’ right to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank.
133.tq: Identify a movement from its precise immediate objective.
xs: **Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha** asserted Dalits' right to **draw water from a public tank** — option **(2)** is correct.
Led by **Ambedkar** on **20 Mar 1927** at Mahad (Maharashtra).
xa: **Centenary (2026-27)** began **20 Mar 2026**.
**Manusmriti Dahan**: **25 Dec 1927**.
⚠ **Kalaram** = temple entry (**1930**, Nashik).

133.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
133.x: The Siddhantam Temple Entry movement took place in Krishna district in 1933 and was one of the earliest such movements in Andhra. The other options confuse its details with those of other movements.
133.tq: Check location and date together to expose swapped movement details.
xs: **Siddhantam Temple Entry — 1933 — Krishna district** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was led by Congress/Gandhian leaders, one of the **earliest in Andhra**.
**Kalaram** was **1930** at **Nashik**; **Mahad** was **1927** in Maharashtra.
xa: **Vaikom** (**1924-25**) was in Travancore.
AP angle also includes **Jashuva**'s **Gabbilam** and **Jogin** rehabilitation.

133.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Jagan Mitra Mandali — Bhagya Reddy Varma
Harijan Sevak Sangh — Manda Krishna Madiga
133.x: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was associated with Gandhi, whereas Manda Krishna Madiga led the Madiga Dandora movement.
133.tq: Use a nearby movement leader as the distractor and identify the swapped association.
xs: **Harijan Sevak Sangh — Manda Krishna Madiga** is NOT correct — option **(4)**; the Sangh was **Gandhi**'s (**1932**).
**Manda Krishna Madiga** founded the **MRPS** (**1994**, Madiga Dandora).
The rest are right: **Gabbilam** — Jashuva; **Jagan Mitra Mandali** — Bhagya Reddy Varma; **Safai Karmachari Andolan** — Bezwada Wilson.
xa: MRPS was founded at **Eedumudi**, **Prakasam** district.
Bhagya Reddy Varma criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as **paternalistic**.

133.s:
With reference to the views of Mahatma Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar, consider the following statements:
1. Gandhi regarded untouchability as a blot on Hinduism.
2. Gandhi coined the term ‘Harijan’.
3. Ambedkar advocated legal-constitutional rights and annihilation of caste.
4. Ambedkar supported reform of caste only from within Hindu society.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: Gandhi is associated with reform from within, whereas Ambedkar advocated legal-constitutional rights and annihilation of caste.
133.tq: Separate the contrasting approaches of Gandhi and Ambedkar; the reversed attribution is the trap.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: **Gandhi** called untouchability "**a blot on Hinduism**" and coined **'Harijan'**.
Statement 3: **Ambedkar** sought **legal-constitutional remedies** and **annihilation of caste**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **reform from within** was **Gandhi**'s approach, not Ambedkar's.
xa: Gandhi relied on **moral persuasion**; founded **Harijan Sevak Sangh** (**1932**).
**Annihilation of Caste** includes a rebuke of Gandhi's approach.

133.s: “I was born a Hindu, but I will not die a Hindu” was declared by B. R. Ambedkar at:
133.x: B. R. Ambedkar made this declaration at Yeola in 1935.
133.tq: Discriminate between a leader’s quotation, place and year.
xs: Ambedkar declared "I was born a Hindu... but I will not die a Hindu" at **Yeola** in **1935** — option **(4)** is correct.
It sits with his other stands: caste is "**a division of labourers**" and **Dalit** over 'Harijan'.
xa: He wrote **Annihilation of Caste** in **1936**.
**Kalaram Temple Entry**: **1930**, Nashik.
**Mahad Satyagraha**: **20 Mar 1927**.

133.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Poona Pact
B. Ambedkar’s declaration at Yeola
C. Karamchedu incident
D. Tsundur incident
133.x: The Poona Pact took place in 1932, the Yeola declaration in 1935, Karamchedu in 1985 and Tsundur in 1991.
133.tq: Fix the earliest two events first, then place the incidents by year.
xs: Correct order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Poona Pact** (**1932**) → **Yeola** declaration (**1935**).
xa: The **Harijan Sevak Sangh** was founded in **1932** after the Poona Pact.
**Khairlanji** (Maharashtra) came in **2006**.
Karamchedu **sparked the independent Dalit movement**.

133.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha led by B.R. Ambedkar was held on 20 March 1927.
2. Its centenary observance began on 20 March 2026.
3. Ambedkar burnt the Manusmriti at Nashik during the Kalaram Temple Entry movement of 1930.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
133.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Mahad Satyagraha took place on 20 March 1927 and its centenary (2026-27) began on 20 March 2026. Statement 3 is wrong: the Manusmriti Dahan was on 25 December 1927, separate from the 1930 Kalaram Temple Entry at Nashik. Hence A; B, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
133.tq: Mahad 20 Mar 1927; Manusmriti Dahan 25 Dec 1927; Kalaram 1930.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha** was on **20 Mar 1927**.
Statement 2: its **centenary (2026-27)** began on **20 Mar 2026**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Manusmriti Dahan** was on **25 Dec 1927**, separate from **Kalaram** (**1930**, Nashik).
xa: ⚠ **Mahad** = water; **Kalaram** = temple.
Ambedkar led **15,000** volunteers at Kalaram.

133.s: Gurram Jashuva’s Gabbilam is based on the idea that
o: A bat can enter a temple while an untouchable cannot
A king grants land to temple servants
A crow carries a message from Buddha to an emperor
A temple priest abolishes caste through ritual
133.x: In Gabbilam, an untouchable labourer sends his plea to Lord Shiva through a bat because the bat may enter the temple while he may not.
133.tq: Test the central image and social contrast in a literary work.
xs: In **Gabbilam**, a bat may **enter the temple** while the untouchable cannot — option **(1)** is correct.
So the **untouchable labourer** sends his plea to **Lord Shiva** through the bat.
xa: Written by **Gurram Jashuva** in **1941**.
Modelled on **Kalidasa's Meghaduta**.
⚠ **Gabbilam** = bat (**1941**); **Gulamgiri** = slavery (**1873**).

133.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Work)
a. Gabbilam
b. Annihilation of Caste
c. Gulamgiri
 d. Jatimimamsa

List-II (Author)
i. Jyotiba Phule
ii. Sree Narayana Guru
iii. Gurram Jashuva
iv. B.R. Ambedkar

Select the correct answer using the code below:
133.x: Gabbilam was written by Gurram Jashuva, Annihilation of Caste by B.R. Ambedkar, Gulamgiri by Jyotiba Phule and Jatimimamsa by Sree Narayana Guru.
133.tq: Start with the sure author–work pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped author.
xs: Correct code is **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Gabbilam** — Gurram Jashuva; **Annihilation of Caste** — B.R. Ambedkar.
**Gulamgiri** — Jyotiba Phule; **Jatimimamsa** — Sree Narayana Guru.
xa: Gulamgiri (**1873**) compares caste oppression with **American slavery**.
Ambedkar also wrote **Who Were the Shudras?** and **The Untouchables**.
Annihilation of Caste: **1936**.

133.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Andhra Dalit newspapers is correct?
133.x: Adi Andhra was associated with Didla Pullaiah, while Nava Jeevan was associated with Undru Subbarao.
133.tq: Discriminate between two similar newspaper–editor associations.
xs: **Adi Andhra** — **Didla Pullaiah** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Nava Jeevan** was by **Undru Subbarao**, not Didla Pullaiah.
xa: The **Adi-Andhra movement** (**1910s-30s**) claimed Dalits were Andhra's original inhabitants.
Gandhi's paper **Harijan** began in **1933**.

133.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Scheduled Caste population data in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: The SC population was 64.47 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population.
The SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 24.85% of the population.
The SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population.
The SC population was 20.14 crore and constituted 16.6% of the population.
133.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population. The other figures refer to India, a district share, or SC literacy.
133.tq: Separate absolute population, population share and literacy figures.
xs: AP SC population: **84.69 lakh** = **17.08%** — option **(3)** is correct.
**64.47%** is **SC literacy**; **24.85%** is the highest district share (**Konaseema**).
xa: Lowest district: **Alluri Sitharama Raju 2.49%**.
**Census 2011**: **1,241** caste groups notified as SCs.
AP Assembly: **29 SC + 7 ST** of **175**.

133.s:
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the following events?
A. Siddhantam temple entry
B. Karamchedu incident
C. Tsundur incident
D. Davinder Singh judgment
133.x: The Siddhantam temple entry took place in 1933, Karamchedu in 1985, Tsundur in 1991, and the Davinder Singh judgment in 2024.
133.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate incidents by year.
xs: Correct order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Siddhantam** temple entry (**1933**) → **Karamchedu** (**1985**).
**Tsundur** (**1991**) → **Davinder Singh** judgment (**2024**).
xa: Siddhantam was in **Krishna** district.
Tsundur was in **Guntur** district.

133.s: Which one of the following statements about constitutional reservation provisions is correct?
o: Article 16(4) formed part of the original Constitution, whereas Article 15(4) was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Article 15(4) formed part of the original Constitution, whereas Article 16(4) was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Both Articles 15(4) and 16(4) were inserted by the 42nd Amendment.
Both Articles 15(4) and 16(4) were inserted by the 1st Amendment.
133.x: Article 16(4) was present in the original Constitution. Article 15(4) was the first reservation clause added by constitutional amendment, through the First Amendment Act, 1951.
133.tq: Discriminate between the original provision and the later amendment-created provision.
xs: **Art. 16(4)** was in the **original Constitution**; **Art. 15(4)** was added by the **1st Amendment, 1951** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 reverses them; neither came from the **42nd** Amendment.
xa: 15(4) is the basis of reserved seats in **educational institutions**.
**15(5)** covers private institutions except minority ones.

133.s: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 is significant because it was:
o: The first law providing reservation in the Lok Sabha
The first law using the expression Scheduled Tribes
The first law creating the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
133.x: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was the first law enacted to enforce Article 17. The Government of India Act, 1935 had earlier used the term Scheduled Castes.
133.tq: Distinguish the first enforcement law from the earlier statutory use of the term Scheduled Castes.
xs: The **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955** was the **first law enforcing Article 17** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was renamed the **Protection of Civil Rights Act** in **1976**.
The NCSC came under **Art. 338**, not this Act.
xa: The **GoI Act 1935** first used "**Scheduled Castes**".
Only **Parliament** can legislate on Art. 17 offences (**Art. 35**).

133.s: Which one of the following statements best reflects the criticism concerning the constitutional treatment of untouchability?
o: Because Article 17 is a directive principle, it cannot support penal legislation.
Because Article 17 applies only to public employment, private discrimination is fully excluded from debate.
Because Article 17 defines every possible form exhaustively, no new form can escape penalty.
Because untouchability is left undefined, new indirect forms may escape penal consequences.
133.x: A major criticism is that untouchability is not constitutionally defined, allowing newer indirect forms to potentially escape effective penal consequences.
133.tq: Apply the legal criticism to a situation involving newer indirect forms rather than relying on an absolute statement.
xs: Because untouchability is **left undefined**, **new indirect forms may escape penal consequences** — option **(4)** is correct.
Art. 17 is a **Fundamental Right** (Right to Equality), not a DPSP, and it binds **private persons** too.
xa: The criticism was raised on **2 Sep 2026**.
**Mysore HC**: untouchability is the practice **as it developed historically**.
Only **24 cases** under the PCR Act in **2023**; **97%** pendency.

133.s: Which statement correctly describes the Centre's position on an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST reservations in August 2026?
o: It transferred the decision exclusively to State SC Commissions.
It opposed an income-based creamy layer and stated that any change requires a holistic empirical review.
It declared that creamy-layer rules already apply identically to all SC and ST quotas.
It supported immediate introduction of an income-based creamy layer without further study.
133.x: The Centre's affidavit opposed an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas and stated that any change would require a holistic empirical review.
133.tq: Identify the authority's stated position and reject the extreme alternatives of immediate or automatic application.
xs: The Centre **opposed an income-based creamy layer** in SC/ST quotas; any change needs a **holistic empirical review** — option **(2)** is correct.
This was in its affidavit of **7 Aug 2026**.
xa: **Davinder Singh (2024)** allowed sub-classification within SCs.
**M. Nagaraj (2006)** required **quantifiable data** for promotion quotas.

133.s:
The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill referred to in April 2026 sought to:
1. Amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A.
2. Enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850 members.
3. Create separate State Commissions for Scheduled Castes through Article 338(9).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
133.x: The Bill sought to amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A and enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850 members. It did not create State SC Commissions through Article 338(9), and the Bill had not been passed.
133.tq: Reject the statement that assigns a State-law function to the wrong constitutional provision.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
The **131st Bill** sought to amend **Arts 330, 332, 334A** and enlarge the Lok Sabha to **850**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Art. 338(9)** only requires consultation with the NCSC; State commissions come from **State law**.
xa: The Bill was **not passed** (Apr **2026**).
⚠ **334A** = women's reservation (**106th**, **2023**).

133.s: In the Sabarimala reference, Justice B.V. Nagarathna observed that Article 17 cannot be applied:
o: After the commencement of the Constitution
Only during the annual pilgrimage season
133.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that Article 17 cannot apply “for three days a month” in the Sabarimala reference.
133.tq: Recall the precise time-related phrase rather than replacing it with a broader limitation.
xs: Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** said Art. 17 cannot apply "**for three days a month**" — option **(2)** is correct.
It was in the **Sabarimala reference** (**8 Apr 2026**).
xa: Art. 17 binds **private persons** too (**PUDR v Union of India**, **1982**).
Haldwani "shuddhikaran" row: **32** SC/ST Congress MPs petitioned the **President** (**8 Sep 2026**).

133.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Protection of Civil Rights Act
(b) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
(c) Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act
(d) Protection of Human Rights Act

List-II
(i) Eliminates manual scavenging
(ii) Establishes NHRC
(iii) Punishes the practice of untouchability
(iv) Prevents atrocities against SCs/STs
133.x: The Civil Rights Act punishes untouchability, the Atrocities Act prevents atrocities on SCs/STs, the 2013 Act ends manual scavenging, and the Human Rights Act set up the NHRC. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
133.tq: Match each Act to its purpose.
n: The Protection of Civil Rights Act punishes the practice of untouchability. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act prevents atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act eliminates manual scavenging. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
