139.x: The Akshaya Patra Foundation, based in Bengaluru, is identified as the largest NGO partner in the mid-day meal programme. The other pairings contain incorrect State, Ministry or year associations.
139.tq: Use the wrong-person or wrong-ministry trap to identify the only correctly matched pair.
xs: **Akshaya Patra Foundation** is the **largest NGO** mid-day meal provider — option **(2)** is correct.
NP-NSPE was renamed PM POSHAN in **2021**, not 2015; Tithi Bhojan began in **Gujarat**.
PM POSHAN is under the **Ministry of Education**, not MoHFW.
xa: Akshaya Patra: **Bengaluru**, **2000**, **Madhu Pandit Dasa**.
⚠ Mid-day meal **first** = **Tamil Nadu**; Tithi Bhojan **first** = **Gujarat**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mid-Day Meal Scheme:
1. The mid-day meal was first started in Tamil Nadu.
2. The national scheme was renamed PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) in 2021.
3. PM POSHAN is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: the mid-day meal first started in Tamil Nadu. Statement 2 is correct: it was renamed PM POSHAN in 2021. Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal ministry is the Ministry of Education (Dept of School Education and Literacy); MWCD runs ICDS. So '1 and 2 only'.
139.tq: MDM: TN first, NP-NSPE 1995, PM POSHAN 2021, Ministry of Education.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the mid-day meal first started in **Tamil Nadu**.
Statement 2: renamed **PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman)** in **2021**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal ministry is the **Ministry of Education**; **MWCD** runs ICDS.
xa: National scheme began **15 Aug 1995** as **NP-NSPE**.
Sharing **60:40**.

139.s: Janani Suraksha Yojana was launched in 2005 under which framework and ministry?
o: National Food Security Act and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Samarthya and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Mission Vatsalya and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
National Rural Health Mission and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
139.x: JSY was launched in 2005 under the National Rural Health Mission and is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It is a 100% Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
139.tq: Separate JSY’s ministry and framework from PMMVY’s institutional arrangement.
xs: **JSY** was launched in **2005** under the **National Rural Health Mission** and **MoHFW** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Samarthya** and **NFSA** are linked to **PMMVY** (MWCD); **Mission Vatsalya** is child protection.
JSY is **100% centrally sponsored**.
xa: JSY gives cash for **institutional delivery**: **₹1,400** rural, **₹1,000** urban.
**JSSK** (**2011**): no out-of-pocket cost for pregnant women and sick newborns.
**PMSMA** (**2016**): free antenatal check-up on the **9th of every month**.

139.s: Which of the following services is covered under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram?
o: A cash incentive exclusively for home delivery
A Rs.10 lakh corpus payable to a child at age 23
Free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport without out-of-pocket expenditure
A monthly take-home ration of 2.5 kg for infants
139.x: JSSK, launched in 2011 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides pregnant women and sick newborns with free delivery, medicines, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport.
139.tq: Match a maternal-health scheme with its service package rather than a cash transfer.
xs: **JSSK** gives **free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport** with **no out-of-pocket cost** — option **(3)** is correct.
It covers **pregnant women and sick newborns** and is run by **MoHFW** (**2011**).
The **Rs 10 lakh** corpus at **23** is **PM CARES for Children**; **2.5 kg** take-home ration is AP's **Balamrutham**.
xa: **JSY** (**2005**) gives cash for institutional delivery: **₹1,400** rural, **₹1,000** urban.
**PMSMA** (**2016**): free antenatal check-up on the **9th of every month**.
**MAA** (**2016**): breastfeeding within one hour of birth.

139.s: The legal basis cited for the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana is which provision?
o: Section 4 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013
139.x: PMMVY has its legal basis in Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013.
139.tq: Distinguish a statutory basis from constitutional provisions and unrelated legislation.
xs: **PMMVY**'s legal basis is **Section 4** of the **National Food Security Act, 2013** (**Sec 4, NFSA 2013**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Article 45** is about ECCE up to age **6**, not maternity benefit.
xa: PMMVY is the only cash maternity benefit written into the **NFSA**.
Launched **1 January 2017**; ministry **MWCD** (**Samarthya**).
Purpose: **wage-loss compensation**.

139.s: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan is associated with which of the following?
o: Promotion of breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Free treatment exclusively for sick newborns
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month and identification of high-risk pregnancies
Cash assistance for institutional delivery at rural and urban rates
139.x: PMSMA, launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month and helps identify high-risk pregnancies.
139.tq: Use the fixed monthly date and service purpose as identifying clues.
xs: **PMSMA** gives a **free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month** and spots **high-risk pregnancies** — option **(3)** is correct.
Breastfeeding is **MAA**; sick newborns are covered by **JSSK**; delivery cash is **JSY**.
xa: PMSMA was launched in **2016** under **MoHFW** (G2-GS **2022**).
**7.47 crore+** pregnant women examined at **22,349** facilities.
⚠ AP **ECCE day** is the **5th** of every month.

139.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its nodal ministry?
o: JSSK — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMSMA — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
JSY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMMVY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
139.x: PMMVY is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. JSY, JSSK and PMSMA are associated with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
139.tq: Apply the ministry-swapping trap, especially between JSY and PMMVY.
xs: **PMMVY** is under **MWCD**, not MoHFW — option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
**JSY**, **JSSK** and **PMSMA** are all **MoHFW** schemes.
xa: PMMVY sits under **Samarthya** (**Mission Shakti**).
Exam angle: **JSY** sits under **NHM**, while **PMMVY** sits under **MWCD**.
JSY is **100% centrally sponsored**.

139.s: Under PMMVY 2.0 (from April 2022), which of the following correctly describes the maternity benefit?
o: Rs 5,000 for the first child, and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl
Rs 5,000 in three instalments for the first two children irrespective of sex
Rs 6,000 for every live birth irrespective of birth order
Rs 1,400 for institutional delivery in rural areas
139.x: PMMVY 2.0 gives Rs 5,000 for the first child and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl. Rs 5,000 in three instalments was the old PMMVY 1.0 design (a trap). It does not cover every birth. Rs 1,400 for rural institutional delivery is the JSY benefit.
139.tq: PMMVY 2.0: 5,000 (1st) + 6,000 (2nd girl); '3 instalments' = old 1.0.
xs: **PMMVY 2.0** gives **Rs 5,000 for the first child** and **Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **₹5,000 in 3 instalments** was the old **PMMVY 1.0** design.
**₹1,400** for rural institutional delivery is the **JSY** benefit.
xa: PMMVY 2.0 began in **April 2022**.
Helpline **1515**; tagline **"Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti"**.
Legal basis: **Sec 4, NFSA 2013**.

139.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is presently implemented under which component of Mission Shakti?
139.x: BBBP is implemented under Sambal, the safety component of Mission Shakti.
139.tq: Identify the correct umbrella mission by matching the scheme with its present administrative component.
xs: **BBBP** now runs under **Sambal** of **Mission Shakti** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Samarthya** houses **PMMVY**; **Mission Vatsalya** is child protection; **Poshan 2.0** is nutrition.
xa: BBBP was launched on **22 January 2015** at **Panipat**.
It has **100% central funding** and covers **all districts**.
Nodal ministry: **MWCD**, with Health and Education.

139.s:
With reference to Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, consider the following statements:
1. It is primarily a behaviour-change campaign.
2. It provides direct benefit transfers to every girl child.
3. It involves no asset creation.
4. Funds for each district vary with its Sex Ratio at Birth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: BBBP is a behaviour-change campaign with no DBT and no asset creation. Funds for each district vary with its Sex Ratio at Birth. Statement 2 is false.
139.tq: Find the false policy-feature statement; direct transfers and asset creation are common traps in scheme questions.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: BBBP is a **behaviour-change campaign**.
Statement 2 is wrong: BBBP has **no DBT**.
Statements 3 and 4: **no asset creation**; district funds linked to **Sex Ratio at Birth**.
xa: Aim: reverse falling **Child Sex Ratio**; secure the girl child's survival and education.
Girls' secondary GER **75.51% → 80.2%**.
BBBP runs under **Sambal** (Mission Shakti).

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana:
1. It is associated with the Ministry of Finance.
2. A family may open accounts for at most two girls.
3. The annual deposit range is ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh.
4. The account matures after 15 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: The scheme is under the Ministry of Finance, permits accounts for at most two girls per family, and allows annual deposits from ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh. It matures at 21 years, not 15 years.
139.tq: Separate the deposit period from the maturity period; the reversed time period is the trap.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana** (**2015**) is under the **Ministry of Finance**; at most **two girls** per family.
Deposits: ₹**250** to ₹**1.5 lakh** a year.
Statement 4 is wrong: deposits run for **15 years**, but the account **matures at 21**.
xa: **4.53 crore+** accounts.
⚠ BBBP is a **behaviour-change** campaign under **MWCD**, not a savings scheme.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Scheme)
a. Balika Samriddhi Yojana
b. Dhanalakshmi
c. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

d. Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana

List-II (Feature)
i. Behaviour-change campaign for survival and education of the girl child
ii. Conditional cash transfer linked with birth registration, immunisation and schooling
iii. Cash grant at birth and scholarships for girls of BPL families
iv. Savings scheme with maturity at 21 years
139.x: Balika Samriddhi provides a birth grant and scholarships; Dhanalakshmi is a conditional cash-transfer pilot; BBBP is a behaviour-change campaign; Sukanya Samriddhi matures at 21 years.
139.tq: Start from the sure scheme-objective pair and eliminate codes containing swapped girl-child schemes.
xs: **a–iii, b–ii, c–i, d–iv** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Balika Samriddhi** (**1997**): cash grant at birth + scholarships for BPL girls; **Dhanalakshmi** (**2008**): conditional cash transfer pilot.
**BBBP**: behaviour-change campaign; **Sukanya Samriddhi**: savings scheme maturing at **21**.
xa: Dhanalakshmi conditions: **birth registration, immunisation, schooling**.
Sukanya Samriddhi: deposits for **15 years**; at most **two girls** per family.
BBBP: **100% central funding**, all districts.

139.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched at which place on 22 January 2015?
139.x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015 at Panipat in Haryana.
139.tq: Use the place-date pair to distinguish the scheme from other women-centric initiatives.
xs: BBBP was launched on **22 January 2015** at **Panipat, Haryana** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Bengaluru** is the base of the **Akshaya Patra Foundation**.
xa: ⚠ POSHAN Abhiyaan = **Jhunjhunu 2018**; BBBP = **Panipat 2015**.
BBBP runs under **Sambal** (**Mission Shakti**).

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):
1. The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal ministry, with the Health and Education ministries.
2. It aims to reverse the falling Child Sex Ratio and secure the girl child's survival and education.
3. It is administered by the Ministry of Finance as a savings scheme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: MWCD is nodal (with Health and Education) and BBBP aims to reverse the falling Child Sex Ratio. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ministry of Finance savings scheme is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
139.tq: BBBP = MWCD + Health + Education; SSY = Finance.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **MWCD** is nodal, with **Health and Education**.
Statement 2: BBBP aims to reverse the falling **Child Sex Ratio** and secure survival and education.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Ministry of Finance** savings scheme is **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana**.
xa: BBBP has **no DBT and no asset creation**.
Launched **22 January 2015** at **Panipat**.
**100% central funding**; covers **all districts**.

139.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum legal age for marriage is:
o: 21 years for both girls and boys
18 years for girls and 21 years for boys
18 years for girls and 18 years for boys
21 years for girls and 18 years for boys
139.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes 18 years for girls and 21 years for boys.
139.tq: Directly discriminate between the two age thresholds in a commonly confused pair.
xs: Under **PCMA 2006** the minimum age is **18 years for girls and 21 years for boys** — option **(2)** is correct.
The other options swap or equalise the ages; raising women's age to **21** was only proposed in a Bill.
xa: The **Amendment Bill 2021** sought to raise women's age to **21**; it lapsed with the **17th Lok Sabha**.
A child marriage is **voidable** at the option of the minor party.
The **Allahabad HC (1 Jul 2026)** held the age limits apply to all citizens irrespective of religion.

139.s: An adult male who contracts, conducts or promotes a child marriage under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 may be punished with:
o: Rigorous imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
Fine up to Rs. 10 lakh only
Simple imprisonment up to five years without fine
Imprisonment up to one year and fine up to Rs. 50,000
139.x: The punishment may extend to two years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine up to Rs. 1 lakh.
139.tq: Retain both components of the penalty instead of selecting a partially correct punishment.
xs: The punishment is up to **2 years RI + fine up to Rs 1 lakh** — option **(1)** is correct.
It applies to an **adult male** who contracts, conducts or promotes a child marriage.
xa: **Child Marriage Prohibition Officers** are appointed by **State Governments**.
Minimum age: **18** (girls) / **21** (boys).
**'100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat'** campaign launched by **MWCD** in **December 2025**.

139.s: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 proposed to raise the minimum marriageable age of women to 21 years. What happened to the Bill?
o: It was withdrawn after being passed by both Houses.
It was rejected by the Supreme Court.
It was enacted as an Act in 2022.
It was referred to a Standing Committee and lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.
139.x: The Bill was sent to a Standing Committee and subsequently lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.
139.tq: Track the legislative stage and final status rather than only the proposed reform.
xs: The **Amendment Bill 2021** was sent to a **standing committee** and **lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was never passed or enacted.
xa: It sought to raise women's marriage age to **21**.
Present law: **18** for girls, **21** for boys.
NFHS-5: **23.3%** of women aged **20-24** married before **18**.

139.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the legal status of a child marriage is that it is:
o: Void ab initio in all cases
Voidable at the option of the party who was a minor at the time of marriage
Voidable only at the option of the State Government
139.x: Under PCMA 2006 a child marriage is voidable at the option of the minor party, not automatically void. It is not fully valid and unchallengeable, and the option lies with the minor party, not the State Government.
139.tq: Child marriage = voidable at minor party's option.
xs: A child marriage is **voidable at the option of the minor party** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not void in all cases, not fully valid, and the option is not the State Government's.
xa: Minimum age: **18** (girls) / **21** (boys).
Punishment: up to **2 years RI** + fine up to **Rs 1 lakh**.
**Child Marriage Prohibition Officers** are appointed by **State Governments**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding child marriage:
1. NFHS-5 found that 23.3% of women aged 20-24 were married before 18.
2. The '100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat' campaign was launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in December 2025.
3. The ALIVA model to end child marriage originated in Ganjam district of Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct (NFHS-5: 23.3%). Statement 2 is correct: MWCD launched the 100-day campaign in December 2025. Statement 3 is wrong: ALIVA is from Nayagarh district, Odisha. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
139.tq: NFHS-5 23.3%; ALIVA = Nayagarh.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: NFHS-5 — **23.3%** of women aged **20-24** married before **18**.
Statement 2: **MWCD** launched the **'100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat'** in **December 2025**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **ALIVA** is from **Nayagarh**, not Ganjam.
xa: Highest: **West Bengal**, **Bihar**, **Tripura**.
The **Amendment Bill 2021** lapsed with the **17th Lok Sabha**.

139.s: CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories under
139.x: Under Mission Vatsalya, CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories.
139.tq: Match the helpline integration with the correct child-protection mission.
xs: **CHILDLINE 1098** is integrated with **ERSS-112** in **36 States/UTs** under **Mission Vatsalya** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Operation Muskaan** rescues children; **Samagra Shiksha** is school education.
xa: Mission Vatsalya outlay **Rs 10,916 crore** (Centre **Rs 6,928 crore**).
It keeps a **JJB and CWC in every district**.
Sponsorship/foster care: **Rs 4,000** per child per month.

139.s: Mission Vatsalya, introduced in 2021–22, subsumed the
139.x: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the Integrated Child Protection Scheme, or ICPS.
139.tq: Distinguish the child-protection scheme absorbed by Mission Vatsalya from education schemes.
xs: **Mission Vatsalya** (**2021-22**) subsumed **Child Protection Services/ICPS** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **NCLP** merged into **Samagra Shiksha**, not Mission Vatsalya.
xa: Ministry: **MWCD**; a **CSS**.
Objective: child protection + happy childhood aligned to **SDGs** (APPSC-G2 **2024**).
**CHILDLINE 1098** integrated with **ERSS-112**.

139.s: Under Mission Vatsalya, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: JJB and CWC — One in every State only
Sponsorship and foster care — Rs.4,000 per child per month
Institutional care — Rs.4,000 per child per month
Aftercare — Available only up to 18 years
139.x: Mission Vatsalya provides Rs.4,000 per child per month for non-institutional care through sponsorship and foster care. JJBs and CWCs are to be established in every district; institutional care is Rs.3,000 per month and aftercare extends beyond 18 years.
139.tq: Start with the distinctive monetary norm and eliminate reversed amounts or age limits.
xs: **Sponsorship/foster care** = **Rs 4,000** per child per month — option **(2)** is correct.
JJBs and CWCs are in **every district**, not one per State.
**Institutional care** (CCI maintenance) is **Rs 3,000**; **aftercare** runs to **18-21**, extendable to **23**.
xa: CCI capacity **50** (**25** in NE/hilly areas).
**CHILDLINE 1098** integrated with **ERSS-112** in **36 States/UTs**.
**JJ Amendment Act 2021**: **DM** = focal point for adoption.

139.s: Palna, the National Creche Scheme, is intended for children in which age group?
139.x: Palna covers children from 6 months to 6 years. Its creches may function whether or not the mother is employed, and 17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches were targeted.
139.tq: Use the exact age range to distinguish Palna from preschool and school-age programmes.
xs: **Palna** covers children **6 months-6 years** — option **(3)** is correct.
**3-8** is the **NEP 2020** foundational stage.
xa: Target: **17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches**.
Open **whether or not the mother is employed**.
⚠ ICDS also covers children **6 months-6 years**.

139.s: Which of the following is a feature of PM CARES for Children?
o: It provides a corpus of Rs.10 lakh at the age of 23 to eligible COVID-19 orphaned children.
It provides support only to children who lost one parent before 2020.
It provides only free school meals and no health support.
It is restricted to children below six years receiving Anganwadi services.
139.x: PM CARES for Children was launched in 2021 for children who lost parents or specified guardians to COVID-19 and provides a corpus of Rs.10 lakh at 23, along with education and health support.
139.tq: Find the option that preserves the scheme’s beneficiary, amount and age details.
xs: **PM CARES for Children** gives a corpus of **Rs 10 lakh** at **23** to children orphaned by **Covid-19** — option **(1)** is correct.
It covers loss of **both parents**, the surviving parent, a legal guardian or adoptive parents — not one parent before 2020.
It also gives **health insurance + education cover**.
xa: Launched in **2021**.
Portal: **pmcaresforchildren.in**.
⚠ Mission Vatsalya aftercare runs to **21**, extendable to **23**.

139.s: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Act, 2021, who has been made the focal point for adoption matters in a district?
139.x: The JJ Amendment Act 2021 made the District Magistrate the focal point for adoption. The CWC is a statutory body for children in need of care, but not the designated focal point; the District Judge and SP are not given this role.
139.tq: JJ Amendment 2021 -> DM handles adoption.
xs: The **JJ Amendment Act 2021** made the **District Magistrate** the focal point for adoption — option **(1)** is correct.
The **CWC** is the body for children needing care, not the adoption focal point.
xa: Mission Vatsalya keeps a **JJB and CWC in every district**.
CCI maintenance: **Rs 3,000** per month.
**Palna** targets **17,000** Anganwadi-cum-Creches.

139.s: Which scheme is described as one of the world’s largest SHG-based rural livelihood programmes?
139.x: DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011, is an SHG-based rural livelihoods programme described as one of the world’s largest.
139.tq: Identify the scheme from its distinctive scale and SHG-based livelihood feature.
xs: **DAY-NRLM** (**2011**) is an SHG-based rural livelihood programme, **one of the world's largest** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Swadhar** gives shelter to women in difficult circumstances.
xa: Swadhar is now inside **Shakti Sadan**.
**Swavalambini** (**2022**): MSDE-NITI Aayog entrepreneurship programme for women students in the North-East.
PM Ujjwala: **10.57 crore+** connections.

139.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Swadhar, which provides shelter to women in difficult circumstances, is now part of Shakti Sadan.
2. Ujjawala is the scheme that provides deposit-free LPG connections to women of poor households.
3. PM Ujjwala Yojana was launched by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: Swadhar now sits inside Shakti Sadan. Statement 2 is wrong: Ujjawala deals with trafficking; LPG connections come under PM Ujjwala Yojana. Statement 3 is correct: PMUY (May 2016) is run by MoPNG. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
139.tq: Ujjawala = trafficking; Ujjwala = LPG (MoPNG).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: **Swadhar** is now inside **Shakti Sadan**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Ujjawala** deals with **trafficking**; LPG is **PM Ujjwala Yojana**.
Statement 3: PMUY (**May 2016**) is run by **MoPNG**.
xa: AP has **28 Shakti Sadans**.
PMUY subsidy: **₹300** per cylinder for up to **12** refills.
PMUY connections: **10.57 crore+**.

139.s: The Allahabad High Court held on 1 July 2026 that the age limits under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act apply:
o: Only to persons governed by personal laws without exceptions
To all citizens irrespective of religion
Only to persons below the age of 18 who reside in Uttar Pradesh
139.x: The Allahabad High Court held that the PCMA age limits apply to all citizens irrespective of religion.
139.tq: Test the constitutional-law scope of a statute by focusing on the phrase that removes the religious distinction.
xs: The **Allahabad HC** (**1 Jul 2026**) held **PCMA** age limits apply to **all citizens irrespective of religion** — option **(3)** is correct.
So the limits are not confined to any religion, personal law or State.
xa: A child marriage is **voidable** at the minor party's option.
Punishment: up to **2 years RI** + fine up to **Rs 1 lakh**.

139.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the criticism of the women and child welfare schemes cited?
o: They continue to focus on survival rather than full child development, and last-mile gaps remain in tribal and Rayalaseema hamlets.
They focus mainly on full child development and have no survival-oriented component.
They have eliminated all implementation gaps in tribal areas.
They are limited exclusively to urban women and children.
139.x: The criticism is that the schemes still emphasise survival rather than complete child development, while last-mile gaps persist in tribal and Rayalaseema hamlets.
139.tq: Choose the balanced evaluative statement; absolute claims such as “all” and “eliminated” are traps.
xs: Schemes still focus on **survival rather than full child development**, and **last-mile gaps** remain in tribal hamlets and **Rayalaseema** — option **(1)** is correct.
So gaps are not eliminated, and schemes are not urban-only.
xa: The survival-focus criticism dates to **13 Jan 2026**; the last-mile gap to **Mar 2026**.
Tribal take-home ration is richer (**200 ml** milk).
AP has **24** tribal ICDS projects.

139.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the cited ‘first’ or unique feature?
o: BBBP — first launched at Varanasi; PMMVY — only nutrition scheme under NFSA
Tithi Bhojan — first began in Gujarat; PMMVY — only cash maternity benefit written into the NFSA
Poshan Maah — first began in Gajuwaka; PMMVY — only LPG subsidy under NFSA
Ujjawala — first began in Panipat; PMMVY — only SHG scheme under NFSA
139.x: Tithi Bhojan began in Gujarat, and PMMVY is identified as the only cash maternity benefit written into the National Food Security Act.
139.tq: Match each unique descriptor with the correct programme and avoid swapping launch locations or policy sectors.
xs: **Tithi Bhojan** first began in **Gujarat**, and **PMMVY** is the **only cash maternity benefit written into the NFSA** — option **(2)** is correct.

141.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the components of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana?
141.x: The four components of AVYAY are the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, State Action Plan, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana and Elder Line. The National Family Benefit Scheme is an NSAP component.
141.tq: Use the programme-family distinction to reject an NSAP component.
xs: The **National Family Benefit Scheme** is not an AVYAY component — option **(1)** is correct.
AVYAY's four components: **Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens**, **State Action Plan**, **RVY** and **Elder Line**.
xa: AVYAY began in **April 2021**, renamed from the **National Action Plan for Senior Citizens**.
**Rs 287.81 crore** utilised (ES **2025-26**).
Innovation: **SAGE**, **AGRASR** elderly SHGs, **silver economy**.

141.s: Under the Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana, which of the following combinations is correct?
o: 10% assured pension for 10 years; maximum purchase price ₹7.5 lakh; maximum pension ₹10,000 per month
8% assured pension for 5 years; maximum purchase price ₹10 lakh; maximum pension ₹7,500 per month
8% assured pension for 10 years; maximum purchase price ₹7.5 lakh; maximum pension ₹5,000 per month
7% assured pension for 15 years; maximum purchase price ₹5 lakh; maximum pension ₹3,000 per month
141.x: PMVVY offered an assured pension at 8 per cent for 10 years, with a maximum purchase price of ₹7.5 lakh and maximum pension of ₹5,000 per month.
141.tq: Match the three numerical limits without confusing duration, purchase price and pension ceiling.
xs: **PMVVY**: **8%** assured pension for **10 years**; max purchase **Rs 7.5 lakh**; max pension **Rs 5,000/month** — option **(3)** is correct.
The other options change the rate, term, purchase price or pension.
xa: Run by the **Ministry of Finance** through **LIC**; **GST-exempt**.
Closed for new subscription after **31 March 2023**.
⚠ **PMVVY** (pension) vs **Ayushman Vay Vandana** (health, **70+**).

141.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPOP):
1. It may provide up to 90 per cent of project cost to eligible NGOs.
2. It supports old-age homes, day-care centres and mobile medicare units.
3. It is a component of AVYAY.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: IPOP can support up to 90 per cent of project cost for NGOs and covers old-age homes, day-care centres and mobile medicare units. It is included under AVYAY.
141.tq: Verify the funding, service and programme-hierarchy statements together.
xs: **All three** statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**IPOP** gives up to **90%** of project cost to NGOs.
It funds **old age homes, day care, mobile medicare units** and is a component of **AVYAY**.
xa: AVYAY's other components: **State Action Plan**, **RVY**, **Elder Line**.
AP: **7** physiotherapy centres treated **87,240** patients.
**Vayoshreshtha Samman** also honours seniors.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about IGNOAPS:
1. It is a component of the National Social Assistance Programme.
2. It is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.
3. Its assistance has remained frozen at Rs 200 since 2007 and it covers about 2.2 crore people.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: All three statements are correct. IGNOAPS is under NSAP and the Ministry of Rural Development; the stated figure records Rs 200 as frozen since 2007 and coverage of about 2.2 crore people.
141.tq: Combine institutional, administrative and numerical features in one coded question.
xs: **All three** statements are correct — option **(4)**.
IGNOAPS is under **NSAP** and **MoRD**.
It is **frozen at Rs 200 since 2007** and covers about **2.2 crore** people.
xa: NSAP pension erosion → calls for an **inflation-indexed minimum pension floor**.
Beneficiaries must be **BPL**.

141.s: The Ayushman Vay Vandana card under AB-PMJAY is meant for:
o: Children below 10 years from SECC households
Only women aged 70 years and above
All persons aged 60 years and above subject to an income ceiling
All persons aged 70 years and above irrespective of income
141.x: All senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for the Ayushman Vay Vandana card irrespective of income.
141.tq: Test the age threshold together with the important income-related exception.
xs: The **Ayushman Vay Vandana card** is for **all aged 70+** (**70 years and above**) **irrespective of income** — option **(4)** is correct.
It gives health cover of **Rs 5 lakh** under **AB-PMJAY** (MoHFW, **2024**).
xa: ⚠ NPOP defines older persons as **60+**.
⚠ **PMVVY** = pension (LIC); **Vayoshri** = aids (ALIMCO).
NPHCE was launched by **MoHFW** in **2010-11**.

141.s:
Consider the following statements about Elder Line:
1. It operates under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
2. Its helpline number is 14567.
3. It is limited to pension disbursement and does not provide broader senior-citizen support.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
141.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Elder Line is a National Helpline for Senior Citizens and is not limited merely to pension disbursement.
141.tq: Find the negative overstatement that narrows a broad public-service helpline to one function.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Elder Line is under **MoSJE**; its number is **14567**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is the **National Helpline for Senior Citizens**, not a pension portal.
xa: Technical support: **Tata Trusts** + **NSE Foundation**.
It is part of **AVYAY** (**April 2021**).
**IGNOAPS** pensions are under **MoRD**.

141.s: Which organisation is associated with elderly-care services and the release of elder-abuse surveys in India?
141.x: HelpAge India runs elderly-care services and releases surveys relating to elder abuse.
141.tq: Match the organisation with its distinctive activity rather than with a general human-rights function.
xs: **HelpAge India** runs elderly-care services and releases **elder-abuse surveys** — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes do not link the other bodies to these surveys.
xa: **World Elder Abuse Awareness Day**: **15 June**.
AP's Senior Citizens Welfare Association flagged rising abuse and **cyber fraud** against elders living alone.
**NPSC 2011** wants **harsh punishment** for elder abuse.

141.s: The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers which period?
141.x: The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers the period 2021–2030.
141.tq: Distinguish the decade framework from the earlier Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing.
xs: The **UN Decade of Healthy Ageing** is **2021-2030** — option **(2)** is correct.
**2002** was the **Madrid** Plan; **1999** NPOP.
xa: **International Day of Older Persons**: **1 October**.
**World Elder Abuse Awareness Day**: **15 June**.
India's **AVYAY** also began in **2021**.

141.s: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on
141.x: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on 1 October.
141.tq: Use direct date recall while distinguishing it from World Elder Abuse Awareness Day.
xs: The **International Day of Older Persons** is on **1 October** — option **(3)** is correct.
**15 June** is **World Elder Abuse Awareness Day**.
xa: **Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing**: **2002**.
**UN Decade of Healthy Ageing**: **2021-2030**.
NPOP: older person = **60+**.

141.s: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on
141.x: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on 15 June.
141.tq: Apply confusable-date discrimination between the two observances relating to older persons.
xs: **World Elder Abuse Awareness Day** is on **15 June** — option **(4)** is correct.
**1 October** is the **International Day of Older Persons**.
xa: **HelpAge India** releases elder-abuse surveys.
The 2007 Act punishes **abandonment**: up to **3 months** and/or **Rs 5,000**.
**Elder Line 14567** is the national senior-citizens helpline.

141.s: The Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing was adopted in which year?
141.x: The Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing dates to 2002. 1999 is India's NPOP, 2011 is India's NPSC, and 2021 is the start of the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing (2021-2030).
141.tq: Madrid Plan 2002; UN Decade 2021-30.
xs: The **Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing** was adopted in **2002** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1999** = India's **NPOP**; **2011** = **NPSC**; **2021** = start of the **UN Decade of Healthy Ageing**.
xa: UN Decade of Healthy Ageing: **2021-2030**.
International Day of Older Persons: **1 October**.
World Elder Abuse Awareness Day: **15 June**.

141.s: Which was the first State to enact a law for the maintenance of parents, before the central Act of 2007?
141.x: Himachal Pradesh enacted the Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, 2001, the first such State law. Kerala is first with a Senior Citizens' Welfare Department; Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are not cited as first.
141.tq: HP 2001 = first parents-maintenance law.
xs: **Himachal Pradesh** was the **first State** with a parents-maintenance law — option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **Himachal Pradesh Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, 2001**.
The notes name no such earlier law for AP, Kerala or Karnataka.
xa: The central Act came in **2007**, administered by **MoSJE**.
⚠ **RVY** was first launched at **Nellore**, AP.
The **2019 Amendment Bill** lapsed.

141.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act creates a legal maintenance obligation on children or heirs.
Statement B: Its commencement was fixed uniformly for all states on December 29, 2007, without a state-wise rollout.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
141.x: A is true and B is false: the Senior Citizens Act puts a duty of maintenance on children or heirs, but it was brought into force state by state from 29 December 2007, not on one date for all.
141.tq: Watch for 'uniformly' in place of state-wise.
n: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act came into force through a state-wise notification rollout beginning on December 29, 2007. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act places a legal maintenance obligation on children. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act places a legal maintenance obligation on heirs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
xs: Statement A is true and Statement B is false — option **(3)**.
A: the **Senior Citizens Act** (**2007**) creates a **legal obligation** on **adult children** and **heirs** to **provide maintenance** — true.
B: it came into force through a **state-wise notification rollout** **beginning** on **December 29, 2007** — not uniformly, so false.
xa: Maximum maintenance: **Rs 10,000 per month**; cases disposed within **90 days**.
**Sec 23**: property transfers on condition of care can be declared **void**.
Abandonment: up to **3 months** and/or **Rs 5,000** fine.
**Himachal Pradesh** (**2001**) had the earlier State law.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about Census 2011:
1. India's population was about 121.09 crore.
2. About 68.9% of the population was rural.
3. The decadal growth rate was 27.7%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: Statement 1 is correct: 121.09 crore. Statement 2 is correct: 68.9% rural. Statement 3 is wrong: decadal growth in 2001-11 was 17.7%, not 27.7%. So '1 and 2 only' is right; options containing 3 are wrong.
142.tq: Census 2011: 121 crore, about 69% rural, 17.7% growth - growth was slowing.
xs: **Census 2011** counted **121.09 crore** people, of whom **68.9%** were **rural** — so statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, option **(1)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **decadal growth** in Census 2011 was **17.7%**, not **27.7%**.
xa: The **next Census** is due in **2027**.
Growth phases: **1911-21** decline, **1921** the **"Great Divide"**, **1961-71** explosion, **1981-2011** high but slowing.
AP's population is **495.77 lakh** — **4.09%** of India, ranked **10th** (2025-26).

142.s:
Arrange the following phases of India’s population growth in chronological order:
A. High but slowing growth
B. Great Divide
C. Population explosion
D. Decline during 1911–1921
142.x: The correct sequence is decline during 1911–1921, the Great Divide in 1921, population explosion during 1961–1971, and high but slowing growth during 1981–2011.
142.tq: Fix the dated turning points first, then place the broad later phase.
xs: The correct order is **D, B, C, A** — option **(1)**.
**D:** decline during **1911-21** → **B:** the **"Great Divide"** of **1921** → **C:** population **explosion** in **1961-71** → **A:** **high but slowing** growth in **1981-2011**.
xa: ⚠ **1921** is the "Great Divide" — after it India's population never declined again.
**Demographic transition:** high birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both low.
India today is in the **youth bulge** stage of the demographic transition.

142.s: Which sequence correctly represents the stages of demographic transition?
o: Both rates low → birth rate falls → death rate falls → high rates
High birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both rates low
High birth and death rates → birth rate falls → death rate rises → both rates high
Death rate falls → both rates low → birth rate rises → high death rate
142.x: The demographic transition proceeds from high birth and death rates, to falling death rates, then falling birth rates, and finally low birth and death rates.
142.tq: Track the sequence of mortality decline before fertility decline.
xs: **Demographic transition** runs: **high birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both low** — option **(2)**.
The **death rate falls first**; the birth rate follows later, which is why population grows fast in the middle stage.
Options that start with low rates or have the death rate rising reverse this sequence.
xa: India is presently in the **youth bulge** stage.
SRS 2024: India's **TFR 1.9**, below the replacement level of **2.1**.

142.s: India is presently described, in demographic-transition terms, as being in the:
142.x: India is described as being in the youth-bulge stage of demographic transition.
142.tq: Identify the current demographic-stage label rather than a general population condition.
xs: In demographic-transition terms, India is in the **youth bulge** stage — option **(1)**.
A youth bulge means a large young and working-age share: SRS 2024 puts working age at **66.4%** and children at **24%**.
xa: **Demographic transition:** high birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both low.
A large workforce pays off only if **employed**; jobs are needed for about **9.7 million** new working-age people each year.

142.s: According to NFHS-5, which of the following correctly represents the total fertility rate of India and Andhra Pradesh?
142.x: NFHS-5 recorded India’s total fertility rate at 2.0 and Andhra Pradesh’s at 1.7.
142.tq: Compare the national and State figures without reversing their order.
xs: **NFHS-5** put India's **TFR at 2.0** and **Andhra Pradesh at 1.7** — option **(4)**.
AP is thus well below the replacement level of **2.1**.
xa: ⚠ **APPCA** quotes AP's TFR at **1.5**.
**Bihar** had the highest TFR in NFHS-5 (**3.0**).

142.s: According to SRS 2024, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: India’s TFR was 2.4, with rural and urban rates equal.
India’s TFR was 2.1 and urban TFR was higher than rural TFR.
India’s TFR was 1.5, with rural TFR at 1.9 and urban TFR at 2.1.
India’s TFR was 1.9, with rural TFR at 2.1 and urban TFR at 1.5.
142.x: SRS 2024 reported India’s TFR at 1.9, rural TFR at 2.1 and urban TFR at 1.5.
142.tq: Check both the national figure and the rural–urban direction of difference.
xs: **SRS 2024** put India's **TFR at 1.9**, with **rural 2.1** and **urban 1.5** — option **(4)**.
Rural fertility is higher than urban, so options showing urban above rural or equal rates are wrong.
xa: India's TFR has been below the replacement level of **2.1** for the **5th year**.
Only **six states** are above **2.1**; **Delhi** is lowest at **1.2**.
SRS 2024 age structure: working age **66.4%**, children **24%**.

142.s: The dependency ratio is calculated by which of the following formulas?
142.x: The dependency ratio is calculated as the population aged 0–14 plus the population aged 65 and above, divided by the population aged 15–64.
142.tq: Separate the dependent-age groups in the numerator from the working-age denominator.
xs: **Dependency ratio** = **(0-14 plus 65+) ÷ (15-64)** — option **(4)**.
The numerator is the dependants (children and the old); the denominator is the **working-age** population.
xa: SRS 2024: working age = **66.4%**; children = **24%**.
Among the elderly, **70%** depend on others and **78%** have no pension.

142.s:
Consider the following statements about the SRS 2024 fertility data:
1. India's TFR has stayed below the replacement level of 2.1 for the fifth year.
2. Only six States have a TFR above 2.1.
3. Bihar recorded the lowest TFR among States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: Statement 1 is correct: India's TFR (1.9) is below 2.1 for the fifth year. Statement 2 is correct: only six States are above 2.1. Statement 3 is wrong: Delhi is lowest (1.2); Bihar is the highest-fertility State (3.0 in NFHS-5). Hence '1 and 2 only'.
142.tq: SRS 2024: 1.9; Delhi lowest 1.2; Bihar highest.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: India's TFR (**1.9**) is below **2.1** for the **5th year** (SRS 2024).
Statement 2 is correct: only **six states** are above **2.1**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Delhi** is the lowest (**1.2**); **Bihar** is the highest (**3.0**, NFHS-5). So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: SRS 2024: rural TFR **2.1**, urban TFR **1.5**.
NFHS-5: India **2.0**; AP **1.7** (APPCA quotes **1.5**).

142.s: India needs jobs for approximately how many new working-age people every year, a figure cited in debates on the demographic dividend?
142.x: About 9.7 million new working-age people enter each year, and a large workforce pays off only if employed. The other figures are not the cited estimate.
142.tq: ~9.7 million new workers/year.
xs: India needs jobs for about **9.7 million** new working-age people each year — option **(2)**.
A large workforce pays off only if it is **employed**.
xa: SRS 2024: working age = **66.4%**; children = **24%**.
India is in the **youth bulge** stage of the demographic transition.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the debate on population control:
1. Population control is considered necessary for environmental protection.
2. Southern States that controlled population may lose relative representation and financial advantages.
3. Population carries 15–25% weight in Finance Commission formulas.
4. Delimitation could cost the southern States 8–10 seats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All four statements reflect the environmental case for population control and the counter-debate concerning the possible demographic and fiscal disadvantage of southern States.
142.tq: Test the environmental argument and the representation–finance counter-debate together.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: population control is necessary for the **environment** (UPPSC 2023 key marks it **true**).
Statement 2 is correct: **southern states** that controlled population lose out.
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: population has **15-25%** weight in **Finance Commission** formulas; **delimitation** could cost them **8-10 seats**. So **1, 2, 3 and 4** — option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ In the UPPSC 2023 key, the assertion was true but the **reason** given was false.
AP's draft **Population Management Policy** (Mar 2026) shifts from control to management.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly states the legal position in Javed v. State of Haryana (2003)?
o: The Supreme Court struck down Haryana’s two-child norm as unconstitutional.
The case abolished two-child norms for local elections throughout India.
The Supreme Court upheld Haryana’s two-child norm.
The case concerned only the calculation of the dependency ratio.
142.x: In Javed v. State of Haryana (2003), the Supreme Court upheld Haryana’s two-child norm.
142.tq: Use the case name and year to identify the precise judicial outcome.
xs: In **Javed v State of Haryana (2003)**, the **Supreme Court upheld Haryana's two-child norm** — option **(3)**.
So the norm was not struck down, and the case did not abolish two-child norms nationwide.
xa: ⚠ AP's draft policy (Mar 2026) **removes the two-child norm for local elections**.
AP's policy also offers **₹25,000** for a second or third child.

142.s: Which of the following is a feature of Andhra Pradesh's draft Population Management Policy (March 2026)?
o: A two-child norm for contesting local body elections
An incentive of Rs 25,000 for a second or third child and removal of the two-child norm for local elections
A cash penalty on families with more than two children
Compulsory sterilisation after the second child
142.x: The draft policy moves from population control to management, offers Rs 25,000 for a second or third child and removes the two-child norm for local elections. Imposing a two-child norm, penalties or sterilisation would be control measures, the opposite of the policy.
142.tq: AP U-turn: pro-natalist, Rs 25,000, two-child norm removed.
xs: AP's draft policy offers **₹25,000** for a **second or third child** and **removes the two-child norm** for **local elections** — option **(2)**.
It moves from **control to management**, so a two-child norm, penalties or sterilisation would contradict it.
xa: ⚠ The SC had upheld Haryana's two-child norm in **Javed v State of Haryana (2003)**.
Counter-debate: southern states that controlled population could lose **8-10 seats** in delimitation.

142.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the problems of the elderly is NOT correct?
o: Persons aged 80 years and above commonly face chronic diseases.
The elderly account for approximately 30–35% of hospitalisation spending.
Insurance policies may impose age caps on the elderly.
Ageing generally eliminates the need for long-term health expenditure.
142.x: Ageing does not eliminate health expenditure; persons aged 80 and above face chronic disease, insurance may have age caps, and the elderly account for about 30–35% of hospitalisation spending.
142.tq: Find the reversal of the stated health and expenditure effects.
xs: The incorrect statement is that ageing **eliminates the need for long-term health expenditure** — option **(4)**.
In fact the **80+** face chronic disease, insurance often has **age caps**, and the elderly account for **30-35%** of hospitalisation spending.
xa: **Dependency:** **70%** depend on others; **78%** have no pension (NITI).
**70% of elderly women** have no pension.
Other problems: **loneliness**, **ageism and abuse**, **feminisation of ageing**.

142.s: Which of the following correctly represents the dependency and pension situation of the elderly?
o: 70% have pensions and 78% are financially independent
78% depend on others and 70% have no pension
70% depend on others and 78% have no pension
30% depend on others and 35% have no pension
142.x: About 70% of elderly persons depend on others and 78% have no pension.
142.tq: Keep the two percentages attached to their correct indicators.
xs: **70%** of the elderly **depend on others** and **78%** have **no pension** (NITI) — option **(3)**.
⚠ Option (2) swaps the two figures.
xa: **70% of elderly women** have no pension.
Elderly = **30-35%** of hospitalisation spending.
**Over 55%** of the elderly now live in **nuclear** households.

142.s:
Consider the following statements regarding family support for the elderly:
1. Care inside the joint family is weakening.
2. More than half of the elderly now live in nuclear households.
3. The weakening of joint-family care is associated with the growing importance of living arrangements outside the traditional joint family.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
142.x: All three statements are correct. Care within joint families is weakening, while over 55% of the elderly live in nuclear households, highlighting changing family support arrangements.
142.tq: Link the demographic figure with its stated social consequence.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: care inside the **joint family** is weakening.
Statement 2 is correct: **over 55%** of the elderly now live in **nuclear** households.
Statement 3 is correct: the weakening of joint-family care goes with living arrangements outside it. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: Children's **migration** leaves parents behind, causing loneliness.
**NPSC 2011** backs **"ageing in place"**.
NGOs get up to **90%** of old-age-home costs under the **Integrated Programme for Older Persons**.

142.s: Under which programme can NGOs receive support of up to 90% of the cost of old age homes?
o: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
142.x: The Integrated Programme for Older Persons provides NGOs with support of up to 90% of the costs of old age homes.
142.tq: Match the welfare intervention with the exact programme responsible for it.
xs: NGOs get up to **90%** of the costs of old age homes under the **Integrated Programme for Older Persons** — option **(1)**.
**AVYAY** (with **SAGE**) is the umbrella scheme giving equity to senior-care start-ups; **NPHCE** is the health-care programme.
xa: **SAGE:** equity of up to **₹1 crore** for senior-care start-ups.

142.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position associated with NPSC 2011?
o: It supported ageing in place and drew attention to destitution among rural elderly persons.
It restricted elderly welfare exclusively to persons living in joint families.
It recommended abolishing NGO support for old age homes.
It favoured institutionalisation of all elderly persons in urban old age homes.
142.x: NPSC 2011 backed the concept of ‘ageing in place’ and highlighted destitution among the rural elderly.
142.tq: Distinguish community-based ageing support from compulsory institutional care.
xs: **NPSC 2011** backs **"ageing in place"** and flags **destitution among the rural elderly** — option **(1)**.
Ageing in place means the elderly staying in their own homes and communities, not being institutionalised.
xa: **NPOP 1999** came first; **NPHCE** in **2010-11**.
**Kerala** is the first state with a Senior Citizens' Welfare Department, Commission and Elderly Budget.

142.s: Which State is the first in India to have a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget?
142.x: Kerala is the first State to establish all three: a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget.
142.tq: Identify the State associated with the complete institutional framework for senior citizens.
xs: **Kerala** is the **first state** with a **Senior Citizens' Welfare Department**, a **Commission** and an **Elderly Budget** — option **(2)**.
**Andhra Pradesh** is instead known for its pro-natalist draft **Population Management Policy** (Mar 2026).
xa: **India:** first national family planning programme (**1952**).

142.s: The National Policy on Older Persons (NPOP) was announced in:
142.x: The National Policy on Older Persons was announced in 1999. NPSC came in 2011, while 2007 is the year of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act.
142.tq: 1999 was the International Year of Older Persons: NPOP 1999.
xs: The **National Policy on Older Persons (NPOP)** came in **1999** — option **(3)**.
**2011** is the year of **NPSC**, not NPOP.
xa: **NPHCE** came in **2010-11**.
**NPSC 2011** backs **"ageing in place"** and flags destitution among the rural elderly.
**AVYAY** with **SAGE**: equity of up to **₹1 crore** for senior-care start-ups.

142.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I                  List-II
A. India                 1. First Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department
B. Kerala                2. First national family planning programme
C. Andhra Pradesh       3. Draft Population Management Policy

Select the correct answer using the code below.
142.x: India introduced the first national family planning programme in 1952, Kerala was first with the senior-citizens institutional framework, and Andhra Pradesh is associated with the draft Population Management Policy.
142.tq: Start with the sure pair India–first national family planning programme and eliminate the codes.
xs: Correct matching: **A-2, B-1, C-3** — option **(2)**.

**India** — first national **family planning** programme (**1952**); **Kerala** — first **Senior Citizens' Welfare Department**; **Andhra Pradesh** — draft **Population Management Policy** (Mar 2026).
xa: Kerala also has the first elderly **Commission** and **Elderly Budget**.
AP's policy offers **₹25,000** for a second or third child.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about NALSA v. Union of India:
1. It was delivered on 15 April 2014.
2. It was delivered by Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri.
3. It held that gender identity must be decided by biological examination and State verification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the judgment came on 15 April 2014 from Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri. Statement 3 is wrong: NALSA held gender identity is self-determined, not decided by biology or State verification. Hence C; A omits the bench, B and D wrongly include statement 3.
143.tq: NALSA = 2014, Radhakrishnan-Sikri, self-identification.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NALSA v. Union of India** was delivered on **15 April 2014**.
Statement 2 is correct: the bench was **Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri**.
Statement 3 is wrong: NALSA held gender identity is **self-determined**, not decided by biology or state verification. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(3)**.
xa: NALSA recognised transgender persons as the **"third gender"**.
It applied **Arts 14, 15, 16, 19(1)(a) and 21** to them.
⚠ **2014** = NALSA judgment + Tiruchi Siva Bill; **2015** = Rajya Sabha passes the Bill.

143.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NALSA v. Union of India:
1. The judgment recognised transgender persons as the third gender.
2. It held that gender identity is self-determined rather than dependent on biology or State verification.
3. It extended the protection of Articles 14, 15, 16, 19(1)(a) and 21 to transgender persons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: All three statements are correct. NALSA recognised the third gender, affirmed self-determined gender identity and applied the listed fundamental-rights provisions to transgender persons.
143.tq: Check whether each statement reflects recognition, self-identification or constitutional protection before choosing the combination.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: NALSA recognised transgender persons as the **"third gender"**.
Statement 2 is correct: gender identity is **self-determined**, not by biology or state verification.
Statement 3 is correct: **Arts 14, 15, 16, 19(1)(a) and 21** apply to them. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: Delivered on **15 April 2014** by **Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri**.
The **2019 Act's** Objects cited NALSA and the **right to self-perceived gender identity**.
⚠ The **2026** amendment **excludes self-perceived identity**.

143.s:
Assertion (A): The NALSA judgment directed that transgender persons be treated as socially and educationally backward for reservation purposes.
Reason (R): The judgment required governments to extend reservation in education and employment to transgender persons on that basis.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
143.x: Both statements are true, and the direction to extend reservation in education and employment explains the treatment of transgender persons as socially and educationally backward.
143.tq: Check whether the reason states the operative consequence of the asserted constitutional direction.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
NALSA directed that transgender persons be treated as **SEBC** (**socially and educationally backward**) precisely so that they get **reservation in education and jobs**.
xa: This is a **vertical** OBC-type quota.
⚠ The community instead demands **horizontal** reservation cutting across **SC/ST/OBC/General**.
The **2019 Act** was criticised for providing **no reservation**.

143.s: Who moved the Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 as a private member's Bill?
143.x: The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 was moved as a private member's Bill by Tiruchi Siva of the DMK.
143.tq: Match the legislative initiative with its mover and party.
xs: The **Rights of Transgender Persons Bill 2014** was a private member's bill moved by **Tiruchi Siva** (**DMK**) — option **(2)**.
It was passed by the **Rajya Sabha in April 2015**.
xa: It was the first private member's bill passed by the RS in **over four decades**.
It was **not passed by the Lok Sabha**.
The **2026 Amendment Bill** was introduced by **Virendra Kumar** in the Lok Sabha on **13 Mar 2026**.

143.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014:
1. It was passed by the Rajya Sabha in April 2015.
2. It was the first private member's Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha in over four decades.
3. It was subsequently passed by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Bill was not passed by the Lok Sabha.
143.tq: Use the legislative-stage trap by distinguishing passage in one House from passage in both Houses.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Rajya Sabha** passed the Bill in **April 2015**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was the first **private member's bill** passed by the RS in **over four decades**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it was **not passed by the Lok Sabha**. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: Mover: **Tiruchi Siva** (**DMK**).
⚠ **2014** = NALSA judgment + the Bill; **2015** = RS passes it.

143.s:
Under the 2019 Act, a transgender person is defined as a person whose gender does not match the gender assigned at birth. Which of the following are included within this definition?
1. Trans men and trans women
2. Persons with intersex variations
3. Genderqueer persons
4. Socio-cultural identities such as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
143.x: The 2019 definition includes trans men and women, intersex variations, genderqueer persons and specified socio-cultural identities including kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta.
143.tq: Read the statutory definition inclusively and check every category listed before selecting the code.
xs: The **2019** definition covers a person whose gender does not match that assigned at birth, including **trans men/women**, **intersex variations** and **genderqueer** persons, alongside socio-cultural identities like **kinner, hijra, aravani, jogta** — option **(4)**, all four.
So all four categories fall within the definition.
xa: ⚠ The **2026** definition is limited to socio-cultural identities, specified intersex/congenital variations and those **forced** to present as transgender.
The 2026 amendment **excludes self-perceived identity** and omits **Section 4(2)**.

143.s:
Under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, consider the following statements:
1. The certificate of identity is issued by the District Magistrate.
2. A revised certificate may be issued after surgery.
3. The certificate of identity is issued by the National Council for Transgender Persons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the District Magistrate issues the certificate of identity, and a revised certificate may be issued after surgery. Statement 3 is wrong: the National Council advises and monitors policy; it does not issue certificates. Hence B; A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
143.tq: Certificate = District Magistrate (in 2026, on a medical board's advice).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **certificate of identity** is issued by the **District Magistrate**.
Statement 2 is correct: a **revised certificate** is issued after **surgery**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **NCTP** advises and monitors policy; it does not issue certificates. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: **Rules 2020** set the application procedure through the **national portal**.
⚠ Certificate: **2019** = DM alone; **2026** = DM on a **medical board's** recommendation.

143.s: Which of the following was a criticism of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019?
o: It prescribed heavier penalties than those for comparable crimes against women.
It completely abolished the role of the District Magistrate in identity certification.
It provided no reservation for transgender persons.
It excluded all socio-cultural transgender identities from its definition.
143.x: Criticisms included lighter penalties than for similar crimes against women, District Magistrate gatekeeping of identity and the absence of reservation. The Act did include several socio-cultural identities.
143.tq: Select the genuine criticism while rejecting options that reverse the Act’s provisions.
xs: A criticism of the 2019 Act was that it provided **no reservation** for transgender persons — option **(3)**.
Other criticisms: **lighter penalties** (not heavier) than for similar crimes against women, and **DM gatekeeping** of identity — so the DM's role was not abolished.
xa: NALSA had directed a **vertical** OBC-type quota; the community wants **horizontal** reservation.
**Karnataka** (2021) was the first state with a **1%** job quota.

143.s: The National Council for Transgender Persons is constituted as a statutory body under which legislation?
o: The National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019
143.x: The National Council for Transgender Persons is a statutory body constituted under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.
143.tq: Identify the parent legislation of the statutory body.
xs: The **NCTP** is a **statutory body** under the **Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019** — option **(4)**.
Its **Chairperson** is the **Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment**.
xa: Members: Health, Home, Minority Affairs etc. + **experts** + **community representatives**.
Role: **advises and monitors** policy.
2026: state/UT members by **rotation** — one each from North, South, East, West and North-East.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019:
1. It came into force on 10 January 2020.
2. It is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
3. The National Council for Transgender Persons under it is chaired by the Union Social Justice Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act came into force on 10 January 2020. Statement 2 is wrong: it is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE). Statement 3 is correct: the National Council is chaired by the Union Social Justice Minister. So B; A misses statement 3, C and D wrongly accept statement 2.
143.tq: Transgender law = MoSJE throughout (Act, Council, SMILE).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the 2019 Act came into force on **10 Jan 2020**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is administered by **MoSJE**, not the Health Ministry.
Statement 3 is correct: the **NCTP** is chaired by the **Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment**. So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: The NCTP **advises and monitors** policy.
**SMILE** (**2022**) is also a **MoSJE** scheme.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2026 amendment:
1. The District Magistrate issues the certificate on the recommendation of a designated medical board.
2. The definition is limited to specified socio-cultural identities, intersex or congenital variations and persons forced to present as transgender.
3. Kidnapping and forcing a person to present as transgender were added as offences.
4. Self-perceived identity continues to be expressly included without restriction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the amendment excludes self-perceived identity and omits Section 4(2).
143.tq: Find the statement that reverses the amendment’s central change concerning self-perceived identity.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **DM** issues the certificate **after a designated medical board's recommendation**.

Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the definition is limited to **socio-cultural identities**, intersex/congenital variations and those **forced** to present; **kidnapping** and forced presentation were added as offences.
Statement 4 is wrong: **self-perceived identity is excluded**. So **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: **Section 4(2)** was **omitted**, ending legal recognition of self-determination.
The Bill was introduced by **Virendra Kumar** on **13 Mar 2026**; assent by **Apr 2026**.

143.s: The 2026 amendment to the transgender persons law was challenged in the Supreme Court by:
o: Madhu Bai Kinnar and Shabnam Mausi
Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel
143.x: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel challenged the amendment as contrary to the principles laid down in NALSA.
143.tq: Separate the petitioners challenging the amendment from the legislator and the NALSA Bench.
xs: The 2026 amendment was challenged in the **Supreme Court** by **Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel** as contrary to **NALSA** — option **(3)**.
**Virendra Kumar** introduced the Bill; **Shabnam Mausi** and **Madhu Bai Kinnar** were the first transgender MLA and mayor; **Joyita Mondal** was the first transgender judge.
xa: **SC, Aug 2026:** the Centre assured that ID cards issued before the 2026 Act remain valid.
Laxmi Narayan Tripathi was the first transgender person from Asia-Pacific to address the **UN General Assembly**.

143.s: The NHRC Advisory 2.0 of May 2026 recommended that Census categories should include which of the following?
o: Only sexual minorities and senior citizens
Intersex persons, trans men and trans women
Only transgender persons and persons with disabilities
143.x: The NHRC Advisory 2.0 recommended Census categories for intersex persons, trans men and trans women.
143.tq: Identify the exact categories proposed in the advisory.
xs: **NHRC Advisory 2.0** (May 2026) asked for separate **intersex, transmen and transwomen** categories in **Census 2027** — option **(2)**.
It also asked the government to **review the amendment**.
xa: Other NHRC asks: admission by **self-identified gender**, ban on **non-consensual intersex surgery** on children, more **Garima Grehs**.
**Census 2011** counted about **4.88 lakh** transgender persons.

143.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature of reservation sought by transgender persons in the context of the NALSA judgment?
o: A separate vertical reservation restricted to the General category
Reservation exclusively under the women’s quota
Horizontal reservation cutting across SC, ST, OBC and General categories
143.x: The transgender community has sought horizontal reservation, which would cut across the SC, ST, OBC and General categories. NALSA had directed treatment as socially and educationally backward, resembling a vertical OBC-type approach.
143.tq: Distinguish the two commonly confused forms of reservation by asking whether the quota cuts across existing categories.
xs: The community seeks **horizontal reservation** cutting across **SC/ST/OBC/General** — option **(4)**.
⚠ NALSA itself had directed a **vertical** OBC-type quota by treating them as **SEBC**.
xa: The demand **resurfaced** on **27 June 2023** with a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra's reply to the **Bombay High Court**.
**Karnataka** (2021) was first to give a **1%** quota in all government services.

143.s: The issue of reservation for transgender persons resurfaced in June 2023 in connection with which State?
143.x: The issue resurfaced through a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra’s reply to the Bombay High Court in June 2023.
143.tq: Use the place of the protest and the State involved to separate a current issue from nearby State measures.
xs: The reservation issue resurfaced in **June 2023** (**27 June 2023**) through a **Mumbai** protest against **Maharashtra**'s reply to the **Bombay High Court** — option **(3)**.
The demand was for **horizontal** reservation across SC/ST/OBC/General.
xa: ⚠ **Karnataka** — first state with **1%** reservation in all government services (**July 2021**).
NALSA's quota was **vertical**, OBC-type.

143.s:
Consider the following statements about the SMILE scheme:
1. It was launched in 2022 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
2. It is an umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
3. Its goal is 'Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
143.x: Statement 1 is correct: SMILE was launched in 2022 by MoSJE. Statement 2 is wrong: it is an umbrella Central Sector scheme (Rs 365 crore), not Centrally Sponsored. Statement 3 is correct: its goal is a begging-free India, 'Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat'. Hence D; A omits statement 3, B and C wrongly include statement 2.
143.tq: SMILE: MoSJE, 2022, Central Sector, begging-free India.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **SMILE** was launched in **2022** by **MoSJE**.
Statement 2 is wrong: SMILE is an umbrella **Central Sector** scheme, not Centrally Sponsored.
Statement 3 is correct: its goal is **"Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat"** (begging-free India). So **1 and 3 only** — option **(4)**.
xa: Outlay: **Rs 365 crore**.
⚠ **Garima Greh** = shelter homes (**23** in **17** States/UTs).
Begging component covers **181 cities**; about **12,710** persons rehabilitated.

143.s: What is the expanded form of SMILE in the context of welfare schemes?
o: Social Mission for Inclusive Livelihood and Employment
Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise
Scheme for Marginalised Inclusion, Livelihood and Education
Support Mission for Independent Living and Empowerment
143.x: SMILE stands for Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise.
143.tq: Test the exact official expansion of the scheme acronym.
xs: **SMILE** = **Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise** — option **(2)**.
It is a **2022** **MoSJE** umbrella **Central Sector** scheme.
xa: Goal: **"Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat"**; outlay **Rs 365 crore**.
Components: welfare of **transgender persons** and rehabilitation of persons engaged in **begging**.

143.s: Garima Greh under SMILE is primarily associated with which service?
143.x: Garima Greh provides shelter homes for transgender persons.
143.tq: Match the named sub-scheme with its core service.
xs: **Garima Greh** = **shelter homes** for transgender persons — option **(2)**.
There are **23** in **17 States/UTs** (ES 2025-26), with at least one per State.
xa: ⚠ **SMILE** is the umbrella scheme (**Rs 365 crore**); Garima Greh is one component.
**NHRC Advisory 2.0** asked for **more Garima Grehs**.

143.s: Which State was the first to formulate a transgender policy?
143.x: Kerala was the first State to formulate a transgender policy, in 2015.
143.tq: Test a first-in-the-country fact against neighbouring States associated with other transgender measures.
xs: **Kerala** was the first state with a transgender policy (**2015**) — option **(4)**.
⚠ Some notes give the year as **2021**.
xa: Kerala's **Sthree Suraksha** scheme covers EWS women and transgender persons.
**Tamil Nadu**: **Transgender Welfare Board (2008)**; **Karnataka**: first **1%** job quota (**2021**).

143.s: According to Census 2011, approximately how many transgender persons were counted in India?
143.x: Census 2011 counted approximately 4.88 lakh transgender persons in India.
143.tq: Test the precise census estimate using close numerical distractors.
xs: **Census 2011** counted about **4.88 lakh** transgender persons — option **(3)**.
**Uttar Pradesh** had the highest count.
xa: Order: **UP** → **undivided Andhra Pradesh** → **Maharashtra** → **Bihar**.
**NHRC Advisory 2.0** wants separate intersex, transmen and transwomen categories in **Census 2027**.

143.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Transgender Welfare Board (2008) - Tamil Nadu
2. Thirunangaigal app for ID registration - Kerala
3. Sthree Suraksha scheme for EWS women and transgender persons - Kerala
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
143.x: Pair 1 is correct: Tamil Nadu set up the Transgender Welfare Board in 2008. Pair 2 is wrong: the Thirunangaigal app (2021) is a Tamil Nadu measure. Pair 3 is correct: Sthree Suraksha is a Kerala scheme. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
143.tq: TN: Welfare Board 2008, Thirunangaigal app; Kerala: first policy, Sthree Suraksha.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **Tamil Nadu** set up the **Transgender Welfare Board (2008)**.
Pair 2 is wrong: the **Thirunangaigal** app for ID registration (**2021**) is a **Tamil Nadu** measure.
Pair 3 is correct: **Sthree Suraksha** is a **Kerala** scheme. So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: Tamil Nadu also has a **Third Gender Tailoring Industrial Cooperative Society** (**2020**).
Kerala framed the first State transgender policy (**2015**).

143.s: Under the NTR Bharosa Pension scheme in Andhra Pradesh, the monthly pension for elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons is:
143.x: NTR Bharosa provides Rs 4,000 per month to elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons.
143.tq: Discriminate between the common-category rate and the higher rates for specified disabilities or diseases.
xs: **NTR Bharosa** pays elderly (**60+**), widows and **transgender persons** **Rs 4,000** a month — option **(2)**.
**Rs 6,000** is the rate for **PwDs**.
xa: Chronic diseases = **Rs 10,000**; fully disabled = **Rs 15,000**.
Release in FY 2025-26: **Rs 32,754.90 crore**.

143.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 41 of the Constitution refers to public assistance in old age.
2. The National Social Assistance Programme rests on Articles 41 and 42.
3. Invalidity and old-age pensions are included in State List Entry 9.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
143.x: Article 41 concerns public assistance in old age, and NSAP rests on Articles 41 and 42. Invalidity and old-age pensions are in Concurrent List Entry 24, not State List Entry 9.
143.tq: The trap is the reversal of the State List and Concurrent List entries.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **NSAP** rests on **Art. 41 and 42**.
Statement 3 is wrong: invalidity and old age pensions are in **Concurrent List Entry 24**, not the State List. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: Central **IGNOAPS** is frozen at **Rs 200**.
AP's **NTR Bharosa** pays **Rs 4,000** to the elderly, widows and transgender persons.

143.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. K. Prithika Yashini — First transgender police sub-inspector
2. Manabi Bandyopadhyay — First transgender college principal
3. Joyita Mondal — First transgender mayor
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
143.x: Pair 1 is correct: K. Prithika Yashini (Tamil Nadu) was the first transgender police sub-inspector.
