Pair 2 is correct: Manabi Bandyopadhyay (West Bengal) became the first transgender college principal in 2015. Pair 3 is wrong: Joyita Mondal was the first transgender judge (Lok Adalat, 2017); the first transgender mayor was Madhu Bai Kinnar (Raigarh, 2015). So only 1 and 2 (B); A misses pair 2, C and D wrongly accept pair 3.
143.tq: Learn the 'firsts' as person-post pairs; the trap swaps judge and mayor.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **K. Prithika Yashini** (Tamil Nadu) — first transgender **police sub-inspector**.
Pair 2 is correct: **Manabi Bandyopadhyay** (West Bengal) — first transgender **college principal** (**2015**).
Pair 3 is wrong: **Joyita Mondal** was the first **judge**; the first **mayor** was **Madhu Bai Kinnar**. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: First transgender MLA: **Shabnam Mausi**, Madhya Pradesh (**1998**).
Madhu Bai Kinnar was mayor of **Raigarh**, Chhattisgarh (**2015**).

143.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Shabnam Mausi — First transgender MLA
2. Madhu Bai Kinnar — First transgender mayor
3. Karnataka — State with a 1% transgender job quota
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
143.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Shabnam Mausi became the first transgender MLA in Madhya Pradesh in 1998, Madhu Bai Kinnar the first transgender mayor in 2015, and Karnataka introduced the 1% job quota in 2021.
143.tq: Verify each first-person or State association separately, paying attention to the office and year.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4)**, **1, 2 and 3**.
**Shabnam Mausi** — first transgender **MLA** (MP, **1998**); **Madhu Bai Kinnar** — first **mayor** (Raigarh, **2015**); **Karnataka** — **1%** job quota (**2021**).
xa: ⚠ **Joyita Mondal** = first transgender **judge** (WB, **2017**).
**Manabi Bandyopadhyay** = first transgender **college principal** (**2015**).

143.s: The 2026 amendment concerning transgender persons has been criticised primarily because it is viewed as:
o: Removing the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court over identity matters
Extending the NALSA principle to old-age pensions
Reversing the self-identification principle recognised in NALSA
Strengthening the self-identification principle of NALSA
143.x: The principal criticism is that medical certification reverses the self-identification principle associated with the NALSA judgment.
143.tq: Contrast the two competing legal principles: self-identification and medical certification.
xs: The 2026 Act is seen as **reversing NALSA's self-identification principle** — option **(3)**.
It replaces **self-identification** with **medical-board certification** and excludes self-perceived identity.
xa: **Section 4(2)** was omitted, ending legal recognition of self-determination.
It is under **SC challenge** by Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel.
**NHRC Advisory 2.0** asked the government to **review the amendment**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka:
1. The case was decided by an 11-judge Bench.
2. The State is the unit for determining minority status.
3. The State may regulate, but not control, the administration of minority institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The 2002 decision was delivered by an 11-judge Bench and adopted a State-wise approach to minority status while permitting regulation without administrative control.
144.tq: Combine bench strength, territorial unit and the distinction between regulation and control.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002)** was decided by an **11-judge** bench.
Statement 2 is correct: the **State is the unit** for minority status.
Statement 3 is correct: the State may **regulate** but **not control** administration. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: APP writes the case as "v. State of Kerala"; it is **v State of Karnataka**.

144.s: The Constitution refers to the term ‘minority’ in which of the following Articles, without defining it?
144.x: The Constitution uses the term ‘minority’ in Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B, but does not provide a general definition of the term.
144.tq: Recall the exact Article group rather than selecting a familiar Fundamental Rights cluster.
xs: The Constitution uses "minority" in **Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B** but never defines it — option **(2)**.
Only **religious and linguistic** minorities are recognised.
xa: The **NCM Act** also does not define it; under **Section 2(c)**, a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government**.
Arts **350A** and **350B** were inserted by the **7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Commission for Minorities Act does not define the term 'minority'.
2. A community notified by the Centre is treated as a minority for the purposes of the Act.
3. States cannot notify minorities of their own for State purposes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. States can also notify their own minorities for State purposes, making statement 3 incorrect.
144.tq: Watch for the absolute word 'cannot' when comparing Union and State roles.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **NCM Act** does not define "minority".
Statement 2 is correct: under **Section 2(c)**, a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **States may notify** their own minorities. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: **Jains** were State minorities in **11 States** before 2014.
The **State** is the unit for minority status (**T.M.A. Pai, 2002**).

144.s: Which one of the following statements regarding State designation of minorities is correct?
o: Jains were declared a minority simultaneously by all States in 2014.
Only the Union Government can designate a community as a minority.
States can designate their own minorities, and 11 States had declared Jains a minority before 2014.
States cannot designate minorities unless authorised by the Supreme Court.
144.x: States have the power to designate their own minorities. Before 2014, 11 States had declared Jains a minority.
144.tq: Test the distinction between Union-level notification and State-level designation.
xs: **States can designate their own minorities**, and **11 States** had declared **Jains** a minority before 2014 — option **(3)**.
So the Union is not the only designating authority, and no Supreme Court authorisation is needed.
xa: Jains were notified nationally on **27 January 2014** as the **sixth** minority.
**Bal Patil (2005)** declined to direct the Centre to notify Jains, leaving it to the **States**.

144.s:
With reference to minority rights in India, consider the following statements:
1. Whether a community is a minority is decided with reference to its population position in the State concerned.
2. The rights of minorities under the Constitution are absolute and cannot be regulated by the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: Statement 1 is correct: after T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002), the State, not the whole of India, is the unit for deciding minority status. Statement 2 is wrong: minority rights are not absolute; the State may regulate standards, though it cannot take away management (APPSC G2 2017 treated 'absolute' as the untrue statement). Hence 1 only; options B, C and D wrongly accept statement 2 or reject statement 1.
144.tq: Minority rights are NOT absolute; the State is the unit (T.M.A. Pai).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: minority status is decided by the **State's** demography (**T.M.A. Pai, 2002**).
Statement 2 is wrong: minority rights are **not absolute** — the State may regulate **standards**, though not take away management. So **1 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC G2 2017** treated "minority rights are **absolute**" as the untrue statement.
**St. Xavier's (1974):** regulations only for **standards/excellence**.
**In re Kerala Education Bill:** the State may impose **reasonable conditions** for aid.

144.s: Which one of the following grounds is NOT expressly included in Article 29(2) as a basis for denying admission to a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution?
144.x: Article 29(2) prohibits denial of admission on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language. Sex and place of birth are not included in this list.
144.tq: Find the omitted ground rather than selecting one of the four expressly listed grounds.
xs: **Place of birth** is NOT a ground in **Art. 29(2)** — option **(2)**.
Art. 29(2) bars denial of admission on grounds **only of religion, race, caste or language**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** **sex** and **place of birth** are not listed.
Art. 29(2) applies to **State-maintained or State-aided** institutions.
**Art. 29** protects any section of **citizens**; **Art. 30** only minorities.

144.s:
With reference to Article 29 of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. Any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture has the right to conserve it.
2. Article 29 is confined exclusively to religious and linguistic minorities.
3. No citizen can be denied admission to a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Article 29(1) protects the language, script or culture of any distinct section of citizens, and Article 29(2) prohibits denial of admission on the specified grounds. Article 29 is not confined exclusively to minorities.
144.tq: Separate the broad protection under Article 29 from the minority-specific protection under Article 30.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Art. 29(1)** — any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture may conserve it.
Statement 2 is wrong: Art. 29 protects **any section of citizens**, not only minorities.
Statement 3 is correct: **Art. 29(2)** — no denial of admission on grounds **only of religion, race, caste or language**. So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **Sex** and **place of birth** are not listed in Art. 29(2).
**Art. 30** applies **only to minorities**; Madrasas are run under it.

144.s: A State seeks to deny aid to an educational institution solely because it is managed by a linguistic minority. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
144.x: Article 30(2) provides that the State shall not discriminate in granting aid to an educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether religious or linguistic.
144.tq: Apply the factual situation to the specific clause dealing with State aid to minority-managed institutions.
xs: **Article 30(2)** — the State shall not discriminate against **minority-managed** institutions in **granting aid** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 29(1)** is about conserving language/culture, **29(2)** about admission, and **350A** about mother-tongue primary instruction.
xa: **Art. 30(1)** covers **all minorities, religious or linguistic** — the "Charter of Education Rights".
**Art. 30(1A)** was added by the **44th Amendment**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 30:
1. The State shall not discriminate against minority institutions in granting aid.
2. The right to administer a minority institution is completely immune from State regulation.
3. The State may regulate standards of education without destroying the minority character of the institution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The right under Article 30 is not absolute; the State may regulate educational standards, but it cannot destroy the minority character of the institution.
144.tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the distinction between regulation of standards and destruction of minority character.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: under **Art. 30(2)** the State shall not discriminate against minority institutions in **aid**.
Statement 2 is wrong: minority rights are **not absolute**.
Statement 3 is correct: the State may regulate **standards** but not take away management. So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: **St. Xavier's (1974):** right to administer protected; regulation only for **standards/excellence**.
**T.M.A. Pai (2002):** the State may **regulate** but not **control** administration.

144.s: Clause (1A) of Article 30, which protects the right of minorities to establish educational institutions when their property is compulsorily acquired, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
144.x: The 44th Amendment, which removed the right to property, added Article 30(1A) so that removal of that right does not affect minorities' right to establish institutions and compensation is ensured on acquisition. The 7th Amendment (1956) inserted Articles 350A and 350B; the 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5) after P.A. Inamdar; the 42nd Amendment did not add Article 30(1A).
144.tq: 30(1A) = 44th Amendment (right to property removed).
xs: **Art. 30(1A)** was added by the **44th Amendment** — option **(2)**.
It ensures that removing the **right to property** does not affect minorities' right to establish institutions, with **compensation** on acquisition.
xa: The **7th Amendment (1956)** inserted Arts **350A** and **350B**.
The **93rd Amendment** inserted Art. **15(5)** after **P.A. Inamdar**.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Case)
A. In re Kerala Education Bill
B. St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
C. T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
D. P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra

List-II (Holding)
1. State is the unit for determining a linguistic or religious minority
2. Aided minority college may prefer its own community up to 50 per cent of seats
3. State cannot impose reservation on unaided minority or non-minority professional institutions
4. State may regulate standards without destroying minority character

Select the correct answer.
144.x: A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3. In re Kerala Education Bill held the Article 30 right is not absolute and the State may impose reasonable conditions (regulating standards); St. Stephen's (1992) let an aided minority college prefer its own community up to about 50%; T.M.A. Pai (2002) made the State the unit for minority status; P.A. Inamdar (2005) barred State reservation quotas in unaided institutions, minority or non-minority.
144.tq: Start from the distinctive case holdings and then verify the remaining pairs.
xs: Correct matching: **A-4, B-2, C-1, D-3** — option **(1)**.
**Kerala Education Bill** — State may impose reasonable conditions (regulate); **St. Stephen's (1992)** — aided minority college may prefer its own community up to about **50%**.
**T.M.A. Pai (2002)** — **State is the unit**; **P.A. Inamdar (2005)** — no State quotas in **unaided** institutions.
xa: **St. Xavier's (1974):** regulations only for **standards/excellence**.
**Bal Patil (2005):** Jain minority status left to the **States**.

144.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: P.A. Inamdar (2005) — Presidential reference under Article 143
In re Kerala Education Bill (1957) — 11-judge Bench and State-wise minority status
St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974) — right to administer protected, subject to standards and excellence regulations
T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) — seven-judge Bench and no State quota in unaided institutions
144.x: C is correct: St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974) protected the right to administer, allowing regulation only for standards and excellence. The others are mismatched: the Article 143 Presidential reference was the Kerala Education Bill case, not P.A. Inamdar; the 11-judge Bench and State-wise minority status belong to T.M.A. Pai; the seven-judge Bench barring State quotas in unaided institutions was P.A. Inamdar.
144.tq: Find the correctly matched case and holding by separating the four landmark decisions.
xs: **St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974)** — right to administer protected; regulations only for **standards/excellence** — option **(3)**.
The **Art. 143** reference was the **Kerala Education Bill** case; the **11-judge** State-wise ruling was **T.M.A. Pai**; the **7-judge** no-quota ruling was **P.A. Inamdar**.
xa: **St. Stephen's (1992):** aided minority college may prefer its own community up to about **50%**.

144.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the decision in P.A. Inamdar (2005)?
o: A seven-judge Bench held that the State could impose its quota in unaided institutions without limitation.
A seven-judge Bench held that there could be no State quota or reservation in unaided institutions, contributing to the subsequent 93rd Amendment framework.
An 11-judge Bench abolished the distinction between aided and unaided institutions.
The Court held that minority status must be determined at the national level.
144.x: P.A. Inamdar was decided by a seven-judge Bench and held that the State could not impose its quota or reservation in unaided institutions. The decision was followed by the constitutional development associated with Article 15(5) through the 93rd Amendment.
144.tq: Combine bench strength, holding and constitutional consequence without confusing it with T.M.A. Pai.
xs: **P.A. Inamdar (2005)**, a **7-judge** bench, held the State cannot impose **reservation quotas** on **unaided** institutions, minority or non-minority — option **(2)**.
This led to Art. **15(5)** through the **93rd Amendment**.
xa: ⚠ **T.M.A. Pai (2002)** was the **11-judge** bench making the **State** the unit for minority status.
**St. Stephen's (1992)** concerned **aided** minority colleges.

144.s: The decision in Bal Patil v. Union of India (2005) is associated with which of the following?
o: Directing the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority
Imposing reservation quotas on unaided minority institutions
Declaring that minority status must be determined nationally
Declining to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority and leaving the matter to the States
144.x: The Court declined to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority, leaving the matter to the States and cautioning against the multiplication of minority claims.
144.tq: Discriminate between a judicial direction and a refusal to issue that direction.
xs: **Bal Patil v Union of India (2005)** **declined to direct the Centre** to notify **Jains** as a national minority, leaving it to the **States** — option **(4)**.
It also warned against **multiplying minority claims**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** UPSC notes describe it as a linguistic-institutions case — inaccurate.
The Centre later notified **Jains** on **27 January 2014**.

144.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is correct?
o: The officer is appointed by the President and reports to the President.
The officer is appointed by the Chief Minister and reports to the Governor.
The officer is appointed by the Parliament and reports to the Prime Minister.
The officer is appointed by the Governor and reports to the State Legislature.
144.x: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President and submits reports to the President.
144.tq: Apply the authority trap by matching appointment and reporting powers with the President.
xs: Under **Art. 350B**, the **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities** is **appointed by the President** and **reports to the President** — option **(1)**.
The President lays the reports before **Parliament** and sends them to the States concerned.
xa: The Special Officer is designated the **Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities** (office set up **1957**).
HQ: **Prayagraj (Allahabad)**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
2. The amendment was associated with the reorganisation of States.
3. The office under Article 350B is styled as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The 7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956, linked to the reorganisation of States, inserted Articles 350A and 350B; the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B is styled the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities (office set up in 1957).
144.tq: Combine amendment, context and official designation; all three details refer to the same constitutional arrangement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Arts **350A** and **350B** were inserted by the **7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956**, linked to **States Reorganisation**.
Statement 3 is correct: the Art. 350B Special Officer is designated the **Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities**. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: The office was set up in **1957**; HQ **Prayagraj (Allahabad)**.
**350A:** instruction in the **mother tongue at the primary stage**.

144.s: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was established in:
144.x: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957.
144.tq: Distinguish the office’s establishment year from the constitutional amendment year.
xs: The office of the **Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities** was set up in **1957** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **1956** is the **7th Amendment** that inserted Art. **350B**; the office followed in 1957.
xa: HQ: **Prayagraj (Allahabad)**.
**1964** is the year of the statutory **Central Waqf Council**.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
 a. Article 347
 b. Article 350
 c. Article 350A
 d. Article 350B

List-II (Provision)
 i. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
 ii. Representation for grievances in any language used in the Union or a State
 iii. Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State
 iv. Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage for linguistic-minority children

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: Article 347 concerns recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State; Article 350 concerns language for grievances; Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction; and Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
144.tq: Start with the sure Article–provision pair and eliminate codes that disturb the remaining relationships.
xs: Correct matching: **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**347:** President may recognise a language of a substantial part of a State; **350:** representation in any language used in the Union or State.
**350A:** **mother tongue at the primary stage**; **350B:** **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities**.
xa: Arts **350A** and **350B** came with the **7th Amendment, 1956**.
The Special Officer is appointed by and **reports to the President**.

144.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes religious and linguistic minorities in India?
o: Religious minorities are associated with the National Commission for Minorities, while linguistic minorities are considered State-wise and linked with the Article 350B officer
Religious minorities are identified only by States, while linguistic minorities are identified by the Union
Both categories are determined exclusively on an all-India basis
Neither category is recognised under the Constitution
144.x: Religious minorities are dealt with through the National Commission for Minorities and the Ministry of Minority Affairs. Linguistic minorities are identified State-wise, with the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
144.tq: Split the comparison by authority and territorial basis.
xs: **Religious minorities** go with the **NCM**; **linguistic minorities** are identified **State-wise** and linked with the **Art. 350B** officer — option **(1)**.
Linguistic minorities are **not** notified under the NCM Act.
xa: Both religious and linguistic minorities are recognised in the Constitution.
Six notified religious minorities ≈ **19%** of India's population.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Minorities:
1. It is a statutory body under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
2. The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was constituted in 1993.
3. The Chairperson and members are appointed by the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Chairperson and members of the NCM are appointed by the Central Government, not by the President.
144.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints?’ trap, especially where a constitutional President may be confused with the Central Government.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the NCM is **statutory** under the **NCM Act, 1992**.
Statement 2 is correct: the first statutory Commission was constituted in **1993**.
Statement 3 is wrong: members are nominated by the **Central Government**, not the President. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: The NCM is **statutory, not constitutional**, under the **Ministry of Minority Affairs**.
⚠ GS 2018 key: appointed by the **Union Government**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis:
1. It was created by the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993.
2. The Act lapsed in 2004.
3. The Commission continues as a non-statutory body with its tenure extended by resolution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The NCSK was created under the 1993 Act; after the Act lapsed in 2004, it continued as a non-statutory body through tenure extensions by resolution.
144.tq: Track the transition from statutory creation to present non-statutory continuation.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NCSK** was created by the **NCSK Act, 1993**.
Statement 2 is correct: the Act **lapsed in 2004**.
Statement 3 is correct: it continues as a **non-statutory body**, its tenure extended by resolution. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: Comparable finance bodies: **NSFDC** (1989, SCs), **NBCFDC** (1992, BCs), **NSTFDC** (2001, STs).

144.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Conducting elections to minority educational institutions
Looking into specific complaints relating to deprivation of minority safeguards
Monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards for minorities
144.x: The Commission evaluates development, monitors safeguards, examines complaints and recommends measures; conducting elections to minority educational institutions is not one of its stated functions.
144.tq: Find the option that assigns an unrelated administrative function to the Commission.
xs: **Conducting elections to minority educational institutions** is NOT an NCM function — option **(1)**.
NCM functions: evaluate minorities' **development**, **monitor constitutional and legal safeguards**, look into **specific complaints**, recommend measures, commission studies.
xa: It has **powers of a civil court** while inquiring.
⚠ Minority status of institutions is decided by the **NCMEI**, not the NCM.

144.s:
While inquiring into complaints, the National Commission for Minorities may exercise powers similar to those of a civil court, including:
1. Summoning witnesses.
2. Requisitioning or calling for records.
3. Imposing criminal sentences.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The Commission may summon witnesses and call for records while conducting an inquiry. It does not possess the power to impose criminal sentences.
144.tq: Separate inquiry powers from the power to impose judicial punishment.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the NCM has **powers of a civil court** — **summon witnesses** and **call for records**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is quasi-judicial and cannot impose criminal sentences. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ APPCA 2026 / older notes say "no automatic civil-court powers"; follow the Act.
The **NCMEI** also has **civil court powers**.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
 a. 1978
 b. 1992
 c. 1993
 d. 1995

List-II
 i. First statutory Commission constituted
 ii. Vice-Chairperson added
 iii. Non-statutory Minorities Commission formed
 iv. NCM Act made the body statutory

Select the correct answer using the code below.
144.x: The milestones are correctly matched as 1978–non-statutory Commission, 1992–statutory NCM Act, 1993–first statutory Commission and 1995–addition of Vice-Chairperson.
144.tq: Start from the sure year-event pair and eliminate codes with mismatched milestones.
xs: Correct matching: **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**1978** non-statutory Commission → **1992** NCM Act made it statutory → **1993** first statutory Commission → **1995** Vice-Chairperson added.
xa: After 1995 the strength became **7**.
⚠ **1993** is also the year the first **five** communities were notified.

144.s:
With reference to the composition of the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements:
1. It consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five Members.
2. All seven members must belong to minority communities.
3. Five of the seven members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities.
4. The term of office is three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The Commission has seven members: a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and five Members. Five, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities, and the term is three years; it is not required that all seven belong to minority communities.
144.tq: Test composition, qualification and tenure separately to catch the overstatement in ‘all’.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson + 5 Members = 7**.
Statement 2 is wrong and 3 is correct: **Section 3(2)** requires **five members including the Chairperson** from minority communities, not all seven.
Statement 4 is correct: tenure is **3 years**. So **1, 3 and 4 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: Older notes list only a Chairperson and five Members (before the **1995** amendment).
July 2026: only **4 of 7** posts filled.

144.s: Which of the following pairs of communities is NOT included among the notified minority communities?
144.x: The notified minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. Jews are not included in this listed group.
144.tq: Find the outsider in a recognised statutory list rather than choosing a community from memory alone.
xs: **Jews** are NOT a notified minority — option **(2)**.
Notified: **Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis** (**1993**) and **Jains** (**2014**).
xa: Jains were added on **27 January 2014** as the **sixth**.
Six notified minorities ≈ **19%** of India's population.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified as minority communities in 1993.
2. Jains were notified as a minority community in 2014.
3. Linguistic minorities are notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The first five communities were notified in 1993 and Jains were added in 2014. Linguistic minorities are not notified under this Act.
144.tq: Check the notified-community list against the separate constitutional mechanism for linguistic minorities.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **five** communities were notified in **1993**; **Jains** in **2014**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **linguistic minorities** are **not** notified under the NCM Act. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: Linguistic minorities come under the **Special Officer** (**Art. 350B**).
⚠ **1993** = five communities + first statutory NCM; **2014** = Jains.

144.s: Under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, a 'minority' means a community notified as such by the Central Government under which provision?
144.x: The Act does not define minority; under Section 2(c) a minority is any community notified by the Central Government. Section 3(2) requires five members including the Chairperson to be from minority communities; Article 29(1) protects the language, script or culture of any section of citizens; Section 9(1) of the Waqf Act, 1995 concerns the Central Waqf Council.
144.tq: Sec 2(c) = Centre notifies minorities (criticised as 'unbridled power').
xs: Under **Section 2(c)** of the NCM Act, a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government** — option **(1)**.
**Section 3(2)** concerns minority members of the Commission; **Art. 29(1)** protects culture; **Section 9(1)** of the Waqf Act 1995 is the **Central Waqf Council**.
xa: Critics say Sec. 2(c) gives the Centre **"unbridled power"**, uneasy with **T.M.A. Pai**.
The Constitution uses "minority" in **Arts 29, 30, 350A, 350B** without defining it.

144.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function or power of the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions?
o: Determining the minority status of an educational institution
Adjudicating disputes relating to affiliation with universities
Amending the Constitution to define the term minority
144.x: The Commission can determine minority status, decide affiliation disputes and issue minority certificates, and it has civil court powers. It has no power to amend the Constitution.
144.tq: Find the option outside the statutory and quasi-judicial jurisdiction of the body.
xs: **Amending the Constitution to define minority** is NOT an NCMEI power — option **(3)**.
The **NCMEI** (Act of **2004**) decides **minority status** of institutions, **affiliation disputes** with universities and **minority certificate** issues, with **civil court powers**.
xa: It has a **quasi-judicial** role.

144.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding institutions related to minority affairs?
1. The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions was established under an Act of 2004.
2. Statutory State Minority Commissions exist in 19 States/Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
144.x: Both statements are correct. The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions is associated with the 2004 Act, and statutory State Minority Commissions exist in 19 States/Union Territories including Andhra Pradesh.
144.tq: Combine two independently verifiable institutional facts and test the ‘both’ option.
xs: Both are correct — option **(3)**.
The **NCMEI** is statutory under the **NCMEI Act, 2004**; statutory **State Minorities Commissions** exist in **19** States/UTs, including **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: ⚠ The APPSC 2016 key said **18**; older notes **15**.
Others include **Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sachar Committee:
1. It was set up in 2005 by the Prime Minister.
2. It was chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar.
3. Its report was submitted in November 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The committee was set up in 2005, chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar, and submitted its report in November 2006.
144.tq: Check the committee’s establishment, chair and report date separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Sachar Committee** was set up in **2005** (**March 2005**) by the **Prime Minister**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was chaired by **Justice Rajinder Sachar**.
Statement 3 is correct: it reported in **November 2006**. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: Mandate: the **social, economic and educational status of Muslims**.
Proposals: **Equal Opportunity Commission**, **National Data Bank**, **Assessment and Monitoring Authority**.
⚠ **2006** = Sachar report; **2007** = Ranganath Misra; **2013-14** = Kundu.

144.s: Which Muslim group was identified as requiring attention similar to that given to Hindu Other Backward Classes?
o: All Muslim groups equally under the same classification
144.x: The Ajlaf, described as backward Muslims or commoners and lower-caste converts, were identified as requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
144.tq: Separate Ajlaf from Arzal by matching the group with the specific policy concern.
xs: The **Ajlaf** (backward Muslims — commoners/lower-caste converts) need attention similar to **Hindu OBCs** — option **(1)**.
The **Ashraf** are upper/claimed foreign origin; the **Arzal** are Dalit converts, the **most deprived**.
xa: ⚠ **Ajlaf** ≈ OBC; **Arzal** ≈ SC.
This classification was asked in **APPSC G2 2024**.

144.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ashraf — upper or claimed foreign origin
Ajlaf — the most deprived Dalit Muslim group
144.x: Arzal, rather than Ajlaf, was described as the Dalit Muslim group and the most deprived category. Ajlaf was identified as a backward group requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
144.tq: Use the confusable-pair trap by checking the precise description of each group.
xs: **Ajlaf — the most deprived Dalit Muslim group** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
The most deprived **Dalit Muslims** are the **Arzal**; the **Ajlaf** are commoners/lower-caste converts comparable to **Hindu OBCs**.
xa: **Ashraf:** upper; claimed foreign/upper-caste origin.
⚠ **Ajlaf** ≈ OBC; **Arzal** ≈ SC (APPSC G2 2024).

144.s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal associated with the Sachar Committee?
144.x: The Sachar Committee proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission, National Data Bank and Assessment and Monitoring Authority. A National Linguistic Minorities Commission was not listed among its proposals.
144.tq: Eliminate the option belonging to a different institutional theme.
xs: A **National Linguistic Minorities Commission** was NOT a Sachar proposal — option **(4)**.
Sachar proposed an **Equal Opportunity Commission**, a **National Data Bank** and an **Assessment and Monitoring Authority**.
xa: It also recommended a **Diversity Index**.
The **Kundu Committee** (**2013-14**) repeated the call for an Equal Opportunity Commission and anti-discrimination law.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Sachar Committee
B. National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities
C. Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee

List-II (Chair or key association)
1. Rajinder Sachar
2. Justice Ranganath Misra
3. Amitabh Kundu

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: The Sachar Committee was chaired by Rajinder Sachar, the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities by Justice Ranganath Misra, and the Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee by Amitabh Kundu.
144.tq: Start from the sure chair-combination and eliminate codes containing a swapped committee.
xs: Correct matching: **A-1, B-2, C-3** — option **(1)**.

**Sachar Committee** — **Rajinder Sachar**; **National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities** — Justice **Ranganath Misra**; **Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee** — Prof. **Amitabh Kundu**.
xa: Reports: Sachar **2006**, Ranganath Misra **2007**, Kundu **2013-14**.
Ranganath Misra suggested a **15%** quota for minorities.

144.s: The Ranganath Misra Commission was associated with which of the following recommendations?
o: Replacement of all State languages by Hindi
A 15% reservation and delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion
Creation of the National Data Bank for census purposes only
144.x: The National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities, chaired by Justice Ranganath Misra, suggested a 15% quota for minorities and delinking SC status from religion.
144.tq: Match the commission with its distinctive recommendation rather than its general subject.
xs: The **Ranganath Misra Commission** suggested a **15%** reservation for minorities and **delinking SC status from religion** — option **(3)**.
It sought concrete steps for socially and economically backward sections among religious and linguistic minorities.
xa: It reported in **2007**.
The **National Data Bank** was a **Sachar** proposal.

144.s:
The PM’s New 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities is associated with which of the following objectives?
1. Education and a fair share in economic activity and jobs
2. Better living conditions
3. Prevention of communal violence
4. Earmarking of outlays for minorities

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: The programme, introduced in 2006, covers education, economic activity and jobs, better living conditions, prevention of communal violence and earmarking of outlays for minorities.
144.tq: Treat each listed objective independently; the comprehensive combination is supported here.
xs: All four apply — option **(4)**, **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The **PM's New 15 Point Programme** (**2006**) aims at **education**, a fair share in **jobs and economic activity**, better **living conditions** and **preventing communal riots**.
About **15%** of targets and outlays in chosen schemes are **earmarked** for minorities.
xa: **Review committees** monitor it.
The **Ministry of Minority Affairs** also dates from **2006**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the PM's New 15 Point Programme:
1. It includes prevention of communal riots among its aims.
2. About 15 percent of targets and outlays in selected schemes are intended for minorities.
3. Review committees monitor its implementation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. The programme includes communal harmony, earmarks about 15 percent of targets and outlays in selected schemes, and is monitored by review committees.
144.tq: Combine objectives, earmarking and monitoring instead of treating the programme as a single-sector scheme.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **preventing communal riots** is one of its four aims.
Statement 2 is correct: about **15%** of targets and outlays are earmarked for minorities.
Statement 3 is correct: **review committees** monitor it. So **1, 2 and 3** — option **(4)**.
xa: The programme dates from **2006**.
⚠ The **Ranganath Misra** **15%** figure is a reservation proposal, not this earmarking.

144.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Hamari Dharohar — preserving the heritage of minorities
Seekho aur Kamao — skill upgradation and placement
Nai Manzil — education and skilling for school dropouts
Nai Roshni — free coaching after clearing civil services preliminaries
144.x: Nai Roshni concerns leadership training for minority women. Free coaching and post-preliminary support are associated with Naya Savera and Nai Udaan.
144.tq: Reject the option that swaps the benefits of two neighbouring minority schemes.
xs: **Nai Roshni — free coaching after prelims** is wrong — option **(4)**.
Nai Roshni is **leadership training for minority women**; coaching is **Naya Savera** and post-prelims support is **Nai Udaan**.
xa: Hamari Dharohar (**2015**), Seekho aur Kamao (**2014**), Nai Manzil (**2015**) are correctly matched.
All five merged into **PM VIKAS** (**2022**).

144.s: PM Jan Vikas Karyakram was restructured from which earlier programme?
144.x: PMJVK was restructured from the Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MSDP), which dates from 2008-09.
144.tq: Use the predecessor-successor relationship to identify the correct programme.
xs: **PMJVK** was restructured in **May 2018** from the **Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MSDP)** of **2008-09** — option **(1)**.
The others are MoMA skilling, leadership and coaching schemes.
xa: It covers **870** minority concentration blocks + **321** towns, now all districts incl. **112 Aspirational Districts**.
**80%** of funds go to education, health and skills.

144.s:
Which of the following statements regarding PM VIKAS is correct?
1. It stands for Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan.
2. It is a Central Sector scheme introduced in 2022.
3. It merges five minority schemes.
4. It is intended to run until 2025-26.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: PM VIKAS means Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan, was introduced in 2022 as a Central Sector scheme, merges five schemes and is intended to run until 2025-26.
144.tq: Verify the expansion, type, year, merger and duration before choosing the combination.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)**.
**PM VIKAS** = **Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan**, a **2022** **Central Sector** scheme merging **five** schemes, running until **2025-26**.
xa: Merged: **Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, Nai Manzil**.
About **9 lakh** beneficiaries; **33%** of skilling seats for women; linked to **NMDFC** loans.

144.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the five schemes merged into PM VIKAS?
144.x: PM VIKAS merges Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil. PMJVK is not one of the five merged schemes.
144.tq: Find the area-based infrastructure scheme that does not belong to the merged skill and heritage package.
xs: **PM Jan Vikas Karyakram** is NOT among the five merged into PM VIKAS — option **(1)**.
PM VIKAS merges **Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, Nai Manzil**.
xa: ⚠ **PM VIKAS** = Central Sector; **PMJVK** = Centrally Sponsored.
Critics say minority schemes lost visibility after the merger.

144.s: Which one of the following correctly describes PMJVK?
o: It is a Central Sector Scheme limited to minority students pursuing higher education.
It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for area development in minority concentration areas.
It is a constitutional programme implemented by the Election Commission.
It is a State scheme restricted to urban minority households.
144.x: PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at area development in minority concentration areas.
144.tq: Identify the scheme from its funding pattern and broad area-development objective.
xs: **PMJVK** is a **Centrally Sponsored** infrastructure scheme for **minority-concentration areas** — option **(2)**.
It benefits **all residents**, not just minority students or urban households.
xa: Restructured in **May 2018** from **MSDP (2008-09)**.
**80%** to education, health and skills; **33-40%** for women.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-YASASVI:
1. It supports top-class school and college education.
2. It includes hostel support.
3. Thirty percent of its slots are earmarked for girls.
4. Its cost-sharing ratio is 60:40.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All four statements are correct. PM-YASASVI includes top-class education and hostel support, reserves 30 percent of slots for girls and follows a 60:40 cost-sharing ratio.
144.tq: Check both qualitative benefits and quantitative design features before selecting the coded option.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)**.
**PM-YASASVI** supports **top-class school/college education** and **hostels**, keeps **30%** of slots for **girls**, and shares cost **60:40**.
xa: Pre-matric (Class IX-X) = **Rs 4,000**.
**SHREYAS** funds **8,571** SC students at IITs and IIMs.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NBCFDC was established in 1992.
2. NBCFDC functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
3. Both NBCFDC and NMDFC lend through State Channelising Agencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: Statement 1 is correct: NBCFDC was set up in 1992. Statement 2 is wrong: NBCFDC is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; it is NMDFC that is under the Ministry of Minority Affairs. Statement 3 is correct: both lend through State Channelising Agencies. Hence A; B omits statement 3, C and D wrongly include statement 2.
144.tq: NBCFDC = MoSJE; NMDFC = MoMA; both via SCAs.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NBCFDC** was set up in **1992**.
Statement 2 is wrong: NBCFDC is under **MoSJE**; **NMDFC** is the one under **MoMA**.
Statement 3 is correct: both lend through **State Channelising Agencies**. So **1 and 3 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: NBCFDC schemes: **New Swarnima** (women), **Saksham** (young professionals).
Comparable bodies: **NSFDC** (1989, SCs), **NSTFDC** (2001, STs).

144.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to NBCFDC schemes?

1. New Swarnima — Women beneficiaries
2. Saksham — Young professionals
3. Virasat — Artisans

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: New Swarnima is intended for women and Saksham for young professionals. Virasat loans are associated with NMDFC and artisans, so statement 3 is incorrect in this context.
144.tq: Split the options by identifying the institution-specific scheme before checking the beneficiary group.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: **New Swarnima** — women; **Saksham** — young professionals (both **NBCFDC**).
Pair 3 is wrong: **Virasat** loans for artisans belong to **NMDFC**. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: NBCFDC (**1992**, MoSJE) lends through **State Channelising Agencies**.
NMDFC also gives **education loans** and **micro-finance**.

144.s: PM Vishwakarma primarily targets:
144.x: PM Vishwakarma is intended for artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades. It is not a fishermen's scheme.
144.tq: Discriminate between the target group and the tempting but incorrect fishermen association.
xs: **PM Vishwakarma** targets **artisans and craftspeople** in **18 trades** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Trap:** it is **not a fishermen's scheme** (APPSC G2 2023).
xa: Toolkit incentive: **Rs 15,000**.
Credit: collateral-free **Rs 1 lakh + Rs 2 lakh** at **5%**.

144.s: Under PM Vishwakarma, the credit support is structured as:
o: Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 5 lakh without any interest
Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 2 lakh at 5 percent interest
Rs 15,000 followed by Rs 2 lakh at 12 percent interest
Rs 2 lakh followed by Rs 1 lakh at 10 percent interest
144.x: The scheme provides collateral-free credit of Rs 1 lakh initially and an additional Rs 2 lakh, with the credit carrying a 5 percent interest rate.
144.tq: Read the staged amount and interest rate together to avoid reversing the figures.
xs: Credit is collateral-free **Rs 1 lakh** followed by **Rs 2 lakh** at **5%** interest — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Rs 15,000** is the **toolkit** incentive, not a loan.
xa: Launched **17 Sept 2023** for **18 trades**.
Training includes a **stipend**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about PM Vishwakarma:
1. The Ministry of MSME is the nodal ministry.
2. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship also implements the scheme.
3. The Department of Financial Services is associated with its implementation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements are correct. MSME is the nodal ministry, while MSDE and the Department of Financial Services are also involved in implementation.
144.tq: Test nodal responsibility separately from the other implementing agencies.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)**.
**MSME** is the **nodal ministry**; **MSDE** and the **Department of Financial Services** also implement it.
xa: Over **1 crore** artisans registered.
Registration through **CSCs**.

144.s: The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, in relation to Denotified Tribes, was:
144.x: Denotified Tribes had been branded under the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, which was repealed in 1952.
144.tq: Pair the historical enactment with its repeal year and beware of confusing repeal with replacement.
xs: The **Criminal Tribes Act 1871**, which branded **DNTs**, was **repealed in 1952** — option **(2)**.
So it was neither expanded nor constitutionalised.
xa: **Census 2027** will count DNTs.
**Renke Commission** (report **2008**) was the first DNT commission.

144.s: Which commission was the first to examine the condition of Denotified Tribes among the commissions mentioned below?
144.x: The Renke Commission, whose report was submitted in 2008, was the first such commission mentioned for Denotified Tribes.
144.tq: Use the ‘first’ marker to distinguish the earlier Renke Commission from the later Idate Commission.
xs: The **Renke Commission** (report **2008**) was the **first** DNT commission — option **(3)**.
The **Idate Commission** came later (**2014-17**); **J.B. Koshy** concerned **Christian minorities** in Kerala; **Sachar** concerned **Muslims**.
xa: Idate: about **1,200** DNTs already in SC/ST/OBC lists; **267-268** never classified.
DNTs were branded under the **Criminal Tribes Act 1871**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the findings associated with the Idate Commission:

1. About 1,200 DNTs were already included in SC, ST or OBC lists.
2. About 267-268 DNTs had never been classified.
3. All DNTs were found to be included in the Scheduled Tribe list.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The Commission found about 1,200 DNTs already in SC/ST/OBC lists and 267-268 never classified. It did not find that all DNTs were included in the Scheduled Tribe list.
144.tq: Reject the absolute statement and retain the two specific numerical findings.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the **Idate Commission (2014-17)** found about **1,200** DNTs already in **SC/ST/OBC** lists and **267-268** never classified.
Statement 3 is wrong: many were never classified at all. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: The first DNT commission was **Renke** (**2008**).
**SEED** (**2022**) is the DNT welfare scheme.

144.s:
Which of the following is the correct combination regarding the SEED scheme?

1. It was launched in 2022.
2. Its stated outlay is Rs 200 crore.
3. It covers coaching, health insurance, livelihoods and housing.
4. The income ceiling is below Rs 2.5 lakh.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: SEED was launched in 2022 with an outlay of Rs 200 crore, an income criterion below Rs 2.5 lakh, and provisions for coaching, health insurance, livelihoods and housing.
144.tq: Verify the year, amount, eligibility and objective separately before choosing the complete combination.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)**.
**SEED** (**2022**): **Rs 200 crore**; income below **Rs 2.5 lakh**; covers **coaching, health insurance, livelihoods, housing**.
xa: Only **Rs 69.3 crore** spent in five years.
Reason: States do not issue **DNT certificates**.

144.s: The principal reason cited for the low expenditure under SEED was that:
o: States did not issue DNT certificates
the scheme covered only urban areas
the Union Government withdrew the scheme
beneficiaries were excluded from health insurance
144.x: Low expenditure was attributed to the failure of States to issue certificates for Denotified Tribes.
144.tq: Link the implementation shortfall to the administrative bottleneck rather than to the scheme’s objectives.
xs: SEED was under-spent because **States did not issue DNT certificates** — option **(1)**.
Only **Rs 69.3 crore** of **Rs 200 crore** was spent in five years.
xa: A special **DNT policy** was demanded in **Vijayawada**.
**Census 2027** will count DNTs.

144.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Waqf Act, 1954
B. Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2013
C. Waqf Act, 1995
D. Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025
144.x: The correct sequence is Waqf Act 1954, Waqf Act 1995, Waqf (Amendment) Act 2013, and Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025.
144.tq: Place the parent enactments before their later amendments.
xs: Order: **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)**.
**Waqf Act 1954** → **Waqf Act 1995** (current parent law) → **Wakf (Amendment) Act 2013** → **2025** changes.
xa: The **Central Waqf Council** became statutory in **1964**.
UMEED portal launched **June 2025**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the Wakf (Amendment) Act, 2013:
1. It barred sale, gift, mortgage, exchange and transfer of waqf property.
2. It barred leasing of all waqf property without exception.
3. It enabled the Central Waqf Council to direct State Waqf Boards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2013 amendment barred sale, gift, mortgage, exchange and transfer of waqf property. Statement 2 is wrong: leasing was allowed, except for properties such as mosques and dargahs. Statement 3 is correct: the Central Waqf Council can direct State Boards. Hence B; A omits statement 3, C and D wrongly include statement 2.
144.tq: 2013: no alienation, leasing allowed with exceptions, Council can direct Boards.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the 2013 Act bars **sale, gift, mortgage, exchange, transfer** of waqf property.
Statement 2 is wrong: **leasing is allowed**, except for **mosques, dargahs** etc.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Central Waqf Council** can **direct State Boards**. So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: The Council was formed under Section 8A of the 1954 Act, now **Section 9(1)** of the 1995 Act.
The 2025 law put all waqf properties on a **central portal within 6 months**.

144.s: Which of the following statements about the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 is correct?
o: Only Muslim members could thereafter serve on the Central Waqf Council and State Boards.
Waqf by user was abolished even for all properties registered before the amendment.
Waqf by user survived only for properties registered before the law.
The Act prohibited the use of any central portal for waqf properties.
144.x: Under the 2025 Act, waqf by user survived only for properties registered before the law. The Act also provided for non-Muslim members and a central portal.
144.tq: Reject absolute statements by identifying the statutory qualification.
xs: Under the 2025 law, **waqf by user survives only for properties registered before the law** — option **(3)**.
It **allowed non-Muslim** members and required a **central portal**, so the other options are wrong.
xa: The **SC interim order (Sep 2025)** did not stay removal of waqf-by-user.
All waqf properties go on a **central portal within 6 months** (UMEED, **June 2025**).

144.s:
Consider the following provisions associated with the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025:
1. Non-Muslim members were allowed in the Central Waqf Council and State Boards.
2. At least two non-Muslim members were required in each State Board.
3. All waqf properties were required to be placed on a central portal within six months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: All three statements describe provisions of the 2025 amendment. The UMEED portal was subsequently launched in June 2025.
144.tq: Test composition requirements together with a time-bound digital requirement.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)**.
**Non-Muslim** members are allowed in the Central Council and State Boards, **at least two** in each Board; all properties go on a **central portal within 6 months**.
xa: The **UMEED** portal was launched in **June 2025**.
⚠ The **SC (Sep 2025)** capped non-Muslims at **3** in State Boards and **4** in the Central Council.

144.s: The Central Waqf Council is best described as:
o: A temporary executive committee established in 1995 to conduct elections
A statutory body established in 1964 to advise the Centre on State Waqf Boards
A judicial body established in 2025 to decide all land disputes
A constitutional body established in 1950 to supervise courts
144.x: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body established in 1964. Its principal role is to advise the Central Government on State Waqf Boards.
144.tq: Distinguish a statutory advisory body from constitutional and judicial bodies.
xs: The **Central Waqf Council** is a **statutory** body of **1964** that **advises the Centre on State Waqf Boards** — option **(2)**.
It was set up under Section 8A of the **1954** Act, now **Section 9(1)** of the **Waqf Act 1995**.
xa: Since **2013**, it can **direct** State Boards.
The 2025 law allows **non-Muslim** members; SC cap = **4** in the Central Council.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court’s interim order of September 2025 concerning the Waqf (Amendment) Act:
1. It stayed the five-years-practising-Islam condition.
2. It stayed the Collector’s power referred to in the amendment.
3. It stayed the removal of waqf by user.
4. It accepted the change applying the Limitation Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
144.x: The Supreme Court stayed the five-years-practising-Islam condition and the Collector’s power, and accepted the Limitation Act change. It did not stay the removal of waqf by user.
144.tq: Find the one reversed interim-order detail before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the **SC interim order (Sep 2025)** stayed the **5-years-practising-Islam** condition and the **Collector's power**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it **did not stay** the removal of **waqf by user**.
Statement 4 is correct: it **accepted the Limitation Act** change. So **1, 2 and 4 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: It capped non-Muslims at **3** in State Boards and **4** in the Central Council.
⚠ The Act itself requires **at least two** non-Muslims in each Board.

144.s: Urdu was made the second official language of Andhra Pradesh under which law?
144.x: Urdu is AP's second official language under the AP Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022. The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 bifurcated the State; the Official Languages Act, 1963 deals with the Union's official languages; the 7th Amendment, 1956 inserted Articles 350A and 350B.
144.tq: Urdu = AP second official language, 2022 amendment.
xs: **Urdu** is AP's **second official language** under the **AP Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022** — option **(1)**.
The **7th Amendment (1956)** instead inserted Arts **350A** and **350B**.
xa: AP runs **Urdu-Ghar-cum-Shadikhanas** and **36** computer training centres across **26** districts.
AP has **6 pre-matric and 10 post-matric** minority hostels.

144.s:
With reference to Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. G.O. 1065 (August 2026) provides 33.33% BC reservation in urban local body polls.
2. The Assembly resolved to seek 33% BC seats in legislatures.
3. AP's Backward Classes comprise 138 communities in Groups A-D.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: Statement 1 is correct: G.O. 1065 gives 33.33% BC reservation in ULB polls. Statement 2 is correct: the Assembly resolved to seek 33% BC seats in legislatures. Statement 3 is wrong: the 138 BC communities are in Groups A-E, not A-D. Hence B; A omits statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3.
144.tq: 33.33% = ULB polls (G.O. 1065); 33% = legislature demand; Groups A-E.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **G.O. 1065 (Aug 2026)** gives **33.33%** BC reservation in **ULB** polls.
Statement 2 is correct: the Assembly resolved to seek **33%** BC seats in legislatures.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **138** communities are in **Groups A-E**, not A-D. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: BCs = **43.17%** of AP's population.
A **Swarnakara** Welfare and Development Corporation has been set up.

144.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised because it gives the Centre:
o: exclusive power to appoint State minority commissions
power to amend the Constitution without Parliament
144.x: Section 2(c) has been criticised as giving the Centre ‘unbridled power’ to notify minorities, raising concerns in the context of T.M.A. Pai.
144.tq: Match the statutory provision with the specific constitutional criticism rather than a broader unrelated power.
xs: Critics say **Section 2(c)** gives the Centre **"unbridled power"** to **notify minorities** — option **(1)**.
It sits uneasily with **T.M.A. Pai (2002)**, which made the **State** the unit for minority status.
xa: The NCM Act does not define minority; a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government**.
States may notify their own minorities — **Jains** in **11 States** before 2014.

144.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly presents the comparative chronology and beneficiary groups of the development finance corporations?

1. NSFDC — 1989 — Scheduled Castes
2. NBCFDC — 1992 — Backward Classes
3. NSTFDC — 2001 — Scheduled Tribes
4. NMDFC — Minorities

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
144.x: NSFDC was established in 1989 for Scheduled Castes, NBCFDC in 1992 for Backward Classes, NSTFDC in 2001 for Scheduled Tribes, and NMDFC serves minorities.
144.tq: Build the comparison from the beneficiary group first, then verify the year where given.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
**NSFDC** (**1989**, SCs), **NBCFDC** (**1992**, BCs), **NSTFDC** (**2001**, STs), **NMDFC** (minorities).
xa: NBCFDC is under **MoSJE**; NMDFC is a **Section 8 company** under **MoMA**.
Both NBCFDC and NMDFC lend through **State Channelising Agencies**.

144.s: The merger of separate minority schemes into PM VIKAS has been criticised mainly because it:
o: reduced the number of minority communities notified by the Centre
made separate minority schemes lose visibility
144.x: The criticism is that separate minority schemes lost visibility after being merged into PM VIKAS.
144.tq: Identify the precise criticism rather than converting a visibility concern into abolition or termination.
xs: Minority schemes **lost visibility** after merger into **PM VIKAS** — option **(3)**.
PM VIKAS (**2022**) merged **Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, Nai Manzil**.
xa: Another criticism: **SEED** was under-spent (only **Rs 69.3 crore**).
PM VIKAS runs until **2025-26** with about **9 lakh** beneficiaries.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Sachar Committee was established in 2005 under Rajinder Sachar to study the socio-economic status of Muslims.
II. The Ranganath Misra Commission was established in 2004 under Ranganath Misra to study religious and linguistic minorities.
III. The Gopal Singh Committee submitted its report on minorities in 1983.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: All three are correct: Sachar (2005) studied the status of Muslims, Ranganath Misra (2004) religious and linguistic minorities, and the Gopal Singh panel on minorities reported in 1983.
144.tq: Match each minority body to its chair.
n: The Sachar Committee was established in 2005. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Rajinder Sachar chaired the Sachar Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Ranganath Misra Commission was established in 2004. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Ranganath Misra chaired the Ranganath Misra Commission. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Ranganath Misra Commission studied religious and linguistic minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Gopal Singh Committee was established in 1983. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Gopal Singh chaired the Gopal Singh Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
I: the **Sachar Committee** (**2005**, **Rajinder Sachar**) studied the **socio-economic** status of the **Muslim community** — correct.
II: the **Ranganath Misra Commission** (**2004**) studied **religious and linguistic minorities** — correct.
III: the **Gopal Singh Committee** on **minority welfare** is dated **1983** — correct.
xa: Sachar reported in **November 2006**; Ranganath Misra in **2007**.
Ranganath Misra recommended **15%** reservation for minorities and **10%** for Muslims.
**Kundu Committee** (**2013-14**) reviewed Sachar's implementation.

144.s: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in which areas?
144.x: The Sachar Committee found Muslims badly under-represented in public jobs and higher education, against their share of the population.
144.tq: Recall the Sachar findings.
n: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in public employment. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in higher education. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee concerned minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee assessed the educational status of the Muslim community in India. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: The **Sachar Committee** found **severe under-representation** of Muslims in **public employment** and **higher education** — option **(1)**.
It assessed the **socio-economic** and **educational status** of the **Muslim community**.
xa: It proposed an **Equal Opportunity Commission**, **National Data Bank** and **Diversity Index**.
**Ajlafs** need attention like Hindu OBCs; **Arzals** (Dalit Muslims) are the most deprived.
⚠ **Ajlaf** ≈ OBC; **Arzal** ≈ SC; **Ashraf** = upper.

144.s:

o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true

144.tq: Discriminate the year set up from the report year.
n: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee was constituted in 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee was a Prime Minister’s High-Level Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: Statement A is false and Statement B is true — option **(4)**.
A: the Sachar Committee was set up in **March 2005** (some notes say **2006**, the report year) — keyed false.
B: it was a **Prime Minister's High-Level Committee** — true.
xa: Report: **November 2006**.
It was the **first national data-based committee** on minorities.
⚠ **2006** = Sachar report; **2007** = Ranganath Misra report.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First National Integration Council
(b) First Constitutional Provision for Minority Rights
(c) First Communal Award
(d) First National Foundation for Communal Harmony

List-II
(i) 1932
(ii) 1961
(iii) Articles 29 and 30
(iv) 1992
144.x: The National Integration Council began in 1961, Articles 29 and 30 first protected minority rights, the Communal Award came in 1932, and the National Foundation for Communal Harmony in 1992. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
144.tq: Match each first to its year or Article.
n: The National Integration Council was first established in 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Articles 29 and 30 were the first Constitutional provisions for minority rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Communal Award was the first Communal Award in 1932. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Foundation for Communal Harmony was first established in 1992. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(2)**.
**National Integration Council**: first established **1961**; first constitutional provisions for minority rights: **Articles 29 and 30**.
**Communal Award**: **1932**; **National Foundation for Communal Harmony**: **1992**.
xa: The NIC's first Chairman was **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
**Article 51A(e)** is the first constitutional duty **promoting harmony**.
**NHRC**: first established **1993**.

144.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Constitutional protection of a section's distinct language, script or culture
(b) First Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities
(c) Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
(d) First Commission on Religious and Linguistic Minorities

List-II
(i) Article 30
(ii) Ranganath Misra Commission
(iii) Article 29
(iv) Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan
144.x: Article 29 protects a section's distinct language, script or culture, Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan was the first NCM chairman, Article 30 gives minorities the right to run educational institutions, and the Ranganath Misra Commission studied religious and linguistic minorities. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
144.tq: Discriminate Articles 29–30 from Article 30 alone.
n: Articles 29 and 30 were the first Constitutional provisions for minority rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan was the first Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Article 30 was the first Minority Educational Rights provision. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Ranganath Misra Commission was the first Commission on Religious and Linguistic Minorities in 2004. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(3)**.
**Article 29** protects a section's distinct **language, script or culture**; **Article 30** lets minorities **establish and administer educational institutions**.
**Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan** was the **first NCM Chairman**; the **Ranganath Misra Commission** was the **first Commission** on religious and linguistic minorities.
xa: ⚠ **Art. 29** = all citizens; **Art. 30** = only minorities.
**Art. 29(2)**: no denial of admission on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language.
The **44th Amendment** added **Art. 30(1A)**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements: I. The first National Commission for Minorities was established in 1992. II. The Prime Minister’s 15-Point Programme for Minorities was first introduced in 1983. III. The Sachar Committee was the first national data-based committee on minorities and was established in 2005. IV. The first National Foundation for Communal Harmony was established in 1992.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: All four are correct: the NCM and the National Foundation for Communal Harmony date from 1992, the original 15-Point Programme from 1983 (the New 15-Point Programme followed in 2006), and the Sachar Committee from 2005.
144.tq: Recall the minority firsts.
n: The first National Commission for Minorities was established in 1992. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Prime Minister’s New 15-Point Programme for Minorities was first introduced in 1983. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Sachar Committee was the first national data-based committee on minorities in 2005. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Foundation for Communal Harmony was first established in 1992. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(1)**.
I and IV: the **NCM** and the **National Foundation for Communal Harmony** were both first established in **1992**.
II: the **PM's 15-Point Programme** was first introduced in **1983** (the **New** programme dates from **2006**).
III: the **Sachar Committee** (**2005**) was the **first national data-based committee** on minorities.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: the first statutory NCM was constituted in **1993**.
The New 15-Point Programme earmarks about **15%** of targets for minorities.
**Ministry of Minority Affairs**: **2006**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PM-VIKAS:
I. It supports convergence of skill development.
II. It provides artisan support.
III. It supports entrepreneurship.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: All three are correct: PM-VIKAS brings together skill training, support for artisans and entrepreneurship for minorities.
144.tq: Recall the three PM-VIKAS components.
n: PM-VIKAS converges skill development, artisan support, entrepreneurship, and education. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**PM-VIKAS** **converges** **skill development**, **artisan support**, **entrepreneurship** and **education** for the **six notified minorities**.
xa: PM VIKAS (**2022**) merges **Seekho aur Kamao**, **USTTAD**, **Hamari Dharohar**, **Nai Roshni** and **Nai Manzil**.
It is a **Central Sector** scheme; **33%** of skilling seats for women.
⚠ **PMJVK** is **Centrally Sponsored**.

144.s: Which of the following statements about Naya Savera & Nai Udaan is incorrect?
o: It is meant for students clearing UPSC and SSC Main examinations.
It provides financial support to minority students.
It provides free coaching to minority students.
It is associated with the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
144.x: Option A is incorrect: Naya Savera and Nai Udaan support minority students who clear the UPSC or SSC prelims, not the mains.
144.tq: Watch for 'Main' replacing 'prelims'.
n: The nodal ministry for Naya Savera and Nai Udaan is the Ministry of Minority Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide free coaching for minority students clearing UPSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide free coaching for minority students clearing SSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide financial support for minority students clearing UPSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide financial support for minority students clearing SSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Minorities are a target group of welfare mechanisms. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera is a key scheme for minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Nai Udaan is a key scheme for minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the schemes are for students clearing **UPSC and SSC Main** — option **(1)**; they support those clearing the **prelims**.
**Naya Savera** and **Nai Udaan** give **free coaching** and **financial support** to **minority students** under **Minority Affairs**.
xa: ⚠ **Nai Roshni** = women's leadership; **Nai Manzil** = dropouts; **Nai Udaan** = after prelims; **Naya Savera** = coaching.
**Seekho aur Kamao** (**2014**): skilling linked to jobs.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The SEED Scheme Portal enables online applications for DNT community health insurance, coaching and dwelling assistance.
Statement B: The SEED Scheme Portal is administered by the National Testing Agency.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true

n: The SEED Scheme Portal is a digital platform for OBC, EBC, and DNT communities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is the nodal agency for the SEED Scheme Portal. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SEED Scheme Portal provides a direct online application platform. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SEED Scheme Portal supports health insurance for DNT communities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SEED Scheme Portal supports coaching for DNT communities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SEED Scheme Portal supports dwelling assistance for DNT communities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]

xs: Statement A is true and Statement B is false — option **(3)**.

SEED (**2022**): **Rs 200 crore**, but only **Rs 69.3 crore** spent in five years.
SEED came from the **Idate Commission**.

The PM-YASASVI Portal is a digital platform for OBC, EBC, and nomadic-tribe students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The National Testing Agency is the nodal agency for the PM-YASASVI Portal. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-YASASVI Portal provides a centralized scholarship application system. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-YASASVI Portal provides a scholarship disbursement system. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]

The PM-YASASVI Portal serves EBC students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]

It is a **centralized scholarship application** and **disbursement system** run by the **National Testing Agency**.
xa: PM-YASASVI (**2021**, MoSJE): family income below **Rs 2.5 lakh**; cost shared **60:40**.
