152.tq: Test whether the candidate can combine strategic, economic and regional-security drivers.
xs: All three are drivers — option **(4)**.
**Countering China**, **new markets** and **instability in West and Central Asia** (**UPSC**).
xa: Look East: early **1990s** (**1991-92**), **P.V. Narasimha Rao**.
Upgraded to **Act East** in **2014** (East Asia Summit, Myanmar).

152.s:
With reference to ASEAN connectivity, consider the following projects:
1. Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project
2. India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway
3. Akhaura-Agartala railway link
Which of the projects given above are ASEAN-linked projects?
152.x: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Project and India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway are ASEAN-linked connectivity projects. The Akhaura-Agartala rail link is associated with Bangladesh.
152.tq: Use the country-partnership distinction to eliminate the project linked with Bangladesh.
xs: **Kaladan Multi-Modal** and the **Trilateral Highway** are ASEAN-linked — **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
⚠ **Akhaura-Agartala rail** is with **Bangladesh**, not ASEAN (**UPSC 2026** answer "1 and 2").
xa: The **North-East** is the gateway to **ASEAN**.
**Kaladan** and the Trilateral Highway are also Neighbourhood First examples (UPSC).

152.s: The Neighbourhood First policy was launched in 2014, as symbolised by:
o: inviting SAARC leaders to the Prime Minister's swearing-in ceremony in May 2014
inviting BIMSTEC leaders to the 2014 swearing-in ceremony
holding the first India-Central Asia Summit in 2014
152.x: The policy was associated with inviting SAARC leaders to the Prime Minister's swearing-in ceremony in May 2014. BIMSTEC leaders were invited in 2019.
152.tq: Use the year and regional grouping together to distinguish SAARC from BIMSTEC.
xs: **Neighbourhood First** (**2014**) was marked by inviting **SAARC leaders** to the PM's **swearing-in** in **May 2014** — option **(1)**.
**BIMSTEC** leaders were invited in **2019**, not 2014.
The first **India-Central Asia Summit** was **2022**; I2U2's first summit was also **2022**.
xa: Aim: **physical, digital and people-to-people connectivity** across South Asia.
Roots in the **Gujral Doctrine**: non-reciprocity, non-interference.

152.s: Which of the following principles is associated with the Gujral Doctrine and forms part of the roots of Neighbourhood First?
o: Strict reciprocity in every bilateral agreement
Non-reciprocity, non-interference and no territory being used against a neighbour
Non-interference only, without any territorial principle
152.x: The Gujral Doctrine emphasised non-reciprocity, non-interference and ensuring that a country's territory is not used against a neighbour.
152.tq: Select the complete set of principles rather than a partial or reversed formulation.
xs: The **Gujral Doctrine** = **non-reciprocity + non-interference + no territory used against a neighbour** — option **(2)**.
It is the **roots of Neighbourhood First**.
Option (4) omits the territorial principle; option (1) is the opposite of non-reciprocity.
xa: **Neighbourhood First** began in **2014** with SAARC leaders at the swearing-in.
BIMSTEC leaders were invited in **2019**.

152.s: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers was hosted by which country and held at which city?
152.x: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019. Afghanistan was also invited.
152.tq: Pair the host country with the city rather than confusing it with the policy-launch venue.
xs: **Uzbekistan** hosted the first India-Central Asia **Dialogue** at **Samarkand** (**2019**) — option **(3)**.
**Afghanistan** was invited (**APPSC 2019**: "Uzbekistan organised the first Dialogue" = correct).
**Bishkek** is where **Connect Central Asia** was announced (**2012**).
xa: ⚠ First Dialogue = **2019**, Samarkand (ministers); first Summit = **2022**, virtual (leaders).
Uzbekistan: **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** (**Aug 2026**).

152.s: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held in:
152.x: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held virtually in January 2022.
152.tq: Combine the year with the mode of meeting to distinguish the Summit from the earlier Dialogue.
xs: The first **India-Central Asia Summit** was in January **2022**, **virtual** — option **(2)**.
**2019** was the first **Dialogue** of foreign ministers, at **Samarkand**.
xa: ⚠ Dialogue = ministers (**2019**); Summit = leaders (**2022**).
**I2U2**'s first leaders' summit was also virtual, **2022**.

152.s: Which of the following developments describes the India-Uzbekistan relationship in August 2026?
o: It was reduced to a strategic partnership with a $1 billion trade target by 2028.
It was raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, with a $5 billion trade target by 2030 and a uranium-supply framework.
It was converted into a defence alliance with a $10 billion trade target by 2030.
It was limited to cultural cooperation without an economic target.
152.x: In August 2026, India-Uzbekistan ties were raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, with a $5 billion trade target by 2030 and a framework for uranium supply.
152.tq: Read the complete development as a partnership-status, target-year and sectoral package.
xs: In **Aug 2026**, India-Uzbekistan ties became a **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**, with a **$5 billion trade target by 2030** and a **uranium supply** framework — option **(2)**.
It was an upgrade, not a reduction or a defence alliance.
xa: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue (**Samarkand, 2019**).
Other upgrades: **Vietnam** CSP **2016**; **Malaysia** CSP **2024**; **Philippines** strategic partner **Aug 2025**.

152.s:
Consider the following statements about Chabahar port:
1. It lies in Iran on the Gulf of Oman.
2. It gives India access to Afghanistan, Central Asia and the INSTC while bypassing Pakistan.
3. In 2026, the USA extended India's Chabahar sanctions waiver.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in 2026 the USA ended India's Chabahar sanctions waiver. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are out and '1 only' misses the gateway role.
152.tq: 2026: US ENDED the Chabahar waiver.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Chabahar** is in **Iran**, on the **Gulf of Oman**.
Statement 2 is correct: it is a gateway to **Afghanistan, Central Asia and the INSTC**, **bypassing Pakistan**.
Statement 3 is wrong: in **2026** the **USA ended** India's Chabahar sanctions waiver — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Link West** covers the **Gulf, Iran and Israel**.
**Connect Central Asia** policy: **2012**, Bishkek.

152.s: The Link West policy primarily seeks to deepen India's relations with:
o: Only the countries of South Asia
Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific Islands
Central Asia, Japan and South Korea
152.x: Link West, also called Think West, focuses on the Gulf, Iran and Israel.
152.tq: Match the policy label with its westward geographical focus.
xs: **Link West** deepens ties with **the Gulf, Iran and Israel** — option **(4)**.
Aims: **energy, trade, diaspora, counter-terrorism** (**UPSC**).
xa: The **GCC** is India's **largest socio-economic partner**: over **$160 billion** trade, **10 million** diaspora.
PM Modi: **15 visits** to GCC states + **two to Israel** (**Mar 2026**).
**I2U2** = **India, Israel, UAE, USA**.

152.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the maritime vision with its year and full form?
1. SAGAR — 2015 — Security and Growth for All in the Region
2. MAHASAGAR — 2025 — Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
3. SHANTI — 13 July 2026 — Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
152.x: All three matches are correct. SAGAR and MAHASAGAR were announced in Mauritius in 2015 and 2025 respectively, while SHANTI was announced on 13 July 2026 by EAM Jaishankar.
152.tq: Verify each acronym against both its date and its expanded form.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)**.
**SAGAR** (**2015**) = **Security and Growth for All in the Region**; **MAHASAGAR** (**2025**) = **Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions**.
**SHANTI** (**13 July 2026**) = **Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity**.
xa: ⚠ SAGAR and MAHASAGAR were both launched in **Mauritius**; **SHANTI** by **EAM Jaishankar**, not the PM.
SHANTI will be operationalised first in the **Bay of Bengal**.

152.s: Which one of the following best describes India's SAGAR doctrine?
o: A trade-only framework excluding security concerns
India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region, including a response to China's String of Pearls
India's withdrawal from maritime security affairs in the Indian Ocean Region
A continental security arrangement limited to Central Asia
152.x: SAGAR presents India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and is associated with countering China's String of Pearls strategy.
152.tq: Infer the doctrine's strategic meaning from its security-provider role and regional setting.
xs: **SAGAR** casts India as **net security provider** in the **IOR** and counters China's "**String of Pearls**" — option **(2)**.
It is not trade-only or continental.
xa: SAGAR: **2015**, **Mauritius**; upgraded to **MAHASAGAR** in **2025**.
**IPOI** builds on SAGAR.
Debate: the US sinking of Iran's **IRIS Dena** (**Mar 2026**) challenges the "net security provider" claim.

152.s: SHANTI is intended to serve as:
o: A replacement for the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative
A normative framework for shared maritime spaces, first to be operationalised in the Bay of Bengal
A trade agreement among Central Asian states
A military alliance for exclusive naval operations
152.x: SHANTI is a normative framework for shared maritime spaces and is to be operationalised first in the Bay of Bengal.
152.tq: Distinguish a normative maritime framework from an alliance or trade agreement.
xs: **SHANTI** is a **normative framework for shared maritime spaces**, first to be operationalised in the **Bay of Bengal** — option **(2)**.
It does not replace the **IPOI**, which is an open, **non-treaty** initiative.
xa: Launched **13 July 2026** by **EAM Jaishankar**.
Tied to India's **UNSC 2028-29** campaign.

152.s: India's free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific vision, with ASEAN centrality, was set out by Prime Minister Modi in the keynote address at the Shangri-La Dialogue in:
152.x: Prime Minister Modi set out this vision in his Shangri-La Dialogue keynote in June 2018.
152.tq: Link the speech, year and core phrase of the Indo-Pacific vision.
xs: PM Modi's **Shangri-La keynote** (**June 2018**) set out a **free, open, inclusive Indo-Pacific** with **ASEAN centrality** — option **(2)**.
**November 2019** is when he proposed the **IPOI** (14th EAS, Bangkok); **January 2022** the first Central Asia Summit.
xa: The **Shangri-La Dialogue** is organised by **IISS** (London), in **Singapore** since **2002**.
**2026 edition**: the US called India a "**critical anchor**".

152.s: The Shangri-La Dialogue is organised by which institution and has been held in Singapore since which year?
152.x: The Shangri-La Dialogue is run by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), based in London, and has been held in Singapore since 2002.
152.tq: Match the forum with its organising institution and established venue timeline.
xs: The **Shangri-La Dialogue** is organised by the **IISS** (London) and held in **Singapore** since **2002** — option **(2)**.
IISS stands apart from **ASEAN**, whose centrality PM Modi stressed there.
xa: PM Modi's keynote was in **June 2018**.
**2026**: US called India a "**critical anchor**"; US reverted **INDOPACOM to PACOM** (**Jun 2026**).

152.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI):
1. PM Modi proposed it at the 14th East Asia Summit, Bangkok, in November 2019.
2. It is a treaty-based initiative that replaced SAGAR.
3. It has seven pillars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
152.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: IPOI is open and non-treaty, and it builds on SAGAR rather than replacing it. So '1 and 3 only'; options with 2 are out and '1 only' misses the seven pillars.
152.tq: IPOI = open, non-treaty, builds on SAGAR.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: PM Modi proposed the **IPOI** at the **14th East Asia Summit, Bangkok, Nov 2019**.
Statement 2 is wrong: IPOI is open and **non-treaty**, and it **builds on SAGAR**.
Statement 3 is correct: it has **7 pillars** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Pillars include **Maritime Security**, **Maritime Ecology**, **Maritime Resources**, **Disaster Risk Reduction and Management**.
**Spain** joined the IPOI in **Jan 2026**.

152.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative?
152.x: The seven IPOI pillars include Maritime Security, Maritime Ecology, Maritime Resources, Capacity Building and Resource Sharing, Disaster Risk Reduction and Management, Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation, and Trade, Connectivity and Maritime Transport. Nuclear Disarmament Verification is not one of them.
152.tq: Find the unrelated sector among the formally listed seven pillars.
xs: **Nuclear Disarmament Verification** is not an IPOI pillar — option **(4)**.
The **7 pillars**: **Maritime Security**; **Maritime Ecology**; **Maritime Resources**; **Capacity Building and Resource Sharing**.
Also: **Disaster Risk Reduction and Management**; **Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation**; **Trade Connectivity and Maritime Transport**.
xa: IPOI was proposed at the **14th East Asia Summit, Bangkok** (**Nov 2019**).
IPOI is open, **non-treaty**, and builds on **SAGAR**.

152.s: Indian coastal surveillance radars have been installed in which of the following group of countries?
o: Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles
Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Mauritius and Seychelles
Sri Lanka, Maldives, Bangladesh and Mauritius
152.x: The coastal radar chain covers Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles.
152.tq: Identify the complete set by eliminating the country substituted from a neighbouring maritime grouping.
xs: India's **coastal surveillance radars** are in **Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles** — option **(1)**.
**Bangladesh** is not in the listed radar chain.
xa: Recommendation (**Mar 2026**): strengthen it along with **IORA**.
Island projects: **Agalega** (Mauritius), **Assumption Island** (Seychelles), **Hanimaadhoo** (Maldives).

152.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Project)
 a. Agalega airstrip and jetty
 b. Assumption Island
 c. Uthuru Thila Falhu harbour
 d. Hanimaadhoo airport

List-II (Country)
 i. Seychelles
 ii. Maldives
 iii. Mauritius

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
152.x: Agalega airstrip and jetty is in Mauritius; Assumption Island is in Seychelles; Uthuru Thila Falhu harbour and Hanimaadhoo airport are in the Maldives.
152.tq: Start from the sure project-country pair and then resolve the two Maldives entries.
xs: **a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Agalega** airstrip and jetty — **Mauritius**; **Assumption Island** — **Seychelles**.
**Uthuru Thila Falhu** harbour and **Hanimaadhoo** airport — **Maldives**.
xa: **SAGAR** (**2015**) and **MAHASAGAR** (**2025**) were both launched in **Mauritius**.
Coastal radar chain: **Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Seychelles**.

152.s: The hosting of MILAN 2026 at Visakhapatnam is particularly significant for Andhra Pradesh because it links the State with:
o: UNSC reform and the IFC-IOR only
Look West and the Colombo Security Conclave only
152.x: MILAN 2026 at Visakhapatnam links Andhra Pradesh with India’s Act East policy and the SAGAR vision.
152.tq: Apply the event-location linkage to identify its policy significance for Andhra Pradesh.
xs: **MILAN 2026 at Visakhapatnam** ties AP to **Act East and SAGAR** — option **(4)**.
This is the **AP angle** of the topic; the other options are not linked to MILAN in the notes.
xa: **SAGAR** (**2015**): **Security and Growth for All in the Region**.
**Act East** (**2014**): economic plus strategic, security, cultural.

152.s: The reported sinking of Iran’s IRIS Dena by the United States has been cited as challenging India’s claim of being a:
152.x: The incident has been cited in criticism of India’s claim to function as a net security provider in the region.
152.tq: Match the reported criticism with the precise strategic role under debate.
xs: The US sinking of Iran's **IRIS Dena** (**Mar 2026**) challenges India's "**net security provider**" claim — option **(4)**.
That claim comes from **SAGAR**, which casts India as net security provider in the **IOR**.
xa: SAGAR also counters China's "**String of Pearls**".
India seeks a **UNSC** seat for **2028-29**; SHANTI was launched with that campaign.

153.s: The 'Pivot to Asia' or 'Rebalance' policy of the United States, associated with the Obama era, was announced in which year?
153.x: The Pivot to Asia, also called the Rebalance, was announced in 2011 during the Obama era to shift greater US strategic attention towards the Asia-Pacific region.
153.tq: Use the date as the discriminator in a doctrine-year question.
xs: The **Pivot to Asia / Rebalance** came in the **Obama era**, **2011** — option **(2)**.
It shifted **USA** focus to the **Asia-Pacific** (**UPPSC 2015**).
xa: **CAATSA** (**2017**): US sanctions on buyers of **Russian arms**.
**Pressler Amendment** (**1985**): barred US aid to **Pakistan** without nuclear certification.
Quad leaders' summits began in **2021**.

153.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pressler Amendment:
1. It was enacted in 1985.
2. It barred US aid to Pakistan unless the US President certified that Pakistan did not possess a nuclear device.
3. Its provisions were applied to Pakistan in 1990.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
153.x: All three statements are correct. The Pressler Amendment was enacted in 1985, linked US aid to presidential certification regarding Pakistan's nuclear capability, and was applied in 1990.
153.tq: Check the date, condition and year of application separately before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)**.
The **Pressler Amendment** (**1985**) barred US aid to **Pakistan** unless the **President certified** it had **no nuclear device**.
It was **applied in 1990**.
xa: Named after US Senator **Larry Pressler**; aimed at **Pakistan's nuclear programme**.
Other US laws: **Hyde Act (2006)**, **CAATSA (2017)**.

153.s: The principal effect of the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA) in the India-US context is related to:
o: US sanctions on countries buying Russian arms
US sanctions on countries importing American nuclear reactors
US aid to countries joining the Quad
US restrictions on Indian software exports
153.x: CAATSA, enacted in 2017, provides for US sanctions against buyers of Russian arms. India sought a waiver in the context of its purchase of the S-400 system.
153.tq: Distinguish the law by matching its sanction-triggering activity with the correct policy.
xs: **CAATSA** (**2017**) means **US sanctions on buyers of Russian arms** — option **(1)**.
India sought a **waiver** for the **S-400**.
Nuclear reactor imports fall under the **123 Agreement** path, not CAATSA.
xa: **Hyde Act (2006)** made the nuclear deal possible under US law.
India's US-origin platforms: **P-8I, C-17, Apache, MH-60R, M777**.

153.s: Kovvada, mentioned in the context of India-US civil nuclear cooperation, is located in:
153.x: Kovvada is in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh and is the proposed site for the Westinghouse AP1000 reactors.
153.tq: Use the AP-specific location clue and distinguish the district from other Andhra Pradesh locations.
xs: **Kovvada** is in **Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh** — option **(3)**.
It is the site for the **Westinghouse AP1000** reactors.
xa: **AP angle**: Kovvada = proposed site for the **US-designed reactors**.
The talks run under **iCET** (**2023**), relaunched as **TRUST** in **2025**.
Nuclear path: **Hyde Act 2006** → **123 Agreement 2008** → **NSG waiver Sept 2008**.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about India-US dialogue mechanisms:
1. The 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue has been held since 2018.
2. The Strategic and Commercial Dialogue began in 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2+2 dialogue dates from 2018. Statement 2 is wrong: the Strategic and Commercial Dialogue dates from 2015. So '1 only'; the other options either accept statement 2 or reject statement 1.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **2+2 Ministerial Dialogue** runs **from 2018**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **Strategic and Commercial Dialogue** dates from **2015** — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Relationship status: **Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership** (UPSC).
**Quad** leaders' summits began in **2021**.

153.s: India-US relations are described as a:
153.x: The relationship is described as a Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.
153.tq: Select the precise official status rather than a narrower defence or trade description.
xs: India-US ties are a **Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership** — option **(4)** (UPSC).
The other labels are not used for the relationship in the notes.
xa: US designated India a **Major Defense Partner** in **2016**.
Mechanisms: **Strategic and Commercial Dialogue (2015)**, **2+2 (2018)**, **Quad** summits (**2021**).

153.s:
Match List-I (India-US foundational agreement) with List-II (purpose):
List-I
a. GSOMIA
b. LEMOA
c. COMCASA
d. BECA
List-II
i. Encrypted communications data and equipment
ii. Geospatial (satellite) data for navigation and missile targeting
iii. Protection of shared military information
iv. Access to each other's facilities for refuelling and replenishment
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
153.x: GSOMIA (2002) = protection of shared military information (iii); LEMOA (2016) = facilities access for refuelling and replenishment (iv); COMCASA (2018) = encrypted communications (i); BECA (2020) = geospatial data (ii). Option B swaps GSOMIA and LEMOA, option C swaps COMCASA and BECA, option D swaps GSOMIA and COMCASA.
153.tq: LEMOA = Logistics, COMCASA = Communications, BECA = Basic geospatial.
xs: **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**GSOMIA** (**2002**) = protection of shared military information; **LEMOA** (**2016**) = facilities for **refuelling and replenishment**.
**COMCASA** (**2018**) = **encrypted communications**; **BECA** (**2020**) = **geospatial** data for navigation and missile targeting.
xa: ⚠ **2016** = LEMOA + **Major Defense Partner**; **2018** = COMCASA + **STA-1**.
**10-year defence framework**: **Oct 2025**, Hegseth-Rajnath Singh.

153.s:
Arrange the following India-US foundational defence agreements in chronological order:
A. BECA
B. GSOMIA
C. COMCASA
D. LEMOA
153.x: GSOMIA was signed in 2002, LEMOA in 2016, COMCASA in 2018 and BECA in 2020. Therefore, the correct order is B, D, C, A.
153.tq: Fix the earliest and latest agreements first, then place the intermediate years.
xs: Order: **GSOMIA 2002 → LEMOA 2016 → COMCASA 2018 → BECA 2020** = **B, D, C, A** — option **(1)**.
Each agreement is two years or more apart; BECA is the latest.
xa: Later steps: **INDUS-X (2023)**, **Security of Supply Arrangement (2024)**, **10-year framework (Oct 2025)**.
⚠ **2018** also gave **STA-1** status.

153.s: India was designated by the United States as a 'Major Defense Partner' in:
153.x: The United States designated India as a Major Defense Partner in 2016.
153.tq: Use the middle-year distinction among the successive defence milestones.
xs: The US named India a **Major Defense Partner** in **2016** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **2016** = **LEMOA** + Major Defense Partner.

153.s: Which one of the following best describes India's STA-1 status with the United States?
o: It applies exclusively to civilian nuclear technology.
It permits India to veto US defence exports to third countries.
It permits faster, licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology.
It provides automatic membership of NATO.
153.x: STA-1, granted to India in 2018, facilitates faster and licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology. It gives India treatment comparable to that available to NATO allies in this sphere, but does not make India a NATO member.
153.tq: Reject the extreme institutional claim and select the option describing the actual technology-access benefit.
xs: **STA-1** (**2018**) gives **faster, licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology** — option **(3)**.
It is a **status like NATO allies** — not NATO membership, and not nuclear-only.
xa: ⚠ **2018** = COMCASA + STA-1.
**Major Defense Partner** came in **2016**.

153.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
153.x: Vajra Prahar is an exercise involving Special Forces. Yudh Abhyas is an Army exercise, Cope India is associated with the Air Force, and Tiger Triumph is tri-service and amphibious.
153.tq: Match each exercise with its service and reject the options that swap service classifications.
xs: **Vajra Prahar — Special Forces** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Yudh Abhyas** is **Army**, not Navy; **Cope India** is **Air Force**, not Army.
**Tiger Triumph** is **tri-service, amphibious**, not Air Force only.
xa: **Malabar**: **Navy** (with Japan, Australia).
**Red Flag**: **US Air Force multinational** exercise.

153.s:
Which of the following exercises is correctly matched with its service or character?
1. Yudh Abhyas — Army
2. Malabar — Navy
3. Tiger Triumph — Tri-service and amphibious
4. Red Flag — US Air Force multinational exercise
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
153.x: All four matches are correct. Yudh Abhyas is an Army exercise, Malabar is naval, Tiger Triumph is tri-service and amphibious, and Red Flag is a US Air Force multinational exercise.
153.tq: Check the service classification of each exercise rather than relying on the exercise name alone.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)**.
**Yudh Abhyas** — **Army**; **Malabar** — **Navy**.
**Tiger Triumph** — **tri-service, amphibious**; **Red Flag** — **US Air Force multinational** exercise.
xa: **Vajra Prahar**: Special Forces; **Cope India**: Air Force.
Malabar includes **Japan, Australia**.

153.s:
Consider the following statements about India-US technology cooperation:
1. iCET was launched in 2023 and relaunched as TRUST in 2025.
2. GE F414 jet engines are to be co-produced with Bharat Electronics Limited.
3. India signed the Artemis Accords in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: GE F414 engines are to be co-produced with HAL (Hindustan Aeronautics Limited), not BEL. So '1 and 3 only'; options with 2 are out and '1 only' misses Artemis.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **iCET** (**2023**) was relaunched as **TRUST** in **2025**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **GE F414** engines are to be co-produced with **HAL**, not BEL.
Statement 3 is correct: India signed the **Artemis Accords** in **2023** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Under iCET: **Westinghouse AP1000** + **SMRs/AMRs** talks.
**India Semiconductor Mission**: **₹76,000 crore**, **Dec 2021**.

153.s:
With reference to the India Semiconductor Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in December 2021.
2. It involves an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
153.x: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in December 2021 with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.
153.tq: Check both the date and the numerical outlay before choosing the coded answer.
xs: Both are correct — option **(3)**.
The **India Semiconductor Mission** was launched in **Dec 2021** with **₹76,000 crore**.
xa: **FORGE**: **Forum on Resource, Geostrategic Engagement** (critical minerals).

153.s: The United States withdrew India's Generalized System of Preferences (GSP) benefits in:
153.x: The United States withdrew India's GSP benefits in June 2019.
153.tq: Use the exact month-year combination to distinguish the trade-policy event from later tariff developments.
xs: The US withdrew India's **GSP** benefits in **June 2019** — option **(1)**.
GSP was not restored; exports later fell (**Apr-Nov 2025**).
xa: **Mission 500** (**Feb 2025**): double trade to **$500 billion by 2030**.
The **10-year defence framework** keeps ties steady **despite trade friction**.

153.s: Mission 500, announced in the Modi-Trump joint statement of February 2025, aims to:
o: Double bilateral trade to $500 billion by 2030
Reduce bilateral trade to $500 billion by 2030
Train 500,000 engineers in the United States by 2025
153.x: Mission 500 aims to double India-US bilateral trade to $500 billion by 2030.
153.tq: Separate the trade target from the tempting but unrelated defence and training figures.
xs: **Mission 500**: **double bilateral trade to $500 billion by 2030** — option **(1)**.
From the **Modi-Trump joint statement** (**Feb 2025**).
xa: The US withdrew India's **GSP** in **June 2019**.
Exports in labour-intensive sectors **fell Apr-Nov 2025**.

153.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Indian diaspora in the United States is correct?
o: The United States has the world's largest Persons of Indian Origin community, while Malaysia is second.
India itself is counted as the world's largest overseas Persons of Indian Origin community.
The United States has the world's largest Indian-origin community and Canada is second.
Malaysia has the world's largest Persons of Indian Origin community, while the United States is second.
153.x: The United States has the world's largest Persons of Indian Origin community, and Malaysia is second.
153.tq: Check the direction of the comparison carefully; the ranking is the key distinction.
xs: The **US** has the **world's largest Persons of Indian Origin** community; **Malaysia** is **second** — option **(1)**.
Reported **Feb 2026**.
xa: US Vice President **JD Vance** visited India in **April 2025**.
Relationship status: **Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership**.

153.s: Which of the following statements best explains the significance of the 2008 India-US civil nuclear deal?
o: It ended India's relations with all other nuclear suppliers.
It marked the turning point in India-US relations.
It established the India Semiconductor Mission.
It created the Quad leaders' summit mechanism.
153.x: The 2008 civil nuclear deal is regarded as the turning point in India-US relations.
153.tq: Identify the broad historical significance rather than confusing the nuclear deal with later strategic initiatives.
xs: The **2008 nuclear deal** was the **turning point** in India-US relations — option **(2)**.
Path: **Hyde Act 2006** → **123 Agreement 2008** → **NSG clean waiver Sept 2008**.
xa: The NSG waiver **allowed civil nuclear trade**.
**AP angle**: **Kovvada** (Srikakulam) is the proposed site for US-designed **AP1000** reactors.

154.s: The Declaration on Strategic Partnership between India and Russia was signed in:
154.x: India and Russia signed the Declaration on Strategic Partnership in 2000, later developing it into a Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership.
154.tq: Separate the historical treaty year from the later strategic-partnership declaration.
xs: India and Russia signed the **Declaration on Strategic Partnership** in **2000** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was later upgraded to the **Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership**.
**1971** is the year of the **Indo-Soviet Treaty**, the historical anchor of ties, not the Declaration.
xa: The **23rd Annual Summit (New Delhi)** marked the **25th anniversary** of the partnership.
⚠ Labels: Russia = "Special and **Privileged**"; Japan = "Special Strategic and **Global**"; Israel = "**Special Strategic**".
Other Gulf labels: **UAE** = Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (**2017**); **Saudi Arabia** = **Strategic Partnership Council** (**2019**).
Soviet-era landmarks: **Bhilai** and **Bokaro** steel plants.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit (New Delhi):
1. It marked the 25th anniversary of the strategic partnership and set a $100 billion trade target by 2030.
2. About 96% of bilateral trade is settled in national currencies.
3. Russia joined the I2U2 grouping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Russia joined the IBCA (International Big Cat Alliance); I2U2 is India, Israel, UAE and USA. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are out and '1 only' misses the 96% figure.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1 correct: the **23rd Summit** marked the **25th anniversary** and set a trade target of **$100 billion by 2030** ("**Programme 2030**").
Statement 2 correct: about **96%** of India-Russia trade is settled in **national currencies**.
Statement 3 wrong: Russia joined the **IBCA**, not I2U2; **I2U2** = **India, Israel, UAE, USA**.
xa: The partnership dates to the **Declaration on Strategic Partnership (2000)**.
Defence deals with Russia: **S-400** (**2018** deal) and the **BrahMos** JV (Brahmaputra + Moskva).
Crude imports from Russia **declined** year-on-year in Apr-Nov **2025** as India diversified sources.
⚠ **23rd** = Russia summit; **16th** = India-EU and Japan summits; **18th** = BRICS.

154.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
154.x: The S-400 deal between India and Russia dates to 2018. BrahMos is an India-Russia joint venture named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers, while Kudankulam is in Tamil Nadu.
154.tq: Use the correctly matched pair while checking both the partner and location or name origin.
xs: **S-400 — 2018 deal** is correctly matched — option **(2)**.
**Kudankulam** nuclear plant is in **Tamil Nadu**, not Gujarat.
**BrahMos** is an **India-Russia** joint venture named after the **Brahmaputra** and **Moskva** rivers — not France, not Volga.
xa: **INSTC** links **India-Iran-Russia** via **Chabahar**.
Russia's historical anchor: the **1971 Indo-Soviet Treaty**, with **Bhilai** and **Bokaro** steel plants.
About **96%** of India-Russia trade is settled in **national currencies**.

154.s: The International North-South Transport Corridor connects India, Iran and Russia and runs through:
154.x: The India-Iran-Russia INSTC runs through the Iranian port of Chabahar.
154.tq: Identify the specific transit location in a regional connectivity corridor.
xs: The **INSTC** (India-Iran-Russia corridor) runs via the Iranian port of **Chabahar** — option **(2)**.
It is one of the key India-Russia connectivity projects, listed with **S-400**, **BrahMos** and **Kudankulam**.
xa: **Kudankulam** = Russia-backed nuclear plant in **Tamil Nadu**.
**BrahMos** = JV named after the **Brahmaputra** + **Moskva**.
Trade target with Russia: **$100 billion by 2030** ("**Programme 2030**").

154.s: At the 16th India-EU Summit held in India in 2026, which of the following outcomes was recorded?
o: The BTIA talks were permanently suspended.
India withdrew from the Trade and Technology Council.
The EU became India's first FTA partner and a Nuclear Partnership was signed.
The EU became India's 22nd FTA partner and a Security and Defence Partnership was signed.
154.x: The India-EU FTA was concluded at the 16th Summit, making the EU India's 22nd FTA partner; an EU-India Security and Defence Partnership was also signed the same day.
154.tq: Identify the paired outcomes of a summit while rejecting exaggerated or reversed claims.
xs: The **EU** became India's **22nd FTA partner** and an **EU-India Security and Defence Partnership** was signed — option **(4)**.
The **India-EU FTA** was concluded at the **16th India-EU Summit**, held in India in **2026**.
The Security and Defence Partnership was signed the **same day** as the FTA; no nuclear partnership is recorded.
xa: **BTIA** (Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement) talks had run since **2007**.
The **Trade and Technology Council** was agreed in **2022**; first **India-EU Strategic Dialogue** in **2025**.
⚠ **16th** is also the number of the **Japan Annual Summit** (2026).
⚠ **CETA** = UK (signed **July 2025**); **BTIA** = EU.

154.s: BTIA, in the context of India-European Union relations, stands for:
154.x: BTIA stands for India-EU Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement; negotiations have been underway since 2007.
154.tq: Test the exact expansion of an international agreement acronym.
xs: **BTIA** stands for **Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement** — option **(4)**.
It is the India-**EU** trade negotiation, with talks under way since **2007** (asked in UPSC **2017**).
xa: The **India-EU FTA** was concluded at the **16th India-EU Summit** (**2026**); EU = India's **22nd FTA partner**.
⚠ **CETA** = UK; **CEPA** = Japan, UAE, Oman; **BTIA** = EU.
The **Trade and Technology Council** with the EU was agreed in **2022**.

154.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India and the UK signed the CETA in July 2025.
2. India-EU negotiations on the BTIA began in 2017.
3. The German Chancellor visited India in January 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x: Statement 1 is correct: the India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025. Statement 2 is wrong: BTIA talks have been under way since 2007 (2017 is the UPSC question year). Statement 3 is correct: the German Chancellor visited India in January 2026. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses the German visit, and options with 2 are wrong.
154.tq: UK CETA July 2025; BTIA talks since 2007; German Chancellor Jan 2026.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1 correct: India and the UK signed the **CETA** in **July 2025**.
Statement 2 wrong: **BTIA** talks have run since **2007**; **2017** is only the UPSC exam year.
Statement 3 correct: the **German Chancellor** visited India in **Jan 2026**.
xa: ⚠ **CETA** = UK; **CEPA** = Japan, UAE, Oman; **BTIA** = EU.
The **India-EU FTA** was concluded at the **16th India-EU Summit** in **2026**.
The **Oman CEPA** was signed in **Dec 2025** and came into force on **1 June 2026**.

154.s: India and Japan are described as having which type of partnership?
154.x: India and Japan have a Special Strategic and Global Partnership.
154.tq: Recall the exact official description of a bilateral relationship.
xs: India and Japan share a **Special Strategic and Global Partnership** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Russia = "Special and **Privileged**"; Israel = "**Special Strategic**" — only Japan carries "**Global**".
xa: India-Japan **CEPA** has been in force since **2011**.
Japan = India's **5th-largest FDI source**; trade **$27.47 billion (FY 2025-26)**.
Defence ties: **2+2 dialogue**, **ACSA (2020)** and the **UNICORN** naval antenna.

154.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India-Japan cooperation:
1. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project uses Shinkansen technology.
2. Japanese Official Development Assistance supports the project.
3. The Act East Forum is concerned with India's North-East.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
154.x: All three statements are correct. Japan supports the Mumbai-Ahmedabad project through Shinkansen technology and ODA, while the Act East Forum focuses on the North-East.
154.tq: Combine infrastructure, finance and regional-cooperation facts in one statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
Statements 1 and 2: the **Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail** (bullet train) uses **Shinkansen** technology with **Japanese ODA**.
Statement 3: the **Act East Forum** with Japan is for the **North-East**.
xa: At the **15th Summit (2025)**, Japanese firms committed **10 trillion yen (~$67 billion)** over ten years.
The **16th India-Japan Annual Summit** was held in **2026**.
India-Japan defence: **2+2 dialogue**, **ACSA (2020)**, **UNICORN** naval antenna.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about India-Japan economic ties:
1. At the 15th Annual Summit (2025), Japanese firms committed 10 trillion yen over ten years.
2. The India-Japan CEPA has been in force since 2011.
3. Japan is India's largest source of FDI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x: Statement 1 is correct: about 10 trillion yen (~$67 billion) over ten years was committed at the 15th Summit. Statement 2 is correct: CEPA dates from 2011. Statement 3 is wrong: Japan is India's 5th-largest FDI source, not the largest. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses CEPA, and options with 3 are wrong.
154.tq: Japan: 10 trillion yen (2025), CEPA 2011, 5th-largest FDI source.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1 correct: at the **15th Summit (2025)**, Japanese firms committed **10 trillion yen (~$67 billion)** over ten years.
Statement 2 correct: the India-Japan **CEPA** has been in force **since 2011**.
Statement 3 wrong: Japan is India's **5th-largest FDI source**, not the largest.
xa: India-Japan trade: **$27.47 billion (FY 2025-26)**.
The **16th Annual Summit** with Japan was held in **2026**.
⚠ **CEPA** = Japan, UAE, Oman; **CETA** = UK.

154.s: Full diplomatic relations between India and Israel were established in which year under which Indian Prime Minister?
154.x: India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992 during the P. V. Narasimha Rao government.
154.tq: Test the exact year and the government associated with a diplomatic milestone.
xs: India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in **1992** under **P.V. Narasimha Rao** — option **(2)**.
Relations have since grown into a **Special Strategic Partnership**, with defence as a key pillar.
xa: **Narendra Modi** became the **first Indian PM to visit Israel** in **2017**; by **March 2026** he had visited **twice**.
**I2U2** = India, Israel, UAE, USA.
India-Israel trade: **$3.75 billion (FY 2024-25)**; India = Israel's **2nd-largest trading partner in Asia**.
A **Bilateral Investment Agreement** was signed in **Sept 2025**; FTA **Terms of Reference** in **Nov 2025**.

154.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India-Israel relations:
1. By March 2026, Narendra Modi had visited Israel twice.
2. Defence is a key pillar of the India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership.
3. The partnership excludes joint research and development in defence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
154.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Defence cooperation includes manufacturing, technology and joint research and development, so statement 3 is false.
154.tq: Find the statement that reverses the scope of a bilateral partnership.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1 correct: by **March 2026**, **Narendra Modi** had visited Israel **twice**.
Statement 2 correct: defence is a **key pillar** of the **Special Strategic Partnership**.
Statement 3 wrong: defence cooperation covers **manufacturing, technology and joint R&D**.
xa: Modi's first visit (**2017**) made him the **first Indian PM to visit Israel**.
Full diplomatic relations: **1992**, under **P.V. Narasimha Rao**.
**Indo-Israel Centres of Excellence** work on agriculture: horticulture and water-efficient farming.

154.s: Who was the first Indian Prime Minister to visit Israel?
154.x: Narendra Modi became the first Indian PM to visit Israel, in 2017 (APPSC-G2 2017). P.V. Narasimha Rao's government set up full diplomatic relations in 1992 but he did not visit Israel. Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh did not visit Israel as PM.
xs: **Narendra Modi** was the **first Indian PM to visit Israel**, in **2017** — option **(3)** (asked in APPSC-G2 **2017**).
**P.V. Narasimha Rao**'s government only established full diplomatic relations in **1992**.
xa: By **March 2026**, Modi had visited Israel **twice**.
India-Israel = **Special Strategic Partnership**; defence is a key pillar.
**I2U2** grouping: India, Israel, UAE, USA.

154.s:
Consider the following statements about India-UAE relations:
1. The two countries have had a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership since 2017.
2. The India-UAE CEPA became operational in 2022.
3. With trade of over $100 billion in FY 2024-25, the UAE is India's second-largest trading partner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
154.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: trade exceeded $100 billion, but that made the UAE India's 3rd-largest trading partner, not 2nd. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are out and '1 only' misses CEPA 2022.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1 correct: India-UAE **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** dates from **2017**.
Statement 2 correct: the **CEPA** became operational in **2022** (with a **BIT** in **2024**).
Statement 3 wrong: trade of **over $100 billion (FY 2024-25)** makes the UAE India's **3rd-largest** trading partner, not 2nd.
xa: The UAE is the **first foreign investor** in India's **SPR (Mangaluru)**.
A **Strategic Defence Partnership** LoI came during the **2026 UAE President's visit**.
The **Oman CEPA** is India's **2nd CEPA in the GCC**, after the UAE.

154.s: The UAE was India's first foreign investor in which of the following?
o: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project
The Strategic Petroleum Reserve at Mangaluru
154.x: The UAE became the first foreign investor in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve at Mangaluru.
154.tq: Identify the precise project associated with a foreign investment distinction.
xs: The UAE was the **first foreign investor** in India's **Strategic Petroleum Reserve** at **Mangaluru** — option **(4)**.
The other options belong elsewhere: **INSTC** and **Kudankulam** are Russia-linked; the **Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail** is Japan-backed.
xa: India-UAE: **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2017)**, **CEPA** operational **2022**, **BIT 2024**.
A **Strategic Defence Partnership** LoI was signed during the **2026 UAE President's visit**.
**I2U2** = India, Israel, UAE, USA.

154.s: Which of the following correctly describes the India-Oman CEPA?
o: It was signed in 2024 and was India's first CEPA in the GCC.
It was signed in June 2026, entered into force in December 2026, and provides 50% duty-free access.
It was signed in 2025 but has not entered into force.
It was signed in December 2025, entered into force on 1 June 2026, and provides 99% duty-free access to Indian exports.
154.x: The India-Oman CEPA was signed in December 2025, entered into force on 1 June 2026, and Oman offered 99% duty-free access to Indian exports. It is India's second GCC CEPA after the UAE agreement.
154.tq: Test agreement date, commencement date and market-access figure together.
xs: The **Oman CEPA** was signed in **December 2025**, entered into force on **1 June 2026**, and gives **99% duty-free access** to Indian exports — option **(4)**.
It is India's **2nd CEPA in the GCC**, after the **UAE** — so it was not the first, and it is already in force.
xa: India-UAE **CEPA** became operational in **2022**.
An **India-GCC FTA** is still under negotiation (**2026**).
⚠ **CETA** = UK; **CEPA** = Japan, UAE, Oman.

154.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (India-Africa Forum Summit)
a. I Summit
b. II Summit
c. III Summit

a. 2008
b. 2011
c. 2015

List-II (Venue)
i. New Delhi
 ii. Addis Ababa

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
154.x: The I Summit was held in New Delhi in 2008, the II Summit in Addis Ababa in 2011, and the III Summit in New Delhi in 2015.
154.tq: Start from the sure venue-year pair and eliminate incompatible codes.
xs: The **III IAFS** in New Delhi brought in **all 54 African states**.
xa: The **African Union** became a permanent **G20** member under India's presidency in **2023**.
The first **Mahatma Gandhi Convention Centre** is at **Niamey, Niger (Jan 2020)**.
**e-VBAB** = **e-VidyaBharati** (tele-education) + **e-ArogyaBharati** (tele-medicine) for Africa.

154.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India-Tanzania relations:
1. Tanzania became a strategic partner of India in 2023.
2. IIT Madras Zanzibar was established in 2023.
3. India extended about $1.1 billion in lines of credit for water supply in Tanzania.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
154.x: All three statements are correct: Tanzania became a strategic partner in 2023, IIT Madras Zanzibar was established in that year, and about $1.1 billion in lines of credit supported water supply.
154.tq: Use an all-inclusive option when the country-specific facts form one coherent set.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
Statements 1 and 2: Tanzania became a **strategic partner** in **2023**, the year **IIT Madras Zanzibar** (first overseas IIT) opened.
Statement 3: India extended **$1.1 billion** in **LoCs** for **water supply** in Tanzania.
xa: **e-VBAB** provides tele-education and tele-medicine across Africa.
New High Commission in **Sierra Leone** announced **Oct 2019**.
⚠ **Zanzibar** = IIT Madras campus; **Niamey** = first **Mahatma Gandhi Convention Centre**.

155.s: The Charter of the United Nations was signed by 50 nations at which place and on which date?
155.x: The UN Charter was signed by 50 nations at San Francisco on 26 June 1945.
155.tq: Use the place-date combination rather than recalling either detail in isolation.
xs: The UN Charter was signed by **50 nations** at **San Francisco** on **26 June 1945** — option **(2)**.
**24 October 1945** is when the Charter **came into force** (UN Day), not the signing date.
xa: The UN has **193** member states and **six official languages**: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish.
**2026** marks the **81st anniversary** of the Charter's entry into force.
India signed the Charter as **British India (June 1945)** — a founding member.

155.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 1 of the Charter of the United Nations:
1. Maintaining international peace and security is one of its purposes.
2. Developing friendly relations among nations is one of its purposes.
3. Harmonising the actions of nations is one of its purposes.
4. Establishing sovereign equality among nations is one of its purposes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: Article 1 includes maintaining peace and security, developing friendly relations, promoting cooperation and harmonising the actions of nations. Sovereign equality is stated in Article 2, not Article 1.
155.tq: Separate the purposes in Article 1 from the principle placed in Article 2.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)** "**1, 2 and 3 only**".
**Art. 1** lists four purposes: **peace and security**, **friendly relations**, **cooperation**, and **harmonising action**.
Statement 4 wrong: **sovereign equality** is in **Art. 2**, not Art. 1.
xa: ⚠ Art. **18** = two-thirds majority on UNGA "important questions"; Art. **23** = no immediate re-election to UNSC; Art. **27** = P5 veto.
**Charter amendment** needs **two-thirds** of members, including **all P5**.
Charter signed **26 June 1945**; in force **24 October 1945**.

155.s: The Charter of the United Nations came into force on:
155.x: The Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, observed as UN Day. 26 June 1945 is when 50 nations signed it at San Francisco. 1 January 1942 and 10 January 1946 are not the dates given for the Charter's entry into force.
155.tq: Signed 26 June 1945 (San Francisco); in force 24 Oct 1945 = UN Day.
xs: The UN Charter came into force on **24 October 1945**, observed as **UN Day** — option **(2)**.
**26 June 1945** is the date **50 nations** signed it at **San Francisco**.
xa: **2026** marks the **81st anniversary**.
First SG: **Trygve Lie** (Norway, **1946**-52).
The **Trusteeship Council** has been inactive since **1994** (Palau).

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the principal organs of the United Nations:
1. The General Assembly consists of all 193 members, with one vote each.
2. The Security Council has 15 members and is the only UN body whose decisions bind members.
3. The Secretariat is headed by the Secretary-General.
4. The Trusteeship Council has remained active continuously since 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Trusteeship Council has been inactive since 1994, following the attainment of self-government by Palau.
155.tq: Look for the time-word reversal in the statement about the Trusteeship Council.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1, 2 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: the **General Assembly** has all **193** members, one vote each.
Statement 2: the **Security Council** has **15** members and is the only body whose decisions **bind** members.
Statement 3: the **Secretariat** is headed by the **Secretary-General**.
Statement 4 wrong: the **Trusteeship Council** has been **inactive since 1994** (Palau).
xa: **ECOSOC** = **54** members, 3-year terms.
**ICJ** = principal judicial organ at **The Hague**; **15 judges**, **9-year** terms.
⚠ **15** = UNSC members and ICJ judges; **54** = ECOSOC.

155.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: International Court of Justice — Principal judicial organ — The Hague
155.x: ECOSOC has 54 members serving three-year terms, not 15 members serving two-year terms. The other pairs are correctly matched.
155.tq: Find the composition and tenure mismatch in an otherwise familiar institutional list.
xs: **ECOSOC — 15 members with two-year terms** is NOT correctly matched — option **(3)**.
ECOSOC actually has **54** members with **3-year** terms.
The others are right: **Secretariat** — Secretary-General; **Trusteeship Council** — inactive since **1994**; **ICJ** — **The Hague**.
xa: ⚠ **15** = UNSC members and **ICJ judges**; **2-year** terms belong to non-permanent **UNSC** members.
ECOSOC's functional commissions: **Commission on the Status of Women (1946)**, **Statistical Commission**, **Commission on Narcotic Drugs**.
**CSW-70** was held in **2026**.

155.s: Which commission reviewed Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration before being replaced by the High-Level Political Forum in 2013?
o: Commission on the Status of Women
155.x: The Commission on Sustainable Development reviewed Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration and was replaced by the High-Level Political Forum in 2013.
155.tq: Link a body with both its mandate and institutional successor.
xs: The **Commission on Sustainable Development** reviewed **Agenda 21** and the **Rio Declaration** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2018**).
It was replaced by the **High-Level Political Forum** in **2013**.
The **Commission on the Status of Women** dates from **1946**; the **Statistical** and **Narcotic Drugs** commissions are other ECOSOC bodies.
xa: **ECOSOC** = **54** members; handles economic, social and **SDG** coordination.
**CSW-70** was held in **2026**.
The **Trusteeship Council** has been inactive since **1994**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the Uniting for Peace resolution:
1. It was adopted as Resolution 377 in 1956.
2. It lets the UNGA act when a veto blocks the UNSC.
3. It was first used in the 1956 Suez Crisis to send peacekeepers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
155.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Resolution 377 was adopted in 1950; 1956 is when it was first used (Suez). Statements 2 and 3 are correct. So '2 and 3 only'; options with 1 fall for the 1956 trap.
155.tq: Adopted 1950, first used 1956 (Suez).
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)** "**2 and 3 only**".
Statement 1 wrong: **Uniting for Peace (Res. 377)** was adopted in **1950**; **1956** is only when it was first used.
Statement 2 correct: it lets the **UNGA act** when a **veto** blocks the UNSC.
Statement 3 correct: first used in the **1956 Suez Crisis** to send **peacekeepers**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: one source dates the resolution itself to **1956** — it was adopted in **1950**.
The P5 veto rests on **Article 27**.
Other committees: **1267** (**1999**, Al-Qaida/ISIL), **1373** (**2001**, Counter-Terrorism), **1540** (**2004**, WMD).

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the UN Security Council:
1. The veto of the five permanent members is provided under Article 27.
2. Non-permanent members are elected by the UNGA by a two-thirds secret ballot for 2 years.
3. A retiring non-permanent member is eligible for immediate re-election.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
155.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 23 bars immediate re-election of a non-permanent member. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are out and '1 only' misses the election rule.
155.tq: Art. 27 = veto; Art. 23 = no immediate re-election.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the **P5 veto** is under **Article 27**.
Statement 2: **10** non-permanent members are elected by the UNGA by **two-thirds** secret ballot for **2 years**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Art. 23** bars **immediate re-election** of non-permanent members.
xa: **P5:** China, France, Russia, UK, USA.
The UNSC has **15** members — the only UN body whose decisions **bind** members.
India has served **eight** UNSC terms, the latest **2021-22**.

155.s: How many times had India served as an elected non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council through the 2021–22 term?
155.tq: Count the complete sequence of terms rather than the number of years served.
xs: India has served **eight** UNSC terms through **2021-22** — option **(1)** "**Eight**".
xa: India's bid for **2028-29** was launched by EAM **Jaishankar** in New York on **13 July 2026**.
The rival for **2028-29** is **Tajikistan**, backed by the **OIC**.
Non-permanent members serve **2 years** and cannot be immediately re-elected (**Art. 23**).

155.s: In the April 2024 vote on full UN membership for Palestine, which combination correctly describes the votes against or abstentions that meant the proposal did not receive unanimous support?
o: Russia vetoed; the United Kingdom and India abstained.
China vetoed; India and France abstained.
The United States vetoed; France and Germany abstained.
The United States vetoed; the United Kingdom and Switzerland abstained.
155.x: The United States used its veto, while the United Kingdom and Switzerland abstained; three members therefore did not vote in favour.
155.tq: Track the different actions—veto and abstention—rather than treating all as negative votes.
xs: In the **April 2024** Palestine full-membership vote, the **United States vetoed** while the **UK** and **Switzerland abstained** — option **(4)**.
So **3** members did not vote yes (BPSC **2024**).
xa: **Palestine** and the **Holy See** are **non-member observer states** in the UNGA.
The P5 veto is under **Article 27**; **Uniting for Peace (Res. 377, 1950)** lets the UNGA act when a veto blocks the UNSC.
In the **22 May 2026** UNGA climate resolution, India **abstained** (**141-8-28**).

155.s:
Match List-I (UNSC committee) with List-II (subject):
List-I
a. 1267 (1999)
b. 1373 (2001)
c. 1540 (2004)
List-II
i. Counter-Terrorism Committee set up after 9/11
ii. Stopping WMD reaching non-state actors
iii. Sanctions on Al-Qaida/ISIL (Da'esh) and associates; terrorist listings
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
155.x: 1267 = Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions and listings (iii); 1373 = Counter-Terrorism Committee after 9/11 (i); 1540 = WMD and non-state actors (ii). Option B swaps 1267 and 1373, option C swaps 1267 and 1540, option D swaps 1373 and 1540.
155.tq: 1267 = listings (Masood Azhar); 1373 = CTC; 1540 = WMD.
xs: **1267** — Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions (iii); **1373** — Counter-Terrorism Committee (i); **1540** — WMD and non-state actors (ii) — option **(1)** "**a-iii, b-i, c-ii**".
xa: **Masood Azhar** (Jaish-e-Mohammed) was listed under the **1267 Committee** (APPSC-G1 **2019**).
India held its first **UNSCR 1540** capacity-building programme for Asia-Pacific at **NACIN, Palasamudram (AP)**, **Feb 2025**.
**Uniting for Peace (Res. 377)** dates from **1950**.

155.s: India conducted its first capacity-building programme on UNSCR 1540 for Asia-Pacific countries in February 2025 at
155.x: The programme was held at the National Academy of Customs, Indirect Taxes and Narcotics (NACIN), Palasamudram, Andhra Pradesh, in February 2025.
155.tq: Test the location and date together; location swaps are common traps.
xs: India's first **UNSCR 1540** capacity-building programme for Asia-Pacific was held at **NACIN, Palasamudram, Andhra Pradesh** — option **(2)**, in **Feb 2025**.
Palasamudram is in **AP**, not Telangana or abroad.
xa: **Resolution 1540 (2004)** aims at stopping **WMD** reaching **non-state actors**.
**1267 (1999)** = Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions; **1373 (2001)** = Counter-Terrorism Committee.
This is the topic's **AP angle**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about UNSC reform groups:
1. The G4 comprises Brazil, Germany, India and Japan.
2. Uniting for Consensus, led by Italy and including Pakistan, opposes new permanent seats.
3. The Ezulwini Consensus (2005) demands two permanent seats without veto for Africa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
155.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ezulwini Consensus demands 2 permanent seats WITH veto (plus 5 non-permanent seats) for Africa. So '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are out and '1 only' misses Uniting for Consensus.
155.tq: Ezulwini = 2 permanent (with veto) + 5 non-permanent.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: **G4** = **Brazil, Germany, India, Japan**.
Statement 2: **Uniting for Consensus** ("Coffee Club"), led by **Italy** and including **Pakistan**, opposes new permanent seats.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Ezulwini Consensus (2005)** seeks **2 permanent seats with veto** and **5 non-permanent** seats for Africa.
xa: **L.69** = developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific; India is a member.
**IGN** (set up **2008**) publishes an annual "**Elements Paper**".
**China** opposes India's permanent seat and is not in the G4 (APPSC-G1 **2012**).

155.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: G4 — Opposition to permanent seats for Africa
Uniting for Consensus — Demand for new permanent seats
L.69 — Developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific
Ezulwini Consensus — Abolition of all non-permanent seats
155.x: The L.69 group consists of developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific. The G4 supports permanent seats, Uniting for Consensus opposes new permanent seats, and Ezulwini seeks African representation.
155.tq: Use the demand and membership columns to eliminate reversed descriptions.
xs: **L.69 — developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific** is correct — option **(3)**; India is a member.
**G4** demands permanent seats, including for **Africa**, not opposition to them.
**Uniting for Consensus** opposes new permanent seats; **Ezulwini** seeks more African seats, not abolition.
xa: **G4** = Brazil, Germany, India, Japan.
**Ezulwini Consensus (2005)** = **African Union** position: **2** permanent (with veto) + **5** non-permanent seats.
Uniting for Consensus is led by **Italy** and includes **Pakistan**.

155.s: A Charter amendment relating to reform of the United Nations Security Council requires approval by
o: two-thirds of the members, including all five permanent members
two-thirds of the permanent members alone
all members of the General Assembly without participation of the P5
a simple majority of all members including any three P5 members
155.x: A Charter amendment requires a two-thirds majority of members and ratification by all five permanent members of the Security Council.
155.tq: Ask which voting threshold and membership condition apply to the constitutional procedure.
xs: A Charter amendment needs **two-thirds of the members, including all five permanent members** — option **(1)**.
So UNSC reform can be blocked by any **one** of the **P5**.
xa: The **P5**: China, France, Russia, UK, USA; veto under **Article 27**.
**China** opposes India's permanent seat.
The **IGN** on reform was set up in **2008** as an informal UNGA working group.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-Governmental Negotiations (IGN) on UNSC reform:
1. The IGN is an informal working group of the UN General Assembly set up in 2008.
2. An annual 'Elements Paper' maps the points of agreement and disagreement.
3. The IGN is a subsidiary body of the Security Council in which the P5 veto applies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
155.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the IGN is an informal UNGA working group set up in 2008, and its annual Elements Paper maps agreements and disagreements. Statement 3 is wrong: it is a General Assembly process, not a Security Council body. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the Elements Paper, and options with 3 are wrong.
155.tq: IGN = UNGA, informal, 2008, annual Elements Paper.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the **IGN** is an **informal UNGA working group** set up in **2008**.
Statement 2: its annual **"Elements Paper"** maps agreements and disagreements.
Statement 3 wrong: it is a **General Assembly** process, not a Security Council body.
xa: India's Permanent Representative criticised the **2026** paper for **diluting consensus**.
**G4** (Brazil, Germany, India, Japan) seeks permanent seats; **Uniting for Consensus** opposes them.
Charter amendment needs **two-thirds** of members including **all P5**.

155.s:
Arrange the following Secretaries-General of the United Nations in chronological order of assuming office:
A. U Thant
B. Trygve Lie
C. Kurt Waldheim
D. Dag Hammarskjold
155.x: The order is Trygve Lie, Dag Hammarskjold, U Thant and Kurt Waldheim, corresponding to 1946, 1953, 1961 and 1972 respectively.
155.tq: Fix the first Secretary-General and then place the remaining officeholders by their starting years.
xs: Order: **Trygve Lie** (**1946**) → **Dag Hammarskjold** (**1953**) → **U Thant** (**1961**) → **Kurt Waldheim** (**1972**) — option **(1)** "**B, D, A, C**".
Lie was from **Norway**, Hammarskjold **Sweden**, U Thant **Burma**, Waldheim **Austria**.
xa: After Waldheim: **Perez de Cuellar** (Peru, first Latin American), **Boutros Boutros-Ghali** (Egypt, first African/Arab), **Kofi Annan** (Ghana).
Then **Ban Ki-moon** (South Korea, **2007**-16) and **Antonio Guterres** (Portugal, **2017**-).
**U Thant** was the **first Asian** SG.

155.s:
Consider the following pairs (Secretary-General - distinction):
1. U Thant - first Asian Secretary-General
2. Javier Perez de Cuellar - first Latin American Secretary-General
3. Kofi Annan - first African Secretary-General
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
155.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: U Thant (Burma) was the first Asian SG and Perez de Cuellar (Peru) the first Latin American. Pair 3 is wrong: the first African (and Arab) SG was Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt; Kofi Annan (Ghana) came after him. So '1 and 2 only'.
155.tq: First African SG = Boutros-Ghali, not Kofi Annan.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Pair 1: **U Thant** (Burma) = **first Asian** SG.
Pair 2: **Javier Perez de Cuellar** (Peru) = **first Latin American** SG.
Pair 3 wrong: the first African (and Arab) SG was **Boutros Boutros-Ghali** (Egypt, **1992**-96); **Kofi Annan** (Ghana) followed.
xa: Present SG: **Antonio Guterres** (Portugal), since **2017**.
The next SG's selection is under way — four candidates addressed the UNGA on **21-22 April 2026**.
The SG is the **"Chief Administrative Officer"**.

155.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Court of Justice:
1. It has 15 judges elected for 9-year terms.
2. Its judges are elected by the UN General Assembly alone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
155.x: Statement 1 is correct: 15 judges, 9-year terms. Statement 2 is wrong: judges are elected by the UNGA and the UNSC voting separately. So '1 only'; the other options either accept statement 2 or reject statement 1.
155.tq: ICJ judges: UNGA + UNSC, voting separately.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)** "**1 only**": the ICJ has **15 judges** with **9-year** terms.
Statement 2 wrong: judges are elected by the **UNGA and UNSC voting separately**.
xa: The ICJ is the **principal judicial organ**, at **The Hague**.
Indian ICJ judges: **B.N. Rau**, **Nagendra Singh**, **R.S. Pathak**, **Dalveer Bhandari**.
⚠ **15** = UNSC members and ICJ judges; **54** = ECOSOC.

155.s: Which Indian judge served as President of the International Court of Justice during 1985–1988?
155.x: Nagendra Singh, one of the Indian judges of the ICJ, served as its President from 1985 to 1988.
155.tq: Match the office and period with the correct person rather than merely identifying an Indian judge.
xs: **Nagendra Singh** was **ICJ President** from **1985-88** — option **(4)**.
**B.N. Rau**, **R.S. Pathak** and **Dalveer Bhandari** were also Indian ICJ judges, but not President in that period.
xa: ICJ = **15 judges**, **9-year** terms, elected by **UNGA and UNSC** separately.
In the **Kulbhushan Jadhav** case (**2019**), the ICJ found Pakistan breached the **Vienna Convention on Consular Relations**.
The ICJ gave a **unanimous advisory opinion on climate obligations** in **July 2025**.

155.s: In the Kulbhushan Jadhav case, the International Court of Justice held that Pakistan had breached which instrument and directed what action?
o: The UN Charter; immediate release without any further process
The Vienna Convention on Consular Relations; review of the conviction
The Rome Statute; annulment of the criminal proceedings
The Geneva Convention; transfer of the case to India
155.x: In 2019, the ICJ held that Pakistan had breached the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations and ordered a review of Kulbhushan Jadhav's conviction.
155.tq: Link the legal instrument to the precise remedy ordered, avoiding the stronger but unsupported remedy of immediate release.
xs: The ICJ held that Pakistan breached the **Vienna Convention on Consular Relations** and ordered a **review of the conviction** — option **(2)**.
The **Kulbhushan Jadhav** verdict came in **2019**.
xa: ICJ's **July 2025** advisory opinion on climate obligations was **unanimous**.
India **abstained** on the **22 May 2026** UNGA climate resolution, citing that ICJ opinion.
**Nagendra Singh** was ICJ President **1985-88**.

155.s:
With reference to the ICJ's advisory opinion on climate obligations, consider the following statements:
1. It was unanimous.
2. It was issued in July 2025.
3. It was a judgment in the Kulbhushan Jadhav dispute.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
155.x: The ICJ gave a unanimous advisory opinion on climate obligations in July 2025. It was not a judgment in the Kulbhushan Jadhav case.
155.tq: Distinguish an advisory opinion on climate obligations from a contentious case involving an individual.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** "**1 and 2 only**": a **unanimous advisory opinion on climate obligations** in **July 2025**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Kulbhushan Jadhav** case was a separate **2019** judgment on the **Vienna Convention on Consular Relations**.
xa: India **abstained** (**141-8-28**) on the **May 2026** UNGA climate resolution, citing the ICJ's **July 2025** opinion.
ICJ judges: **15**, with **9-year** terms.
Seat of the ICJ: **The Hague**.

155.s: Who delivered India's first speech in Hindi in the United Nations General Assembly in 1977?
155.x: Atal Bihari Vajpayee delivered India's first UN General Assembly speech in Hindi in 1977 while serving as External Affairs Minister.
155.tq: Link the speaker with both the year and the ministerial position.
xs: **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** gave India's first UNGA speech in **Hindi** in **1977** — option **(4)**.
He spoke as **External Affairs Minister**, not as Prime Minister.
xa: **Ruchira Kamboj** was the first woman **Permanent Representative of India to the UN**.
The UN has **six official languages**; Hindi is not one of them.
India's UNSC term **1977-78** coincided with that year.

155.s: Who was the first woman to serve as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York?
155.x: Ruchira Kamboj was the first woman Permanent Representative of India to the UN (BPSC 2024). Sushma Swaraj was External Affairs Minister, not PR. Nirupama Rao was Foreign Secretary. Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was President of the UN General Assembly, not India's PR in New York.
155.tq: First woman PR of India to the UN = Ruchira Kamboj.
xs: **Ruchira Kamboj** was the first woman **Permanent Representative of India to the UN** — option **(2)**.
This was asked as a FIRST in BPSC **2024**; the PR is India's envoy at the UN in **New York**.
xa: Other India-at-UN firsts: **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** gave the first UNGA speech in **Hindi** (**1977**).
India signed the Charter as **British India (June 1945)**.
India's UNSC **2028-29** bid was launched by EAM **Jaishankar** on **13 July 2026**.

156.s: Which of the following is a specialised agency of the United Nations?
156.x: IFAD is a UN specialised agency as well as an international financial institution serving rural poor populations.
156.tq: Distinguish specialised agencies from funds and programmes.
xs: The **International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)** is a UN **specialised agency** — option **(4)**; it is also an **international financial institution** for the rural poor.
**WFP**, **UNICEF** and **UNDP** are **funds and programmes** created by the GA with **voluntary funding**, not specialised agencies.
xa: IFAD is headquartered in **Rome** (**1977**).
⚠ **Rome** = FAO, IFAD, WFP; **Nairobi** = UNEP, UN-Habitat.
⚠ **IAEA, WTO, OPCW** are **related organisations**, not specialised agencies.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about UN specialised agencies:
1. They are autonomous organisations with their own treaties and budgets.
2. They are linked to the Economic and Social Council.
3. They are created exclusively through voluntary funding by the General Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: Specialised agencies are autonomous, have their own treaties and budgets, and are linked to ECOSOC. The description of creation through voluntary General Assembly funding applies to funds and programmes, not specialised agencies.
156.tq: Reject the category-swapping statement about voluntary funding.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: specialised agencies are **autonomous**, with their **own treaty and budget**.
Statement 2: they are **linked to ECOSOC**.
Statement 3 wrong: creation by the **GA** with **voluntary funding** describes **funds and programmes** (UNICEF, UNDP, UNEP), not agencies.
xa: Specialised agencies include **WHO, ILO, UNESCO, FAO, IFAD, ITU, UPU, WIPO, IMO, ICAO, UNIDO, WMO, IMF, World Bank**.
**UNHCR** (**1950**, Geneva) is an **office of the GA**.
**IAEA, WTO, OPCW** = related organisations reporting to GA/UNSC.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about the classification of UN bodies:
1. UNICEF, UNDP and UNEP are funds and programmes created by the General Assembly.
2. UNHCR is a specialised agency linked to ECOSOC.
3. IAEA, WTO and OPCW are related organisations, not specialised agencies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: UNICEF, UNDP and UNEP are funds and programmes created by the GA with voluntary funding. Statement 2 is wrong: UNHCR (1950, Geneva) is an Office of the General Assembly for refugee protection, not a specialised agency. Statement 3 is correct: IAEA, WTO and OPCW are related organisations reporting to the GA/UNSC. So 1 and 3 only (C); A and B include the wrong statement 2, D includes all.
156.tq: Three tiers: specialised agencies (own treaty, ECOSOC), funds/programmes (GA, voluntary), related organisations (IAEA, WTO, OPCW); UNHCR is a GA office.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: **UNICEF, UNDP and UNEP** are **funds and programmes** created by the GA.
Statement 2 wrong: **UNHCR** (**1950**, Geneva) is an **office of the GA** for refugee protection, not a specialised agency.
Statement 3: **IAEA, WTO and OPCW** are **related organisations**, not specialised agencies.
xa: Other funds and programmes: **UNFPA**, **UN-Habitat**, **WFP**.
**UNHCR** won the Nobel Peace Prize twice: **1954, 1981**.
**IAEA** is based in **Vienna** (**1957**).

156.s:
Consider the following statements about the mandates of UN bodies:
1. UNEP's mandate covers climate, biodiversity and pollution.
2. UNICEF's mandate is the protection of refugees.
3. WFP is the world's largest humanitarian agency against hunger and is funded entirely by voluntary contributions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: UNEP deals with climate, biodiversity and pollution. Statement 2 is wrong: UNICEF deals with children's rights; refugees are UNHCR's mandate. Statement 3 is correct: WFP is the largest humanitarian agency against hunger and is funded entirely by voluntary contributions. So 1 and 3 only (C); A and B include statement 2, D includes all.
156.tq: Swap traps: UNICEF = children, UNHCR = refugees.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: **UNEP** covers **climate, biodiversity and pollution**.
Statement 2 wrong: **UNICEF** = **children's rights**; refugees are **UNHCR's** mandate.
Statement 3: **WFP** is the world's largest humanitarian agency against hunger, funded entirely by **voluntary contributions**.
xa: **WFP** won the Nobel Peace Prize in **2020**.
India signed a **5-year rice supply agreement with WFP** (**2026**).
**UNEP** HQ: **Nairobi, Kenya** (**1972**, after the Stockholm Conference).

156.s: The Global Environment Facility, established in 1992, is run in partnership by which of the following?
156.x: The GEF is a financial mechanism operated in partnership by UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank.
156.tq: Use the three-body partnership as the identifying feature.
xs: The **GEF (1992)** is a financial mechanism run in partnership by **UNDP, UNEP and World Bank** — option **(1)**.
The other trios (ILO/FAO/IFAD, UNICEF/UNHCR/UNESCO, WHO/WFP/UNFPA) have no role in the GEF per the notes.
xa: **UNDP** = development + poverty; co-builds the **Global MPI** with **OPHI**.
**UNEP** = climate, biodiversity, pollution; publishes the **Emissions Gap Report**.
The **World Bank** and **IMF** are counted among the **specialised agencies**.

156.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The WHO is headquartered at Geneva and was founded in 1948.
2. The FAO was founded on 16 October 1945 and is headquartered at Rome.
3. The World Food Programme was founded in 1961 and is headquartered at Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: WHO, Geneva, 1948 (7 April). Statement 2 is correct: FAO, Rome, 16 October 1945. Statement 3 is wrong: WFP was founded in 1961 but its HQ is Rome, not Geneva. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, while C and D wrongly include statement 3.
156.tq: Rome hosts the food trio - FAO, WFP and IFAD; Geneva hosts WHO, ILO, ITU, WIPO.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
