Statement 1: **WHO** — **Geneva**, **1948** (7 April).
Statement 2: **FAO** — **Rome**, **16 Oct 1945**.
Statement 3 wrong: **WFP** dates from **1961** but is headquartered at **Rome**, not Geneva.
xa: **World Health Day** = **7 April**; **World Food Day** = **16 October**.
**IFAD** is also in **Rome** (**1977**).
**WFP** won the Nobel Peace Prize in **2020**.

156.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
156.x: IFAD is headquartered in Rome and was founded in 1977. WFP is headquartered in Rome, UPU in Bern and UNIDO in Vienna.
156.tq: Start with the sure headquarters pair and verify the year.
xs: **IFAD — Rome — 1977** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**WFP** is in **Rome** (not Geneva); **UPU** is in **Bern** (not Paris); **UNIDO** is in **Vienna** (not Nairobi).
xa: IFAD is both a **specialised agency** and an **international financial institution** for the rural poor.
⚠ **Rome** = FAO, IFAD, WFP.

156.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
156.x: UNICEF was founded in 1946 but its headquarters is in New York, not Geneva.
156.tq: Find the wrong location while keeping the founding year in view.
xs: **UNICEF — Geneva — 1946** is NOT correctly matched — option **(4)**: UNICEF dates from **1946** but its HQ is **New York**.
The others are correct: **UNEP** — Nairobi — **1972**; **UNIDO** — Vienna — **1966**; **IAEA** — Vienna — **1957**.
xa: UNICEF's founding year **1946** was asked in **2019**.
UNICEF won the Nobel Peace Prize in **1965**.
UNICEF's mandate: **children's rights**.

156.s: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), set up after the 1972 Stockholm Conference, is headquartered at:
156.x: UNEP was created in 1972 following the Stockholm Conference and has its HQ at Nairobi, Kenya. Geneva hosts WHO/ILO/ITU, Vienna hosts UNIDO/IAEA, and New York hosts UNICEF.
156.tq: UNEP HQ asked twice (2018, 2025): Nairobi.
xs: **UNEP**, set up in **1972** after the **Stockholm Conference**, is headquartered at **Nairobi, Kenya** — option **(2)**.
**Geneva** hosts WHO/ILO/ITU, **Vienna** hosts UNIDO/IAEA, and **New York** hosts UNICEF.
xa: UNEP HQ was asked twice (**2018**, **2025**).
**Emissions Gap 2025**: current policies → ~**2.8°C**; full NDCs → **2.3-2.5°C**.
**UN-Habitat** also has its HQ in **Nairobi**.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Labour Organization:
1. It was founded in 1919.
2. It became a UN specialised agency in 1946.
3. It is headquartered at Rome.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: ILO was founded in 1919. Statement 2 is correct: it became a UN specialised agency in 1946. Statement 3 is wrong: ILO is headquartered at Geneva; Rome hosts FAO, IFAD and WFP. So 1 and 2 only.
156.tq: ILO older than the UN: 1919, Geneva.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the **ILO** was founded in **1919**; statement 2: it became a UN **specialised agency** in **1946**.
Statement 3 wrong: the ILO is at **Geneva**; **Rome** hosts FAO, IFAD and WFP.
xa: ILO is **tripartite**: governments, employers and workers.
ILO Director-General: **Gilbert F. Houngbo**.
The ILO won the Nobel Peace Prize in **1969**.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about India's roles in UN bodies:
1. Dr Harsh Vardhan chaired the WHO Executive Board in 2020-21.
2. Apurva Chandra chaired the ILO Governing Body in 2020-21.
3. India was re-elected to the ICAO Council for 2022-2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: Dr Harsh Vardhan chaired the WHO Executive Board in 2020-21. Statement 2 is correct: Apurva Chandra chaired the ILO Governing Body in 2020-21. Statement 3 is wrong: India was re-elected to the ICAO Council for 2025-2028, not 2022-2025. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
156.tq: Pair the person with the body (Harsh Vardhan - WHO, Apurva Chandra - ILO) and check the years of the ICAO term.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: **Dr Harsh Vardhan** chaired the **WHO Executive Board** (**2020-21**).
Statement 2: **Apurva Chandra** chaired the **ILO Governing Body** (**2020-21**).
Statement 3 wrong: India was re-elected to the **ICAO Council** for **2025-2028**, not 2022-2025.
xa: India chaired the **Commission on Narcotic Drugs** (**68th session**, **March 2025**).
ILO DG: **Gilbert F. Houngbo**.
ICAO stems from the **1944 Chicago Convention**; HQ **Montreal**.

156.s: In March 2025, India chaired the 68th session of which UN body?
o: UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
156.x: India chaired the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, a functional commission of ECOSOC, at its 68th session in March 2025. UNODC is the UN office (secretariat) on drugs and crime, the UN Drug Control Programme is a predecessor programme, and the INCB is a separate treaty body; none of these was the chaired body.
156.tq: Chaired body = CND (ECOSOC functional commission), not UNODC.
xs: India chaired the **Commission on Narcotic Drugs (CND)** at its **68th session** in **March 2025** — option **(3)**.
The CND is an **ECOSOC functional commission**; **UNODC** and the "**UN Drug Control Programme**" are the usual distractors.
xa: Other ECOSOC functional commissions: **Commission on the Status of Women (1946)**, **Statistical Commission**.
India's other roles: **WHO Executive Board** chair (**2020-21**), **ILO Governing Body** chair (**2020-21**).
India re-elected to the **ICAO Council** for **2025-2028**.

156.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Labour Organization:
1. It has a tripartite structure of governments, employers and workers.
2. Its tripartite structure operates in the International Labour Conference and ECOSOC.
3. It describes itself as the leading normative agency on labour standards.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: Statement 1 is correct: governments, employers and workers form the ILO's tripartite structure. Statement 2 is wrong: the tripartite bodies are the International Labour Conference and the Governing Body, not ECOSOC. Statement 3 is correct: the ILO calls itself the leading normative agency on labour standards. So 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D include statement 2.
156.tq: ILO tripartism lives in two ILO organs: the Conference and the Governing Body.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: the ILO is **tripartite** — **governments, employers and workers**.
Statement 2 wrong: tripartism operates in the **International Labour Conference** and the **Governing Body**, not ECOSOC.
Statement 3: the ILO calls itself the **leading normative agency** on labour standards.
xa: ILO founded **1919**; UN specialised agency **1946**; HQ **Geneva**.
The **Universal Social Protection report** urges decoupling social protection from **single-employer contracts** (gig work).
**Global Coalition for Social Justice**: ILO works with India on a network of **AI observatories**.

156.s: Which pair of ILO Fundamental Conventions has India NOT ratified?
156.x: India has not ratified Convention C87 on Freedom of Association and Convention C98 on the Right to Organise and Collective Bargaining. The other listed pairs have been ratified.
156.tq: Find the exception among otherwise ratified convention pairs.
xs: India has NOT ratified **C87 and C98** — option **(1)**: **Freedom of Association** (C87) and **Collective Bargaining** (C98).
India **has ratified** **C100 and C111** (equal pay, discrimination), **C29 and C105** (forced labour), and **C138 and C182** (child labour, **2017**).
xa: ⚠ India has **not ratified C87, C98, C189**.
**C189** = **Domestic Workers Convention (2011)**, adopted by the ILC.
ILO-UNICEF estimate: **160 million** child labourers globally.

156.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India and ILO conventions:
1. India has ratified C29 and C105.
2. India has ratified C100 and C111.
3. India has ratified C189 on Domestic Workers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: India has ratified C29, C105, C100 and C111. It has not ratified the Domestic Workers Convention C189, adopted by the ILC in 2011.
156.tq: Use the convention number and ratification status together to identify the false statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: India has ratified **C29** and **C105** (forced labour).
Statement 2: India has ratified **C100** (equal remuneration) and **C111** (discrimination).
Statement 3 wrong: India has **not ratified C189** on Domestic Workers (adopted **2011**).
xa: India ratified **C138** and **C182** in **2017**.
Also not ratified: **C87** (freedom of association) and **C98** (collective bargaining).
The ILO is the **leading normative agency** on labour standards.

156.s: According to the ILO–UNICEF joint estimate, the number of child labourers globally is approximately:
156.x: The ILO–UNICEF joint estimate places the number of child labourers globally at 160 million.
156.tq: Place the figure correctly by checking the order of magnitude.
xs: The **ILO-UNICEF** joint estimate puts global child labourers at **160 million** — option **(3)**.
It is a **joint** estimate of the labour agency (**ILO**) and the children's-rights fund (**UNICEF**).
xa: India ratified the child-labour conventions **C138** and **C182** in **2017**.
**ILO Employment and Social Trends 2026**: unemployment **4.9% (186 million)**; **284 million** workers below **$3/day**.
UNICEF's mandate: **children's rights**.

156.s: The World Heritage Convention was adopted in which year?
156.x: The World Heritage Convention was adopted in 1972.
156.tq: Use the direct year-recall approach for a foundational convention.
xs: The **World Heritage Convention** was adopted in **1972** — option **(2)**.
**1981** is a UNHCR Nobel year and **1988** the UN Peacekeeping Forces' Nobel — not the Convention.
xa: Inscription needs a **Tentative List** entry + **Outstanding Universal Value** + **1 of 10 criteria**.
**WHL (July 2026)**: **1,273 properties in 173 countries**; **Italy 62**, China **61**.
The **ASI** is India's nodal agency for World Heritage.

156.s: Sarnath was inscribed as India's 45th World Heritage Site at which session and venue?
156.x: Sarnath was inscribed at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee held in Busan, South Korea, in July 2026. It became India's 45th World Heritage Site and Uttar Pradesh's fourth.
156.tq: Match the site with the correct committee session and venue.
xs: **Sarnath** was inscribed at the **48th session** of the World Heritage Committee in **Busan, South Korea** (**Jul 2026**) — option **(2)**.
It became **India's 45th** WH Site and **UP's 4th**.
**20th ICH Committee (New Delhi)** = Deepavali; **43rd General Conference (Samarkand)** = Lucknow; **47th session (Paris)** = Maratha Military Landscapes.
xa: **Hoysala temples** (Karnataka) were inscribed in **Sep 2023**.
The **ASI** looks after **28** WH properties among **3,688** centrally protected monuments.
First Indian WH site: **Ajanta** (with Ellora), **1983**.

156.s: The Hoysala temples of Karnataka were inscribed on the World Heritage List in:
156.x: The Hoysala temples of Karnataka were inscribed in September 2023. The year 1983 relates to India's first World Heritage inscription involving Ajanta and Ellora.
156.tq: Distinguish a recent inscription date from the earlier landmark inscription year.
xs: The **Hoysala temples** of Karnataka were inscribed in **September 2023** — option **(2)** (a PYQ).
**1983** = India's first inscription (**Ajanta** with Ellora); **2025** = Maratha Military Landscapes; **July 2026** = Sarnath.
xa: Sarnath = **India's 45th** WH Site, inscribed at the **48th session** in **Busan**.
The **ASI** is nodal for World Heritage in India.
Inscription needs **Outstanding Universal Value** + 1 of **10 criteria**.

156.s: The first Indian World Heritage site, inscribed along with Ellora, was:
156.x: Ajanta, along with Ellora, was India's first World Heritage site inscription in 1983.
156.tq: Use the historical first rather than the latest inscription in the same subject area.
xs: **Ajanta**, inscribed with **Ellora** in **1983**, was India's first World Heritage site — option **(3)**.
The others are recent: **Hoysala temples** (**Sep 2023**), **Maratha Military Landscapes** (**2025**), **Sarnath** (**Jul 2026**).
xa: Sarnath = **India's 45th** WH Site (UP's **4th**).
The **ASI** is the nodal agency for World Heritage in India.
The **World Heritage Convention** was adopted in **1972**.

156.s: The Information for All Programme is associated with which organisation?
156.x: The Information for All Programme, or IFAP, is a UNESCO programme.
156.tq: Match the programme title to the responsible agency.
xs: The **Information for All Programme (IFAP)** is a **UNESCO** programme — option **(3)**.
It was asked in **2019**; **UNDP**, **ILO** and **UNEP** have development, labour and environment mandates.
xa: Other UNESCO programmes: **Man and the Biosphere (MAB)**; UNESCO leads **SDG-4** (Education 2030).
UNESCO reports: **GEM**, **UNESCO Science Report**, **World Water Development Report**.
UNESCO HQ: **Paris**; **194 members + 12 associate members**.

156.s:
Which of the following statements about UNESCO is correct?
1. It runs the Man and the Biosphere Programme.
2. It leads SDG-4 concerning Education 2030.
3. It is the agency responsible for the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
156.x: UNESCO runs the Man and the Biosphere Programme and leads SDG-4 on Education 2030. The Global MPI is co-built by UNDP and OPHI.
156.tq: Reject the agency swap in the third statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: UNESCO runs **Man and the Biosphere (MAB)**; statement 2: it leads **SDG-4** (Education 2030).
Statement 3 wrong: the **Global MPI** is co-built by **UNDP** with **OPHI**.
xa: UNESCO also runs the **Information for All Programme (IFAP)**.
UNESCO Executive Board: **58** members.
India is a **founding member** of UNESCO (**1945**).

156.s:
With reference to Indian entries in UNESCO lists, consider the following statements:
1. Lucknow is India's second City of Gastronomy after Hyderabad.
2. Hyderabad received the designation in 2019.
3. Deepavali was inscribed at the 20th Intangible Cultural Heritage Committee meeting in New Delhi in December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
156.x: All three statements are correct. Lucknow followed Hyderabad as India's second gastronomy city, while Deepavali was inscribed at the 20th ICH Committee meeting at the Red Fort, New Delhi.
156.tq: Separate World Heritage, Intangible Heritage and Creative Cities categories before selecting the code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
Statements 1 and 2: **Lucknow** is India's **2nd** City of Gastronomy after **Hyderabad (2019)**.
Statement 3: **Deepavali** was inscribed at the **20th ICH Committee**, **Red Fort, New Delhi (Dec 2025)**.
xa: Lucknow's designation came at the **43rd General Conference**, **Samarkand**.
**Yoga** is on the Intangible Heritage list (**2016**).
Memory of the World International Register: **Bhagavad Gita** manuscripts and the **Natyashastra**.

156.s: Yoga was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in:
156.x: Yoga was inscribed on the Intangible Heritage list in 2016. 2019 is the year of Hyderabad's gastronomy designation and 2025 (December) is Deepavali's inscription; 2014 is not the year of any of these inscriptions.
156.tq: Yoga ICH 2016; Deepavali ICH Dec 2025.
xs: **Yoga** was inscribed on the Intangible Heritage list in **2016** — option **(2)**.
**2019** = Hyderabad's gastronomy title; **2025** = **Deepavali** (Dec, **20th ICH Committee**, New Delhi).
xa: **International Day of Yoga** = **21 June** (UN GA).
**Deepavali** was inscribed at the **Red Fort, New Delhi**.
Memory of the World International Register: **Natyashastra**, **Bhagavad Gita** manuscripts.

156.s: The WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine is located at which place?
156.x: The WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine is located at Jamnagar, Gujarat. Its foundation stone was laid in April 2022.
156.tq: Use the exact city-state location rather than the country alone.
xs: The **WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine** is at **Jamnagar, Gujarat** — option **(4)**.
Its foundation stone was laid in **April 2022**; it is the **first** such global centre.
xa: **WHO**: HQ **Geneva**, founded **1948** (7 April = **World Health Day**).
**Dr Harsh Vardhan** chaired the **WHO Executive Board** (**2020-21**).
An **Apr 2026** US memorandum to quit **31 UN entities** includes **WHO**.

156.s: Which report is published by UNFPA?
156.x: The State of World Population is a flagship report of UNFPA.
156.tq: Match the report title with the agency’s mandate.
xs: The **State of World Population** is a **UNFPA** report — option **(4)**.
**World Employment and Social Outlook** = **ILO**; **Human Development Report** = **UNDP**; **Emissions Gap Report** = **UNEP**.
xa: **UNFPA** is a **fund/programme** created by the GA.
UNESCO reports: **GEM**, **Science Report**, **World Water Development Report**.
**SOFI** is joint: **FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP, WHO**.

156.s: Which one of the following is NOT a UNESCO report?
156.x: The Emissions Gap Report is published by UNEP. The other three reports are associated with UNESCO.
156.tq: Find the report belonging to the neighbouring environmental agency.
xs: The **Emissions Gap Report** is NOT a UNESCO report — option **(4)**; it is published by **UNEP**.
**World Water Development Report**, **UNESCO Science Report** and **Global Education Monitoring (GEM)** are UNESCO's.
xa: **Emissions Gap 2025**: current policies ~**2.8°C**; full NDCs **2.3-2.5°C**.
The earlier **2024** report projected **2.5-2.9°C**.

156.s: The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) is jointly associated with which group?
o: FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO
UNDP, UNEP, UNESCO, ILO and UNHCR
FAO, UNFPA, WIPO, WTO and IAEA
WHO, UNESCO, ICAO, IMO and ITU
156.x: SOFI is jointly published by FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO.
156.tq: Recognise the complete multi-agency reporting partnership.
xs: **SOFI** is jointly produced by **FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO** — option **(1)**.
Three of them are **Rome**-based (**FAO, IFAD, WFP**); the other groups mix in unrelated bodies like **UNHCR**, **WTO** or **ITU**.
xa: **SOFI 2026** theme: **high cost of a healthy diet**.
Hunger fell for a **3rd** year to **7.8% (645 million)**; **Africa (309 million)** overtook Asia.
Healthy diet cost = **4.28 PPP$/day**.

156.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: World Employment and Social Outlook — UNESCO
156.x: The Human Development Report is a flagship UNDP publication. The other reports are associated respectively with UNFPA, UNEP and ILO.
156.tq: Use the report’s subject area to identify its agency.
xs: **Human Development Report — UNDP** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**State of World Population** = **UNFPA** (not ILO); **Emissions Gap** = **UNEP** (not UNFPA); **World Employment and Social Outlook** = **ILO** (not UNESCO).
xa: UNDP also co-builds the **Global MPI** with **OPHI** (**2010**).
ILO **Employment and Social Trends 2026**: unemployment **4.9% (186 million)**.
UNESCO reports: **GEM**, **Science Report**, **World Water Development Report**.

156.s: Which of the following correctly states the Emissions Gap Report 2025 projections?
o: Current policies imply 1.5°C warming and full NDCs imply 3.0°C warming.
Full NDCs imply 2.3–2.5°C warming, while current policies imply about 2.8°C.
Full NDCs imply about 2.8°C warming, while current policies imply 1.5–2.0°C.
Both current policies and full NDCs imply exactly 2.5°C warming.
156.x: The report projects approximately 2.8°C under current policies and 2.3–2.5°C if full NDCs are implemented.
156.tq: Compare the two policy scenarios without reversing their order.
xs: **Emissions Gap 2025**: full NDCs imply **2.3-2.5°C**, while current policies imply about **2.8°C** — option **(2)**.
The other options swap or invent the figures; **1.5°C** and **2°C** are targets, not projections.
xa: The earlier **2024** report projected **2.5-2.9°C**.
The Emissions Gap Report is published by **UNEP** (HQ **Nairobi**).

156.s: The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) was received in which years?
156.x: UNHCR received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and again in 1981.
156.tq: Pair the organisation with its distinctive two-year Nobel record.
xs: **UNHCR** won the Nobel Peace Prize in **1954 and 1981** — option **(4)**.
**1988** = UN Peacekeeping Forces, **2001** = UN and Kofi Annan, **2005** = IAEA, **2013** = OPCW, **1965** = UNICEF, **1969** = ILO.
xa: ⚠ UNHCR is the agency that won **twice**.
**World Refugee Day** = **20 June** (UNHCR).
UNHCR (**1950**, Geneva) is an **office of the GA**.

156.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists.

List-I (Body or recipient)
a. UNICEF
b. ILO
c. UN Peacekeeping Forces
d. UN and Kofi Annan

List-II (Year)
i. 1965
ii. 1969
iii. 1988
iv. 2001

The correct matching is:
156.x: UNICEF won in 1965, ILO in 1969, the UN Peacekeeping Forces in 1988, and the UN together with Kofi Annan in 2001.
156.tq: Begin with the organisation-year pairs that are most distinctive and verify the complete code.
xs: **UNICEF** — **1965**; **ILO** — **1969**; **UN Peacekeeping Forces** — **1988**; **UN and Kofi Annan** — **2001** — option **(2)** "**a–i, b–ii, c–iii, d–iv**".
The years run in the same order as List-I, so each is matched straight across.
xa: **IAEA and ElBaradei** = **2005**; **IPCC** (with Al Gore) = **2007**; **OPCW** = **2013**.
**WFP** = **2020**, for combating hunger.
**UNHCR** won twice: **1954, 1981**.

156.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
156.x: WFP received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020, not 2019. IAEA and ElBaradei, IPCC and Al Gore, and OPCW correspond to 2005, 2007 and 2013 respectively.
156.tq: Use the NOT formulation to identify the altered year in an otherwise familiar Nobel sequence.
xs: **WFP — 2019** is NOT correctly matched — option **(1)**: WFP won in **2020**.
The rest are right: **OPCW** — **2013**; **IPCC and Al Gore** — **2007**; **IAEA and ElBaradei** — **2005**.
xa: The **IPCC** shared **2007** equally with **Al Gore**.
WFP won for **combating hunger** and improving conditions for **peace in conflict areas**.
**OPCW** and **IAEA** are **related organisations**, not specialised agencies.

156.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
156.x: International Day of Yoga is associated with the UN General Assembly, not UNHCR.
156.tq: Identify the agency substitution in a familiar day-agency pairing.
xs: **International Day of Yoga — UNHCR** is NOT correctly matched — option **(2)**; Yoga Day is a **UN GA** day.
**World Food Day** — **FAO** and **World Health Day** — **WHO** are correct; UNHCR's day is **World Refugee Day** (**20 June**).
xa: **International Day of Yoga** = **21 June**.
**Yoga** is on UNESCO's Intangible Heritage list (**2016**).
**World Food Day** = **16 October**; **World Health Day** = **7 April**.

156.s: Which one of the following pairs of International Day and date is correctly matched?
156.x: World Food Day (FAO) is on 16 October, the FAO's founding date. World Refugee Day (UNHCR) is 20 June, World Health Day (WHO) is 7 April and the International Day of Yoga is 21 June, so the other pairs are mismatched.
156.tq: Food Day = FAO founding day, 16 Oct.
xs: **World Food Day — 16 October** is correctly matched — option **(2)**, the **FAO's** founding date (**1945**).
**World Refugee Day** is **20 June**, **World Health Day** is **7 April**, and **Yoga Day** is **21 June**.
xa: FAO HQ: **Rome** (with **IFAD** and **WFP**).
**WHO** was founded on **7 April 1948**.
**UNHCR** won the Nobel Peace Prize in **1954** and **1981**.

156.s: India signed a five-year rice supply agreement in 2026 with which organisation?
156.x: India signed a five-year rice supply agreement with the World Food Programme in 2026.
156.tq: Apply the “food supply” clue to distinguish WFP from other UN agencies.
xs: India signed a **5-year rice supply agreement** with the **WFP** in **2026** — option **(3)**.
**FAO** is the Rome food agency for **World Food Day**; **UNHCR** handles refugees; **UNDP** development.
xa: WFP: **Rome**, founded **1961**; funded entirely by **voluntary contributions**.
WFP won the Nobel Peace Prize in **2020**.
WFP is a co-author of **SOFI** with FAO, IFAD, UNICEF and WHO.

157.s: The Bretton Woods plan was substantially based on the ideas of:
o: John Maynard Keynes and Friedrich Hayek
Harry Dexter White and Milton Friedman
Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes
157.x: The plan was built on the ideas of Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes.
157.tq: Test the persons associated with the formulation of the institutional framework.
xs: The Bretton Woods plan was built on the ideas of **Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes** — option **(4)** — its **architects**.
Hayek, Friedman, Ricardo and Smith are not named as architects of the plan.
xa: The system rested on **fixed exchange rates**: currencies pegged to the **dollar**, dollar pegged to **gold**.
Created at Bretton Woods: **IMF + IBRD** (**July 1944**).
India was a **founding member** of both the IMF and IBRD.

157.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
157.x: The IMF and IBRD were founded in 1944. The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945, began operations on 1 March 1947, and France was its first borrower on 8 May 1947.
157.tq: Separate the closely spaced dates and verify the person or country attached to each event.
xs: **IMF and IBRD — founded in 1944** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
The other dates are swapped: formal existence = **27 December 1945**; financial operations = **1 March 1947**.
The **first IMF borrower** was **France** (**8 May 1947**), not India.
xa: The IMF came into formal existence with **29 members**.
**SDR** ("paper gold") was created in **1967-69**.
⚠ All three IMF dates (**1944**, **27 Dec 1945**, **1 March 1947**) have been asked.

157.s: Which one of the following was NOT created at the Bretton Woods Conference?
o: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
157.x: The IMF and IBRD were created at Bretton Woods. The proposed International Trade Organization was not created; GATT filled the gap from 1947 until the WTO was established in 1995.
157.tq: Find the institution that was proposed but did not emerge from the conference.
xs: The **International Trade Organization** was NOT created at Bretton Woods — option **(2)**.
Bretton Woods created the **IMF** and the **IBRD**.
The gap was filled by **GATT (1947)** until the **WTO (1995)**.
xa: Conference: **Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA, July 1944**.
Architects: **Harry Dexter White** and **John Maynard Keynes**.
Both the IMF and the World Bank are headquartered in **Washington D.C.**

157.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Bretton Woods system, currencies were pegged to the dollar and the dollar was pegged to gold.
2. The Smithsonian Agreement of 1971 widened the exchange-rate band to 2.5%.
3. The Smithsonian Agreement lasted about 14 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bretton Woods had fixed exchange rates, currencies pegged to the dollar and the dollar to gold. Statement 2 is correct: the Smithsonian Agreement (1971) widened the band to 2.5%. Statement 3 is wrong: it lasted only 14 months, not 14 years. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
157.tq: Smithsonian = 2.5% band, 14 months - a short-lived patch on Bretton Woods.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: under Bretton Woods, currencies were pegged to the **dollar**, and the dollar to **gold** (fixed exchange rates).
Statement 2: the **Smithsonian Agreement (1971)** widened the band to **2.5%**.
Statement 3 wrong: it lasted only **14 months**, not 14 years.
xa: The IMF began financial operations on **1 March 1947**.
The **SDR** ("paper gold") was created in **1967-69**.
The **ITO** never came up; **GATT (1947)** filled the gap.

157.s: India's position in relation to the IMF and IBRD is that it:
o: Joined the IBRD as a founding member but joined the IMF later
Was not a member of either institution at their founding
Joined the IMF in 1947 but not the IBRD
Joined both as a founding member
157.x: India was a founding member of both the IMF and the IBRD.
157.tq: Test membership status directly, using the paired institutions as a confusable combination.
xs: India **joined both as a founding member** — option **(4)**: a founding member of the **IMF** and the **IBRD**.
India is also a **founding member** of the **ADB** (**1966**).
xa: The IMF came into formal existence with **29 members** on **27 December 1945**.
During the **1991 BoP crisis**, India took ~**$7 billion** from the IMF/World Bank.
⚠ India is **not a member** of **ICSID**.

157.s: During India's balance-of-payments crisis in 1991, approximately how much was obtained from the IMF and World Bank, contributing to the New Economic Policy?
157.x: India obtained about $7 billion from the IMF and World Bank during the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis, preceding the New Economic Policy.
157.tq: Distinguish the billion-scale figure from misleading million and larger-billion alternatives.
xs: India obtained about **$7 billion** from the IMF/World Bank in the **1991 BoP crisis** — option **(1)**.
This led into the **New Economic Policy**.
xa: India's allocated **SDRs** are usable for **BoP** needs.
IBRD's **$1.5 billion** facility supports the **National Green Hydrogen Mission**.
**Criticism**: IMF/WB loans carry **structural adjustment conditions**.

157.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the weights in the IMF quota formula?
157.x: The quota formula assigns weights of GDP 50%, openness 30%, variability 15% and reserves 5%.
157.tq: Preserve the exact order and percentages in the quota formula.
xs: IMF quota formula weights: **GDP 50%, openness 30%, variability 15%, reserves 5%** — option **(2)**.
The other options shuffle the same four numbers.
xa: **Quotas** decide a member's financial contribution, borrowing access and **voting power**.
The **US alone holds a veto** in the IMF (May **2026**).
The Global North (**15%** of population) holds ~**60%** of votes.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about the IMF:
1. Members' quotas are reviewed periodically.
2. The International Monetary and Financial Committee (IMFC) advises the Board of Governors.
3. Article IV consultations are annual bilateral surveillance of each member's economy.
4. The IMF is headquartered at New York.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: quotas are reviewed periodically, the IMFC advises the Board of Governors, and Article IV means annual bilateral surveillance. Statement 4 is wrong: the IMF is headquartered at Washington D.C. So 1, 2 and 3 only (B); A omits statement 3, C and D include statement 4.
157.tq: Both Bretton Woods twins (IMF and World Bank) sit in Washington D.C.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1, 2 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: **quotas** are **reviewed periodically**; statement 2: the **IMFC** advises the **Board of Governors**.
Statement 3: **Article IV** = **annual bilateral surveillance** of each member's economy.
Statement 4 wrong: the IMF is headquartered at **Washington D.C.**, not New York.
xa: IMF facilities: **Stand-By Arrangement**, **Extended Fund Facility**, **Rapid Financing Instrument**, **PRGT**.
**SDR** basket has **five currencies** since **Oct 2016**.
⚠ **Washington D.C.** = IMF + World Bank; **Manila** = ADB; **Beijing** = AIIB; **Shanghai** = NDB.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about Special Drawing Rights (SDRs):
1. Since October 2016, the SDR basket has consisted of five currencies.
2. The Chinese renminbi is not part of the SDR basket.
3. India's allocated SDRs can be used for balance-of-payments needs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: Statement 1 is correct: since October 2016 the basket has five currencies - US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, yen and pound. Statement 2 is wrong: the renminbi was added in 2016. Statement 3 is correct: India's allocated SDRs are usable for BoP needs. So 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D include statement 2.
157.tq: Older notes say four currencies - outdated; five since 2016 with the renminbi.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: since **Oct 2016**, the **SDR** basket has **five currencies** — US dollar, euro, **Chinese renminbi**, yen, pound.
Statement 2 wrong: the **renminbi** is in the basket.
Statement 3: India's allocated SDRs are usable for **BoP needs**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: older notes say **four** currencies — outdated.
The SDR ("**paper gold**") was created in **1967-69**.
**Article IV** = annual bilateral surveillance.

157.s: Which of the following is NOT an IMF lending or financing facility mentioned in the institutional framework?
157.x: Stand-By Arrangement, Extended Fund Facility and Rapid Financing Instrument are IMF facilities. Political-risk guarantees are associated with MIGA, not an IMF facility listed here.
157.tq: Separate IMF financing facilities from a World Bank Group risk-insurance function.
xs: **Political Risk Guarantee Facility** is NOT an IMF facility — option **(1)**; political-risk insurance is **MIGA's** job.
IMF facilities: **Stand-By Arrangement**, **Extended Fund Facility**, **Rapid Financing Instrument**, **PRGT**.
xa: **MIGA** (**1988**) gives **political-risk insurance and guarantees** to foreign investors.
**ESAF** had the **softest servicing terms**.
**Article IV** = annual bilateral surveillance of each member.

157.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the distribution of influence in the IMF and World Bank:
1. The Global North accounts for about 15% of the population but holds approximately 60% of the votes.
2. The United States alone holds a veto.
3. The BRICS New Delhi Declaration of September 2026 demanded quota and voting reform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: All three statements are correct. The declaration demanded reform in the context of the unequal distribution of population and voting power.
157.tq: Combine numerical inequality, veto power and the reform demand into one institutional-governance question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
Statements 1 and 2: the Global North (**15%** of population) holds ~**60%** of votes, and the **US alone holds a veto**.
Statement 3: the BRICS **New Delhi Declaration (Sep 2026)** demanded IMF/WB **quota and voting reform**.
xa: ⚠ **NDB** = equal votes, **no veto**; **IMF** = **quota-based** votes.
The declaration came at the **18th BRICS Summit**, New Delhi.
Criticism: **structural adjustment conditions**, sovereign immunity and Northern control of votes.

157.s:
Which of the following is a function of IMF quotas of member countries?
1. Determining the member's contribution
2. Influencing access to borrowing
3. Influencing voting power
4. Fixing the exchange rate of every member's currency
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
157.x: IMF quotas determine a member's contribution, borrowing access and voting power, and are reviewed periodically. They do not fix the exchange rate of every member's currency.
157.tq: Identify the institutional functions of a quota and reject an unrelated monetary-power claim.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)** "**1, 2 and 3 only**".
IMF **quotas** decide a member's **financial contribution**, **borrowing access** and **voting power**.
Statement 4 wrong: quotas do not fix exchange rates; the old **fixed-rate** peg was the Bretton Woods system itself.
xa: Formula weights: **GDP 50%**, **openness 30%**, **variability 15%**, **reserves 5%**.
Quotas are **reviewed periodically**.
The **US alone holds a veto** (May **2026**).

157.s: Which of the following institutions is correctly matched with its principal function?
o: IBRD — loans to middle-income governments for infrastructure and heavy capital projects
IDA — political-risk insurance for foreign investors
157.x: The IBRD provides loans to middle-income governments for infrastructure and heavy capital projects. MIGA provides political-risk insurance, ICSID settles investment disputes, and IFC undertakes private-sector investment and advisory work.
157.tq: Match each World Bank Group institution with its distinctive function.
xs: **IBRD — loans to middle-income governments** for infrastructure and heavy capital projects — option **(1)**.
**IDA** gives **interest-free credits and grants**; **MIGA** gives **political-risk insurance**; **ICSID** **settles investment disputes**; **IFC** handles **private-sector** work.
xa: World Bank loans are generally **medium and long term**.
⚠ India is **not a member** of **ICSID**.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about the World Bank Group:
1. IDA provides long-term interest-free credits and grants to the poorest countries.
2. IFC is concerned with private-sector investment, advisory services and asset management.
3. MIGA provides political-risk insurance and guarantees for foreign investors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: All three statements correctly describe IDA, IFC and MIGA.
157.tq: Use the distinctive service offered by each institution to eliminate swapped functions.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
**IDA** = long-term **interest-free credits and grants** to the poorest; **IFC** = **private-sector** investment, advisory and asset management; **MIGA** = **political-risk insurance**.
xa: **IFC** has **184** members and conceived the "**Doing Business**" report.
**ICSID** settles investment disputes; India is **not a member**.
**IBRD** lends to **middle-income** governments.

157.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
157.x: ICSID was established in 1966, not 1976. IDA, IFC and MIGA were established in 1960, 1956 and 1988 respectively.
157.tq: Check the year attached to each institution, especially the easily altered final digit.
xs: **ICSID — 1976** is NOT correctly matched — option **(4)**; ICSID dates from **1966**.
The others are correct: **IFC** — **1956**; **IDA** — **1960**; **MIGA** — **1988**.
xa: **IBRD** = **1944**, the first of the five.
ICSID **settles investment disputes**; **India is not a member**.
**ADB** was also established in **1966**.

157.s: With reference to the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes, which one of the following is correct?
o: It lends to middle-income governments, and India has veto power
It insures political risks, and India is a founding member
It settles investment disputes, and India is not a member
It provides interest-free credits to the poorest countries, and India is a member
157.x: ICSID settles investment disputes, and India is not a member of it.
157.tq: Distinguish dispute settlement from political-risk insurance and concessional lending.
xs: **ICSID** **settles investment disputes**, and **India is not a member** — option **(3)**.
Lending to middle-income governments is **IBRD**; political-risk insurance is **MIGA**; interest-free credits are **IDA**.
xa: ICSID dates from **1966**.
India **is** a **founding member** of the **IBRD**.

157.s: World Bank loans are generally characterised as:
o: Only emergency loans repayable within one year
Loans available exclusively to private corporations
157.x: World Bank loans are generally medium- and long-term in nature.
157.tq: Test the broad maturity classification rather than confusing loans with grants or guarantees.
xs: World Bank loans are generally **medium and long term** — option **(1)** (asked **2019**).
**IBRD** loans finance **infrastructure and heavy capital projects** — not short emergency loans.
**Private-sector** investment is the **IFC's** role, so loans are not only for corporations.
xa: **IDA** gives long-term **interest-free credits and grants** to the poorest.
World Bank in India: **Maharashtra Resilience Development Programme** (**USD 400 million**, **70%** WB).
IBRD **$1.5 billion** facility for the **National Green Hydrogen Mission**.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about the Asian Development Bank:
1. It was established in 1966.
2. It was created at the initiative of UNCTAD.
3. India is a founding member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: Statement 1 is correct: ADB was established in 1966 (HQ Manila). Statement 2 is wrong: it was created at UN-ESCAP's initiative, not UNCTAD's. Statement 3 is correct: India is a founding member. So 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D include statement 2.
157.tq: ADB is a child of the Asia-Pacific regional commission, UN-ESCAP.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: the **ADB** was established in **1966**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was set up at **UN-ESCAP's** initiative, not UNCTAD's.
Statement 3: India is a **founding member** of the ADB.
xa: ADB HQ: **Manila, Philippines**; **69 members** (**49** Asia-Pacific, **20** non-regional).
**Türkiye** is the newest member (**2025**).
ADB President is **traditionally Japanese**.

157.s: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank is located at
157.x: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank is in Manila, Philippines.
157.tq: Test the headquarters-location fact directly.
xs: The ADB is headquartered in **Manila, Philippines** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Beijing** = AIIB; **Shanghai** = NDB; **Washington D.C.** = IMF + World Bank.
xa: ADB was set up in **1966** at **UN-ESCAP's** initiative.
ADB has **69 members**; newest = **Türkiye (2025)**.
ADB raised India's FY26 growth forecast to **7.2%** (**Dec 2025**).

157.s:
Consider the following statements about the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB):
1. Its Articles of Agreement were signed in 2015.
2. It began operations in January 2017.
3. It holds an AAA rating.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Articles were signed in 2015. Statement 2 is wrong: operations began in January 2016, not 2017. Statement 3 is correct: the AIIB is AAA-rated. So 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D include statement 2.
157.tq: AIIB: signed 2015, operational January 2016, HQ Beijing.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: **AIIB Articles** were signed in **2015**.
Statement 2 wrong: AIIB operations began in **January 2016**, not 2017.
Statement 3: the AIIB is rated **AAA**.
xa: AIIB HQ: **Beijing**; **111 approved members** (**Sep 2026**).
AIIB scale: ~**$69 billion** across **350** projects.
**China** is the largest, **India the second** shareholder.

157.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
o: It is headquartered in Beijing, China, with India as its largest shareholder and China as its second-largest shareholder.
It is headquartered in Beijing, China, with China as its largest shareholder and India as its second-largest shareholder.
It is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with Japan as its largest shareholder and India as its second-largest shareholder.
It is headquartered in Manila, Philippines, with India as its largest shareholder and China as its second-largest shareholder.
157.x: The AIIB is headquartered in Beijing. China is its largest shareholder and India is its second-largest shareholder.
157.tq: Separate headquarters, largest shareholder and second-largest shareholder instead of swapping their relationships.
xs: The **AIIB** is headquartered in **Beijing**, with **China as its largest** and **India as its second-largest shareholder** — option **(2)**.
**Tokyo** hosts neither, and **Manila** is the ADB's HQ.
xa: AIIB has **111 approved members** (**Sep 2026**) and an **AAA** rating.
AIIB in India co-funds **Mumbai MUTP-III** and **NIIF Phase II**.
AIIB funds the **AP Rural Roads Project**.

157.s:
Which of the following projects are co-funded by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
1. Mumbai MUTP-III
2. NIIF Phase II
3. Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor
4. AP Disaster Recovery Project
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
157.x: The AIIB co-funds Mumbai MUTP-III and NIIF Phase II. The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is identified with ADB, while the AP Disaster Recovery Project is identified with the World Bank.
157.tq: Identify the correct lender by eliminating projects assigned to neighbouring institutions.
xs: AIIB co-funds **Mumbai MUTP-III** and **NIIF Phase II** — option **(1)** "**1 and 2 only**".
The **Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor** is an **ADB** project; the **AP Disaster Recovery Project** is the **World Bank's**.
xa: The AIIB's AP project is the **AP Rural Roads Project**.
AIIB: ~**$69 billion** across **350** projects (**Sep 2026**).
AIIB operations began in **January 2016**.

157.s: The agreement establishing the New Development Bank was signed at the:
157.x: The agreement was signed at the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza, Brazil, in 2014; it is associated with the Fortaleza Declaration.
157.tq: Distinguish the summit where the idea originated from the summit where the agreement was signed.
xs: The NDB agreement was signed at the **6th BRICS Summit, Fortaleza, Brazil** (**2014**) — option **(3)** — the **Fortaleza Declaration**.
The NDB **idea** came earlier, at the **4th BRICS Summit, New Delhi (2012)**.
xa: NDB operations began in **2015**.
NDB record (**Sep 2026**): **139 projects, ~$43 billion** approved; only ~**$20 billion** disbursed.
The **18th BRICS Summit (New Delhi)** sought Bretton Woods reform.

157.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the New Development Bank's institutional structure?
o: Its headquarters is in Fortaleza and it has no regional offices
Its headquarters is in Washington, D.C. and it has regional offices only in Europe
Its headquarters is in Shanghai and it has regional offices in Johannesburg, São Paulo, Ahmedabad/GIFT City and Moscow
Its headquarters is in New Delhi and all regional offices are in BRICS capitals
157.x: The NDB is headquartered in Shanghai and has regional offices in Johannesburg, São Paulo, India's Ahmedabad/GIFT City and Moscow.
157.tq: Use the headquarters–regional office combination to distinguish NDB from Bretton Woods institutions.
xs: NDB HQ is **Shanghai**, with regional offices in **Johannesburg, São Paulo, Ahmedabad/GIFT City and Moscow** — option **(3)**.
**Fortaleza** is where the agreement was signed (**2014**), not the HQ.
xa: NDB is open to **all UN members**.
Founding members hold **equal voting rights**; **no veto**.
⚠ **Shanghai** = NDB; **Beijing** = AIIB; **Manila** = ADB.

157.s: The New Development Bank froze Russia-linked operations in March 2022. This was significant because:
o: Russia was a 20% shareholder of the Bank
Russia was the sole shareholder of the Bank
Russia held a permanent veto over all NDB decisions
Russia had no connection with the Bank's founding structure
157.x: Russia was a 20% shareholder of the NDB. The Bank froze Russia-linked operations in March 2022.
157.tq: Connect the operational decision with the precise shareholder relationship, not with an invented veto power.
xs: **Russia** was a **20% shareholder** of the NDB — option **(1)** — which made the **March 2022** freeze significant.
No one holds a veto in the NDB: founding members have **equal voting rights**.
xa: Russia also **gave up its turn** at the NDB presidency.
NDB has a regional office in **Moscow**.
NDB approvals: **139 projects, ~$43 billion** (**Sep 2026**).

157.s:
Consider the following statements about the New Development Bank:
1. The idea was mooted at the 4th BRICS Summit in New Delhi in 2012.
2. It began operations in 2015.
3. Its founding members hold weighted votes, with a veto for the largest shareholder.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: Statement 1 is correct: the NDB idea came at the 4th BRICS Summit, New Delhi, 2012. Statement 2 is correct: operations began in 2015. Statement 3 is wrong: founding members hold equal voting rights and there is no veto. So 1 and 2 only.
157.tq: NDB: idea Delhi 2012, signed Fortaleza 2014, ops 2015, equal votes.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the NDB **idea** came at the **4th BRICS Summit, New Delhi (2012)**.
Statement 2: NDB **operations began in 2015**.
Statement 3 wrong: founding members hold **equal voting rights**, with **no veto**.
xa: Agreement signed at the **6th Summit, Fortaleza (2014)**.
⚠ NDB = equal votes, no veto; IMF = **quota-based** votes with a **US veto**.
First NDB President: **K.V. Kamath**.

157.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the heads of international financial institutions is correct?
o: Raghuram Rajan became World Bank President in June 2023
Gita Gopinath became the first President of the New Development Bank in 2015
K.V. Kamath became IMF Chief Economist during 2003–06
Ajay Banga became World Bank President in June 2023
157.x: Ajay Banga has been the World Bank President from June 2023. K.V. Kamath was the first NDB President, while Raghuram Rajan was IMF Chief Economist from 2003 to 2006.
157.tq: Apply the person-role association and reject swapped institutional positions.
xs: **Ajay Banga** became **World Bank President** in **June 2023** — option **(4)**.
**Raghuram Rajan** was **IMF Chief Economist (2003-06)**; **Gita Gopinath** was IMF Chief Economist, later **First Deputy MD**; **K.V. Kamath** was the **first NDB President**.
xa: **Masatsugu Asakawa** was elected **ADB President** in **Dec 2019**.
Bretton Woods architects: **Harry Dexter White** and **John Maynard Keynes**.
World Bank HQ: **Washington D.C.**

157.s: Masatsugu Asakawa, elected in December 2019, became the President of which institution?
157.x: Masatsugu Asakawa was elected ADB President in December 2019, in line with the tradition of a Japanese ADB President. K.V. Kamath was the first NDB President; the AIIB and IMF are headed by others.
157.tq: Japanese name + president = ADB.
xs: **Masatsugu Asakawa** was elected President of the **Asian Development Bank** in **Dec 2019** — option **(2)** (asked in the **2018** paper).
This follows the tradition of a **Japanese** ADB President; the first **NDB** President was **K.V. Kamath**.
xa: ADB: HQ **Manila**; **69** members.
Japan holds **15.7%** of ADB votes, equal to the USA.
**Ajay Banga** = World Bank President from **June 2023**.

157.s: Which one of the following pairs of Andhra Pradesh project and lender is correctly matched?
o: AP Rural Roads Project - New Development Bank
157.x: The AP Rural Roads Project is funded by AIIB. The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is funded by ADB, and the AP Disaster Recovery Project (post-Hudhud) by the World Bank; the NDB is not the lender for AP Rural Roads.
157.tq: AP lenders: VCIC-ADB, Disaster Recovery-WB, Rural Roads-AIIB.
xs: **AP Rural Roads Project — AIIB** is correctly matched — option **(2)**.
**VCIC** is funded by the **ADB** (not AIIB); the **AP Disaster Recovery Project** by the **World Bank** (not ADB); the NDB is not the AP Rural Roads lender.
xa: VCIC: **33,000 acres**; nodes **Vizag, Chittoor, Kopparthy**.
**AP Road Sector Project** — **World Bank**.
AIIB in India also co-funds **Mumbai MUTP-III** and **NIIF Phase II**.

157.s:
Which of the following have been identified as criticisms or areas of debate concerning Bretton Woods institutions?
1. Structural adjustment conditions
2. Sovereign immunity
3. Northern control of votes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
157.x: Structural adjustment conditions, sovereign immunity and Northern control of votes are all identified as criticisms or areas of debate concerning Bretton Woods institutions.
157.tq: Treat each listed criticism as an independent statement before choosing the combined code.
xs: All three are listed criticisms — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
The debates are **structural adjustment conditions**, **sovereign immunity** and **Northern control of votes** (May **2026**).
xa: The Global North (**15%** of population) holds ~**60%** of IMF/WB votes; the **US alone holds a veto**.
The BRICS **New Delhi Declaration (Sep 2026)** demanded **quota and voting reform**.
⚠ The **NDB** gives founding members **equal voting rights**, with no veto.

157.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. IFC — year of establishment
 b. IDA — year of establishment
 c. IFC — area of focus
 d. IDA — form of assistance

List-II
 i. 1956
 ii. 1960
 iii. Private-sector focus
 iv. Concessional loans and grants
157.x: The IFC was set up in 1956 and the IDA in 1960. The IFC focuses on the private sector, and the IDA gives soft loans and grants. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
157.tq: Discriminate the IFC from the IDA.
n: The IFC was established in 1956. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 46-47]
The IDA was established in 1960. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 46-47]
The IFC focuses on the private sector. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 46-47]
The IDA provides concessional loans and grants. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 46-47]
The IFC is associated with private-sector development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 46-47]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — option **(4)**.
The **IFC** was established in **1956** and focuses on the **private sector**.
The **IDA** was established in **1960** and gives **concessional loans** and **grants** to the **poorest countries**.
xa: **IBRD** (**1944**) lends to middle-income governments.
**MIGA** (**1988**): political-risk insurance; **ICSID** (**1966**): investment disputes — **India is not a member**.
⚠ **IDA** = interest-free credits to poorest; **IFC** = private sector.

157.s: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) located?
157.x: The IMF and the World Bank are both headquartered in Washington, D.C. The WTO is in Geneva.
157.tq: Match each institution to its city.
n: The headquarters of the IMF is in Washington, D.C. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
xs: The **IMF** is headquartered in **Washington, D.C.** — option **(3)**.
**Bretton Woods** (New Hampshire) is where the **July 1944** conference founded the IMF and IBRD, not the HQ.
xa: The **World Bank** is also in **Washington, D.C.**
⚠ **Manila** = ADB; **Beijing** = AIIB; **Shanghai** = NDB.
IMF formally existed from **27 December 1945**; operations began **1 March 1947**.

157.s:
Consider the following statements about the IMF:

I. It promotes international monetary stability.
II. It provides practical and technical assistance.
III. It provides development or project financing.
IV. It provides financial assistance to members facing Balance of Payments difficulties.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
157.x: I, II and IV are correct: the IMF promotes monetary stability, gives technical help, and lends for BoP problems. III is false because project finance is the World Bank's job.
157.tq: Discriminate the IMF from the World Bank.
n: The IMF provides financial assistance to members facing balance of payments difficulties. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The IMF provides practical and technical assistance. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The IMF promotes international monetary stability. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The World Bank provides development and project financing. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The main objective of the IMF is international monetary stability. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The IMF is associated with monetary stability. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The World Bank is associated with development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The IMF addresses balance of payments problems. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The IMF provides lending. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
The World Bank provides development assistance. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 41-43]
xs: Statements **I, II and IV** are correct — option **(3)**.
I and IV: the **IMF** is associated with **monetary stability** and **lending for balance of payments problems** — correct.
III is wrong: **development and project financing** is the **World Bank's** role.
xa: IMF voting is by **quota**; quota formula weights **GDP 50%**, openness **30%**, variability **15%**, reserves **5%**.
**SDR** basket has **five currencies** since Oct **2016**, including the **renminbi**.
**Article IV**: annual bilateral surveillance of each member.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the Uruguay Round:
1. It was the eighth round of GATT negotiations.
2. It was held from 1986 to 1993/94.
3. It involved 123 countries.
4. It created the World Trade Organization.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, ran from 1986 to 1993/94, involved 123 countries and led to the creation of the WTO.
158.tq: Check all four identifying features of a major negotiation round, including its numerical details.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2, 3 and 4**".
The **Uruguay Round** was the **8th** GATT round, ran **1986-1993/94**, involved **123** countries and created the **WTO**.
xa: It produced **TRIPS**, **GATS** and the **AoA**.
⚠ **Marrakesh** = WTO agreement; **Uruguay** = round that created it; **Geneva** = HQ.
**Dunkel Draft**: **20 Oct 1991**, by **Arthur Dunkel**.

158.s:
Which of the following agreements or subjects emerged from the Uruguay Round?
1. TRIPS
2. GATS
3. Agreement on Agriculture
4. Non-tariff barrier codes
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
158.x: The Uruguay Round produced TRIPS, GATS and the Agreement on Agriculture. Non-tariff barrier codes are associated with the Tokyo Round.
158.tq: Separate Uruguay Round outputs from the outcome of the Tokyo Round.
xs: **TRIPS**, **GATS** and the **AoA** came from the Uruguay Round — option **(1)** "**1, 2 and 3 only**".
**Non-tariff barrier codes** came from the **Tokyo Round** (**1973-79**).
xa: **TRIPS** = minimum standards for all forms of IPR; **GATS** = trade in services; **AoA** = market access, domestic support, export subsidies.
The **Kennedy Round** (**1964-67**) gave the first **Anti-Dumping Code**.
Since then only two new agreements: **Trade Facilitation** and **Fisheries Subsidies**.

158.s: The Dunkel Draft associated with the Uruguay Round was dated and prepared under the leadership of:
158.x: The Dunkel Draft was associated with Arthur Dunkel and dated 20 October 1991.
158.tq: Combine a precise date with the responsible person to avoid date-person substitution.
xs: The **Dunkel Draft** is dated **20 October 1991** and was prepared under **Arthur Dunkel** — option **(2)**.
**1 January 1995** is the WTO's establishment date, not the Draft's.
xa: ⚠ The Dunkel Draft belongs to the **Uruguay Round**, not Doha.
The Uruguay Round ran **1986-1993/94** with **123** countries.
It created the **WTO** with **TRIPS, GATS, AoA**.

158.s:
Arrange the following GATT/WTO negotiation rounds in chronological order:
A. Doha Development Agenda
B. Kennedy Round
C. Uruguay Round
D. Tokyo Round
158.x: The correct order is Kennedy Round (1964–67), Tokyo Round (1973–79), Uruguay Round (1986–93/94), and Doha Development Agenda (launched in 2001).
158.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two middle rounds by their periods.
xs: Doha is the only one launched after the WTO's creation in **1995**.
xa: GATT held **8 rounds** in all; Uruguay was the **8th**.
Kennedy = **first Anti-Dumping Code**; Tokyo = **non-tariff barrier codes**.
Uruguay created the **WTO**.

158.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GATT held nine rounds of trade negotiations.
2. GATT Article XXIV allows free trade agreements as exceptions to the MFN principle.
3. Such an FTA qualifies only if it covers substantially all trade.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is wrong: GATT held 8 rounds, the Uruguay Round being the eighth. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Article XXIV permits FTAs as MFN exceptions if they cover substantially all trade. So 2 and 3 only (B); A and C include the wrong statement 1, D includes all.
158.tq: Eight GATT rounds, Uruguay the last; FTAs ride on Article XXIV.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**2 and 3 only**".
Statement 1 wrong: GATT held **8 rounds**, Uruguay being the 8th.
Statements 2 and 3: **GATT Article XXIV** allows **FTAs** as **MFN exceptions** if they cover "**substantially all trade**".
xa: India has **15 FTAs** and **6 PTAs**; latest **EFTA TEPA** and **UK CETA**.
The **India-EU FTA** covers **97.5%** of EU tariff lines.
GATT survives as an **integral WTO agreement**.

158.s: The World Trade Organization was established on 1 January 1995 under which agreement?
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
158.x: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement after the Uruguay Round.
158.tq: Use the founding agreement and date as the identifying pair.
xs: The WTO was established on **1 January 1995** under the **Marrakesh Agreement** — option **(2)**.
**GATT** was the predecessor system; **Doha** is a later round; **Singapore** hosted **MC1** (**1996**).
xa: ⚠ **Marrakesh** = WTO agreement; **Uruguay** = round; **Geneva** = HQ.
WTO membership: **166** (Mar **2026**).
Decision-making is **one-country-one-vote**, by consensus.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the World Trade Organization:
1. It had 166 members as of March 2026.
2. Comoros and Timor-Leste joined it in 2024.
3. It is headquartered at Vienna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is correct: 166 members in March 2026 (older sources say 164). Statement 2 is correct: Comoros and Timor-Leste are the latest members (2024). Statement 3 is wrong: the WTO is headquartered at Geneva. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
158.tq: WTO = Geneva; 164 is the outdated count, 166 the current one.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: **166** members (Mar **2026**); older notes say **164**.
Statement 2: **Comoros and Timor-Leste** joined in **2024**.
Statement 3 wrong: the WTO is headquartered at **Geneva**, not Vienna.
xa: The WTO was set up on **1 January 1995** (**Marrakesh Agreement**).
**MC12** was also held in **Geneva** (**June 2022**).
Decision-making: **one-country-one-vote**, consensus-based.

158.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (WTO body)
A. General Council
B. Dispute Settlement Body
C. Trade Policy Review Body
D. Ministerial Conference

List-II (Function)
1. Periodic review of members’ trade policies
2. Highest decision-making body
3. Operates between Ministerial Conferences
4. Deals with panels and Appellate Body rulings

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
158.x: The General Council runs the WTO between Ministerial Conferences; the DSB handles dispute rulings; the TPRB reviews trade policies; and the Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body.
158.tq: Start from the sure pair of each body with its distinctive function.
xs: **General Council** — runs WTO between MCs; **DSB** — panels and **Appellate Body** rulings; **TPRB** — periodic trade-policy review; **Ministerial Conference** — highest body — option **(1)** "**A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2**".
The **General Council** also sits as the **DSB** and **TPRB**.
xa: The Ministerial Conference must meet **at least once every two years**.
The **Council for Trade in Goods** oversees **GATT** (committees on agriculture, market access, **TBT**, **SPS**).
The US **blocked Appellate Body appointments**, paralysing the two-tier system.

158.s: Which WTO Ministerial Conferences are specifically associated with a breakdown of negotiations?
158.x: The Seattle Ministerial Conference of 1999 and the Cancún Ministerial Conference of 2003 broke down.
158.tq: Separate failed negotiating conferences from conferences identified mainly by their locations or dates.
xs: **Seattle (1999)** and **Cancún (2003)** Ministerials **broke down** — option **(1)** "**Seattle and Cancún**".
**Singapore** was **MC1 (1996)**; **Geneva** hosted **MC12 (2022)**; **Abu Dhabi** hosted **MC13 (2024)**.
xa: **MC12** adopted a limited **TRIPS waiver** for vaccine patents.
At **MC14** (Yaoundé, **2026**), the **e-commerce** and **TRIPS non-violation** moratoria lapsed.
The **Doha Development Agenda** (**2001**) has stalled.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO Ministerial Conference:
1. It must meet at least once every two years.
2. MC14 was held at Yaounde, Cameroon, in March 2026.
3. MC13 was held at Geneva in 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is correct: the MC, the highest decision-making body, must meet at least once every two years. Statement 2 is correct: MC14 was at Yaounde, Cameroon (March 2026). Statement 3 is wrong: MC13 was at Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024); Geneva 2022 was MC12. So 1 and 2 only.
158.tq: MC12 Geneva 2022, MC13 Abu Dhabi 2024, MC14 Yaounde 2026.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the **Ministerial Conference** must meet **at least once every two years**.
Statement 2: **MC14** was held at **Yaoundé, Cameroon (March 2026)**.
Statement 3 wrong: **MC13** was at **Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024)**; **Geneva (June 2022)** was **MC12**.
xa: **MC1** = **Singapore 1996**.
Seattle (**1999**) and Cancún (**2003**) broke down.
MC14 left **PSH** and **fisheries Phase 2** unresolved.

158.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Anti-dumping — Duties on goods sold below normal value
TRIPS — Minimum standards for all forms of intellectual property rights
TRIMS — Investment measures that distort trade
GATS — Subsidies that are prohibited, actionable and non-actionable
158.x: GATS deals with trade in services. The classification of subsidies as prohibited, actionable and non-actionable belongs to the SCM Agreement.
158.tq: Detect the agreement-subject swap among neighbouring WTO agreements.
xs: **GATS — prohibited, actionable and non-actionable subsidies** is NOT correctly matched — option **(4)**.
**GATS** covers **trade in services** (banking, insurance); that subsidy classification belongs to **SCM**.
The others are correct: **Anti-dumping** — goods below normal value; **TRIPS** — minimum IPR standards; **TRIMS** — trade-distorting investment measures.
xa: **SCM** non-actionable subsidies: **R&D, regional, environment**.
**TRIMS** example: **local content** requirements.
**AoA** covers market access, domestic support and export subsidies.

158.s: In India, which body handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations under WTO rules?
158.x: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations in India.
158.tq: Ask which domestic authority performs the specified trade-remedy function.
xs: The **Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR)** handles **anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard** investigations — option **(3)**.
The **TPRB** is a WTO body reviewing members' trade policies, not an Indian investigator.
xa: **Anti-dumping** = duties on goods sold below **normal value**.
Countervailing duties target **actionable** subsidies under **SCM**.
India raised the **UK steel safeguard** at the **Council for Trade in Goods** (**May 2026**).

158.s: Which two agreements are identified as the only new WTO agreements concluded in the first 30 years of the organisation?
o: Trade Facilitation Agreement and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
158.x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only new WTO agreements in that period.
158.tq: Use the word “only” carefully to identify the complete pair rather than older Uruguay Round agreements.
xs: The only new WTO agreements in **30** years are the **Trade Facilitation Agreement** and the **Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies** — option **(1)**.
**AoA, TRIPS, GATS, TRIMS, SPS, TBT** all came with the **Uruguay Round** package.
xa: **Fisheries Phase 2** (overcapacity, overfishing) remained unresolved at **MC14** → deferred to the **General Council**.
The WTO began on **1 January 1995**.
Plurilaterals like **Investment Facilitation for Development** are disputed; **India opposes** bringing them in.

158.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India amended the Patents Act in 2005 to comply with TRIPS.
2. India enacted the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 to meet TRIPS obligations.
3. India is a member of the Lisbon Agreement and its Geneva Act (2015).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Patents Act was amended in 2005 to comply with TRIPS. Statement 2 is correct: the GI Act, 1999 was enacted to meet TRIPS. Statement 3 is wrong: India is not in the Lisbon Agreement or the Geneva Act (2015). So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
158.tq: TRIPS drove India's 2005 patent amendment and 1999 GI Act, but India stays out of the Lisbon system.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: India amended the **Patents Act** in **2005** to comply with **TRIPS**.
Statement 2: the **GI of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999** was enacted to meet TRIPS.
Statement 3 wrong: India is **not** in the **Lisbon Agreement/Geneva Act (2015)**.
xa: **TRIPS (1995)** sets **minimum global IPR standards**.
India's flexibilities: **Section 3(d)** (anti-evergreening) + **compulsory licensing**.
First compulsory licence: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).

158.s: The Doha Declaration on TRIPS and public health affirmed that TRIPS:
o: Prevents members from regulating medicines in public interest
Must not stop members from protecting public health
Eliminates compulsory licensing by developing countries
158.x: The Doha Declaration of 2001 affirmed that TRIPS must not prevent members from taking measures to protect public health.
158.tq: Test the public-health flexibility principle against restrictive distractors.
xs: The **Doha Declaration (2001)** said TRIPS **must not stop members from protecting public health** — option **(3)**.
So it supports, not eliminates, flexibilities like **compulsory licensing**.
xa: First compulsory licence in India: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).
**India-South Africa** proposed a **COVID TRIPS waiver** (**2020**); **MC12** adopted a limited waiver (**2022**).
**Section 3(d)** is India's anti-evergreening clause.

158.s: Which provision and mechanism were used by India to address public-health concerns under the TRIPS framework?
158.x: India used Section 3(d) of the Patents Act against evergreening and compulsory licensing as TRIPS flexibilities.
158.tq: Identify the domestic legal tools associated with the international flexibility.
xs: India relies on **Section 3(d) and compulsory licensing** — option **(1)**.
**Section 3(d)** of the Patents Act blocks **evergreening**; **compulsory licensing** lets others produce patented goods.
xa: First compulsory licence: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).
The **Doha Declaration (2001)** backs public-health measures under TRIPS.
India amended the **Patents Act** in **2005** to comply with TRIPS.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the COVID-19 TRIPS waiver:
1. It was proposed jointly by India and Brazil in 2020.
2. MC12 (2022) adopted a limited waiver for vaccine patents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the proposal (2020) came from India and South Africa, not Brazil. Statement 2 is correct: MC12 at Geneva in 2022 adopted a limited waiver for vaccine patents. So 2 only (B); A and C accept the wrong statement 1, D rejects the correct statement 2.
158.tq: COVID waiver = India + South Africa; outcome only a limited vaccine-patent waiver at MC12.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(2)** "**2 only**".
Statement 1 wrong: the **2020** waiver proposal came from **India and South Africa**, not Brazil.
Statement 2 correct: **MC12 (2022)** adopted a **limited waiver for vaccine patents**.
xa: MC12 was held at **Geneva (June 2022)**.
The **Doha Declaration (2001)** on TRIPS and public health.
First compulsory licence: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).

158.s: The present crisis in the WTO dispute-settlement system primarily resulted from:
o: The African Group rejecting all panel reports
The General Council refusing to meet between Ministerial Conferences
India withdrawing from the Marrakesh Agreement
The United States blocking appointments to the Appellate Body
158.x: The United States blocked Appellate Body appointments, paralysing the WTO’s two-tier dispute-settlement system.
158.tq: Identify the actor responsible for the institutional blockage rather than the affected body.
xs: The crisis arose because the **United States blocked appointments to the Appellate Body** — option **(4)**.
This paralysed the WTO's **two-tier** dispute system.
xa: India's appeals now sit "**into the void**".
The crisis, with consensus paralysis, pushes countries towards **FTAs**.
The **DSB** handles panels and **Appellate Body** rulings.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about WTO disputes involving India:
1. The USA challenged the domestic-content requirements of the JNNSM solar programme, and India lost in 2016.
2. The EU, Japan and Chinese Taipei challenged India's ICT tariffs, and a panel ruled against India in 2023.
3. The dispute over India's export subsidy schemes such as MEIS and SEZ was brought by the European Union.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is correct: the USA won the solar panels (JNNSM) case in 2016. Statement 2 is correct: the EU, Japan and Chinese Taipei won a panel on ICT tariffs in 2023; India appealed. Statement 3 is wrong: the export subsidy (MEIS, SEZ) case was brought by the USA (panel 2019). So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
158.tq: The USA is behind two of India's three listed disputes - solar panels and export subsidies; ICT tariffs is the EU-Japan-Taipei case.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the **USA** challenged domestic content in **JNNSM** solar; India **lost (2016)**.
Statement 2: **EU, Japan and Chinese Taipei** won a panel on India's **ICT tariffs** (**2023**); India appealed.
Statement 3 wrong: the **MEIS/SEZ** export-subsidy case was brought by the **USA** (panel **2019**), not the EU.
xa: India's appeals sit "**into the void**" as the **Appellate Body** lacks members.
The US **blocked Appellate Body appointments**.
**SCM** classes subsidies as prohibited, actionable or non-actionable.

158.s:
With reference to the WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions, consider the following statements:
1. It lapsed on 31 March 2026.
2. Its extension failed at the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference.
3. A separate plurilateral agreement was signed by 66 members to ban such duties.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: All three statements are correct: the moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026 after MC14 failed to extend it, while 66 members signed a separate plurilateral e-commerce agreement banning such duties.
158.tq: Check the date, institutional event and membership figure together in a current-affairs statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
The **e-commerce moratorium** lapsed on **31 March 2026** after **MC14** failed to extend it.
**66 members** signed a separate **plurilateral** E-commerce Agreement banning such duties.
xa: The moratorium had run since **1998**.
The **TRIPS non-violation** moratorium (since **1995**) also lapsed at MC14.
**Investment Facilitation for Development** has **120+** backers.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about Special and Differential Treatment (SDT) at the WTO:
1. The US wants to deny SDT to China, India, Brazil and Indonesia.
2. India supports withdrawing SDT from developing countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is correct: the US wants to deny SDT to China, India, Brazil and Indonesia. Statement 2 is wrong: India defends SDT. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong statement 2, D rejects the correct statement 1.
158.tq: India is on the defending side of SDT, the US on the denying side.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)** "**1 only**".
Statement 1: the **US** wants to deny **SDT** to **China, India, Brazil, Indonesia**.
Statement 2 wrong: **India defends SDT**.
xa: India's core food-security demand: a **permanent solution for PSH**.
India **opposes** bringing **plurilaterals** into the WTO rulebook.
**One-country-one-vote** gives developing countries bargaining space.

158.s: Which one of the following is India's core demand in the WTO food-security negotiations?
o: A permanent solution for public stockholding
A permanent ban on agricultural exports
A common currency for food imports
158.x: India's core food-security demand is a permanent solution for public stockholding, or PSH.
158.tq: Match the policy issue with India’s specific negotiating demand rather than a general agricultural measure.
xs: India's core demand is a **permanent solution for public stockholding (PSH)** — option **(2)**.
No PSH deal was reached at **MC14** (Yaoundé, **2026**).
xa: **AoA** governs market access, **domestic support** and **export subsidies**.
India also defends **SDT** for developing countries.
**Fisheries Phase 2** was deferred to the **General Council**.

158.s:
Consider the following statements regarding plurilateral initiatives in the WTO:
1. Investment Facilitation for Development has more than 120 backers.
2. The E-commerce Agreement is a plurilateral initiative.
3. India opposes bringing these initiatives into the WTO rulebook.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Investment Facilitation for Development has more than 120 backers, the E-commerce Agreement is plurilateral, and India opposes bringing these initiatives into the WTO rulebook.
158.tq: Combine the initiative type, support level and India’s negotiating position in one coded question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
**Investment Facilitation for Development** has **120+** backers; the **E-commerce agreement** is a plurilateral; **India opposes** bringing them into the WTO rulebook.
xa: **66 members** signed the plurilateral E-commerce Agreement banning duties on electronic transmissions.
The multilateral e-commerce moratorium lapsed on **31 March 2026**.
The only new multilateral agreements: **Trade Facilitation** + **Fisheries Subsidies**.

158.s:
The WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference, held at Yaoundé in March 2026, was associated with which of the following developments?
1. The e-commerce moratorium lapsed.
