2. The TRIPS non-violation moratorium lapsed.
3. No permanent solution for public stockholding was reached.
4. No fisheries Phase 2 deal was reached.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
158.x: All four developments were associated with MC14 at Yaoundé in March 2026: both moratoria lapsed, and no deal was reached on PSH or fisheries subsidies Phase 2.
158.tq: Combine several current outcomes and test whether any one of them has been incorrectly omitted.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2, 3 and 4**".
At **MC14 Yaoundé (Mar 2026)**, the **e-commerce** and **TRIPS non-violation** moratoria lapsed, with **no PSH** and **no fisheries Phase 2** deal.
xa: The e-commerce moratorium dated from **1998**; the TRIPS one from **1995**.
Fisheries Phase 2 (overcapacity, overfishing) was **deferred to the General Council**.
**MC13** was at **Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024)**.

158.s:
Assertion (A): Developing countries can obtain bargaining space in WTO negotiations.
Reason (R): The WTO follows a one-country-one-vote principle.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
158.x: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the one-country-one-vote principle explains why developing countries receive bargaining space in WTO negotiations.
158.tq: Test whether the institutional rule directly explains the negotiating consequence.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
The WTO's **one-country-one-vote** principle gives **developing countries bargaining space**.
xa: WTO decisions are **consensus-based**.
⚠ Consensus can also cause **paralysis**, pushing countries to **FTAs**.
WTO membership: **166** (Mar **2026**).

159.s: Which one of the following organisations was established through the Bangkok Declaration of 1967?
159.x: ASEAN was established in 1967 through the Bangkok Declaration.
159.tq: Identify the organisation from its founding declaration and year.
xs: **ASEAN** was set up by the **1967 Bangkok Declaration** — option **(3)**, by Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
**SAARC** came from the **Dhaka** Charter (**1985**); **BIMSTEC** from a **1997** Bangkok Declaration; **SCO** from **Shanghai** (**2001**).
xa: ASEAN Secretariat: **Jakarta**; members now **11** with **Timor-Leste** (**2025**).
⚠ Two "Bangkok Declarations": **1967** = ASEAN; **1997** = BIMSTEC (as BIST-EC).
**Myanmar** is the only ASEAN state bordering India.

159.s: Which one of the following correctly describes BIMSTEC?
o: Founded through the 1997 Bangkok Declaration and headquartered at Dhaka
Founded through the 1985 Dhaka Charter and headquartered at Kathmandu
Founded through the 1992 Maastricht Treaty and headquartered at Brussels
Founded through the 2001 Shanghai Declaration and headquartered at Beijing
159.x: BIMSTEC originated through the 1997 Bangkok Declaration and its Secretariat is in Dhaka.
159.tq: Match the organisation with its founding instrument, year and headquarters.
xs: **BIMSTEC** began with the **1997 Bangkok Declaration** and its Secretariat is at **Dhaka** — option **(1)**.
**1985 Dhaka Charter / Kathmandu** = SAARC; **Maastricht / Brussels** = EU; **Shanghai / Beijing** = SCO.
xa: It began as **BIST-EC**: Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand.
BIMSTEC has **7** members; **Nepal + Bhutan** joined in **2004**.
⚠ BIMSTEC Secretariat = **Dhaka**; ASEAN = **Jakarta**.

159.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The African Union was set up in 2002, replacing the OAU (1963).
2. The European Union is based on the Maastricht Treaty of 1992/93.
3. The Council of Europe, founded in 1949, is headquartered at Brussels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: Statement 1 is correct: the AU (2002) replaced the OAU (1963). Statement 2 is correct: the EU rests on the Maastricht Treaty of 1992/93. Statement 3 is wrong: the Council of Europe (1949) sits at Strasbourg; Brussels is the EU's seat. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
159.tq: Council of Europe = Strasbourg, not Brussels - a classic EU look-alike trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the **African Union (2002)** replaced the **OAU (1963)**.
Statement 2: the **EU** rests on the **Maastricht Treaty 1992/93**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Council of Europe (1949)** sits at **Strasbourg**; **Brussels** is the EU's seat.
xa: Council of Europe: **47** members (asked **2019**); **Russia expelled March 2022**.
EU: **27** members; last to join **Croatia (2013)**.
**Article 50** TEU (Lisbon Treaty) = exit clause, used for **Brexit**.

159.s: How many members does SAARC have?
159.x: SAARC comprises eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
159.tq: Recall the exact membership count and verify it against the member list.
xs: SAARC has **8** members — option **(3)**.
It includes **every land neighbour of India except China** (and Myanmar).
xa: SAARC Charter: **Dhaka, 8 Dec 1985**; Secretariat: **Kathmandu**.
SAARC observers: **China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran**.
⚠ "Number of members" is a favourite: SAARC **8**, BIMSTEC **7**, ASEAN **11**, Council of Europe **47**.

159.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. China is not a member of BIMSTEC.
2. Myanmar is not a member of SAARC.
3. Myanmar is the only ASEAN state bordering India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: All three statements are correct. China is outside BIMSTEC, Myanmar is outside SAARC, and Myanmar is the only ASEAN country sharing a land border with India.
159.tq: Test closely related membership and geographical-relationship statements together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
Statements 1 and 2: **China is not in BIMSTEC** and **Myanmar is not in SAARC**.
Statement 3: **Myanmar** is the **only ASEAN state bordering India**.
xa: Myanmar joined **ASEAN + BIMSTEC** in **1997**.
China is a SAARC **observer**, with Japan, USA, EU and Iran.
BIMSTEC's **7**: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about membership of regional groupings:
1. The European Union has 27 members.
2. The Gulf Cooperation Council has 6 members.
3. ASEAN still has 10 members, as Timor-Leste has not been admitted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: Statement 1 is correct: the EU has 27 members. Statement 2 is correct: the GCC has 6 (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman). Statement 3 is wrong: Timor-Leste joined in 2025, so ASEAN has 11. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
159.tq: ASEAN is now 10 + Timor-Leste = 11.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the **EU** has **27** members; statement 2: the **GCC** has **6**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Timor-Leste** joined in **2025**, so ASEAN has **11**.
xa: GCC (**1981**, Riyadh): Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman.
⚠ Newest: ASEAN = **Timor-Leste**; EU = **Croatia**; NATO = **Finland + Sweden**.
The **East Asia Summit** has **19** members, incl. all **11** ASEAN states.

159.s: Which one of the following statements about the Council of Europe is correct?
o: It had 47 members in 2019, and Russia joined in March 2022.
It had 27 members in 2019, and Russia joined in March 2022.
It had 47 members in 2019, and Russia was expelled in March 2022.
It had 27 members in 2019, and Russia was expelled in March 2022.
159.x: The Council of Europe had 47 members in 2019; Russia was expelled in March 2022.
159.tq: Combine the membership count with the dated membership change.
xs: The **Council of Europe** had **47** members in **2019** and **Russia was expelled in March 2022** — option **(3)**.
**27** is the **EU's** membership, not the Council of Europe's.
xa: Council of Europe: founded **1949**, HQ **Strasbourg**.
⚠ **Strasbourg** = Council of Europe; **Brussels** = EU.
**NATO** also dates from **1949**.

159.s: The headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation is located at
159.x: The SAARC Secretariat is located in Kathmandu, while its Charter was signed in Dhaka.
159.tq: Use the location trap involving the Charter venue and Secretariat headquarters.
xs: The SAARC Secretariat is at **Kathmandu** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Trap: the Charter was signed at **Dhaka** (**1985**), which also hosts the **BIMSTEC** Secretariat.
**Thimphu** hosts the **SAARC Development Fund**; **Colombo** hosted the **5th BIMSTEC Summit**.
xa: The **18th SAARC summit** (Kathmandu, **2014**) is the last one held.
The **19th** (Islamabad, **2016**) was cancelled after **Uri**.
**SAFTA** replaced **SAPTA**; in force **1 Jan 2006**.

159.s:
Which of the following initiatives was proposed by India in the SAARC framework?
1. South Asia Satellite
2. COVID emergency fund
3. Bangkok Vision 2030
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
159.x: India proposed the South Asia Satellite in 2017 and the COVID emergency fund in 2020. Bangkok Vision 2030 belongs to BIMSTEC.
159.tq: Identify the correct organisation behind each named initiative.
xs: India proposed the **South Asia Satellite** (**2017**) and the **COVID emergency fund** (**2020**) in SAARC — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
**Bangkok Vision 2030** belongs to **BIMSTEC** (**6th Summit**, **2025**).
xa: In BIMSTEC, **India leads security** (counter-terrorism, disaster management, energy).
India gave a **21-point Action Plan** at the 6th BIMSTEC Summit.
The last SAARC summit was the **18th** (Kathmandu, **2014**).

159.s: The 19th SAARC Summit, scheduled at Islamabad in 2016, was cancelled after the
159.x: The 19th SAARC Summit at Islamabad was cancelled after the Uri attack. The 18th Summit at Kathmandu in 2014 remains the last summit.
159.tq: Link the cancelled event to its immediate stated cause.
xs: The **19th SAARC Summit** (**Islamabad, 2016**) was cancelled after the **Uri** attack — option **(2)**.
So the **18th summit** (**Kathmandu, 2014**) remains the **last** SAARC summit.
xa: SAARC and BIMSTEC are both constrained by India's tensions with **Islamabad** and **Dhaka**.
No neighbourhood leader attended the **Sep 2026** BRICS Summit.
India's SAARC proposals: **South Asia Satellite** (**2017**), **COVID emergency fund** (**2020**).

159.s: Which one of the following countries has not ratified the BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement?
159.x: The BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement was signed by Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal at Thimphu in 2015, but Bhutan has not ratified it.
159.tq: Distinguish signing from ratification and identify the exceptional member.
xs: **Bhutan** has not ratified the **BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement** — option **(2)**.
The MVA was signed at **Thimphu** in **2015** by **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal**.
xa: ⚠ **Thimphu** = BBIN MVA + **SAARC Development Fund**.
Bhutan and Nepal joined **BIMSTEC** in **2004**.
**SAFTA** in force **1 Jan 2006**.

159.s: Which one of the following is NOT an observer of SAARC?
159.x: SAARC's observers include China, Japan, the USA, the EU and Iran. Russia is not a SAARC observer.
159.tq: SAARC observers incl. China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran - not Russia.
xs: **Russia** is NOT a SAARC observer — option **(4)**.
SAARC observers: **China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran**.
xa: ⚠ China is a SAARC **observer** but **not** a member of **BIMSTEC**.
Russia was **expelled** from the **Council of Europe** (**March 2022**).
Russia is in the **East Asia Summit**'s **19** members.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about BIMSTEC:
1. It began as BIST-EC with Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
2. Nepal and Bhutan joined it in 2004.
3. It now has eight members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: Statement 1 is correct: BIST-EC (1997) comprised Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Statement 2 is correct: Nepal and Bhutan joined in 2004. Statement 3 is wrong: BIMSTEC has seven members (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand). So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
159.tq: BIMSTEC = 7: five South Asian plus Myanmar and Thailand.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: it began as **BIST-EC** — **Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand**.
Statement 2: **Nepal + Bhutan** joined in **2004**.
Statement 3 wrong: BIMSTEC has **7** members, not eight (Myanmar also joined in **1997**).
xa: Full name: **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**.
BIMSTEC sectors were cut from **14** to **7**, each with a lead country.
Secretariat: **Dhaka**.

159.s: The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the
159.x: The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the Fifth Summit held at Colombo in 2022.
159.tq: Match the summit number, venue and year with the institutional development.
xs: The **BIMSTEC Charter** was adopted at the **5th Summit, Colombo (2022)** — option **(4)**.
The **6th Summit, Bangkok (2025)** gave **Bangkok Vision 2030** and the **Maritime Transport Cooperation Agreement**.
xa: ⚠ BIMSTEC Charter = **Colombo**; Bangkok Vision 2030 = **Bangkok**; BBIN MVA = **Thimphu**.
**Bangladesh** chairs BIMSTEC for **2024-26**.
India's **21-point Action Plan** came at the 6th Summit.

159.s:
Consider the following statements about BIMSTEC:
1. Its sectors were reduced from 14 to 7.
2. Each sector has a lead country.
3. India leads the security sector.
4. Myanmar earlier led the energy sector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: All four statements are correct. BIMSTEC reduced its sectors from 14 to 7, assigned a lead country to each, assigned security to India and had Myanmar earlier leading energy.
159.tq: Verify the numerical restructuring and the sector-leadership assignments separately.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2, 3 and 4**".
BIMSTEC cut its sectors from **14** to **7**, each with a **lead country**; **India leads security**; **Myanmar** earlier led **energy**.
xa: India's security lead covers **counter-terrorism**, **disaster management** and **energy**.
First BIMSTEC army exercise: **MILEX 2018, Pune**.
BIMSTEC weaknesses: **few summits**, **broad focus**, **Rohingya + border issues**, **BCIM rivalry**.

159.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to BIMSTEC initiatives of India?
o: MILEX — first BIMSTEC army exercise, Pune, 2018
Energy Centre Host Country Agreement — November 2022
159.x: MILEX was the first BIMSTEC army exercise and was held at Pune in 2018. The first Youth Summit was at Gandhinagar in February 2025, the Cancer Care programme was at Tata Memorial in July 2025, and the Energy Centre agreement was signed in November 2024.
159.tq: Use the sure date-place pair and reject the swapped locations or years.
xs: **MILEX — first BIMSTEC army exercise, Pune, 2018** is correct — option **(1)**.
The **Youth Summit** was at **Gandhinagar** (Feb **2025**); **Cancer Care** at **Tata Memorial** (July **2025**); the **Energy Centre** Host Country Agreement was **Nov 2024**.
xa: ⚠ BIMSTEC has a **military component** (MILEX); SAARC and ASEAN lack it.
**India leads security** in BIMSTEC.
India's **21-point Action Plan** came at the **6th Summit** (Bangkok, **2025**).

159.s:
With reference to the 6th BIMSTEC Summit (Bangkok, April 2025), consider the following statements:
1. India presented a 21-point Action Plan.
2. Bangladesh took over as chair for 2024-26.
3. The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at this summit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: Statement 1 is correct: India put forward a 21-point Action Plan. Statement 2 is correct: Bangladesh is chair for 2024-26. Statement 3 is wrong: the Charter was adopted at the 5th Summit, Colombo (2022). So 1 and 2 only.
159.tq: Charter = Colombo 2022; Bangkok 2025 = Vision 2030 + 21-point plan.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: India presented a **21-point Action Plan**; statement 2: **Bangladesh** is chair for **2024-26**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **BIMSTEC Charter** was adopted at the **5th Summit, Colombo (2022)**.
xa: 6th Summit theme: "**Prosperous, Resilient, and Open**"; outcome **Bangkok Vision 2030**.
The **Maritime Transport Cooperation Agreement** was signed there.
1st **BIMSTEC Youth Summit**: **Gandhinagar** (**Feb 2025**).

159.s: Which one of the following correctly states the sequence of India’s relations with ASEAN?
o: Sectoral dialogue partner — 1992; full dialogue partner — 1996; summit-level partner — 2002; Comprehensive Strategic Partnership — 2022
Sectoral dialogue partner — 1996; full dialogue partner — 1992; summit-level partner — 2002; Comprehensive Strategic Partnership — 2022
Sectoral dialogue partner — 1992; full dialogue partner — 2002; summit-level partner — 1996; Comprehensive Strategic Partnership — 2022
Sectoral dialogue partner — 1992; full dialogue partner — 1996; summit-level partner — 2022; Comprehensive Strategic Partnership — 2002
159.x: India became a sectoral dialogue partner in 1992, a full dialogue partner in 1996, a summit-level partner in 2002 and a Comprehensive Strategic Partner in 2022.
159.tq: Arrange milestone labels with their exact years and watch for swapped stages.
xs: India-ASEAN: sectoral partner **1992** → full dialogue partner **1996** → summit-level **2002** → **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership 2022** — option **(1)**.
The other options swap two of these years.
xa: **AIFTA (goods)** came into force in **2010**.
India opted out of **RCEP** in **2019**.
ASEAN Regional Forum founded **1994**; East Asia Summit **2005**.

159.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The ASEAN-India FTA in goods (AIFTA) came into force in 2010.
2. The ASEAN Regional Forum was set up in 1994.
3. At the 32nd ARF (Kuala Lumpur, July 2025), India sought early completion of the RCEP review.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: Statement 1 is correct: AIFTA (goods) came into force in 2010. Statement 2 is correct: the ARF dates from 1994. Statement 3 is wrong: India sought early completion of the AITIGA review; India opted out of RCEP in 2019. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
159.tq: India wants AITIGA reviewed; RCEP it left in 2019.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: **AIFTA (goods)** came into force in **2010**; statement 2: the **ARF** dates from **1994**.
Statement 3 wrong: at the **32nd ARF** (Kuala Lumpur, **July 2025**), India sought the **AITIGA review**, not RCEP.
xa: India **opted out** of **RCEP** in **2019**.
The **20th EAS** (Kuala Lumpur **2025**) adopted the **Kuala Lumpur Declaration**.
India-ASEAN **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**: **2022**.

159.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the East Asia Summit is correct?
o: It was founded in 1994 at Jakarta and has 17 members.
It was founded in 2005 at Bangkok and has 18 members.
It was founded in 2005 at Kuala Lumpur and has 19 members.
It was founded in 2010 at Kuala Lumpur and has 19 members.
159.x: The East Asia Summit was founded in 2005 at Kuala Lumpur and has 19 members: 11 ASEAN members plus India, China, Japan, the United States, Russia, Australia, New Zealand and South Korea.
159.tq: Combine the founding venue, year and membership count.
xs: The **East Asia Summit** was founded in **2005** at **Kuala Lumpur** and has **19 members** — option **(3)**.
Members: **11 ASEAN** + **India, China, Japan, US, Russia, Australia, NZ, South Korea**.
xa: The **20th EAS** (Kuala Lumpur **2025**) adopted the **Kuala Lumpur Declaration**.
**1994** = ASEAN Regional Forum.
ASEAN Secretariat: **Jakarta**.

159.s: The 20th East Asia Summit held at Kuala Lumpur in 2025 adopted the
159.x: The 20th East Asia Summit adopted the Kuala Lumpur Declaration in 2025.
159.tq: Distinguish the declaration of the East Asia Summit from BIMSTEC’s Bangkok Vision 2030.
xs: The **20th East Asia Summit** (Kuala Lumpur, **2025**) adopted the **Kuala Lumpur Declaration** — option **(4)**.
**Bangkok Vision 2030** is BIMSTEC's; **Colombo** gave the BIMSTEC Charter; **Dhaka** the SAARC Charter.
xa: EAS founded **2005**, Kuala Lumpur; **19** members.
The **32nd ARF** was also held in **Kuala Lumpur** (**July 2025**).
**Timor-Leste** became ASEAN's **11th** member (**2025**).

159.s: India opted out of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership in
159.x: India opted out of RCEP in 2019.
159.tq: Identify the withdrawal year from closely spaced policy dates.
xs: India **opted out of RCEP** in **2019** — option **(3)**.
**RCEP** dates from **2019**; India stayed with its **ASEAN** trade track via **AIFTA**.
xa: **AIFTA (goods)** has been in force since **2010**.
India seeks early completion of the **AITIGA review** (**32nd ARF**, July **2025**).
India-ASEAN: **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** (**2022**).

159.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA):
1. It was formed in 1997.
2. It has 23 members.
3. Its last summit before 2027 was held at Durban in 2017.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: Statement 1 is correct: IORA was formed in 1997. Statement 2 is correct: it has 23 member states. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2027 summit is the first since Jakarta 2017 (20th anniversary), not Durban. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
159.tq: IORA: 1997, 23 members, last summit Jakarta 2017.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: **IORA** was formed in **1997**; statement 2: it has **23** members.
Statement 3 wrong: the **2027** summit is the first since **Jakarta 2017** (20th anniversary), not Durban.
xa: **Nelson Mandela** was among IORA's leaders.
IORA Secretariat: **Ebene, Mauritius**.
**India is chair** of IORA.

159.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union is the exit clause and was invoked for Brexit.
2. The United Kingdom left the European Union on 31 January 2020.
3. Article 50 was inserted by the Maastricht Treaty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
159.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 50 TEU is the withdrawal clause used for Brexit. Statement 2 is correct: the UK left on 31 January 2020. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 50 came through the Lisbon Treaty, not Maastricht. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
159.tq: Article 50 = Lisbon Treaty exit clause.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: **Article 50** of the Treaty on European Union is the **exit clause**, invoked for **Brexit**.
Statement 2: the UK left the EU on **31 Jan 2020**.
Statement 3 wrong: Article 50 came through the **Lisbon Treaty**, not Maastricht.
xa: EU rests on the **Maastricht Treaty 1992/93**.
Last to join the EU: **Croatia (2013)**.
EU strategy: **Digital Single Market** (**2015**).

159.s: Which country was the latest to join the European Union?
159.x: Croatia was the last country to join the European Union, in 2013.
159.tq: Recall the latest enlargement rather than an earlier enlargement round.
xs: **Croatia** (**2013**) was the last country to join the EU — option **(4)**.
The UK left the EU on **31 Jan 2020** (**Brexit**).
xa: EU: **27** members; HQ **Brussels**.
⚠ Newest: ASEAN = **Timor-Leste**; NATO = **Finland + Sweden**.
**Article 50** TEU = exit clause.

159.s: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is associated with which of the following organisations?
159.x: RATS is the counter-terrorism structure of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
159.tq: Identify the organisation from the specialised institutional function.
xs: **RATS** is the counter-terror structure of the **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation** — option **(4)**.
RATS is located at **Tashkent**, while the SCO HQ is **Beijing**.
xa: SCO was founded in **2001** at **Shanghai**.
India and Pakistan became full SCO members in **2017 (Astana)**.
⚠ IORA's Secretariat is at **Ebene, Mauritius**; NATO dates from **1949**.

159.s: NACIN Palasamudram in Rayalaseema is associated with which of the following functions?
o: It hosts the permanent secretariat of IORA.
It functions as the ASEAN Secretariat.
It is the headquarters of the SCO's RATS.
It serves as a WCO regional training centre for tax officials.
159.x: NACIN Palasamudram is a World Customs Organization regional training centre that trains tax officials from SAARC, ASEAN and African nations.
159.tq: Identify the institution from its location and specialised training function.
xs: **NACIN Palasamudram** is a **WCO regional training centre** for **tax officials** — option **(4)**.
It trains officials from **SAARC, ASEAN and African** nations; it is not the IORA, ASEAN or RATS seat.
xa: It is in **Rayalaseema**, Andhra Pradesh — the topic's **AP angle**.
IORA Secretariat: **Ebene**; ASEAN: **Jakarta**; RATS: **Tashkent**.
SAARC Secretariat: **Kathmandu**.

160.s: Which of the following countries is a member of the G7?
160.x: Japan is one of the seven G7 members, along with the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy and Canada. China, India and Russia are not G7 members.
160.tq: Separate formal membership from regular outreach participation.
xs: **Japan** is a member of the **G7** — option **(3)**.
**Russia**, **China** and **India** are common distractors: none is a G7 member; India is only an **outreach invitee**.
xa: Russia joined in **1997-98** to form the **G8**; suspended in **2014** after Crimea.
Other non-member distractors: **Netherlands**, **New Zealand**.
The **EU** attends G7 meetings.

160.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the G7:
1. The European Union attends G7 meetings.
2. Russia became associated with the G8 in 1997–98.
3. Russia was suspended after the Crimea crisis in 2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: All three statements are correct. The EU attends G7 proceedings, Russia joined in 1997–98 to form the G8, and its participation was suspended in 2014 after the Crimea crisis.
160.tq: Check the sequence of accession, suspension and present composition.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2 and 3**".
The **EU attends** the G7; **Russia** joined in **1997-98** making it the **G8**; Russia was **suspended in 2014** after **Crimea**.
xa: India is a regular **outreach invitee**; entry into the G7 is uncertain (**Jul 2025**).
The G7 launched **PGII** in **2022** (Germany) as a counter to **BRI**.
PM Modi met President Trump at the **G7 summit in France (2026)**.

160.s: The Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII) was launched by the G7 in:
160.x: The G7 launched PGII in Germany in 2022 as an infrastructure plan and a counter to the Belt and Road Initiative.
160.tq: Link the programme with its launch year, venue and strategic purpose.
xs: The G7 launched **PGII** in **2022 in Germany** — option **(3)**.
It is a G7 infrastructure plan meant as a **counter to BRI**.
xa: The **2026** G7 summit was held in **France**.
The G7 became the **G8** with Russia in **1997-98**, until **2014**.
The G20 was foreshadowed at the G7 **Cologne summit (June 1999)**.

160.s:
Consider the following statements about the origin of the G20:
1. It was foreshadowed at the G7 Cologne summit in June 1999.
2. It was set up on 26 September 1999 as a forum of heads of state and government.
3. Its first meeting was held at Berlin in December 1999.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: Statement 1 is correct: the G20 was foreshadowed at the G7 Cologne summit (June 1999). Statement 2 is wrong: it began as a forum of finance ministers and central bank governors; leaders' summits began only in 2008 at Washington. Statement 3 is correct: the first meeting was at Berlin, December 1999. So 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D include statement 2.
160.tq: G20 started as a finance-ministers forum after the Asian crisis (1999); leaders came in 2008.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: the G20 was foreshadowed at the G7 **Cologne summit (June 1999)**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was set up on **26 Sep 1999** as a forum of **finance ministers and central bank governors**, not leaders.
Statement 3: its first meeting was in **Berlin, Dec 1999**, after the **Asian Financial Crisis**.
xa: The first **leaders' summit** was in **Washington D.C., 2008** (global financial crisis).
⚠ G20 first meeting = **Berlin 1999**; first leaders' summit = **Washington 2008**.
The G20 has **no permanent secretariat**; presidency rotates annually.

160.s: The first G20 Leaders' Summit was held in 2008 at:
160.x: The first G20 Leaders' Summit was held in Washington, D.C., in 2008, in the context of the global financial crisis.
160.tq: Match the first leaders' summit with its venue and crisis context.
xs: The first G20 **leaders' summit** was in **Washington, D.C.** in **2008** — option **(4)**, during the global financial crisis.
**Berlin** hosted the first (ministerial) meeting in **1999**; **Cologne** foreshadowed it; **New Delhi** hosted in **2023**.
xa: G20 = **19 countries + EU + African Union** (AU since **2023**).
G20 share: **~85% GDP**, **>75% trade**, **two-thirds** of population.
2025 G20 meetings: **Johannesburg, South Africa**.

160.s: The G20 troika consists of:
o: The three largest economies of the G20
The current, previous and next presidencies
The G7, BRICS and European Union
The three permanent members of the G20 Secretariat
160.x: The G20 troika comprises the previous, current and next presidencies (B). In 2022 it was Italy (previous, 2021), Indonesia (current, 2022) and India (next, 2023). The G20 has no permanent secretariat, and the troika is not based on economic size or on G7/BRICS/EU.
160.tq: Resolve a terminology trap by identifying the institutional meaning of troika.
xs: The **G20 Troika** = **past, current and next presidencies** — option **(2)**.
In **2022** it was **Indonesia**, **Italy** and **India**.
The G20 has **no permanent secretariat or HQ**, so option 4 is wrong.
xa: India's presidency summit: **New Delhi, 9-10 Sep 2023**.
The presidency **rotates annually**.
**2025** G20: **Johannesburg, South Africa**.

160.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with India's 2023 G20 presidency?
o: Creation of a permanent G20 headquarters
Admission of the African Union as a permanent member
Launch of the Global Biofuels Alliance
160.x: India's presidency produced the New Delhi Declaration, admitted the African Union as a permanent member and launched the Global Biofuels Alliance. The G20 has no permanent headquarters.
160.tq: Find the institutional statement that conflicts with the G20's non-permanent structure.
xs: A **permanent G20 headquarters** was NOT created — option **(1)**; the G20 has **no permanent secretariat or HQ**.
The **New Delhi Declaration (2023)** admitted the **African Union** and launched the **Global Biofuels Alliance**.
xa: The G20 runs on an annual **rotating presidency** and a **Troika**.
⚠ Two **New Delhi Declarations**: G20 (**2023**) admitted AU; BRICS (**2026**) sought IMF/WB + UNSC reform.
Theme: "**Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam**".

160.s: The term “BRIC” was coined in 2001 by:
o: Amartya Sen of the United Nations
Joseph Stiglitz of the World Bank
160.x: The term BRIC was coined in 2001 by Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs.
160.tq: Match the coined term with its author and institution.
xs: The term "**BRIC**" was coined in **2001** by **Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs** — option **(4)**.
BRIC was **formalised in 2006**.
xa: First BRIC summit: **Yekaterinburg, Russia, 2009**.
**South Africa** joined in **2011**, making it BRICS.
BRICS now has **10** members (+ **Saudi Arabia** ambiguous).

160.s:
Consider the following statements about BRICS:
1. BRIC was formalised in 2006.
2. The first BRIC summit was held at Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009.
3. South Africa joined in 2013, turning BRIC into BRICS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: Statement 1 is correct: BRIC was formalised in 2006. Statement 2 is correct: the first summit was at Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009. Statement 3 is wrong: South Africa joined in 2011. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
160.tq: BRIC timeline: term 2001, formalised 2006, first summit 2009, South Africa 2011.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: BRIC was **formalised in 2006**; statement 2: first summit at **Yekaterinburg, Russia, 2009**.
Statement 3 wrong: **South Africa** joined in **2011**, not 2013.
xa: Term "BRIC": **2001**, **Jim O'Neill**.
UKPSC **2024**: "first summit **2009** in Russia" was correct; "BRICS = **46%** of global trade" was wrong.
**Indonesia** joined BRICS in **2025**.

160.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the BRICS chairmanship:
1. The chair rotates in the order B-R-I-C-S.
2. Russia chaired BRICS in 2024.
3. Brazil chaired BRICS in 2025.
4. India is scheduled to chair BRICS in 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: All four statements are correct. The chairmanship follows the B-R-I-C-S order: Russia in 2024, Brazil in 2025 and India in 2026.
160.tq: Follow the acronym-based rotation and verify each year in sequence.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** "**1, 2, 3 and 4**".
The chair rotates **B-R-I-C-S**: **Russia 2024** (Kazan), **Brazil 2025** (Rio), **India 2026** (New Delhi).
xa: Next: **China 2027**.
India's earlier BRICS hostings: **2012, 2016, 2021 (virtual)**.
India's **2026** theme: "**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability**".

160.s: India's 2026 BRICS theme is:
o: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – One Earth, One Family, One Future
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
160.x: India's 2026 BRICS theme is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
160.tq: Distinguish the BRICS theme from India's separate G20 theme.
xs: India's **2026 BRICS** theme is "**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability**" — option **(4)**.
"**Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam - One Earth, One Family, One Future**" was India's **G20 (2023)** theme.
xa: The theme's initials spell out **BRICS**.
Summit: **New Delhi, 12 Sep 2026**, Bharat Mandapam.
India also hosted BRICS in **2012**, **2016** and **2021** (virtual).

160.s: The New Development Bank (NDB) was established at Fortaleza in 2014 and has its headquarters at:
160.x: The NDB was established at Fortaleza in 2014 and its headquarters is located in Shanghai.
160.tq: Match an institution with its founding venue and headquarters rather than confusing the two.
xs: The **NDB**, set up at **Fortaleza** in **2014**, is headquartered at **Shanghai** — option **(3)**.
**Fortaleza** is where it was agreed, not its HQ.
xa: The BRICS **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** (**2014**) is a **$100 billion** liquidity pool.
**Johannesburg** hosted the **2025** G20 meetings.
BRICS in **2011** had **20%** of GDP but only **11%** of IMF votes.

160.s: The Contingent Reserve Arrangement associated with BRICS has a liquidity pool of:
160.x: The BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement, created in 2014, has a liquidity pool of 100 billion dollars.
160.tq: Test the exact financial magnitude and distinguish it from the NDB.
xs: The BRICS **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** (**2014**) is a **100 billion dollars** liquidity pool — option **(3)**.
It was set up the same year as the **NDB** (Fortaleza, **2014**).
xa: The **NDB** was also set up in **2014** (Fortaleza); HQ **Shanghai**.
⚠ The CRA is a **BRICS** body, not a Quad initiative.
India **avoids de-dollarisation** within BRICS.

160.s:
Consider the following statements about IBSA:
1. It was founded in 2003 through the Brasilia Declaration.
2. The IBSA Trust Fund is managed by UNDP.
3. IBSAMAR is its naval exercise.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: Statement 1 is correct: IBSA was founded in 2003 by the Brasilia Declaration. Statement 2 is wrong: the IBSA Trust Fund (operational 2004, funds LDC projects) is managed by UNOSSC, not UNDP. Statement 3 is correct: IBSAMAR is the IBSA naval exercise. So 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D include statement 2.
160.tq: IBSA Fund = UN Office for South-South Cooperation (UNOSSC).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: **IBSA** was founded in **2003** via the **Brasilia Declaration**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **IBSA Trust Fund** is managed by **UNOSSC**, not UNDP.
Statement 3: **IBSAMAR** is IBSA's naval exercise.
xa: The IBSA Trust Fund became operational in **2004** and funds **LDC** projects.
IBSA = **India, Brazil, South Africa**.
India's IBSA proposals (**Nov 2025**): **Fund for Climate-Resilient Agriculture**, **Digital Innovation Alliance**, **NSA-level dialogue**.

160.s: BASIC was formed in 2009 before which international climate conference?
160.x: The BASIC grouping was formed in 2009 before the Copenhagen COP15.
160.tq: Anchor the grouping to the conference immediately associated with its formation.
xs: **BASIC** was formed in **2009** before **COP15 at Copenhagen** — option **(2)**.
Its members are **Brazil, South Africa, India, China** — the initials spell BASIC.
xa: BASIC stands for **CBDR-RC** and **climate finance from developed countries**.
⚠ **China** is in BASIC but **not in IBSA**.

160.s: Which of the following positions is associated with the BASIC grouping?
o: CBDR-RC and climate finance from developed countries
Opposition to the principle of differentiated responsibilities
Exclusive reliance on private climate finance
160.x: BASIC stands for the principle of CBDR-RC and supports climate finance from developed countries.
160.tq: Match a grouping with its characteristic negotiating position.
xs: **BASIC** stands for **CBDR-RC and climate finance from developed countries** — option **(2)**.
So it supports differentiated responsibilities and public climate finance — not withdrawal or private-only finance.
xa: BASIC formed in **2009**, before **Copenhagen COP15**.
Members: **Brazil, South Africa, India, China**.
India is also in **IBSA** (**2003**) with Brazil and South Africa.

160.s: The first Quad leaders' summit was held:
o: In person in Washington in September 2021
160.x: The first Quad leaders' summit was held virtually in March 2021. The first in-person leaders' summit was held in Washington in September 2021.
160.tq: Distinguish the first virtual summit from the first in-person summit.
xs: The first **Quad leaders' summit** was **virtual, in March 2021** — option **(2)**.
The first **in-person** summit followed in **Washington, Sep 2021**.
xa: The Quad was **revived in 2017**.
Quad initiatives: **Quad Vaccine Partnership**, **Critical and Emerging Technologies** group, **IPMDA (2022)**.
⚠ **New Delhi, Sep 2023** = G20 Summit, not Quad.

160.s: Which of the following is NOT a Quad initiative?
o: Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness
160.x: The Quad initiatives include the Quad Vaccine Partnership, the Critical and Emerging Technologies group and IPMDA. The Contingent Reserve Arrangement is associated with BRICS.
160.tq: Identify the institution belonging to a different grouping.
xs: The **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** is NOT a Quad initiative — option **(2)**; it is a **BRICS** pool (**2014**, **$100 billion**).
Quad initiatives: **Quad Vaccine Partnership**, **IPMDA**, **Critical and Emerging Technologies** group.
xa: **IPMDA** = Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness (**2022**).
Quad origin: **Tsunami Core Group** after the **2004** tsunami.
BRICS also runs the **NDB** (HQ **Shanghai**).

160.s: The Colombo Security Conclave originated as which arrangement in 2011?
160.x: The Colombo Security Conclave began in 2011 as a maritime trilateral among India, Sri Lanka and Maldives.
160.tq: Identify the original composition and character of the forum.
xs: The **Colombo Security Conclave** began as the **India-Sri Lanka-Maldives maritime trilateral** in **2011** — option **(2)**.
It was renamed the CSC in **2020**.
xa: Members now: **India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh**; observer **Seychelles**.
Secretariat: **Colombo**.
Five pillars include **maritime safety and security** and **HADR**.

160.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Colombo Security Conclave:
1. India is a member.
2. Mauritius is a member.
3. Seychelles is an observer.
4. Bangladesh is an observer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: India and Mauritius are members, and Seychelles is an observer. Bangladesh is a member, not an observer; therefore statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct.
160.tq: Use membership-status discrimination to catch the swapped member and observer.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)** "**1, 2 and 3 only**".
**India** and **Mauritius** are members; **Seychelles** is the **observer**.
Statement 4 wrong: **Bangladesh** is a **member**, not an observer.
xa: CSC members: **India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh**.
Origin: India-Sri Lanka-Maldives trilateral (**2011**); renamed **2020**.
Secretariat: **Colombo**.

160.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five pillars of the Colombo Security Conclave?
160.x: The five pillars include maritime safety and security, counter-terrorism and radicalisation, trafficking and organised crime, cyber security and critical infrastructure, and HADR. Food security and agricultural subsidies is not a stated pillar.
160.tq: Identify the unrelated policy area among a list of closely associated security pillars.
xs: **Food security and agricultural subsidies** is NOT a CSC pillar — option **(4)**.
The **five pillars**: maritime safety and security; counter-terrorism and radicalisation; trafficking and organised crime; cyber security and critical infrastructure; **HADR**.
xa: CSC began as a **maritime trilateral** (**2011**).
It was renamed in **2020**; secretariat **Colombo**.
Observer: **Seychelles**.

160.s: Which one of the following groupings consists of India, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and the United States?
160.x: I2U2 comprises India, Israel, the UAE and the United States.
160.tq: Identify a grouping from its complete membership rather than its acronym alone.
xs: **I2U2** = **India, Israel, UAE, USA** — option **(4)**.
**BASIC** = Brazil, South Africa, India, China; **IBSA** = India, Brazil, South Africa; **MIKTA** = Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye, Australia.
xa: India is **not** in MIKTA.
India **is** a member of I2U2, IBSA and BASIC.
**G4** = India, Brazil, Germany, Japan (UNSC bid).

160.s: Which of the following countries is a member of BASIC but not of IBSA?
160.x: BASIC comprises Brazil, South Africa, India and China, whereas IBSA comprises India, Brazil and South Africa. China is therefore the additional BASIC member.
160.tq: Compare overlapping memberships and identify the additional country.
xs: **China** is in **BASIC** but not **IBSA** — option **(2)**.
**BASIC** = Brazil, South Africa, India, China; **IBSA** = India, Brazil, South Africa — so India, Brazil and South Africa are in both.
xa: BASIC formed in **2009** before **COP15**.
IBSA formed in **2003** (**Brasilia Declaration**).
China chairs BRICS in **2027**.

160.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. G4 — India, Brazil, Germany and Japan
2. MIKTA — Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye and Australia
3. Quad — India, China, Japan and Australia
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
160.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Quad comprises India, the United States, Japan and Australia, not China; hence pair 3 is false.
160.tq: Use membership composition to catch a swapped-country trap.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Pair 1: **G4** = **India, Brazil, Germany, Japan**; pair 2: **MIKTA** = **Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye, Australia**.
Pair 3 wrong: the **Quad** = India, **USA**, Japan, Australia — not China.
xa: ⚠ **Indonesia** is in **BRICS (2025)** + **MIKTA**, but not in the Quad or IBSA.
India is **not** a MIKTA member.
The G4 seeks permanent UNSC seats.

160.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Indonesia?
o: Indonesia is not associated with any of the listed groupings.
Indonesia is a member of the Quad and IBSA.
Indonesia is a member of G7 and BASIC only.
Indonesia is a member of BRICS and MIKTA, but not of the Quad or IBSA.
160.x: Indonesia joined BRICS in 2025 and is also a member of MIKTA. It is not a member of the Quad or IBSA.
160.tq: Discriminate a country appearing in several overlapping groupings but not in the commonly confused ones.
xs: **Indonesia** is in **BRICS and MIKTA**, but **not** in the **Quad** or **IBSA** — option **(4)**.
It joined **BRICS** in **2025**.
xa: Quad = **India, USA, Japan, Australia**; IBSA = **India, Brazil, South Africa**.
MIKTA = **Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye, Australia**.
Indonesia was in the G20 **Troika** of **2022** (with Italy and India).

160.s: The G20 accounts for approximately:
o: More than 40% of global GDP, 46% of trade and 55% of population
40% of global GDP, 50% of trade and one-third of population
85% of global GDP, more than 75% of trade and two-thirds of population
20% of global GDP, 11% of trade and half of population
160.x: The G20 represents approximately 85% of global GDP, more than 75% of global trade and two-thirds of the world's population.
160.tq: Keep the three indicators together and reject figures belonging to other groupings or periods.
xs: The **G20** accounts for **~85%** of GDP, **>75%** of trade and **two-thirds** of population — option **(3)**.
Option 1 mixes **BRICS** figures (**>40%** GDP, **55%** population) with the false "**46%** of trade" claim.
xa: G20 = **19 countries + EU + AU**.
BRICS in **2011**: **20%** of GDP but only **11%** of IMF votes.
G20 first leaders' summit: **Washington D.C., 2008**.

160.s: Which of the following correctly describes the share of the expanded BRICS grouping?
o: More than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and about 50% of the world's population
Exactly 46% of global trade and one-third of the world's population
About 85% of global GDP and more than 75% of global trade
About 20% of global GDP and 11% of the world's population
160.x: The expanded BRICS grouping accounts for more than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and approximately 50% of the world's population. The exact estimates vary by source.
160.tq: Distinguish BRICS indicators from the G20 figures and avoid an unsupported exact percentage.
xs: The expanded **BRICS** has **>40%** of global GDP (**PPP**) and ~**50%** of population — option **(1)**.
Another source gives **nearly 40%** of GDP and **55%** of population; **85%** GDP / **>75%** trade is the **G20**.
xa: ⚠ "BRICS = **46%** of global trade" was the **wrong** statement in UKPSC **2024**.
BRICS in **2011**: **20%** of GDP but **11%** of IMF votes.
BRICS has **10** members (+ **Saudi** ambiguous).

160.s: Which of the following best reflects the debate concerning the identity of BRICS?
o: It is viewed by some as anti-West, while others describe it as non-West.
It is defined by all members as a de-dollarisation coalition.
It is universally accepted as a formal military alliance against NATO.
It is regarded exclusively as a trade bloc with a coherent common identity.
160.x: BRICS is criticised for lacking a coherent identity: Russia, China and Iran are associated with an “anti-West” orientation, whereas India, Brazil and South Africa are described as “non-West.”
160.tq: Distinguish the competing descriptions rather than treating BRICS as a single-purpose alliance.
xs: BRICS is seen by some as **anti-West** and by others as **non-West** — option **(1)**.
**Russia, China, Iran** lean "anti-West"; **India, Brazil, South Africa** are "non-West" — so BRICS **lacks a coherent identity**.
xa: India **avoids de-dollarisation**.
India's multi-alignment makes it a **bridge** between the Global South and the industrialised North.
BRICS chair rotates in **B-R-I-C-S** order.

160.s: Which statement best describes India’s position on de-dollarisation in the context of BRICS?
o: India supports replacing all national currencies with a BRICS currency immediately.
India has withdrawn from BRICS because of de-dollarisation.
India has made de-dollarisation its exclusive foreign-policy objective.
160.x: India avoids de-dollarisation, even while participating in BRICS and other plurilateral forums.
160.tq: Use the stated national-position distinction to reject extreme policy claims.
xs: **India avoids de-dollarisation** — option **(3)**.
This is part of the **anti-West vs non-West** split: India stays in the **non-West** camp with Brazil and South Africa.
xa: India is a BRICS **founder** and hosted the **18th Summit** (**2026**).
**Russia, China, Iran** are seen as the "**anti-West**" wing.
India's multi-alignment = **bridge** between the Global South and the North.

161.s: North Korea withdrew from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) in:
161.x: North Korea left the NPT in 2003.
161.tq: Recall the specific withdrawal year rather than a nearby nuclear-crisis date.
xs: **North Korea** left the **NPT** in **2003** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The NPT was signed in **1968**, came into force in **1970** and was extended indefinitely in **1995**.
xa: The NPT recognises only the **P5 — US, Russia, UK, France, China** as nuclear-weapon states.
**NPT Review Conferences** are held **every 5 years**; the consensus rule lets a single state block outcomes.
**North Korea** is also outside the **MTCR**.
**Iran's Parliament** weighed an **NPT exit** in **Mar 2026** after US-Israel strikes on its nuclear sites (**June 2025**).

161.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the NPT:
1. It was signed in 1968 and entered into force in 1970.
2. It was extended indefinitely in 1995.
3. It recognises only the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom, France and China as nuclear-weapon states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
161.x: All three statements are correct. The NPT was signed in 1968, entered into force in 1970, was extended indefinitely in 1995, and recognises only the five NPT nuclear-weapon states.
161.tq: Check the complete chronology and the exhaustive P5 list.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: The NPT was **signed 1968** and entered into force in **1970**.
Statement 2: It was **extended indefinitely in 1995**.
Statement 3: It recognises only the **P5 — US, Russia, UK, France, China** as nuclear-weapon states.
xa: ⚠ UPSC 2015 trap: only **China** and **France** among the options were NPT nuclear-weapon states.
India calls the NPT **discriminatory ("nuclear apartheid")** and won't sign until nuclear powers accept a **time-bound disarmament plan**.
**North Korea** left the NPT in **2003**; Review Conferences are held **every 5 years**.
Criticism: the NPT lets recognised powers **modernise without disarmament deadlines**.

161.s: India's principal objection to the NPT is that it:
o: does not contain any provision on nuclear energy
is discriminatory and perpetuates nuclear apartheid
recognises India as a nuclear-weapon state without conditions
161.x: India rejects the NPT as discriminatory, describing its structure as nuclear apartheid. India also seeks a time-bound disarmament plan from the nuclear powers before signing.
161.tq: Identify the stated policy objection rather than a consequence of the treaty.
xs: India rejects the NPT as **discriminatory**, calling it **"nuclear apartheid"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
India won't sign until the nuclear powers accept a **time-bound disarmament plan**.
The NPT recognises only the **P5** as nuclear-weapon states, so it does not recognise India as one.
xa: India is also **not a signatory to the CTBT** and **did not sign the TPNW**.
⚠ India is a party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
India is called a **"de facto responsible nuclear state"** — **NFU doctrine**, export controls, entry into **3 of 4 regimes**.
The **2008 NSG India-specific waiver** opened civil nuclear trade despite India staying outside the NPT.

161.s: India has not signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) primarily because it:
o: lacks a time-bound disarmament commitment and permits subcritical tests
does not ban any form of nuclear explosion
161.x: India objects to the CTBT because it lacks a time-bound disarmament plan and still permits subcritical tests. The CTBT bans all nuclear explosions and was adopted in 1996.
161.tq: Separate India's objection to the treaty from the treaty's stated prohibition.
xs: India has not signed the **CTBT** because it has **no time-bound disarmament** and still **allows subcritical tests** — option **(1)**.
The CTBT (**1996**) **bans all nuclear explosions**, so option (3) is wrong; it is a nuclear, not chemical, treaty.
It says nothing about recognising nuclear-weapon states — that is the **NPT**, which recognises the **P5**.
xa: The CTBT is **not in force**.
The **PTBT (1963)** bans tests **except underground**; **India is a party** to it.
India **did not sign the TPNW** (in force **2021**) — it "adds nothing to customary law".
⚠ India is not a party to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.

161.s: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is located at:
161.x: The IAEA is headquartered in Vienna and was established in 1957.
161.tq: Separate the locations of the IAEA, FATF and OPCW.
xs: The **IAEA** is headquartered at **Vienna** — option **(2)**.
**The Hague** hosts the **OPCW**; **Paris (OECD)** hosts the **FATF** secretariat.
The IAEA was established in **1957** and verifies that civil nuclear material is **not diverted to weapons**.
xa: **India joined the IAEA in 1957** as a **founding member**.
⚠ **Vienna** is also the seat of the **Wassenaar Arrangement** (**1996**, **42** members).
IAEA DG **Rafael Grossi** voiced worry over hits on Iran's nuclear sites (**Apr 2026**); he chaired the **NSG in 2016**.

161.s:
Consider the following statements about India and the IAEA:
1. India joined the IAEA in 1957 as a founding member.
2. IAEA safeguards verify that civil nuclear material is not diverted to weapons.
3. India's safeguards agreement covers its military nuclear facilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
161.x: India joined the IAEA in 1957 as a founding member, and safeguards verify the non-diversion of civil nuclear material. India's India-specific safeguards agreement excludes military facilities.
161.tq: Identify the scope limitation in a safeguards agreement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **India joined the IAEA in 1957** as a **founding member** — correct.
Statement 2: IAEA safeguards **verify civil nuclear material is not diverted to weapons** — correct.
Statement 3: The **India-Specific Safeguards Agreement (2009)** covers **civilian facilities** and **excludes military** ones — wrong.
xa: ⚠ NSG waiver = **2008**; safeguards agreement = **2009**; **Additional Protocol** = **2014**.
The IAEA is headquartered at **Vienna**, established **1957**.
India-Canada uranium (**10,000 tonnes, 2027-2035**) is for PHWRs **under IAEA safeguards**.

161.s: India's Additional Protocol to the IAEA safeguards arrangement came into force in:
161.x: India's Additional Protocol came into force in 2014.
161.tq: Distinguish the year of the safeguards agreement from the year of the Additional Protocol.
xs: India's **Additional Protocol** came into force in **2014** — option **(3)**.
**2009** is the year of the **India-Specific Safeguards Agreement**, not the Additional Protocol.
xa: ⚠ Sequence: **NSG waiver 2008** → **safeguards agreement 2009** → **Additional Protocol 2014**.
The safeguards agreement covers **civilian facilities, excludes military**.
The **2008 waiver** stemmed from the **India-US Civil Nuclear Deal** → uranium/reactor imports.

161.s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) was formed in 1975 in response to:
161.x: The NSG was formed in 1975, popularly known as the London Club, in response to India's 1974 Pokhran-I test.
161.tq: Match the organisation's origin with the triggering event.
xs: The **NSG** was formed in **1975** in response to India's **1974 Pokhran-I** test — option **(3)**.
It was popularly called the **"London Club"**.
The **CTBT** came later (**1996**) and North Korea's NPT exit was in **2003**, so neither could have triggered a 1975 body.
xa: The NSG is **voluntary, consensus-based**, with **no permanent secretariat** and **48 members**.
It controls **nuclear materials and technology**.
India got the **India-specific NSG waiver in 2008** (India-US Civil Nuclear Deal).
IAEA DG **Rafael Grossi** chaired the NSG in **2016**.

161.s:
Consider the following statements about the NSG:
1. It is voluntary and consensus-based.
2. It has a permanent secretariat.
3. It has 48 members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
161.x: The NSG is voluntary and consensus-based and has 48 members. Statement 2 is false because it has no permanent secretariat.
161.tq: Use the institutional-structure trap involving a permanent secretariat.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: The NSG is **voluntary and consensus-based** — correct.
Statement 2: It has **no permanent secretariat** — wrong.
Statement 3: It has **48 members** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **MTCR = 35** members (**500 kg / 300 km**); **Wassenaar = 42** (Vienna); **NSG = 48**.
The NSG ("**London Club**") was formed in **1975** after India's **1974 Pokhran-I**.
The NSG controls **nuclear materials and technology**.

161.s: The India-specific NSG waiver of 2008, associated with the India-US Civil Nuclear Deal, permits India to:
o: trade in civilian nuclear material and import uranium and reactors
join the NPT as a nuclear-weapon state
161.x: The 2008 waiver permits civil nuclear trade and the import of uranium and reactors by India. It does not make India an NPT member.
161.tq: Distinguish the practical effect of a waiver from formal membership in another treaty.
xs: The **2008 NSG waiver** lets India carry out **civil nuclear trade** and **import uranium and reactors** — option **(1)**.
It came through the **India-US Civil Nuclear Deal**; it does not make India an NPT member or give it a veto.
The NSG is **consensus-based**, so no member holds a special veto through the waiver.
xa: ⚠ NSG waiver = **2008**; safeguards agreement = **2009**; Additional Protocol = **2014**.
Uranium deals followed: **Canada (10,000 tonnes, 2027-2035)** and **Australia (July 2026)**.
The **India-Specific Safeguards Agreement** covers civilian facilities and **excludes military** ones.

161.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India's position on the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW)?
o: India rejected the TPNW only because it does not prohibit conventional weapons.
India did not sign the TPNW and holds that it adds nothing to customary international law.
India supports the TPNW because it is backed by all nuclear-armed States.
India signed and ratified the TPNW but has not implemented it.
161.x: India did not sign the TPNW and has stated that the treaty adds nothing to customary law.
161.tq: Discriminate between non-signature and ratification, and between India’s stated legal objection and unrelated grounds.
xs: **India did not sign the TPNW**, holding that it **adds nothing to customary law** — option **(2)**.
The TPNW has **no nuclear-armed or NATO support**, so option (3) is wrong.
It is the **first binding ban on nuclear weapons**, not a conventional-weapons treaty.
xa: The TPNW entered into force in **2021**.
⚠ India: party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
India supports **FMCT** negotiation at the **Conference on Disarmament**.

161.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW):
1. It entered into force in 2021.
2. It has the support of all nuclear-armed States and NATO.
3. It is a binding treaty banning nuclear weapons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
161.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the TPNW does not have the support of nuclear-armed States or NATO.
161.tq: Find the extreme universal claim in statement 2 and retain the date and defining legal character.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: The **TPNW** came into force in **2021** — correct.
Statement 2: It has **no nuclear-armed or NATO support** — wrong.
Statement 3: It is the **first binding ban on nuclear weapons** — correct.
xa: **India did not sign** the TPNW — it **adds nothing to customary law**.
The **CTBT** (**1996**) bans all nuclear explosions but is **not in force**.
**US + Russia** hold about **90%** of global arsenals.

161.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Nuclear-weapon-free-zone treaty)
A. Treaty of Tlatelolco

xa: The fifth NWFZ treaty, **Semipalatinsk**, covers **Central Asia**.
The **TPNW** (in force **2021**) is the first binding global ban on nuclear weapons.
