xa: India is the **largest** contributor to **UNMISS** alone (**1,775** personnel).
Cumulative: **53 of 72** missions, **over 2,97,000 personnel**.
Present deployments: **DR Congo, South Sudan, Abyei, Lebanon, Golan Heights**.

162.s: The Development Partnership Administration (DPA) was set up in which Ministry and in which year?
o: Ministry of Commerce and Industry in 2014
162.x: The Development Partnership Administration was established in the Ministry of External Affairs in 2012.
162.tq: Identify the institution and the ministry responsible for it.
xs: The **DPA** was set up in the **Ministry of External Affairs** in **2012** — option **(1)**.
It manages India's development partnership, including grant projects and **Lines of Credit**.
xa: **ITEC** (**15 Sept 1964**) is a **training-based capacity-building** programme; **e-ITEC** is its online form.
**EXIM Bank** (HQ **Mumbai**) extends concessional **Lines of Credit** to foreign governments.

162.s:
With reference to the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme, consider the following statements:
1. ITEC was launched on 15 September 1964.
2. It is primarily a training-based capacity-building programme.
3. e-ITEC is the online form of ITEC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
162.x: ITEC was launched on 15 September 1964 as a training-based capacity-building programme, and e-ITEC is its online form.
162.tq: Test the date, purpose and digital counterpart together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **ITEC** was launched on **15 Sept 1964** — correct.
Statement 2: It is a **training-based capacity-building programme** — correct.
Statement 3: **e-ITEC** is its **online form** — correct.
xa: ICCR scholarships + **ITEC/e-ITEC** training are key **soft-power tools**.
The **DPA** sits in the **MEA**.

162.s:
Consider the following statements about the Export-Import (EXIM) Bank of India:
1. It was established on 1 January 1982 under the EXIM Bank Act, 1981.
2. Its headquarters is in New Delhi.
3. It extends concessional Lines of Credit to foreign governments to import Indian goods and services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
162.x: Statement 1 is correct: established 1 Jan 1982 under the EXIM Bank Act, 1981. Statement 2 is wrong: its headquarters is in Mumbai. Statement 3 is correct: it extends concessional LoCs to foreign governments to import Indian goods and services. So 1 and 3 only (B); A, C and D include the false statement 2 or omit a true one.
162.tq: Act 1981, bank 1982, HQ Mumbai.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **EXIM Bank** was established **1 Jan 1982** under the **EXIM Bank Act, 1981** — correct.
Statement 2: Its HQ is **Mumbai**, not New Delhi — wrong.
Statement 3: It extends **concessional Lines of Credit** to foreign governments to import Indian goods and services — correct.
xa: Example: a **$1 billion LoC** for **Central Asia** (announced **2020**).
India signed an **MoU on Ethiopia's debt restructuring** during the PM's visit (**Dec 2025**).

162.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Project)
(a) Salma Dam
(b) Parliament building
(c) Metro Express
(d) Indian Housing Project

List-II (Recipient)
(i) Sri Lanka
(ii) Mauritius
(iii) Afghanistan

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
162.x: The Salma Dam and Parliament building are in Afghanistan; Metro Express is in Mauritius; and the Indian Housing Project is in Sri Lanka.
162.tq: Start with the sure project-country pairs and eliminate codes.
xs: **Salma Dam – Afghanistan**, **Parliament building – Afghanistan**, **Metro Express – Mauritius**, **Indian Housing Project – Sri Lanka** → option **(1)**.
So a–iii, b–iii, c–ii, d–i.
xa: The Salma Dam is also called the **Afghan-India Friendship Dam**.
Mauritius also got a **new Supreme Court building** from India.
Such grants are run by the **DPA** in the **MEA** (**2012**).

162.s:
Match the following operations with the associated event:

(a) Dost
(b) Kaveri
(c) Ajay
(d) Ganga

(i) Israel evacuation
(ii) Ukraine evacuation
(iii) Türkiye and Syria earthquakes
(iv) Sudan evacuation

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
162.x: Dost concerned the Türkiye and Syria earthquakes; Kaveri concerned Sudan; Ajay concerned Israel; and Ganga concerned Ukraine.
162.tq: Start from the distinctive operation names and verify all four pairings.
xs: **Dost – Türkiye-Syria earthquake**, **Kaveri – Sudan**, **Ajay – Israel**, **Ganga – Ukraine** → option **(1)**.
So a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii.
xa: Dates: Dost **Feb 2023**; Kaveri **Apr 2023**; Ajay **Oct 2023**; Ganga **2022**.
**Sankat Mochan** = **South Sudan** evacuation, **2016**.
**Vande Bharat Mission** = worldwide **COVID-19** repatriation, **2020**.

162.s: Vaccine Maitri, launched in January 2021, primarily refers to India’s:
o: Programme for training foreign diplomats in India
Supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries
Evacuation of citizens from conflict zones
Financial support for overseas infrastructure projects
162.x: Vaccine Maitri refers to India’s supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries and was launched in January 2021.
162.tq: Separate health diplomacy from evacuation and development-finance initiatives.
xs: **Vaccine Maitri** (launched **January 2021**) was India's **supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries** — option **(2)**.
Evacuations had their own operations, e.g. **Ganga** (Ukraine) and **Kaveri** (Sudan); training is **ITEC**.
xa: ⚠ **Operation Maitri** (**2015**) was the **Nepal** earthquake relief — not Vaccine Maitri.
**DPI diplomacy** offers **India Stack** (Aadhaar, **UPI**, DigiLocker) to partners.
**Vande Bharat Mission** (**2020**) was the worldwide COVID-19 repatriation.

162.s:
Consider the following statements about the L.M. Singhvi High Level Committee on the Indian Diaspora:
1. It was set up in 2000 and submitted its report in 2002.
2. It recommended Pravasi Bharatiya Divas and a dual-citizenship-type status.
3. It was set up after the first Pravasi Bharatiya Divas of 2003.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
162.x: Statement 1 is correct: set up 2000, report 2002. Statement 2 is correct: it recommended PBD and a dual-citizenship-type status. Statement 3 is wrong: the committee (2000) came before the first PBD (2003), which it recommended. So 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
162.tq: Committee (2000) -> report (2002) -> first PBD (2003): the recommendation comes before the event.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: The **L.M. Singhvi Committee** was set up in **2000** and reported in **2002** — correct.
Statement 2: It recommended **PBD** and a **dual-citizenship-type status** — correct.
Statement 3: The committee (**2000**) came **before** the first PBD (**2003**) — wrong.
xa: The first **PBD** was held in **2003 at New Delhi**; **biennial since 2015**.
**OCI** came in **2005**; **PIO merged into OCI in 2015**.
PBD marks Gandhi's return from South Africa on **9 January 1915**.

162.s: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is observed on 9 January because Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on that date in which year?
162.x: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas commemorates Gandhi's return from South Africa on 9 January 1915.
162.tq: Link the commemorative date with the historical event and year.
xs: **Gandhi** returned from **South Africa** on **9 January 1915** — option **(3)**.
That date is marked as **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**.
xa: First PBD: **2003, New Delhi**; **biennial since 2015**.
**18th PBD**: **Bhubaneswar**, **8-10 Jan 2025**, theme **"Diaspora's Contribution to a Viksit Bharat"**.
The **President** confers the **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman** at PBD.

162.s: The Pravasi Bharatiya Samman is best described as which of the following?
o: An award given exclusively to foreign diplomats
A citizenship document issued by Indian missions abroad
The highest honour for overseas Indians, conferred by the President at Pravasi Bharatiya Divas
A migration training certificate issued by the Ministry of External Affairs
162.x: The Pravasi Bharatiya Samman is the highest honour for overseas Indians and is conferred by the President at PBD.
162.tq: Distinguish an honour from a citizenship document or migration scheme.
xs: The **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman** is the **highest honour for overseas Indians**, conferred by the **President** at **PBD** — option **(3)**.
It is an award, not a citizenship document — that is **OCI** (**2005**).
xa: PBD marks Gandhi's return on **9 January 1915**.
The **L.M. Singhvi Committee** (**2000**) recommended PBD.
First PBD in **2003**; **biennial since 2015**.

162.s: Which country had approximately 3.5 million Indians according to the cited diaspora data?
162.x: The United Arab Emirates had approximately 3.5 million Indians in the cited December 2025 data.
162.tq: Distinguish the country-specific diaspora count from general largest-diaspora claims.
xs: The **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** had about **3.5 million** Indians (**Dec 2025**) — option **(2)**.
It was the key for **"largest Indian population"** (**BPSC 2020**, Dec 2018 data).
xa: In **Australia**, Indian-origin people became the **largest immigrant-born community**, overtaking the UK-born (**Jul 2026**).
**1.46 crore passports** were issued in **2024**.
**"4 Ds"** of the Modi Doctrine: **Democracy, Demography, Demand, Diaspora**.

162.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) scheme was introduced in 2005.
2. The PIO card was merged into OCI in 2015.
3. Pravasi Bharatiya Divas has been held annually without a break since 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
162.x: Statement 1 is correct: OCI was introduced in 2005. Statement 2 is correct: PIO was merged into OCI in 2015. Statement 3 is wrong: PBD, first held in 2003, has been biennial since 2015. So 1 and 2 only.
162.tq: OCI 2005; PIO merged 2015; PBD biennial since 2015.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **OCI** was introduced in **2005** — correct.
Statement 2: **PIO merged into OCI in 2015** — correct.
Statement 3: PBD, first held **2003**, has been **biennial since 2015** — wrong.
xa: The **L.M. Singhvi Committee** (**2000**) recommended a **dual-citizenship-type status** and PBD.
**18th PBD**: **Bhubaneswar**, **8-10 Jan 2025**.
The **President** confers the **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman**.

162.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR):
1. It was set up in 1950 by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
2. It runs cultural centres, festivals and scholarships.
3. It was set up in 1982 to hold the first Festival of India in the United Kingdom.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
162.x: Statement 1 is correct: ICCR was set up in 1950 by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. Statement 2 is correct: it runs cultural centres, festivals and scholarships. Statement 3 is wrong: 1982 is the year of the first Festival of India (UK), not of ICCR's founding. So 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
162.tq: ICCR 1950 (Azad); Festival of India 1982 (UK) - do not mix the two years.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **ICCR** was set up in **1950** by **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** — correct.
Statement 2: It runs **cultural centres, festivals and scholarships** — correct.
Statement 3: **1982** is the **first Festival of India (UK)**, not ICCR's founding — wrong.
xa: Festival of India: **UK 1982** → **USA, France 1985-86** → **USSR 1987-88**.
**Study in India** (**2018**) is a **Ministry of Education** programme.
ICCR scholarships + **ITEC/e-ITEC** = soft-power tools.

162.s:
Consider the following statements about Nalanda University:
1. It was revived under the Nalanda University Act, 2010.
2. Its new campus at Bodh Gaya was inaugurated in June 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
162.x: Statement 1 is correct: it was revived under the Nalanda University Act, 2010. Statement 2 is wrong: the new campus inaugurated in June 2024 is at Rajgir, not Bodh Gaya. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept the wrong campus location or reject statement 1.
162.tq: Nalanda campus = Rajgir (June 2024).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **Nalanda University** was revived under the **Nalanda University Act, 2010** — correct.
Statement 2: The new campus inaugurated in **June 2024** is at **Rajgir**, not Bodh Gaya — wrong.
xa: **Study in India** (**2018**) attracts foreign students.
The **Buddhist circuit** and **Buddha Purnima** events use shared Buddhist heritage as soft power.
**ICCR** (**1950**) runs cultural centres and scholarships.

162.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four Ds of the Modi Doctrine?
162.x: The four Ds are Democracy, Demography, Demand and Diaspora. Development is not included in the stated formulation.
162.tq: Recall the complete four-item list and identify the substituted term.
xs: **Development** is not one of the **"4 Ds"** — option **(4)**.
The four Ds are **Democracy, Demography, Demand** and **Diaspora**.
xa: **UAE** has **3.5 million** Indians (**Dec 2025**).
**1.46 crore passports** were issued in **2024**.
Indian-origin people are now **Australia's largest immigrant-born community**.

162.s: The Netherlands returned which historical artefacts to India?
o: The Nalanda seals, consisting of Mughal copper plates
The Amaravati sculptures, consisting of Gupta marble panels
The Leiden Plates, consisting of 21 Chola copper plates from the time of Rajaraja Chola I
The Sanchi relics, consisting of Mauryan stone inscriptions
162.x: The Netherlands returned the Leiden Plates, 21 Chola copper plates dating from the time of Rajaraja Chola I.
162.tq: Match the returned artefact with its dynasty, material and historical ruler.
xs: The **Netherlands** returned the **Leiden Plates** — **21 Chola copper plates** from **Rajaraja Chola I**'s time (**May 2026**) — option **(3)**.
The return is listed among India's heritage **repatriation** gains (**May 2026**).
xa: The PM visited the diaspora in the **Netherlands** and **Australia** in **2026**.
**Nalanda University**'s new **Rajgir** campus opened in **June 2024**.
The **Buddhist circuit** is another heritage-based soft-power tool.

162.s: The International Day of Yoga was established by a UN General Assembly resolution in December 2014 and was first observed in:
162.x: The UNGA adopted the resolution in December 2014 and the first International Day of Yoga was observed in 2015. 2014 is the resolution year, not the first observance; 2016 and 2017 are later.
162.tq: Resolution Dec 2014 -> first Yoga Day 2015.
xs: **International Yoga Day** was first observed in **2015** — option **(2)**.
**2014** is the year of the **UNGA resolution (Dec 2014)**, not the first observance.
xa: Yoga is listed among India's soft-power tools with **ITEC training, scholarships, Bollywood**.
**ICCR** (**1950**) runs cultural centres and festivals.
**Study in India** launched in **2018**.

162.s: Which statement best reflects the distinction between recognition and strategic alignment in diaspora diplomacy?
o: Strategic alignment is possible only when diaspora groups are excluded from domestic politics.
Recognition and strategic alignment are identical concepts in international relations.
Recognition of diaspora contributions does not by itself amount to strategic alignment.
Recognition of a diaspora community necessarily establishes strategic alignment with its host country.
162.x: Recognition of a diaspora community or its contribution is not the same as strategic alignment with the host country.
162.tq: Separate symbolic recognition from a broader strategic relationship.
xs: **Recognition** of diaspora contributions **does not by itself** amount to **strategic alignment** — option **(3)**.
The notes state **"Recognition ≠ strategic alignment"** (**Jul 2026**).
xa: In Australia the diaspora can be recast **"as a liability"** in domestic politics.
Indian-origin people now form **Australia's largest immigrant-born community**.
**Diaspora** is one of the **"4 Ds"** of the Modi Doctrine.

163.s:
Consider the following statements about SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region):
1. It was set out in 2015.
2. It aims to make India the net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and counters China's 'String of Pearls'.
3. It widened India's maritime vision to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
163.x: Statement 1 is correct: SAGAR was set out in 2015. Statement 2 is correct: it makes India the net security provider in the IOR and counters the String of Pearls. Statement 3 is wrong: widening to the Indo-Pacific and Global South is MAHASAGAR (2025). So 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
163.tq: SAGAR = IOR (2015); MAHASAGAR = Indo-Pacific + Global South (2025); SHANTI = Bay of Bengal.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **SAGAR** was set out in **2015** — correct.
Statement 2: It makes India the **net security provider** in the **IOR** and counters China's **"String of Pearls"** — correct.
Statement 3: Widening to the **Indo-Pacific + Global South** is **MAHASAGAR (2025)**, not SAGAR — wrong.
xa: SAGAR = **Security and Growth for All in the Region**.
⚠ Order: **SAGAR → MAHASAGAR → SHANTI** (SHANTI = **Bay of Bengal** maritime-security framework).
String of Pearls sites: **Gwadar**, **Hambantota**, **Djibouti**.

163.s:
Consider the following statements regarding maritime frameworks associated with India:
1. MAHASAGAR was introduced in 2025.
2. MAHASAGAR widens the scope of SAGAR to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South.
3. SHANTI has been framed as the next step in maritime security for the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
163.x: All three statements are correct. MAHASAGAR was introduced in 2025, extends SAGAR to the Indo-Pacific and Global South, and SHANTI is framed as a subsequent Bay of Bengal maritime-security framework.
163.tq: Test a cluster of closely related policy names, years and geographical scopes.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statements 1-2: **MAHASAGAR (2025)** widens SAGAR to the **Indo-Pacific** and **Global South** — correct.
Statement 3: **SHANTI** is framed as the next step — a maritime-security framework for the **Bay of Bengal** — correct.
xa: MAHASAGAR = **"Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security Across the Regions"**.
**SAGAR** (**2015**) made India the **net security provider** in the IOR.
⚠ Order: **SAGAR → MAHASAGAR → SHANTI**.

163.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS):
1. It was launched in 2008 as an Indian Navy initiative and first held in New Delhi.
2. Its inaugural meeting was held in 2015.
3. It is a voluntary forum covering maritime security, domain awareness and HADR.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
163.x: Statement 1 is correct: IONS was launched in 2008 by the Indian Navy, first held in New Delhi. Statement 2 is wrong: the 'inaugural IONS in 2015' claim is the UPSC 2017 trap; it began in 2008. Statement 3 is correct: it is voluntary and covers maritime security, domain awareness and HADR. So 1 and 3 only (B).
163.tq: IONS 2008, New Delhi; 2015 is the trap year (SAGAR's year).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: **IONS** began in **2008** as an **Indian Navy initiative**, first held in **New Delhi** — correct.
Statement 2: ⚠ **"Inaugural IONS in 2015"** is the **UPSC 2017** trap — wrong.
Statement 3: It is **voluntary**, covering maritime security, domain awareness and **HADR** — correct.
xa: India holds the **IONS Chairmanship** and hosted the **9th Conclave of Chiefs at Visakhapatnam** (**2026**).
⚠ **2015** = SAGAR; **2008** = IONS; **2011** = Colombo Security Conclave.
**IOS SAGAR** carried **16 IONS countries** on **INS Sunayna**.

163.s: The 9th Conclave of Chiefs of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium was hosted at:
163.x: India hosted the 9th IONS Conclave of Chiefs at Visakhapatnam.
163.tq: Current institutional event and venue recall.
xs: India hosted the **9th IONS Conclave of Chiefs** at **Visakhapatnam** (**2026**) — option **(1)**.
India currently holds the **IONS Chairmanship**.
xa: **IONS** began in **2008**, first held in **New Delhi**.
Vizag also hosted the **Colombo Security Conclave table-top exercise** (**Sep 2026**) and **IFR 2026**.
**MILAN** began in **1995 at Port Blair**; **2022** and **2024** editions at Visakhapatnam.

163.s:
Consider the following statements about the Information Fusion Centre - Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR):
1. It was set up by the Indian Navy at Gurugram in December 2018.
2. It is meant for maritime domain awareness and information sharing.
3. It is located at Visakhapatnam under the Eastern Naval Command.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
163.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Navy set up IFC-IOR at Gurugram in Dec 2018. Statement 2 is correct: its purpose is maritime domain awareness and information sharing. Statement 3 is wrong: it is at Gurugram, not Visakhapatnam. So 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
163.tq: A naval centre located inland at Gurugram is the classic trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: The **Indian Navy** set up **IFC-IOR** at **Gurugram** in **Dec 2018** — correct.
Statement 2: It is for **maritime domain awareness + information sharing** — correct.
Statement 3: It is at **Gurugram**, not Visakhapatnam — wrong.
xa: ⚠ **Gurugram** hosts both **ISA** HQ and **IFC-IOR**.
APPSC **2018** keyed "a and b" as correct on IFC-IOR.
**Visakhapatnam** is HQ of the **Eastern Naval Command**.

163.s:
With reference to the Djibouti Code of Conduct, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted in 2009.
2. It is an IMO-backed framework.
3. India joined it as an observer in 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
163.x: The Djibouti Code of Conduct was adopted in 2009, is backed by the International Maritime Organization, and India joined as an observer in 2020.
163.tq: Verify the year, sponsoring body and nature of participation together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: The **Djibouti Code of Conduct** dates from **2009** — correct.
Statement 2: It is an **IMO-backed** framework against **piracy** in the western Indian Ocean + **Gulf of Aden** — correct.
Statement 3: India joined as an **observer (2020)** — correct.
xa: **Djibouti** hosts **China's first overseas base (2017)** and the US **Camp Lemonnier**.
India took **CTF-154** command (HQ **Bahrain**) for the first time.
⚠ **2020** is also the year the **Colombo Security Conclave** was rebranded.

163.s: The Malabar naval exercise is correctly matched with which of the following statements?
o: It began as an India-Japan exercise in 1995; Australia became permanent in 2015.
It began in 2005 at Port Blair and is permanently hosted by India.
It began as an India-US exercise in 1992; Japan became a permanent participant in 2015 and Australia joined in 2020.
It is conducted exclusively between India and the United States and has no Quad association.
163.x: Malabar began as an India-US exercise in 1992, Japan became a permanent participant in 2015, and Australia joined in 2020. These participants constitute the Quad grouping.
163.tq: Build the answer from the sequence of origin, permanent participation and later expansion.
xs: **Malabar** began as **India-US (1992)**; **Japan** became permanent in **2015**; **Australia** joined in **2020** — option **(3)**.
All four partners make up the **Quad**, and the exercise **rotates among partners**.
Port Blair (**1995**) is where **MILAN** began, not Malabar.
xa: **MILAN** is a **multilateral** exercise hosted by the Indian Navy; **2022/2024** at **Visakhapatnam**.
**AIKEYME** = Africa-India Key Maritime Engagement, first edition **2025**, **Tanzania**.
**CTF-154** (HQ **Bahrain**): India took **command for the first time**.

163.s:
Consider the following statements about naval exercises and maritime platforms:
1. MILAN is a multilateral exercise hosted by the Indian Navy.
2. The 2022 and 2024 editions of MILAN were held at Visakhapatnam.
3. AIKEYME means Africa-India Key Maritime Engagement.
4. The first edition of AIKEYME was held in Tanzania in 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
163.x: All four statements are correct. MILAN is hosted by the Indian Navy, its 2022 and 2024 editions were at Visakhapatnam, and AIKEYME's first edition was held at Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, in 2025.
163.tq: Check every row of a compact exercise table before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Statements 1-2: **MILAN** is a **multilateral** exercise hosted by the **Indian Navy**; **2022** and **2024** at **Visakhapatnam** — correct.
Statements 3-4: **AIKEYME** = **Africa-India Key Maritime Engagement**; first edition **2025**, **Tanzania** — correct.
xa: MILAN began in **1995** at **Port Blair**.
AIKEYME's first venue was **Dar es Salaam**.
**Malabar** brings together all **Quad** members.

163.s: India took command for the first time of which maritime task force in 2026?
o: Indian Ocean Naval Symposium Task Force
163.x: India took command for the first time of CTF-154, a task force of the Combined Maritime Forces headquartered in Bahrain.
163.tq: Distinguish the exact task-force number from neighbouring maritime force designations.
xs: India took **command for the first time** of **Combined Task Force 154** — option **(2)**.
CTF-154 belongs to the **Combined Maritime Forces**, HQ **Bahrain**.
xa: India's **IONS** chairship + **CTF-154** command are listed as **2026** current relevance.
⚠ **CTF-154** = **Bahrain**; **AIKEYME** = **Tanzania**.
India joined the **Djibouti Code of Conduct** (anti-piracy) as an **observer (2020)**.

163.s: Which one of the following sets is associated with the concept of China’s ‘String of Pearls’?
163.x: Gwadar, Hambantota and Djibouti are associated with the String of Pearls concept.
163.tq: Group-recognition question using a known strategic cluster.
xs: **Gwadar, Hambantota and Djibouti** form China's **String of Pearls** — option **(4)**.
**Chabahar, Sittwe, Sabang** are **India's counters** to BRI; **Duqm, Agalega, Colombo West** are India's strategic-access sites.
xa: ⚠ **Hambantota / Gwadar** = String of Pearls (China); **Sittwe / Sabang** = India's counters.
**Djibouti** = China's **first overseas base (2017)**.
China's **"Malacca dilemma"** drives its port-building.

163.s: Which one of the following port-country pairs is NOT correctly matched?
163.x: Sittwe is in Myanmar, not Sri Lanka. Sabang is in Indonesia, Duqm in Oman and Agalega in Mauritius.
163.tq: Find the wrong location by checking the port-country association.
xs: **Sittwe — Sri Lanka** is wrong: **Sittwe** is in **Myanmar** — option **(3)**.
**Duqm – Oman**, **Sabang – Indonesia**, **Agalega – Mauritius** are correct.
xa: Sri Lanka's site is the **Colombo West Container Terminal**.
**Agalega** has an **airstrip and jetty**.
**Kaladan**: Kolkata → **Sittwe** by sea → Paletwa → road to **Mizoram**.

163.s: Which of the following ports are India’s counters to China’s Belt and Road Initiative?
163.x: Chabahar, Sittwe and Sabang are identified as India’s counters to China’s BRI.
163.tq: Identify the strategic trio rather than individual port locations.
xs: **Chabahar, Sittwe and Sabang** are India's **counters to BRI** — option **(1)**.
**Gwadar, Hambantota, Djibouti** are China's **String of Pearls**; **Diego Garcia** is a **US-UK** base.
xa: **Chabahar** (Iran) gives access to **Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan**.
**Sittwe** (Myanmar) is the sea port of the **Kaladan** project.
**Sabang** is in **Indonesia**.

163.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Continental shelf — exactly 200 nautical miles in every case
163.x: The EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles. The contiguous zone extends to 24 nautical miles, the territorial sea to 12 nautical miles, and the continental shelf may extend up to 350 nautical miles.
163.tq: Separate maritime-zone limits and reject reversed or absolute claims.
xs: The **EEZ** extends **200 nm** from the baseline — option **(1)**.
**Territorial sea = 12 nm** and **contiguous zone = 24 nm**, so options (2)-(3) swap them.
The **continental shelf** goes **up to 350 nm**, not exactly 200 nm.
xa: These zones come from **UNCLOS 1982**.
India's coastline: **11,098.81 km**.
**PCA award of 2014** gave Bangladesh about **19,467 sq km** of the **25,602 sq km** disputed area.

163.s: Which of the following is a component of India’s Deep Ocean Mission?
o: Samudrayaan, involving deep-sea mining and study of polymetallic nodules
Sagarmala, involving only coastal road construction
163.x: Samudrayaan is part of the Deep Ocean Mission and concerns deep-sea mining and the study of polymetallic nodules.
163.tq: Identify the programme component from its objective and domain.
xs: **Samudrayaan** (deep-sea mining + study of **polymetallic nodules**) is part of the **Deep Ocean Mission** — option **(1)**.
**OSOWOG** belongs to the **ISA**; **Camp Lemonnier** is a US base in **Djibouti**.
xa: The Deep Ocean Mission is run by **MoES**.
Its manned submersible is **Matsya-6000**.
Under **UNCLOS 1982**, the **EEZ** extends **200 nm**.

163.s: The India-Bangladesh maritime boundary dispute was settled by an award of the Permanent Court of Arbitration in:
163.x: The PCA award of 2014 settled the India-Bangladesh maritime boundary, giving Bangladesh about 19,467 sq km of the 25,602 sq km disputed area. 2009, 2012 and 2015 are not the year of this award.
163.tq: India-Bangladesh sea boundary: PCA 2014, Bangladesh got the larger share (~19,467 of 25,602 sq km).
xs: The **PCA award of 2014** settled the **India-Bangladesh** maritime boundary — option **(3)**.
It gave Bangladesh about **19,467 sq km** of the **25,602 sq km** disputed area.
xa: Under **UNCLOS 1982**: territorial sea **12 nm**, contiguous zone **24 nm**, EEZ **200 nm**.
India's coastline: **11,098.81 km**.
Deep Ocean Mission (**MoES**) includes **Samudrayaan** and the submersible **Matsya-6000**.

163.s: Chabahar port is located in which part of Iran?
o: Fars on the Gulf of Oman
Sistan-Baluchestan on the Gulf of Oman
163.x: Chabahar is located in Iran’s Sistan-Baluchestan province on the Gulf of Oman.
163.tq: Discriminate between Iranian provinces and adjoining maritime regions.
xs: **Chabahar** is in **Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan**, on the **Gulf of Oman** — option **(3)**.
India develops its **Shahid Beheshti terminal** via **IPGL**.
xa: It gives India **access to Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan** (UPSC **2017** key).
It links into the **INSTC**.
A **10-year** operating contract was signed in **May 2024**.

163.s:
Consider the following statements about Chabahar port:
1. India develops its Shahid Beheshti terminal through India Ports Global Ltd (IPGL).
2. A 20-year operating contract for the terminal was signed in May 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
163.x: Statement 1 is correct: India develops the Shahid Beheshti terminal through IPGL. Statement 2 is wrong: the contract signed in May 2024 is for 10 years. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept the wrong duration or reject statement 1.
163.tq: Chabahar contract: 10 years, May 2024, via IPGL.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: India develops the **Shahid Beheshti terminal** through **India Ports Global Ltd (IPGL)** — correct.
Statement 2: The **May 2024** operating contract is for **10 years**, not 20 — wrong.
xa: **US strikes on Chabahar** (**2026**): MEA said the terminal was **not damaged**.
Chabahar sits in **Sistan-Baluchestan**, on the **Gulf of Oman**.
It is one of India's **counters to BRI** with **Sittwe** and **Sabang**.

163.s:
Consider the following statements about the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC):
1. Its agreement was signed in 2000 by India, Iran and Russia.
2. It is a multimodal sea-rail-road route from Mumbai via Iran to Central Asia, Russia and Europe.
3. Its western branch runs through Armenia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
163.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2000 agreement was signed by India, Iran and Russia. Statement 2 is correct: it is a multimodal route from Mumbai via Iran to Central Asia, Russia and Europe. Statement 3 is wrong: the western branch runs through Azerbaijan (UPSC 2025 key); Armenia figures in the newer Armenia-Iran-India Persian Gulf-Black Sea corridor. So 1 and 2 only (B).
163.tq: INSTC western branch = Azerbaijan; Armenia = the separate Gulf-Black Sea trilateral.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: The **INSTC** agreement (**2000**) was signed by **India, Iran, Russia** — correct.
Statement 2: It is a **multimodal sea-rail-road** route from **Mumbai via Iran** to Central Asia, Russia and Europe — correct.
Statement 3: Its western branch runs through **Azerbaijan**, not Armenia (UPSC **2025** key) — wrong.
xa: **Armenia** is in the newer **Armenia-Iran-India** trilateral for a **Persian Gulf-Black Sea** corridor (**Jan 2026**).
⚠ **INSTC = 2000**; **IMEC = Sept 2023**; **Ashgabat = 2011**, India joined **2018**.
**Chabahar** links into the INSTC.

163.s: The IMEC was announced at the G20 New Delhi Summit in:
163.x: The India-Middle East-Europe Corridor was announced at the G20 New Delhi Summit in September 2023.
163.tq: Use the event-year association for a recently announced corridor.
xs: **IMEC** was announced at the **G20 New Delhi** summit in **September 2023** — option **(3)**.
IMEC = **India-Middle East-Europe Corridor**.
xa: Partners: **India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, EU, France, Germany, Italy, USA**.
⚠ **INSTC = 2000** agreement; **Ashgabat = 2011**, India joined **2018**.
The **Global Biofuels Alliance** was also launched at the **G20** in India (**2023**).

163.s:
Arrange the following projects in the order of their stated beginning or agreement years, from earliest to latest:
A. Ashgabat Agreement
B. INSTC agreement
C. IMEC announcement
D. India’s joining of the Ashgabat Agreement
163.x: The INSTC agreement dates to 2000, the Ashgabat Agreement to 2011, India joined Ashgabat in 2018, and IMEC was announced in 2023.
163.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate dates.
xs: Order: **INSTC (2000)** → **Ashgabat (2011)** → **India joins Ashgabat (2018)** → **IMEC (2023)** = **B, A, D, C**, option **(1)**.
INSTC was signed by **India, Iran, Russia**; IMEC was announced at **G20 New Delhi**.
xa: Ashgabat is a **transit corridor** linking **Central Asia** with the **Persian Gulf**.
The **Armenia-Iran-India** trilateral (**Jan 2026**) is the newest route.
INSTC's western branch runs through **Azerbaijan** (UPSC **2025** key).

163.s: A newer trilateral initiative promotes a Persian Gulf–Black Sea corridor involving:
163.x: The newer initiative involves Armenia, Iran and India and promotes a Persian Gulf–Black Sea corridor.
163.tq: Identify the countries from a small trilateral arrangement rather than a larger corridor membership list.
xs: The newer **Persian Gulf-Black Sea** corridor involves **Armenia, Iran and India** — option **(2)**.
This trilateral was noted in **Jan 2026**.
xa: ⚠ The **INSTC**'s western branch runs through **Azerbaijan** (UPSC **2025**), not Armenia.
INSTC agreement: **2000**, **India, Iran, Russia**.
**Chabahar** links into the INSTC.

163.s:
Consider the following statements about India's energy profile:
1. India imports about 88% of its crude oil needs and about 50% of its natural gas needs.
2. India is the world's second-largest energy consumer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
163.x: Statement 1 is correct: about 88% of crude and about 50% of gas are imported (older estimates said 80% and 25%). Statement 2 is wrong: India is the third-largest energy consumer. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept the wrong rank or reject statement 1.
163.tq: Remember 88/50 (current) vs 80/25 (old) and 'third-largest consumer'.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: India imports about **88% of crude oil** and **50% of natural gas** needs (**2026**) — correct.
Statement 2: India is the **third-largest** energy consumer, not second — wrong.
xa: ⚠ Older notes said **80%** (crude) and **25%** (gas).
About **50% of crude imports** pass through the **Strait of Hormuz**.
Thin SPR buffer: **9.5 days** vs IEA's **90**.

163.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four ‘A’s guiding India’s energy policy?
163.x: The four ‘A’s are availability, accessibility, affordability and acceptability. Autonomy is not included in the stated formulation.
163.tq: Find the look-alike substitute for an exact policy formulation.
xs: **Autonomy** is not one of the four 'A's — option **(2)**.
The four 'A's: **availability, accessibility, affordability, acceptability**.
xa: India imports about **88% of crude** and **50% of gas**.
India is the **third-largest energy consumer**.
Pipelines: **TAPI** and **IPI** ("**Peace Pipeline**").

163.s: TAPI and IPI pipelines are respectively associated with which countries?
163.x: TAPI stands for Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India, while IPI stands for Iran-Pakistan-India and is also called the Peace Pipeline.
163.tq: Expand both similar pipeline acronyms before selecting the country sequence.
xs: **TAPI** = **Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India**; **IPI** = **Iran-Pakistan-India** — option **(2)**.
IPI is called the **"Peace Pipeline"**.
xa: **UAE** is India's **4th**-largest crude supplier and only country storing oil in India's **SPR**.
**Uranium** comes from **Kazakhstan** and **Uzbekistan**.
About **50% of crude imports** pass the **Strait of Hormuz**.

163.s: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched on 30 November 2015 at:
o: The G20 Summit in New Delhi
163.x: The ISA was launched on 30 November 2015 at COP21 in Paris.
163.tq: Combine a precise date with the correct international forum and venue.
xs: The **ISA** was launched on **30 Nov 2015** at **COP21, Paris** — option **(2)**.
Its HQ is **Gurugram**, not Paris.
xa: ISA is **treaty-based** with **116+ members** (**2024**).
Flagship: **One Sun One World One Grid**.
The **Global Biofuels Alliance** was launched at the **G20** in India (**2023**).

163.s: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 at:
o: The World Energy Congress in Abu Dhabi
The BRICS Summit in South Africa
163.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 at the G20 Summit in India.
163.tq: Identify the launch forum and year of a global initiative.
xs: The **Global Biofuels Alliance** was launched in **2023** at the **G20** in **India** — option **(4)**.
It now has **32 countries + 14 international organisations** (**2026**).
xa: **IMEC** was also announced at **G20 New Delhi** (**Sept 2023**).
The **ISA** was launched at **COP21, Paris** (**2015**).
**IEF** secretariat: **Riyadh**.

163.s: India’s status in the International Energy Agency is that of a/an:
163.x: India has been an Association country of the IEA since 2017 and is not a full member.
163.tq: Distinguish association status from full membership.
xs: India is an **IEA Association country since 2017** — option **(4)**.
⚠ India is **not a full member** of the IEA.
xa: The thin SPR buffer (**9.5 days**) falls short of the IEA's **90 days**.
India engages the **IEF** (secretariat **Riyadh**) and holds an **Energy Dialogue with OPEC**.
**ISA** HQ: **Gurugram**.

163.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Energy Forum (IEF):
1. Its secretariat is located at Riyadh.
2. India hosted the 16th IEF ministerial meeting in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
163.x: Statement 1 is correct: the IEF secretariat is at Riyadh. Statement 2 is wrong: India hosted the 16th IEF ministerial in 2018, not 2023. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept the wrong year or reject statement 1.
163.tq: IEF = Riyadh; India hosted the 16th ministerial in 2018.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: The **IEF** secretariat is at **Riyadh** — correct.
Statement 2: India hosted the **16th IEF** ministerial in **2018**, not 2023 — wrong.
xa: India is an **IEA Association country** (since **2017**).
India holds an **Energy Dialogue with OPEC**.
The **ISA** (HQ **Gurugram**) was launched at **COP21** in **2015**.

163.s: The headquarters of the treaty-based International Solar Alliance (ISA) is located at:
163.x: The ISA is treaty-based with its headquarters at Gurugram. Paris (COP21) is where it was launched, not its HQ; New Delhi is a distractor; Riyadh hosts the IEF secretariat.
163.tq: ISA: launched Paris (COP21, 2015), HQ Gurugram. IEF: Riyadh.
xs: The **ISA**'s HQ is at **Gurugram** — option **(3)**.
**Paris** is where it was launched (**COP21, 30 Nov 2015**); **Riyadh** hosts the **IEF** secretariat.
xa: ⚠ **Gurugram** hosts both **ISA** HQ and **IFC-IOR**.
ISA is **treaty-based**, **116+ members**; flagship **One Sun One World One Grid**.
The **Global Biofuels Alliance** began at the **G20** (**2023**).

163.s:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Naval Command:
1. Its headquarters is at Visakhapatnam and it faces the Bay of Bengal.
2. It is India's smallest naval command.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
163.x: Statement 1 is correct: ENC is headquartered at Visakhapatnam, facing the Bay of Bengal. Statement 2 is wrong: it is India's largest naval command. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept the wrong size or reject statement 1.
163.tq: ENC = Vizag = largest naval command.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: The **Eastern Naval Command** has HQ at **Visakhapatnam** and faces the **Bay of Bengal** — correct.
Statement 2: It is India's **largest** naval command, not the smallest — wrong.
xa: **IFR 2026**: President **Droupadi Murmu** reviewed the fleet from **INS Sumedha**; previous Vizag IFR **2016**.
Vizag hosted the **IONS Conclave of Chiefs** (**2026**) and holds one of the **three SPRs**.
⚠ IFR yacht = **INS Sumedha**; IOS SAGAR ship = **INS Sunayna**.

163.s: Visakhapatnam holds one of India’s three:
163.x: Visakhapatnam holds one of India’s three Strategic Petroleum Reserves.
163.tq: Use the exact institutional term rather than a look-alike expansion.
xs: **Visakhapatnam** holds one of India's **three Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPRs)** — option **(3)**.
It is part of Vizag's role as the **hub of naval diplomacy** (ENC, IFR, IONS, CSC exercise, **SPR**).
xa: The **UAE** is the **only** country storing oil in India's **SPR** and India's **4th**-largest crude supplier.
⚠ Thin SPR buffer: **9.5 days** vs the IEA's **90**.
About **50% of crude imports** pass through the **Strait of Hormuz**.

163.s: China’s port-building strategy in the Indian Ocean is linked in strategic analysis to its:
163.x: China’s port-building is linked to its perceived Malacca dilemma.
163.tq: Match a strategic behaviour with the specific security dilemma driving it.
xs: China's port-building is driven by its **"Malacca dilemma"** (**Jul 2026**) — option **(1)**.
That port network is the **"String of Pearls"**: **Gwadar**, **Hambantota**, **Djibouti**.
xa: **Djibouti** = China's **first overseas base (2017)**.
**SAGAR** (**2015**) counters the String of Pearls.
India's counters to BRI: **Chabahar**, **Sittwe**, **Sabang**.
**Chagos** hosts the US-UK base at **Diego Garcia** — not a "dilemma" of China.

164.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indo-Tibetan Border Police:
1. It was raised in 1962 after the Chinese aggression.
2. It guards the border from Karakoram Pass to Jachep La.
3. It maintains more than 200 border posts at altitudes ranging from 9,000 to 18,800 feet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
164.x: All three statements are correct. The ITBP was raised in 1962 and operates along the high-altitude China border between Karakoram Pass and Jachep La.
164.tq: Check each numerical and geographical detail before selecting the combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **ITBP** was raised in **1962**, after the Chinese aggression — correct.
Statement 2: It guards the **China** border (**3,488 km**) from **Karakoram Pass to Jachep La** — correct.
Statement 3: It has **200+ border posts** at **9,000-18,800 ft** — correct.
xa: ITBP now has **64 battalions** (IYB **2026**).
⚠ **SSB** = Nepal + Bhutan; **ITBP** = China; **Assam Rifles** = Myanmar; **BSF** = Pakistan + Bangladesh.
China border (**3,488 km**) is India's second-longest, after **Bangladesh (4,096.7 km)**.

164.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
164.x: Assam Rifles guards the Myanmar border. The BSF, ITBP and SSB are correctly matched with their principal border responsibilities.
164.tq: Find the force whose assigned border has been substituted with a neighbouring border.
xs: **Assam Rifles — Bangladesh border** is wrong: **Assam Rifles** guards the **Myanmar** border — option **(1)**.
The **Bangladesh** border is guarded by the **BSF** (with Pakistan).
**SSB – Nepal and Bhutan**, **ITBP – China**, **BSF – Pakistan and Bangladesh** are correct.
xa: ⚠ Oldest = **Assam Rifles** (**1835**); **SSB** = **newest border force**.
**BSF** (**1965**) has **193 battalions** (incl. **3 NDRF**).
India-Myanmar border: **1,643 km**.

164.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Coast Guard — 1977
b. Assam Rifles — 1835
c. Sashastra Seema Bal — 1963
d. Border Security Force — 1962
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
164.x: The Coast Guard was raised in 1977, Assam Rifles in 1835 and SSB in 1963. The BSF was raised in 1965, not 1962.
164.tq: Test the list by isolating the altered raising year.
xs: Pairs a, b and c are correct — option **(1) a, b and c only**.
**Coast Guard – 1977**, **Assam Rifles – 1835**, **SSB – 1963** are correct.
Pair d is wrong: the **BSF** was raised in **1965**; **1962** is the **ITBP**.
xa: ⚠ Oldest paramilitary = **Assam Rifles**; newest border force = **SSB**.
**CRPF** began on **27 July 1939** as the **Crown Representative's Police**.
The **Coast Guard** works under the **MoD**, guarding **territorial waters**.

164.s: The Coast Guard is responsible for coastal security in territorial waters and functions under which Ministry?
164.x: The Coast Guard provides coastal security in territorial waters and functions under the Ministry of Defence.
164.tq: Ask which ministry would normally exercise authority over the maritime defence function.
xs: The **Coast Guard** handles coastal security in **territorial waters** under the **Ministry of Defence** — option **(1)**.
It was raised in **1977**.
xa: Post-**26/11** three tiers: **Navy** = overall; **Coast Guard** = territorial waters; **coastal police** = shallow waters.
**Sagar Kavach** is the **biannual** Coast Guard coastal-security exercise.
Coastline: **11,098.81 km**.

164.s:
Consider the following statements about the extension of BSF jurisdiction:
1. In Punjab and West Bengal it was extended from 15 km to 50 km inside the international border.
2. States challenged it as an entry into Police and Public Order, which are subjects in the Union List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
164.x: Statement 1 is correct: the jurisdiction went from 15 km to 50 km in Punjab and West Bengal. Statement 2 is wrong: States objected precisely because Police and Public Order are in the State List (List II), not the Union List. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept the wrong list or reject statement 1.
164.tq: A States' challenge only makes sense if the subject is in List II.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: In **Punjab** and **West Bengal**, BSF jurisdiction went from **15 km to 50 km** inside the international border — correct.
Statement 2: **Police/Public Order** are in the **State List (List II)**, not the Union List — wrong.
xa: Critics say **CBI general-consent withdrawals** and extended **NIA/BSF** reach enter **state subjects**.
**BSF** (**1965**) guards **Pakistan and Bangladesh** borders.
BSF also does **anti-infiltration in Kashmir** and **anti-Naxal** work in Odisha/Chhattisgarh.

164.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF):
1. It began on 27 July 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police.
2. It was renamed by the CRPF Act, 1949.
3. It is India's oldest paramilitary force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
164.x: Statement 1 is correct: it began on 27 July 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police. Statement 2 is correct: it was renamed by the CRPF Act, 1949. Statement 3 is wrong: Assam Rifles (1835) is the oldest paramilitary force. So 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
164.tq: Oldest paramilitary = Assam Rifles (1835), not CRPF (1939).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **CRPF** began on **27 July 1939** as the **Crown Representative's Police** — correct.
Statement 2: It was renamed by the **CRPF Act, 1949** — correct.
Statement 3: The **oldest** paramilitary force is **Assam Rifles** (**1835**) — wrong.
xa: CRPF marked its **88th** Raising Day in **2026**.
The **Internal Security Academy** of the CRPF is at **Mount Abu**.
The **MHA** controls all **CAPFs**.

164.s: The Department of Border Management, created in 2004, functions under which Ministry?
164.x: The Department of Border Management is in the Ministry of Home Affairs (APPSC 2018 key), which also controls all CAPFs. The Ministry of Defence controls the Army and Coast Guard, not this department; MEA handles foreign relations; the Cabinet Secretariat houses RAW.
164.tq: Border Management Dept = MHA (2004); MHA controls all CAPFs.
xs: The **Department of Border Management** is in the **Ministry of Home Affairs** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2018** key).
The **MHA** also controls all **CAPFs**; the **Cabinet Secretariat** houses **RAW**.
xa: The department was created in **2004**.
The **Coast Guard** is under the **MoD**.
The **Army** guards the **LoC** and **LAC**.

164.s:
Arrange the following international borders of India in descending order of length:
A. China
B. Bangladesh
C. Nepal
D. Pakistan
164.x: The correct order is Bangladesh (4,096.7 km), China (3,488 km), Pakistan (3,323 km) and Nepal (1,751 km).
164.tq: Arrange the items by comparing the largest and the next two border lengths first.
xs: Descending order: **Bangladesh (4,096.7)** → **China (3,488)** → **Pakistan (3,323)** → **Nepal (1,751)** = **B, A, D, C**, option **(1)**.
Bangladesh is the **longest** land border.
xa: Others: **Myanmar 1,643**, **Bhutan 699**, **Afghanistan 106** (shortest).
**CIBMS** smart fencing covers the **Pakistan + Bangladesh** borders.
The **BSF** guards both the longest (**Bangladesh**) and the **Pakistan** border.

164.s: The Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System is primarily associated with:
o: Technology-based smart fencing on the Pakistan and Bangladesh borders
Coastal policing in shallow waters only
164.x: CIBMS is a technology-based smart-fencing system intended for the Pakistan and Bangladesh borders.
164.tq: Match the technology-based border-management system with its operational location.
xs: **CIBMS** is **technology-based smart fencing** on the **Pakistan and Bangladesh** borders — option **(3)**.
Protecting PMs is the **SPG**; investigating scheduled offences is the **NIA**; shallow waters are the **coastal police**.
xa: The **BSF** guards both these borders.
Bangladesh border: **4,096.7 km**; Pakistan: **3,323 km**.
**VVP-II** (**2024-25 to 2028-29**) develops border villages.

164.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vibrant Villages Programme-II (VVP-II):
1. It runs from 2024-25 to 2028-29.
2. It covers villages on the Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan borders.
3. Its roads are built under PMGSY-IV.
4. It covers Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Ladakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
164.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: VVP-II runs 2024-25 to 2028-29, covers villages on the Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan borders, with roads under PMGSY-IV. Statement 4 is wrong: HP, Uttarakhand, Arunachal, Sikkim and Ladakh (the China-border states) are covered by Viksit VVP Phase I. So B; A omits statement 3, C and D include statement 4.
164.tq: VVP-II = the non-China borders; Phase I = the northern (China) border states.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statements 1-3: **VVP-II** runs **2024-25 to 2028-29**, covers villages on **Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal, Bhutan** borders, with roads under **PMGSY-IV**.
Statement 4: **HP, Uttarakhand, Arunachal, Sikkim, Ladakh** fall under **Viksit VVP Phase I** (**2026**) — wrong.
xa: **CIBMS** = smart fencing on Pakistan + Bangladesh borders.
The **Department of Border Management** (**2004**) is in the **MHA**.
⚠ **ITBP** guards the **China** border these Phase I states face.

164.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the three-tier coastal-security arrangement after 26/11?
o: Navy—overall responsibility; Coast Guard—territorial waters; coastal police—shallow waters
Coast Guard—overall responsibility; Navy—shallow waters; coastal police—territorial waters
Coastal police—overall responsibility; Navy—territorial waters; Coast Guard—shallow waters
NIA—overall responsibility; Navy—territorial waters; Coast Guard—shallow waters
164.x: The Navy has overall responsibility, the Coast Guard operates in territorial waters, and coastal police operate in shallow waters.
164.tq: Match each agency with its level of coastal responsibility.
xs: Post-**26/11**: **Navy** = overall maritime security, **Coast Guard** = territorial waters, **coastal police** = shallow waters — option **(1)**.
The **NIA** is an investigating agency, not part of the coastal tiers.
xa: **Sagar Kavach** = **biannual** Coast Guard exercise.
The **NIA Act (2008)** and the **NSG**'s key role both trace to **26/11**.
Coastline: **11,098.81 km**.

164.s: The Intelligence Bureau was set up in which year?
164.x: The Intelligence Bureau was set up in 1887.
164.tq: Use the agency-specific year rather than the dates associated with RAW or SPG.
xs: The **Intelligence Bureau** was set up in **1887** — option **(1)**.
xa: The **IB** is under the **MHA** (internal intelligence).
Head: **Mahesh Dixit** (AP cadre, **1993** IPS), appointed **Jun 2026**.
⚠ **IB** = MHA (internal); **RAW** = Cabinet Secretariat (external); **CERT-In** = MeitY.

164.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Research and Analysis Wing is India's external intelligence agency.
2. It was established in 1968.
3. It functions under the Cabinet Secretariat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
164.x: All three statements are correct. RAW deals with external intelligence, was established in 1968 and functions under the Cabinet Secretariat.
164.tq: Confirm the agency, establishment year and administrative location together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**RAW** handles **external intelligence**, was set up in **1968**, and is under the **Cabinet Secretariat**.
xa: ⚠ **IB** = MHA, internal intelligence, set up **1887**.
The **NIA** and **NATGRID** are also under the **MHA**.
**CERT-In** is under **MeitY** (cyber incident response).

164.s:
With reference to the National Investigation Agency, consider the following statements:
1. It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. It can investigate scheduled offences anywhere in India without the consent of the concerned State Government.
3. It is primarily a voluntary auxiliary force raised by the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
164.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Home Guards, not the NIA, are voluntary auxiliary forces under the States.
164.tq: Reject the statement that assigns an auxiliary-force role to an investigative agency.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: The **NIA** is under the **MHA** — correct.
Statement 2: It can investigate **scheduled offences anywhere without state consent** — correct.
Statement 3: The voluntary auxiliary force under the states is the **Home Guards** — wrong.
xa: The **NIA Act** came in **2008**, after **26/11**.
NIA's chargesheet against **Hafiz Saeed** (Pahalgam) cites **BNS, 2023** + **UAPA, 1967**.
Extended **NIA/BSF** reach is criticised as entering state subjects of police and public order.

164.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Security Guard (NSG):
1. It is an MHA counter-terror force popularly called the 'Black Cats'.
2. It played a key role in the 26/11 response.
3. It protects the Prime Minister and former Prime Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
164.x: Statement 1 is correct: NSG is the MHA counter-terror force known as Black Cats. Statement 2 is correct: it was key in the 26/11 response. Statement 3 is wrong: protecting the PM and former PMs is the SPG's role (SPG Act 1988). So 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
164.tq: NSG = counter-terror (Black Cats); SPG = PM protection.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: The **NSG** is the **MHA** counter-terror force, the **"Black Cats"** — correct.
Statement 2: It was key in the **26/11** response — correct.
Statement 3: Protecting the PM and former PMs is the **SPG**'s job — wrong.
xa: The **SPG** was set up in **1985**; **SPG Act 1988**.
The **NIA Act (2008)** also followed **26/11**.
**NATGRID** (MHA) is to be widened under the counter-terror policy.

164.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Home Guards — voluntary auxiliary force under the States
CERT-In — Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Internal Security Academy — CRPF, Mount Abu
164.x: NATGRID is an intelligence grid under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Ministry of External Affairs. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
164.tq: Use the parent-ministry trap to identify the incorrectly matched institution.
xs: **NATGRID — Ministry of External Affairs** is wrong: **NATGRID** is an **MHA** intelligence grid — option **(4)**.
**Home Guards – states**, **CERT-In – MeitY**, **Internal Security Academy – CRPF, Mount Abu** are correct.
xa: NATGRID is to be **expanded** under the **National Counter-Terrorism Policy** (**Dec 2025**).
⚠ **IB** = MHA; **RAW** = Cabinet Secretariat; **CERT-In** = MeitY.
The **MHA** sets policy for Home Guards.

164.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS):
1. The CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs.
2. The CDS is the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.
3. The CDS is military adviser to the Nuclear Command Authority.
4. The CDS is the principal military adviser to the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
164.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs, is Permanent Chairman of the COSC and military adviser to the Nuclear Command Authority. Statement 4 is wrong: the CDS is principal military adviser to the Defence Minister, not the Prime Minister. So A; B, C and D include statement 4.
164.tq: CDS advises the Defence Minister (and the NCA), not the PM directly.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statements 1-3: The **CDS** heads the **Department of Military Affairs**, is **Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee**, and military adviser to the **Nuclear Command Authority**.
Statement 4: The CDS is **principal military adviser to the Defence Minister**, not the PM — wrong.
xa: Post created **Dec 2019**; first CDS **Gen Bipin Rawat** (**1 Jan 2020**).
Age limit: **65**.
The Department of Military Affairs sits in the **MoD**.

164.s: Who became India's first Chief of Defence Staff on 1 January 2020?
164.x: Gen Bipin Rawat became the first CDS on 1 January 2020, after the post was created in December 2019. Naravane, Dalbir Singh and V.K. Singh were Army Chiefs but not the first CDS.
164.tq: CDS: post created Dec 2019; first CDS Bipin Rawat from 1 Jan 2020; age limit 65.
xs: **Gen Bipin Rawat** became the first **CDS** on **1 Jan 2020** — option **(2)**.
The post was created in **Dec 2019**.
xa: The CDS heads the **Department of Military Affairs** (MoD).
The CDS advises the **Nuclear Command Authority**.
Age limit: **65**.

164.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. ULFA — Assam
2. NSCN — Nagaland
3. Lashkar-e-Taiba — Pakistan
4. People's War Group — Andhra Pradesh
164.x: All four group-base pairs are correct. ULFA is based in Assam, NSCN in Nagaland, Lashkar-e-Taiba in Pakistan and the People's War Group in Andhra Pradesh.
164.tq: Verify each organisation against its base before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**ULFA – Assam**, **NSCN – Nagaland**, **Lashkar-e-Taiba – Pakistan**, **People's War Group – Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: **LeT** = **Hafiz Saeed**; proxy **The Resistance Front (TRF)**.
**PWG** (**1980**, **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah**) merged into **CPI (Maoist)** in **2004**.
**NSCN** (**1980**) demands **"Greater Nagaland"**.

164.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: ULFA — Paresh Baruah and Arabinda Rajkhowa
NSCN — Isak Chishi Swu, Th. Muivah and S.S. Khaplang
164.x: Lashkar-e-Taiba is associated with Hafiz Saeed. Masood Azhar is associated with Jaish-e-Mohammed.
164.tq: Separate the founders or leaders of two Pakistan-based terrorist organisations.
xs: **Lashkar-e-Taiba — Masood Azhar** is wrong: **LeT** = **Hafiz Saeed** — option **(4)**.
**Masood Azhar** heads **Jaish-e-Mohammed**.
**ULFA – Paresh Baruah, Arabinda Rajkhowa** and **NSCN – Isak Chishi Swu, Th. Muivah, S.S. Khaplang** are correct.
xa: LeT's proxy is **The Resistance Front (TRF)**.

Both **LeT** and **JeM** are based in **Pakistan**.

164.s:
Consider the following statements about the People's War Group:

2. It was based in Andhra Pradesh.
3. It merged into the CPI (Maoist) in 1995.

164.x: Statement 1 is correct: PWG was founded in 1980 by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah. Statement 2 is correct: it was based in Andhra Pradesh. Statement 3 is wrong: it merged into the CPI (Maoist) in 2004. So 1 and 2 only (B); A omits statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
164.tq: PWG 1980 -> CPI (Maoist) 2004.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **PWG** was founded in **1980** by **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah** — correct.
Statement 2: It was based in **Andhra Pradesh** — correct.
Statement 3: It merged into **CPI (Maoist)** in **2004**, not 1995 — wrong.
xa: AP's anti-Naxal force **Greyhounds** was raised in **1989**, based at **Anandapuram** (Visakhapatnam).
