xa: ⚠ **2015** = PMKSY + Soil Health Card; **2016** = PMFBY + e-NAM.
**PM-PRANAM** (**2023**) aims to cut chemical fertiliser use.
**e-NAM** (April **2016**) lead agency is **SFAC**.

166.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
166.x: NREP was introduced in 1980, not 1983. RLEGP was introduced in 1983.
166.tq: Find the single scheme-year mismatch among otherwise familiar chronology pairs.
xs: **NREP — 1983** is wrong: NREP began in **1980** — option **(1)** is the mismatched pair.
**RLEGP — 1983** is correct; **IRDP** dates from **1978-79** (nationwide **1980**).
xa: **JRY (1989)** merged **NREP and RLEGP**.
RLEGP gave employment to **landless households**.
IRDP was a **Sixth Plan** self-employment scheme; later merged into **SGSY**.

166.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the lineage of rural self-employment programmes is correct?
o: NRLM was formed by merging NREP and RLEGP in 1989.
DAY-NRLM was renamed as SGSY in 2011.
NRLM was restructured from SGSY and was renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016.
SGSY was restructured from NRLM and renamed in 1999.
166.x: NRLM was restructured from SGSY in 2011 and was renamed Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission in 2016.
166.tq: Trace the direction of scheme succession carefully; do not reverse predecessor and successor.
xs: **NRLM** was restructured from **SGSY** in **2011** and renamed **DAY-NRLM** in **2016** — option **(3)**.
**JRY** (**1989**), not NRLM, merged **NREP and RLEGP**.
**SGSY** (**1 April 1999**) came before NRLM, so options (2) and (4) reverse the lineage.
xa: SGSY merged **IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA** and allied schemes.
DAY-NRLM sub-schemes: **SVEP, AGEY, MKSP, DDU-GKY, RSETIs**.
**Lakhpati Didi** target: **3 crore women**.

166.s: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), which merged IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA and allied schemes, started on:
166.x: SGSY started on 1 April 1999 by merging IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA and allied schemes (some keys, including APPSC 2025, give 1995). 1989 is JRY, 1993 is EAS, and 2011 is when NRLM was restructured from SGSY.
166.tq: SGSY = 1 April 1999 (learn 1999; recognise 1995 if it is the key's option).
xs: **SGSY** started on **1 April 1999** — option **(3)**.
It merged **IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA** and allied schemes.
**1989** = **JRY**; **1993** = **EAS**; **2011** = NRLM restructured from SGSY.
xa: ⚠ The **APPSC 2025** key gave SGSY as **1995**; learn **1999** but recognise the key's option.
NRLM was renamed **DAY-NRLM** in **2016**.

166.s: Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) was formed by merging:
166.x: JRY (1989) merged NREP (1980) and RLEGP (1983). IRDP and TRYSEM went into SGSY (1999); EAS and JGSY formed SGRY (2001); DWCRA was also merged into SGSY.
166.tq: JRY 1989 = NREP + RLEGP; SGRY 2001 = EAS + JGSY; SGSY 1999 = IRDP + TRYSEM + DWCRA.
xs: **JRY (1989)** merged **NREP and RLEGP** — option **(2)**.
**IRDP and TRYSEM** went into **SGSY**; **EAS and JGSY** formed **SGRY (2001)**.
xa: SGSY started **1 April 1999** (with DWCRA also merged).
**VB-G RAM G** now replaces **MGNREGA**.

166.s: With reference to the employment guarantee framework in rural areas, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: VB-G RAM G — 100 days of work per household per year
MGNREGA — 100 days of unskilled manual work per household per year
VB-G RAM G — 75 days of skilled work per household per year
MGNREGA — 125 days of work per household per year
166.x: MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days of unskilled manual work per household per year, whereas VB-G RAM G provides a 125-day guarantee.
166.tq: Use the comparison table to distinguish the changed numerical guarantee.
xs: **MGNREGA** guaranteed **100 days** of unskilled manual work per household per year — option **(2)**.
**VB-G RAM G** guarantees **125 days**, so options (1), (3) and (4) mix up the two.
xa: MGNREGA is **repealed**; VB-G RAM G in force from **1 July 2026**.
MGNREGA: **one-third** of workers women; **Gram Sabha** ran the social audit.
VB-G RAM G is implemented by **Panchayati Raj Institutions**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements regarding VB-G RAM G:
1. It replaces MGNREGA.
2. It provides a guarantee of 125 days of work per household.
3. It is implemented by Panchayati Raj Institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
166.x: All three statements are correct. VB-G RAM G replaces MGNREGA, raises the guarantee to 125 days and is implemented through Panchayati Raj Institutions.
166.tq: Check each statement against the status, guarantee and implementing-body rows.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**VB-G RAM G** replaces **MGNREGA** and guarantees **125 days**.
It is implemented by **Panchayati Raj Institutions**.
xa: Funding: CSS **60:40**, NE/Himalayan **90:10**, UT without legislature **100%**.
Total **₹1,51,282 crore**; Centre **₹95,692.31 crore**.
Tagline: **"Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi"**.
AP Budget **2026-27** allotted **₹8,365 crore** to it.

166.s:
Arrange the following events relating to VB-G RAM G in chronological order:
A. The Act came into force
B. The Act was introduced
C. Presidential assent was given
D. The Act was notified
166.x: The sequence is introduction on 16 December 2025, assent on 20 December 2025, notification on 11 May 2026 and commencement on 1 July 2026.
166.tq: Fix the first and last dates, then arrange the intermediate milestones.
xs: Order **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)**.
Introduced **16 Dec 2025** → Presidential assent **20 Dec 2025** → notified **11 May 2026** → in force **1 July 2026**.
The Act was passed within **two days** of its introduction.
xa: It guarantees **125 days**, replacing MGNREGA's **100 days**.
**Section 4(5)**: Centre fixes state-wise normative allocations; rules pending as of **Mar 2026**.
Unemployment allowance and delay compensation now **borne fully by states**.

166.s: VB-G RAM G is the abbreviated form of:
o: Viksit Bharat—Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
Viksit Bharat—Gram Rozgar and Awas Mission
Viksit Bharat—Gramin Rehabilitation and Manufacturing Mission
Village Bharat—Guarantee for Rural Agriculture and Migration
166.x: VB-G RAM G stands for Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin).
166.tq: Test the exact expansion of the scheme acronym.
xs: **VB-G RAM G** = **Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)** — option **(1)**.
It replaces **MGNREGA** with a **125-day** guarantee.
xa: Tagline: **"Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi"**.
It is a **Centrally Sponsored** scheme (**60:40**).
In force from **1 July 2026**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about unemployment allowance:
1. Under MGNREGA, it was payable if work was not given within 15 days.
2. Under VB-G RAM G, the allowance and delay compensation are borne fully by the Centre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under VB-G RAM G the allowance and delay compensation are borne fully by the States. So '1 only'.
166.tq: Allowance cost falls on States.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: under **MGNREGA**, allowance was due if no work within **15 days** (paid by states).
Statement 2 is wrong: under **VB-G RAM G**, allowance and delay compensation are **borne fully by states**, not the Centre.
xa: Criticism: **States now bear unemployment allowance**.
Debate: **normative allocation formula vs demand-driven funding**.
MGNREGA material cost was shared **75:25**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about MGNREGA:
1. One-third of workers had to be women.
2. The Gram Sabha ran the social audit.
3. It is linked to SDG 1 and SDG 5.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: MGNREGA links to SDG 1 (No Poverty) and SDG 8 (Decent Work). So '1 and 2 only'.
166.tq: Work = SDG 8.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **one-third** of workers had to be **women**.
Statement 2: the **Gram Sabha** ran the **social audit**.
Statement 3 is wrong: MGNREGA links to **SDG 1** (No Poverty) and **SDG 8** (Decent Work), not SDG 5.
xa: Guarantee: **100 days** of unskilled manual work per household per year.
MGNREGA is now **repealed**, replaced by **VB-G RAM G** (**125 days**).
CAG audit: planned **Green India Mission-MGNREGS** convergence not achieved.

166.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Council for Land Reforms, set up in 2008, is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. DILRMP began as NLRMP in 2008.
3. DILRMP became a Central Sector scheme in 2020.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: DILRMP became a Central Sector scheme in 2016. So '1 and 2 only'.
166.tq: 2008 for both NCLR and NLRMP; Central Sector from 2016.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **National Council for Land Reforms** (**2008**) is chaired by the **Prime Minister**.
Statement 2: **DILRMP** began as **NLRMP** in **2008**.
Statement 3 is wrong: DILRMP became **Central Sector** in **2016**, not 2020.
xa: **DILRMP 3.0** guidelines have been issued.
**SVAMITVA** (**24 Apr 2020**): drone survey of village houses + property cards.
⚠ **2020** = SVAMITVA, not the DILRMP change.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana:
1. It is under the Ministry of Rural Development.
2. It was launched on 11 October 2014, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 11 October is Jayaprakash Narayan's birth anniversary. So '1 only'.
166.tq: SAGY date = JP Narayan's birthday, 11 Oct.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **SAGY** is under the **Ministry of Rural Development**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **11 Oct 2014** is **Jayaprakash Narayan's** birth anniversary.
xa: Under SAGY each **MP** develops model gram panchayats.
**MPLADS (1993)** is run by **MoSPI**, not MoRD.
MPLADS earmarks **15% for SC** + **7.5% for ST** areas.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about MPLADS:
1. It is administered by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
2. Its funds are non-lapsable.
3. Members of Parliament recommend works, while the district authority executes them.
4. It earmarks 15 per cent for SC areas and 7.5 per cent for ST areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
166.x: All four statements correctly describe MPLADS: MoSPI administers it, funds are non-lapsable, MPs recommend works, district authorities execute them, and the specified SC/ST earmarks apply.
166.tq: Verify administration, fund character, division of roles and earmarking as separate features.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**MPLADS (1993)** is run by **MoSPI**; funds are **non-lapsable**.
**MPs only recommend** works; the **district authority executes**.
Earmark: **15% for SC** + **7.5% for ST** areas.
xa: **SAGY** (**11 Oct 2014**) is under **MoRD**: each MP develops model gram panchayats.
⚠ MPLADS = **MoSPI**; SAGY = **Rural Development**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about DAY-NRLM:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Ministry of Rural Development.
2. Funding is 60:40, and 90:10 for North-Eastern States including Sikkim.
3. Union Territories fund it entirely from their own resources.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: UTs get 100% Central funding. So '1 and 2 only'.
166.tq: UTs = 100% Centre in CSS norms.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **DAY-NRLM** is a **Centrally Sponsored** scheme of **MoRD**.
Statement 2: funding **60:40**; NE incl. Sikkim **90:10**.
Statement 3 is wrong: UTs get **100% Centre** funding.
xa: An older quiz says **75:25** — the original NRLM ratio.
**Delhi** and **Chandigarh** are excluded.
Implemented via **State Rural Livelihood Missions**.

166.s: The target under the Lakhpati Didi initiative is to enable how many women to earn more than ₹1 lakh a year?
166.x: The Lakhpati Didi target is three crore women earning more than ₹1 lakh annually.
166.tq: Distinguish the livelihood-income target from the wider DAY-NRLM membership figure.
xs: **Lakhpati Didi** targets **3 crore women** earning over **₹1 lakh** a year — option **(3)**.
It is part of **DAY-NRLM** (MoRD).
xa: DAY-NRLM has **9 lakh+** Community Resource Persons (2025-26).
Funding: **60:40**; NE incl. Sikkim **90:10**.
NRLM came in **2011**, renamed DAY-NRLM in **2016**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements about SVAMITVA:
1. It is a scheme of the Ministry of Rural Development.
2. It uses drone surveys of village houses and gives property cards.
3. It was launched on 24 April 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
166.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: SVAMITVA is under the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (24 April is National Panchayati Raj Day). So '2 and 3 only'.
166.tq: SVAMITVA = Panchayati Raj ministry.
xs: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 2: **drone survey** of village houses and **property cards**.
Statement 3: launched on **24 Apr 2020**.
Statement 1 is wrong: SVAMITVA is under the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**, not Rural Development.
xa: **DILRMP** began as NLRMP (**2008**); Central Sector in **2016**.
**National Council for Land Reforms** (**2008**) is chaired by the **Prime Minister**.

166.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. PM Vishwakarma — Ministry of MSME
2. PM-AJAY — Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
3. PM SVANidhi — Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
4. PMEGP — Khadi and Village Industries Commission as nodal agency
166.x: All four pairs are correct. PM Vishwakarma is under MSME, PM-AJAY under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, PM SVANidhi under MoHUA, and KVIC is the nodal agency for PMEGP.
166.tq: Use institution–scheme matching and eliminate options containing a swapped ministry.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**PM Vishwakarma** (**2023**) → **Ministry of MSME**; **PM-AJAY** (2021-22) → **MoSJE**.
**PM SVANidhi** (**2020**) → **MoHUA** (with **SIDBI**); **PMEGP** (**2008**) → nodal **KVIC**.
xa: PM SVANidhi: first loan **₹10,000**, **7% interest subsidy**, **75 lakh+** vendors.
PM-AJAY's **Adarsh Gram**: villages with **500+** people and over **40%** SC, **₹20 lakh** per village.
PM Vishwakarma: **24.50 lakh** craftspeople trained and given credit.

166.s: Which one of the following is NOT a benefit associated with PM Vishwakarma?
o: Collateral-free credit up to ₹3 lakh at 5 per cent interest
Working-capital loans beginning at ₹10,000 for street vendors
166.x: The ₹10,000 working-capital loan is associated with PM SVANidhi. PM Vishwakarma provides the stipend, toolkit support and collateral-free credit mentioned in the other options.
166.tq: Find the benefit belonging to the neighbouring scheme rather than the target scheme.
xs: **Working-capital loans from ₹10,000 for street vendors** are **PM SVANidhi**, not PM Vishwakarma — option **(3)**.
PM Vishwakarma gives a **₹500/day** stipend, toolkit up to **₹15,000** and credit up to **₹3 lakh at 5%**.
xa: PM SVANidhi (**2020**, **MoHUA**, **SIDBI**): **7% interest subsidy**, digital cashback.
PM Vishwakarma covers **18 traditional trades**; **24.50 lakh** craftspeople trained and given credit.
PM Vishwakarma is under the **Ministry of MSME** (**2023**).

166.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-AJAY:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of MoSJE for development of SC-majority villages.
2. Its Adarsh Gram component covers villages with 500+ people and over 40% SC population.
3. Its Adarsh Gram component was formerly known as HRIDAY.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Adarsh Gram component was formerly PMAGY (2009-10). So '1 and 2 only'.
166.tq: Adarsh Gram = old PMAGY; HRIDAY is a heritage-city scheme.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **PM-AJAY** (**2021-22**) is a **CSS** of **MoSJE** for SC-majority villages.
Statement 2: **Adarsh Gram** covers villages with **500+** people and over **40%** SC.
Statement 3 is wrong: Adarsh Gram was formerly **PMAGY** (**2009-10**); **HRIDAY** is unrelated (Amaravati is in HRIDAY).
xa: Adarsh Gram grant: **₹20 lakh per village**.
**47,300** villages covered; **16,700** declared Adarsh Grams.

166.s: PM SVANidhi is associated with which of the following?
o: Loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for greenfield enterprises
Loans to street vendors, including a first loan of ₹10,000 and a 7 per cent interest subsidy
Loans to artisans up to ₹3 lakh at 5 per cent interest
166.x: PM SVANidhi supports street vendors through working-capital loans; the first loan is ₹10,000 and the scheme provides a 7 per cent interest subsidy and digital cashback.
166.tq: Separate similar credit schemes by beneficiary, initial loan and interest support.
xs: **PM SVANidhi** gives loans to **street vendors**: first loan **₹10,000**, **7% interest subsidy** — option **(2)**.
Loans up to **₹3 lakh at 5%** for artisans are **PM Vishwakarma**; SC-majority villages are **PM-AJAY**.
xa: PM SVANidhi: **2020**, **MoHUA**, **SIDBI**; digital cashback.
**75 lakh+** vendors covered.
**DAY-NULM** also supports street vendors among the urban poor.

166.s: PM Vishwakarma (2023, Ministry of MSME) is NOT meant for which of the following?
o: Craftspeople needing collateral-free credit up to Rs 3 lakh
Artisans receiving a toolkit up to Rs 15,000
166.x: PM Vishwakarma covers artisans and craftspeople in 18 traditional trades with an ID card, Rs 500/day training stipend, toolkit up to Rs 15,000 and collateral-free credit up to Rs 3 lakh at 5%. It is not for fishermen with non-mechanised boats (the APPSC 2023 trap), so C is the answer; A, B and D are features of the scheme.
166.tq: PM Vishwakarma: 18 trades, MSME; not fishermen (APPSC 2023 trap).
xs: PM Vishwakarma is **not** for **fishermen with non-mechanised boats** — option **(3)**, the **APPSC 2023** trap.
It covers artisans in **18 traditional trades** with toolkit up to **₹15,000** and credit up to **₹3 lakh at 5%**.
xa: Training carries a **₹500/day** stipend; artisans get an ID card.
**24.50 lakh** craftspeople trained and given credit (Jul **2026**).
PM Vishwakarma is a **Central Sector** scheme.

166.s: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs was formed in 2017 by merging which two ministries?
o: Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation and Urban Development
Housing and Finance and Urban Development
Social Justice and Housing and Urban Affairs
166.x: MoHUA was formed in 2017 by merging the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation with the Ministry of Urban Development.
166.tq: Test the exact predecessor ministries rather than a related ministry.
xs: **MoHUA (2017)** merged **Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation** with **Urban Development** — option **(1)**.
**Rural Development** remains a separate ministry (it runs DAY-NRLM and SAGY).
xa: MoHUA runs **PM SVANidhi**, **Urban Challenge Fund** and **SBM-Urban 2.0**.
**DAY-NULM** serves the urban poor (SHGs, shelters, street vendors).
**AP angle**: **Amaravati** is in **HRIDAY**.

166.s: In June 2023, DAY-NULM entered into a partnership with which organisation to empower women?
166.x: DAY-NULM partnered with UNDP in June 2023 to empower women (APPSC 2023). The World Bank backs Atal Bhujal and SANKALP; UN-Habitat and ADB are distractors.
166.tq: DAY-NULM + UNDP (June 2023) = women's empowerment.
xs: **DAY-NULM** partnered with **UNDP** in **June 2023** to empower **women** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2023**).
The **World Bank** backs **Atal Bhujal Yojana** and **SANKALP**, not DAY-NULM.
xa: DAY-NULM serves the urban poor: **SHGs**, skilled wage and self-employment, **shelters for the homeless**, **street vendors**.
Its rural counterpart is **DAY-NRLM** (**Lakhpati Didi**: **3 crore** women).
MoHUA was formed in **2017**.

166.s: Which one of the following urban programmes is correctly matched with its objective?
o: Smart Cities Mission - 10,000 e-buses on PPP
AMRUT 2.0 - tap water to all households in statutory towns
166.x: AMRUT 2.0 (2021) aims at tap water to all households in statutory towns and sewerage in AMRUT cities. The Smart Cities Mission covers 100 cities, PM e-Bus Sewa provides 10,000 e-buses, and SBM-Urban 2.0 targets garbage-free cities, so A, C and D are mismatched.
166.tq: Smart Cities 100 cities; AMRUT 2.0 tap water; SBM-U 2.0 garbage-free; e-Bus Sewa 10,000 buses.
xs: **AMRUT 2.0 (2021)** aims at **tap water to all households in statutory towns** — option **(2)**.
**10,000 e-buses** on PPP is **PM e-Bus Sewa**, not Smart Cities.
Tech-led transformation of **100 cities** is the **Smart Cities Mission**, not SBM-Urban 2.0.
**Garbage-free cities** is **SBM-Urban 2.0**, not PM e-Bus Sewa.
xa: AMRUT 2.0 also provides **sewerage in AMRUT cities**.
Smart Cities Mission dates from **2015**; PM e-Bus Sewa from **2023**.
SBM-Urban 2.0 was halved to **₹2,500 crore** in Budget **2026-27**.

166.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Skill India Mission was launched in 2015 with PMKVY as its flagship for short-term training and certification.
2. The nodal ministry for Skill India and PMKVY is the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
3. PMKVY 1.0 was launched in 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
166.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: PMKVY 1.0 was launched in 2015 (later versions 2.0, 3.0, 4.0). So '1 and 2 only'.
166.tq: Skill India and PMKVY 1.0 both 2015.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Skill India Mission (2015)**'s flagship is **PMKVY** (short-term training + certification).
Statement 2: nodal ministry is **MSDE**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **PMKVY 1.0** came in **2015**, not 2016.
xa: **Skill India Digital Hub** is MSDE's digital platform (**2023**).
**SANKALP** is a **World Bank**-supported MSDE programme.

166.s: SANKALP is best described as a:
o: MoHUA programme providing e-buses to cities
MoRD programme providing self-employment through rural industrial estates
World Bank-supported MSDE programme strengthening district-level skilling institutions
Central Sector scheme providing toolkit grants to artisans
166.x: SANKALP is a World Bank-supported programme of MSDE intended to strengthen district-level skilling institutions.
166.tq: Identify the programme through its international support, ministry and institutional objective.
xs: **SANKALP** is a **World Bank**-supported **MSDE** programme strengthening **district-level skilling institutions** — option **(3)**.
E-buses are **PM e-Bus Sewa** (MoHUA); artisan toolkits are **PM Vishwakarma**.
xa: The **World Bank** also assists **Atal Bhujal Yojana**.
MSDE's other platform: **Skill India Digital Hub** (**2023**).
**Jan Shikshan Sansthan** trained **36.52 lakh**.

166.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two skilling programmes of the Ministry of Rural Development?
o: DDU-GKY provides artisan toolkits, while RSETIs provide e-buses.
DDU-GKY is placement-linked for rural youth, while RSETIs focus on self-employment.
DDU-GKY focuses on urban street vendors, while RSETIs provide heritage conservation.
DDU-GKY is a World Bank programme, while RSETIs are run by MoHUA.
166.x: DDU-GKY is a placement-linked programme for rural youth, whereas RSETIs are associated with self-employment.
166.tq: Discriminate between two programmes under the same ministry by their livelihood pathway.
xs: **DDU-GKY** is **placement-linked skilling for rural youth**, while **RSETIs** focus on **self-employment** — option **(2)**.
Both are **MoRD** programmes and DAY-NRLM sub-schemes, not World Bank or MoHUA.
xa: Other DAY-NRLM sub-schemes: **SVEP, AGEY, MKSP**.
**SANKALP** is the World Bank-supported MSDE programme.
**PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana**: **₹2,400 crore** to **15 lakh** first-time employees.

166.s: Which one of the following is a Central Sector scheme?
166.x: PM Vishwakarma is listed as a Central Sector scheme funded and run centrally. DAY-NRLM, PMAY-G and PM-AJAY are Centrally Sponsored examples.
166.tq: Separate Central Sector schemes from Centrally Sponsored schemes using the funding pattern.
xs: **PM Vishwakarma** is a **Central Sector** scheme (**100% Centre**, run centrally) — option **(4)**.
**PMAY-G, PM-AJAY and DAY-NRLM** are **Centrally Sponsored** (shared funding).
xa: Other Central Sector examples: **PM-KISAN**, **DILRMP** (since **2016**), **SEED**.
CSS norm: **60:40**; **90:10** NE/Himalayan; **100%** UTs without legislature.
PM Vishwakarma (**2023**) is under the **Ministry of MSME**.

166.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: DAY-NRLM, VB-G RAM G, PMAY-G and PM-AJAY
SEED, PM Vishwakarma and Urban Challenge Fund only
166.x: DAY-NRLM, VB-G RAM G, PMAY-G and PM-AJAY are listed as Centrally Sponsored Schemes. PM-KISAN, PM Vishwakarma, DILRMP and SEED are Central Sector examples, while the Urban Challenge Fund is also Centrally Sponsored.
166.tq: Classify the entire group rather than relying on one familiar scheme.
xs: **DAY-NRLM, VB-G RAM G, PMAY-G and PM-AJAY** are all **Centrally Sponsored** — option **(2)**.

167.tq: UDAY = DISCOM debt; UJALA = LED.
xs: **UDAY** (**2015**, Power) aimed at the **financial turnaround of DISCOMs**, with **states taking over DISCOM debt** — option **(2)**.
LED bulbs via **EESL** = **UJALA**; LPG subsidy transfer = **PAHAL**; solar pumps = **PM-KUSUM**.
xa: ⚠ **UJALA** and **UDAY** are both **Power, 2015**.
Criticism: **DISCOM finances still need scheme support**.
**REC** handles DDUGJY and Saubhagya.

167.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Aadhaar is a 12-digit number and was started in 2009.
2. UIDAI works under the Aadhaar Act, 2016, which was amended in 2019.
3. UIDAI works under the National Food Security Act, 2013.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
167.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: UIDAI is governed by the Aadhaar Act, 2016, not the NFSA. So '1 and 2 only'.
167.tq: Aadhaar: 2009 start, 2016 Act, 2019 amendment.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Aadhaar** is a **12-digit** number, started **2009**.
Statement 2: **UIDAI** works under the **Aadhaar Act, 2016**, amended **2019**.
Statement 3 is wrong: UIDAI is not under the NFSA.
xa: Aadhaar is part of India's **DPI backbone** with BharatNet, 5G, UPI, DigiYatra, FASTag.
The 12-digit fact was asked in **APPSC 2023**.
**Digital India** began on **1 July 2015**, coordinated by **MeitY**.

167.s: The Digital India programme rests on how many pillars?
167.x: Digital India rests on nine pillars, extending from Broadband Highways to Early Harvest.
167.tq: Test the exact count and use the named range as a confirmation clue.
xs: **Digital India** rests on **9 pillars** — option **(1) Nine**.
They run from **Broadband Highways** to **Early Harvest**, incl. universal mobile access and public internet access.
xa: Launched **1 July 2015**; coordinated by **MeitY**.
Central Sector sub-schemes: **e-Governance, National Knowledge Network, cyber security, IndiaAI Mission**.
**BharatNet** began as **NOFN**.

167.s: Which of the following correctly describes BharatNet?
o: A scheme for providing satellite television to all villages
A scheme for providing optical-fibre broadband to all gram panchayats
A programme for manufacturing semiconductor chips
167.x: BharatNet aims to provide optical-fibre broadband connectivity to all gram panchayats.
167.tq: Match the programme with its distinctive infrastructure objective.
xs: **BharatNet** gives **optical-fibre broadband to all gram panchayats** — option **(2)**.
Digital commerce = **ONDC**; semiconductor chips = **India Semiconductor Mission**.
xa: BharatNet began as **NOFN**.
Rural gaps: **weak fibre upkeep + power cuts** at GP level.
BharatNet is part of the **DPI backbone**.

167.s: Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is promoted by:
167.x: ONDC is an open network for digital commerce promoted by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
167.tq: Use the ‘who promotes it?’ approach to separate DPIIT from digital and financial agencies.
xs: **ONDC** is promoted by **DPIIT** — option **(3)**.
**MeitY** runs Digital India; **DoT** runs PM-WANI; **SIDBI** manages the startup Fund of Funds.
xa: ONDC scale: **20 crore** buyers + **5 lakh** sellers (15 Aug **2026**).
**NICDC** is also under **DPIIT**.
ONDC is an **open network for digital commerce**.

167.s: PM-WANI, launched in 2020, seeks to provide public Wi-Fi through:
o: PDOAs under the Department of Telecommunications
167.x: PM-WANI provides public Wi-Fi through Public Data Office Aggregators (PDOAs) and is associated with the Department of Telecommunications.
167.tq: Match the scheme with both its delivery mechanism and nodal department.
xs: **PM-WANI (2020)** gives public Wi-Fi through **PDOAs** under **DoT** — option **(2)**.
Gram panchayat broadband is **BharatNet**, not PM-WANI.
xa: **BharatNet** began as **NOFN**.
**5G** coverage nationwide (2025-26).
**Digital India** pillars include **public internet access**.

167.s: Digital India was launched on:
167.x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015.
167.tq: Distinguish the exact launch date from other major national programme dates.
xs: **Digital India** was launched on **1 July 2015** — option **(2)**.
It is coordinated by **MeitY**.
xa: **APPSC 2025** key: Digital India-**2015**, Make in India-**2014**, Startup India-**2016**, Atmanirbhar-**2020**.
Digital India has **9 pillars**, from Broadband Highways to Early Harvest.
**MUDRA** also dates from **2015**.

167.s:
Consider the following statements about the IndiaAI Mission:
1. It was approved in March 2024.
2. Its approved outlay is about Rs 10,372 crore.
3. It gives incentives for fabs, display and ATMP units.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
167.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: fabs, display and ATMP incentives belong to the India Semiconductor Mission; IndiaAI covers compute, datasets and AI innovation. So '1 and 2 only'.
167.tq: IndiaAI = compute and data; ISM = chips.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **IndiaAI Mission** was approved in **March 2024**.
Statement 2: outlay about **Rs 10,372 crore**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **fabs, display and ATMP** incentives belong to the **India Semiconductor Mission (2021)**.
xa: IndiaAI covers **compute, datasets and AI innovation**; a **Digital India** sub-scheme.
It is expanding **compute, data-centre capacity, HPC** (1 Jul **2026**).
India Semiconductor Mission is under **MeitY**.

167.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. SIDBI — MUDRA refinance
2. SIDBI — Fund of Funds for Startups
3. IREDA — renewable-energy financing
4. NHAI — Bharatmala highways
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
167.x: SIDBI is associated with MUDRA refinance and the Fund of Funds for Startups; IREDA is the renewable-energy financing arm; and NHAI is associated with Bharatmala highways.
167.tq: Match agencies with their schemes and watch for authority-swapping traps.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**SIDBI** handles **MUDRA refinance** and the **Fund of Funds for Startups**.
**IREDA** is MNRE's **renewable-energy financing** arm; **NHAI** builds **Bharatmala** (MoRTH).
xa: SIDBI is also linked to **PM SVANidhi**.
The startup Fund of Funds is **₹10,000 crore**.
**NICDC** (under **DPIIT**) handles industrial corridors and smart industrial cities.

167.s: NICDC is associated with:
o: Industrial corridors and smart industrial cities under DPIIT
Rural electrification under the Ministry of Power
167.x: NICDC is associated with industrial corridors and smart industrial cities under DPIIT.
167.tq: Distinguish the industrial-corridor agency from financing and electrification agencies.
xs: **NICDC** handles **industrial corridors and smart industrial cities** under **DPIIT** — option **(3)**.
RE finance is **IREDA**; startup loans/funds are **SIDBI**; rural electrification is **REC** (DDUGJY, Saubhagya).
xa: **ONDC** is also promoted by **DPIIT**.
AP has **three industrial corridors** (VCIC with **ADB**).
AP corridor nodes: **Krishnapatnam, Orvakal, Kopparthy**.

167.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. EESL — UJALA
2. REC — DDUGJY and Saubhagya
3. KVIC — PMEGP
4. KVIC — Solar Charkha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
167.x: EESL implements UJALA and REC is the nodal agency for DDUGJY and Saubhagya, while KVIC is associated with PMEGP and Solar Charkha.
167.tq: Group multiple agency–scheme pairs and verify each before selecting the code.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**EESL** → **UJALA**; **REC** → **DDUGJY and Saubhagya**.
**KVIC** → **PMEGP** and **Solar Charkha**.
xa: **UJALA** (Power, **2015**) supplies LED bulbs and efficient appliances.
**Solar Charkha Mission** (**2018**, MSME) builds solar spinning and weaving clusters.
**IREDA** is MNRE's renewable-energy financing arm.

167.s:
Arrange the following schemes in chronological order of their launch:
A. Startup India
B. Make in India
C. Atmanirbhar Bharat
D. Digital India
167.x: Make in India was launched in 2014, Digital India in 2015, Startup India in 2016 and Atmanirbhar Bharat in 2020.
167.tq: Fix the earliest and latest schemes first, then order the two middle years.
xs: Order **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
**Make in India** (**25 Sept 2014**) → **Digital India** (**1 July 2015**) → **Startup India** (**16 Jan 2016**) → **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (May **2020**).
xa: This matches the **APPSC 2025** key.
**MUDRA** (**April 2015**) and **Stand-Up India** (**2016**) fall in the same window.
**PAHAL**: **Nov 2014**, nationwide **Jan 2015**.

167.s: Which of the following sets consists of industrial-corridor nodes in Andhra Pradesh?
167.x: Krishnapatnam, Orvakal and Kopparthy are the AP industrial-corridor nodes. Kandla, Paradip and Tuticorin are NGHM hydrogen hubs; Dadri, JNPT and Ludhiana are on the Dedicated Freight Corridors; Sonnagar and Dankuni are Eastern DFC termini and Haldia is a port in West Bengal.
167.tq: AP nodes: K-O-K (Krishnapatnam, Orvakal, Kopparthy).
xs: AP industrial-corridor nodes: **Krishnapatnam, Orvakal and Kopparthy** — option **(1)**.
**Kandla, Paradip, Tuticorin** = **NGHM hydrogen hubs**.
**Dadri, JNPT, Ludhiana, Sonnagar, Dankuni** = **Dedicated Freight Corridor** termini.
xa: AP has **three industrial corridors** (**VCIC** with **ADB**).
Eastern DFC: Ludhiana-Sonnagar/Dankuni; Western DFC: Dadri-JNPT.
DFCs are built by **DFCCIL**.

168.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine pillars of Navaratnalu?
168.x: Navaratnalu included Jalayagnam, Pedalandariki Illu, and YSR Aasara/Cheyutha. Stree Shakti is a current Super Six guarantee, not one of the nine Navaratnalu pillars.
168.tq: Find the item belonging to the current guarantee package rather than the earlier nine-pillar programme.
xs: **Stree Shakti** is not a Navaratnalu pillar — option **(1)**; it is a current **Super Six** guarantee (free bus travel for women).
**Jalayagnam**, **Pedalandariki Illu** (housing) and **YSR Aasara/Cheyutha** are Navaratnalu pillars.
xa: Other pillars: **Rythu Bharosa, fee reimbursement, Aarogyasri, prohibition, Amma Vodi, pensions, Pension Kanuka**.
Navaratnalu (YSRCP, **2019**) was funded from **revenue expenditure**.
Stree Shakti was launched on **15 Aug 2025**.

168.s: Navaratnalu was associated with which period?
168.x: Navaratnalu was the nine-pillar welfare framework associated with the period 2019–2024.
168.tq: Discriminate between the programme period and the periods of other State initiatives.
xs: **Navaratnalu** belongs to **2019-24** — option **(3)**; it was the YSRCP government's package.
**2014-19** was the earlier **NTR Bharosa** pension era; the **present government** runs **Super Six**.
xa: Navaratnalu = **nine** flagship welfare promises, funded from **revenue expenditure**.
Cheyutha's name first belonged to a Naidu-era scheme (**1995-2004**).
CM Naidu reviewed Super Six at the **8th Collectors' Conference** (12 Sep **2026**).

168.s: The annual benefit under Rythu Bharosa, as specified for Andhra Pradesh, is:
168.x: AP’s Rythu Bharosa provides ₹13,500 a year per family, including tenants and ROFR holders. The ₹12,000 per acre figure belongs to Telangana’s Rythu Bharosa, while ₹20,000 is associated with its replacement, Annadata Sukhibhava.
168.tq: Trap a reversed State comparison and distinguish the replacement scheme.
xs: AP's **Rythu Bharosa** gave **₹13,500 a year per family** (Centre + State) — option **(4)**.
⚠ **₹12,000 an acre** is **Telangana's** Rythu Bharosa.
**₹20,000** belongs to its successor, **Annadata Sukhibhava**.
xa: Rythu Bharosa covered farmers including **tenants and ROFR holders**.
Annadata Sukhibhava = **₹14,000 State + ₹6,000 PM-KISAN**.
**₹10,000** a year was **Vahana Mitra**.

168.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vahana Mitra — ₹10,000 a year to auto and taxi owner-drivers
Matsyakara Bharosa — support during the fishing ban
Rythu Bharosa — ₹24,000 a year to handloom weavers
Nethanna Nestham — ₹24,000 a year to handloom weavers owning looms
168.x: ₹24,000 a year is the benefit mentioned for Nethanna Nestham, not Rythu Bharosa. Matsyakara Bharosa supports marine fishermen during the fishing ban, and Vahana Mitra was specified at ₹10,000 a year.
168.tq: Find the wrong beneficiary-benefit combination in a scheme table.
xs: **Rythu Bharosa — ₹24,000 to handloom weavers** is mismatched — option **(3)**.
**₹24,000** a year to loom-owning handloom weavers is **Nethanna Nestham**; Rythu Bharosa is for **farmers** (**₹13,500**).
**Vahana Mitra** (**₹10,000**) and **Matsyakara Bharosa** (fishing-ban relief) are correctly matched.
xa: ⚠ Telangana's Rythu Bharosa = **₹12,000** an acre.
Matsyakara Bharosa now pays **₹20,000** per family.
Rythu Bharosa → **Annadata Sukhibhava ₹20,000**.

168.s: Which of the following correctly describes Navaratnalu?
o: A self-help group movement based on community participation
A Five-Year Plan focused exclusively on industrial growth
The previous government’s welfare package funded from revenue expenditure
A current central index measuring inclusive development
168.x: Navaratnalu was the previous government’s welfare package and was funded from revenue expenditure.
168.tq: Identify the programme by its character and funding source.
xs: **Navaratnalu** was the **previous government's welfare package**, funded from **revenue expenditure** — option **(3)**.
It had **nine** flagship promises (**2019-24**).
xa: Revenue expenditure also funded **rice and power subsidies and pensions**.
Criticism: **"new welfarism"** favours DBT and tangible transfers over public goods.
Fiscal strain from debt of about **36%** of GSDP.

168.s: The stated objective of Talliki Vandanam is to reduce schooling costs and thereby improve the
168.x: Talliki Vandanam is intended to reduce the cost of schooling and raise the Gross Enrolment Ratio.
168.tq: Link the immediate welfare benefit with its stated educational outcome.
xs: **Talliki Vandanam** cuts schooling costs to raise the **Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER)** — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2025**).
It is an education scheme, so MMR, irrigation or labour-force indicators are not its stated target.
xa: It pays **₹15,000 per child per year** to the mother.
It replaced **Jagananna Amma Vodi** (launched **January 2020**).
AP Budget 2026-27: **Rs 8,456 crore**.
AP's **MMR (45)** and **IMR (24)** are better than national.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about the Stree Shakti scheme of Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was launched on 15 August 2025.
2. Free travel is available in all APSRTC bus categories without exception.
3. It was later extended to persons with disabilities.
4. Women's share of bus travel rose from 40% to 65%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct: Stree Shakti was launched on 15 August 2025, was later extended to PwD, and women's share of bus travel rose from 40% to 65%. Statement 2 is wrong: free travel covers 5 APSRTC bus categories, not all. So options with 2 (1 and 2 only; 2, 3 and 4 only; all four) are wrong.
168.tq: Remember '5 categories' - any 'all buses' claim is the trap.
xs: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 3 and 4 only**.
Statement 1: launched **15 Aug 2025**; statement 3: later extended to **PwD**.
Statement 4: women's share of bus travel rose **40% → 65%**.
Statement 2 is wrong: free travel covers **5 APSRTC bus categories**, not all.
xa: Beneficiaries: **women and transgender persons** with AP domicile.
**71 crore+** free journeys by 13 Jun **2026**.
Free bus travel for women was a **G2-GS 2025** key.

168.s: Matsyakara Bharosa provides support to marine fishermen during the fishing ban. The benefit was raised from:
168.x: The benefit under Matsyakara Bharosa was raised from ₹10,000 to ₹20,000 per family.
168.tq: Test the original and revised values together rather than either figure alone.
xs: **Matsyakara Bharosa** was raised from **₹10,000 to ₹20,000** per family — option **(2)**.
It supports **marine fishermen** during the seasonal fishing ban.
xa: ⚠ **₹20,000** = Annadata Sukhibhava (per farmer family) and Matsyakara Bharosa (per fisher family).
⚠ **₹15,000** = Talliki Vandanam and Auto Driver Sevalo.
**Fishermen** are also an **NTR Bharosa** pension category.

168.s: The Rs 20,000 annual benefit under Annadata Sukhibhava consists of:
o: Rs 10,000 each from the State and PM-KISAN
Rs 15,000 from the State and Rs 5,000 from PM-KISAN
Rs 14,000 from the State and Rs 6,000 from PM-KISAN
Rs 14,000 from PM-KISAN and Rs 6,000 from the State
168.x: The benefit comprises Rs 14,000 from the State and Rs 6,000 through PM-KISAN.
168.tq: Split a composite figure into its stated components.
xs: The **₹20,000** is **Rs 14,000 from the State + Rs 6,000 from PM-KISAN** — option **(3)**.
Option (4) reverses the two shares.
xa: Paid in **₹7,000 / ₹7,000 / ₹6,000** instalments.
Tenant farmers are included.

168.s: Deepam-2 provides which of the following benefits?
o: Three free LPG cylinders per year to 33.32 lakh families
Three free LPG cylinders per year to 83 lakh families
Two free LPG cylinders per year to 83 lakh families
One free LPG cylinder per month to all households
168.x: Deepam-2 provides three free LPG cylinders annually to 83 lakh families.
168.tq: Check the combination of benefit, frequency and coverage.
xs: **Deepam-2** gives **3 free LPG cylinders a year** to **83 lakh** families — option **(2)**.
**33.32** (crore) is the count of **Stree Shakti** trips, not Deepam families.
xa: Deepam-2 launched **2024**; about **2 crore** cylinders, **₹2,684 crore** (1 Jan **2026**).
Earlier **Deepam (1999)** gave LPG connections.
Deepam is part of **Super Six**.

168.s: The employment-related promise under the Super Six programme consists of
168.x: The promise is for 20 lakh jobs or an unemployment allowance of ₹3,000.
168.tq: Compare the paired job target and allowance amount as one combined promise.
xs: Super Six job promise: **20 lakh jobs** or **₹3,000** unemployment allowance — option **(2)**.
Tracked via **ITI and skill placements** (2024-25).
xa: **Aadabidda Nidhi**: **₹1,500** a month to women.
**Talliki Vandanam**: **₹15,000** per child per year.
Opposition: Super Six **only partly delivered**.

168.s: Which of the following correctly describes the change from YSR Vahana Mitra to Auto Driver Sevalo?
o: The scheme changed from annual assistance to free LPG cylinders.
The annual assistance increased from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000 for owners of self-owned autos.
The beneficiary changed from auto drivers to marine fishermen.
The annual assistance decreased from ₹15,000 to ₹10,000 for all transport workers.
168.x: YSR Vahana Mitra provided ₹10,000 annually to self-owned auto or taxi drivers, while the current Auto Driver Sevalo provides ₹15,000 annually to owners of self-owned autos.
168.tq: Compare the old and current scheme names by beneficiary and benefit amount.
xs: Assistance rose from **₹10,000** (**YSR Vahana Mitra**) to **₹15,000** (**Auto Driver Sevalo**) for owners of self-owned autos — option **(2)**.
Free LPG is **Deepam**; marine fishermen get **Matsyakara Bharosa**.
xa: Vahana Mitra covered **auto and taxi owner-drivers**.
⚠ **₹15,000** = Talliki Vandanam and Auto Driver Sevalo.
Other renames: **Rythu Bharosa → Annadata Sukhibhava**; **Spandana → PGRS**.

168.s: Talliki Vandanam of Andhra Pradesh replaced which earlier scheme that paid ₹15,000 a year to the mother or guardian of a poor child sent to school?
168.x: Talliki Vandanam replaced Jagananna Amma Vodi (launched January 2020), which credited ₹15,000 a year to the mother/recognised guardian of a poor child sent to school or college (APPSC 2023). YSR Cheyutha gave ₹18,750 to women aged 45-60; Aasara repaid SHG loans; Vidya Deevena is fee reimbursement.
168.tq: Amma Vodi (2020) → Talliki Vandanam.
xs: **Talliki Vandanam** replaced **Jagananna Amma Vodi** (launched **January 2020**) — option **(2)**.
Amma Vodi paid **₹15,000** a year to the mother/recognised guardian of a poor child sent to school or college (**APPSC 2023**).
**YSR Cheyutha** gave **₹18,750** to women aged **45-60**; **YSR Aasara** repaid SHG loans; **Vidya Deevena** is listed as RTF (fee reimbursement).
xa: Talliki Vandanam: **₹15,000 per child per year**; Budget 2026-27 **Rs 8,456 crore**.
Aim: raise **GER** (**APPSC 2025**).
Other renames: **YSR Pension Kanuka → NTR Bharosa Pension**.

168.s:
With reference to the NTR Bharosa Pension scheme in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It was earlier known as YSR Pension Kanuka.
2. The monthly pension for old-age and widow beneficiaries was enhanced from ₹3,000 to ₹4,000 from April 2024.
3. The scheme was renamed NTR Bharosa from June 2024 onwards.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All three statements are correct. The scheme was known as YSR Pension Kanuka during 2019–24 and was renamed NTR Bharosa, with the pension enhanced to ₹4,000 from April 2024.
168.tq: Use the timeline and check whether the name, period and amount agree.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
It was **YSR Pension Kanuka** in **2019-24**.
Old age and widow pension rose from **₹3,000 to ₹4,000** w.e.f. **April 2024**.
Renamed back to **NTR Bharosa** from **June 2024**.
xa: Overall range **₹4,000-15,000/month** to **65+ lakh** beneficiaries.

168.s: The minimum age prescribed for eligibility as an old-age pensioner under NTR Bharosa in Andhra Pradesh is:
168.x: Old-age pension under NTR Bharosa is available to persons aged 60 years and above.
168.tq: Directly recall the age threshold rather than confusing it with the widow-pension age.
xs: Old-age pension under **NTR Bharosa** starts at **60 years** and above — option **(3)**.
Widows qualify from **18 years**.
xa: Old age and widow pension is **₹4,000/month** from **April 2024**.
⚠ Exam angle: the **₹3,000 → ₹4,000** revision and the **60/18** age limits.
Bihar's **Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana** is for the poor above **60** (**APPSC 2019**).

168.s: A widow becomes eligible for the widow pension category under NTR Bharosa from the age of:
168.x: The age criterion for widow pension under NTR Bharosa is 18 years and above.
168.tq: Separate the special category age limit from the 60-year old-age pension limit.
xs: Widows qualify for NTR Bharosa pension from **18 years** and above — option **(1)**.
**60 years** is the **old-age** limit.
xa: Widow pension: **₹4,000/month** (from ₹3,000, w.e.f. **April 2024**).
Categories also include **single women** and **transgender** persons.
**Spouse pensions** go to surviving wives (**6,268** new, Sep **2026**).

168.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the social security pension amount in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Persons with 40% or more disability — ₹6,000 per month, with no age limit
Persons with 40% or more disability — ₹4,000 per month, subject to age above 60
Thalassaemia patients — ₹6,000 per month, subject to age above 60
Widows — ₹10,000 per month, without an age criterion
168.x: Persons with 40% or more disability receive ₹6,000 per month without an age limit. Thalassaemia and similar patients receive ₹10,000.
168.tq: Separate disability eligibility from age-based pensions and disease-specific support.
xs: Persons with **40%+ disability** get **₹6,000** a month with **no age limit** — option **(1)**.
**Thalassaemia** patients get **₹10,000**, with no age-60 condition.
**Widows** get **₹4,000** and must be **18+**.
xa: About **65+ lakh** beneficiaries overall.

168.s: The Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana, for poor people above 60 years, is a scheme of which State?
168.x: Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana is Bihar's old-age pension scheme for poor people above 60 (APPSC 2019). AP's scheme is NTR Bharosa; Kerala and Telangana are not linked to this scheme name.
168.tq: Vriddhajan = Bihar.
xs: **Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana** is a scheme of **Bihar**, for the poor above **60** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2019**).
AP's scheme is **NTR Bharosa Pension**.
xa: Kerala pays **₹2,000/month** and is moving pensions from doorstep delivery to **DBT**.
AP has the **highest per-capita social security pension spending** among States (**16th FC**).
AP old-age pension: **60+**, **₹4,000/month**.

168.s: The Chief Minister’s stated approach to welfare delivery treats which of the following as the basic unit?
168.x: The Chief Minister stated that the family should be the unit for welfare, including family mapping before sanctioning new pensions.
168.tq: Apply the policy principle to the administrative action described in the question.
xs: The CM treats **the family** as the unit of welfare delivery — option **(2)**.
He ordered **family mapping** before new pensions are sanctioned (Collectors' Conference, **12 Sep 2026**).
xa: Existing pensioners continue.
Ration: **5 kg rice for every family member**, family as the unit.
**Village/Ward Secretariats** have mapped **1.68 crore** households.

168.s: Which agency is the nodal agency for NTR Bharosa pensions in Andhra Pradesh?
168.x: SERP is the nodal agency for NTR Bharosa pensions.
168.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this function?’ test to distinguish the nodal agency from health and recruitment bodies.
xs: **SERP** is the nodal agency for NTR Bharosa pensions — option **(2)**.
The **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust** runs health insurance, not pensions.
xa: Pensions are delivered at the **doorstep** with **Aadhaar biometric (ABBA)** authentication.
SERP also reaches **84.47 lakh** rural women (SHGs).
⚠ **SERP** = rural women; **MEPMA** = urban SHGs.

168.s: The automated monthly distribution of NTR Bharosa pensions uses which mechanism to remove ghost beneficiaries?
168.x: Pension distribution is automated using Aadhaar-based biometric authentication, intended to eliminate ghost beneficiaries.
168.tq: Identify the operational mechanism that directly addresses the stated administrative problem.
xs: Distribution is automated with **Aadhaar-based biometric authentication** (Jan **2026**) — option **(4)**.
This **removes ghost beneficiaries**.
xa: Delivery is at the **doorstep** with **ABBA**; **SERP** is nodal.
**DBT** on the **JAM trinity** also cuts ghost beneficiaries and middlemen.
Dec 2025: **63.12 lakh** pensions, **₹2,744 cr** a month.

168.s: Which statement correctly describes the funding of National Social Assistance Programme pensions in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The pension is financed exclusively through beneficiary contributions.
The entire pension is financed only by municipal bodies.
The State does not contribute to NSAP pensions.
The State tops up the central NSAP pension from its own funds.
168.x: Andhra Pradesh supplements the central NSAP pension amount with funds from the State government.
168.tq: Identify the correct funding relationship instead of assuming a single-level government contribution.
xs: AP **tops up the central NSAP pension from its own funds** — option **(4)**.
So the State does contribute; it is not beneficiary- or municipality-funded.
xa: AP's old-age pension is **₹4,000/month**.
AP has the **highest per-capita social security pension spending** (**16th FC**).
Budget 2026-27: **₹27,719 crore** for NTR Bharosa.

168.s: The 16th Finance Commission found that Andhra Pradesh had the highest among States in respect of:
168.x: The 16th Finance Commission found Andhra Pradesh to have the highest per-capita social security pension spending among States.
168.tq: Focus on the precise comparison—per-capita pension spending—not a broader welfare indicator.
xs: The **16th Finance Commission** found AP has the **highest per-capita social security pension spending** — option **(1)**.
The notes call AP the State that spends the most per head on social pensions.
xa: CM claims NTR Bharosa is **India's largest welfare scheme**.
**₹73,506 crore** spent on pensions since June **2024**.

168.s: The expenditure on NTR Bharosa pensions in Andhra Pradesh was estimated at what amount in 2026-27?
168.x: NTR Bharosa pension expenditure was estimated at ₹27,719 crore in 2026-27.
168.tq: Distinguish the welfare allocation from interest, capital outlay and revenue-deficit figures.
xs: NTR Bharosa got **₹27,719 crore** in Budget **2026-27** — option **(2)**.
It is far above the **₹4,407 crore** of Budget 2024-25 BE.
xa: **₹73,506 crore** spent on pensions since June **2024**.
⚠ **Rs 8,456 crore** = Talliki Vandanam (2026-27).

168.s: Aarogyasri was initially introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 2007 under the leadership of:
168.x: Aarogyasri began in 2007 under Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy.
168.tq: Match the scheme’s launch year with the person associated with its introduction.
xs: **Aarogyasri** began in **2007** under **YSR — Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy** — option **(3)**.
Name trail: **Rajiv Aarogyasri (2007)** → **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva (2014)** → **Dr YSR Aarogyasri (2019)** → **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva (2024)**.
xa: Coverage: cashless care to **1.43 crore families**, **3,257 procedures**; linked with **PM-JAY**.
**108** and Aarogyasri are YSR-era schemes.
**EHS** covers State government employees and pensioners through the same Trust.

168.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the new health insurance model announced in Andhra Pradesh in May 2025:
1. It proposed coverage of up to ₹25 lakh per family per year.
2. It was intended for about 1.65 crore poor and middle-class families.
3. It was announced by Health Minister Y. Satya Kumar Yadav.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All three statements are correct. The model announced in May 2025 proposed annual coverage up to ₹25 lakh for about 1.65 crore poor and middle-class families and was announced by Y. Satya Kumar Yadav.
168.tq: Verify the amount, target population and announcing authority together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Cover up to **₹25 lakh per family per year** for about **1.65 crore** poor and middle-class families.
Announced by Health Minister **Y. Satya Kumar Yadav** (May **2025**).
xa: ⚠ **G2-GS 2024** keyed "covers up to ₹25 lakh per family a year" as correct.
⚠ **Universal Health Policy**: **₹2.5 lakh** for every citizen; **₹25 lakh** for poor families.
Health budget 2026-27: **₹19,305 crore**.

168.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the functions of the 104 and 108 services in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 104 is the health-insurance trust and 108 is the employees’ health scheme.
104 provides mobile medical units with fixed-day village health services, while 108 is an emergency service.
104 provides emergency ambulance services, while 108 conducts fixed-day village clinics.
168.x: The 104 service operates mobile medical units providing fixed-day village health services, whereas 108 provides emergency ambulance services.
168.tq: Discriminate between the two similar-numbered services by matching each number with its function.
xs: **104** runs **mobile medical units** with **fixed-day village health services**; **108** is the **emergency service** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) swaps them; neither is an insurance trust, employees' scheme or pension service.
xa: 108 runs **768 ambulances** and has transported **9.22 lakh patients**.
**108 and Aarogyasri** are YSR-era schemes.
**EHS** gives cashless treatment to State employees and pensioners via the **NTR Vaidya Seva Trust**.

168.s: Aarogyasri (Rajiv Aarogyasri in 2007, later Dr YSR Aarogyasri) in Andhra Pradesh, is presently known as:
168.x: The Aarogyasri scheme, introduced in 2007 as Rajiv Aarogyasri and renamed Dr YSR Aarogyasri in 2019, is now known as Dr NTR Vaidya Seva.
168.tq: Test a renamed scheme through a direct predecessor-successor distinction.
xs: Aarogyasri is now called **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva** (**2024**) — option **(4)**.
Name trail: **Rajiv Aarogyasri (2007)** → **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva (2014)** → **Dr YSR Aarogyasri (2019)** → **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva (2024)**.
xa: It gives cashless care to **1.43 crore families** for **3,257 procedures**.
It is linked with **Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY**.
Other renames: **Spandana → PGRS**; **YSR Pension Kanuka → NTR Bharosa Pension**.

168.s: Under the Universal Health Policy described for Andhra Pradesh, which statement is correct?
o: Every citizen receives free treatment up to ₹2.5 lakh, while poor persons receive treatment up to ₹25 lakh through the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.
Every citizen receives free treatment up to ₹25 lakh, while poor persons receive only ₹2.5 lakh.
Poor persons are excluded from the insurance mode of treatment.
Only government employees receive free treatment up to ₹2.5 lakh.
168.x: The Universal Health Policy provides free treatment up to ₹2.5 lakh for every citizen, while poor persons receive treatment up to ₹25 lakh through the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.
168.tq: Watch for the reversal of the ₹2.5 lakh and ₹25 lakh limits between the two beneficiary groups.
xs: **Every citizen** gets free treatment up to **₹2.5 lakh**; the **poor** get up to **₹25 lakh** via the **NTR Vaidya Seva Trust** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the amounts; the poor are not excluded.
xa: ⚠ **₹2.5 lakh** = every citizen (insurance mode); **₹25 lakh** = poor families.
May **2025** model: up to **₹25 lakh** per family for about **1.65 crore** families.
**EHS** covers State government employees through the same Trust.

168.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Talli Bidda Express — Free bicycles for adolescent girls
YSR Sampoorna Poshana — Supplementary nutrition through Anganwadis
Giri Gorumudda — Nutrition support for tribal mothers and young children
Badikosta — Free bicycles for Class IX girl students
168.x: Talli Bidda Express provides post-delivery transport for a mother and newborn. Free bicycles for Class IX girl students are provided under Badikosta.
168.tq: Find the swapped beneficiary and service in the incorrectly matched pair.
xs: **Talli Bidda Express — free bicycles** is mismatched — option **(1)**.
Talli Bidda Express is a **free drop-back vehicle** taking **mother and newborn home** from a government hospital.
Free bicycles to **Class IX** girls are **Badikosta**.
xa: **Giri Gorumudda**: nutrition for tribal mothers and young children in **Agency areas**.
**YSR Sampoorna Poshana**: supplementary nutrition for children **6-72 months** and pregnant/lactating women.
AP's **MMR (45)** and **IMR (24)** beat the national figure.

168.s: Giri Gorumudda is primarily intended to provide nutrition support to which group?
o: Class IX girl students in municipal areas
Tribal mothers and young children in Agency areas
Poor minority brides in urban areas
168.x: Giri Gorumudda provides nutrition support to tribal mothers and young children in Agency areas.
168.tq: Identify the scheme through its special geographical and beneficiary focus.
xs: **Giri Gorumudda** supports **tribal mothers and young children in Agency areas** — option **(3)**.
Tailors and barbers (nayee brahmins) = **Jagananna Chedodu**; Class IX girls = **Badikosta**; minority brides = **Dulhan/Shaadi Tohfa**.
xa: Tribal take-home package is richer: **egg + 200 ml milk**.
**YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus** runs in tribal mandals.
**55,746 AWCs** in **257 projects**.

168.s: Sampoorna Poshana or Poshana Plus is primarily associated with:
o: Free house sites for homeless households
Richer take-home rations through Anganwadi Centres
168.x: Sampoorna Poshana/Poshana Plus provides richer take-home rations through Anganwadi Centres.
168.tq: Identify the central service rather than a neighbouring welfare objective.
xs: **Sampoorna Poshana / Poshana Plus** = **richer take-home rations at AWCs** — option **(4)**.
House sites = **Pedalandariki Illu**; SHG loan support = **Aasara**; post-matric scholarships = **Vidya/Vasathi Deevena (RTF)**.
xa: Plain areas: **Bala Sanjeevani** (**47,296** AWCs) in 2024-25.
**Anganwadi reforms**: Saksham Anganwadi upgrades; **fortified** take-home ration.
**55,746 AWCs** in **257 projects**.

168.s: Which of the following statements regarding SERP and MEPMA is correct?
o: SERP covers 84.47 lakh rural women, while MEPMA covers 2.74 lakh urban SHGs.
SERP covers 2.74 lakh rural women, while MEPMA covers 84.47 lakh urban SHGs.
SERP is confined to nutrition delivery and MEPMA to housing construction.
Both agencies cover only urban SHGs.
168.x: SERP works with 84.47 lakh rural women, while MEPMA covers 2.74 lakh urban SHGs, so option A is right. Option B swaps the two figures, and SERP and MEPMA are SHG agencies (rural and urban respectively), not nutrition or housing bodies.
168.tq: Use the rural–urban institutional comparison to reject reversed figures.
xs: **SERP** covers **84.47 lakh rural women**; **MEPMA** covers **2.74 lakh urban SHGs** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps the figures; both are **SHG agencies**, not nutrition or housing bodies.
xa: **SERP** is also the nodal agency for **NTR Bharosa** pensions.
**Aasara**: **69,597** SHG members, **₹633.74 crore** by DBT (2024-25).
⚠ **SERP** = rural; **MEPMA** = urban.

168.s: YSR Cheyutha (2019-24) provided ₹18,750 a year to which beneficiaries?
o: Kapu, Balija, Telaga and Ontari women aged 45-60
BC, SC, ST and minority women aged 45-60
Self-employed tailors, rajakas and nayee brahmins
168.x: YSR Cheyutha gave ₹18,750 a year to BC/SC/ST/minority women aged 45-60, linking them to livestock units and Pasu Kisan Credit Cards. Kapu, Balija, Telaga and Ontari women of the same age got ₹15,000 under YSR Kapu Nestham; tailors, rajakas and nayee brahmins got Jagananna Chedodu; mothers got Amma Vodi/Talliki Vandanam.
168.tq: Cheyutha ₹18,750 (BC/SC/ST/minority); Kapu Nestham ₹15,000.
xs: **YSR Cheyutha (2019-24)** gave **₹18,750** a year to **BC/SC/ST/minority women** aged **45-60** — option **(2)**.
**Kapu, Balija, Telaga, Ontari** women (45-60) got **₹15,000** under **YSR Kapu Nestham**.
Tailors, rajakas, nayee brahmins = **Jagananna Chedodu**; mothers = **Amma Vodi / Talliki Vandanam**.
xa: Cheyutha beneficiaries were linked to **livestock units** and **Pasu Kisan Credit Cards**.
The name Cheyutha first belonged to a **1998** TDP scheme for **handicapped persons**.

168.s: The Andhra Pradesh Disha Bill, 2019 sought to provide for completion of investigation and trial in sexual-offence cases against women within which of the following periods?
o: Investigation within 30 days and trial within 60 days
Investigation within 14 days and trial within 21 days
Investigation within 7 days and trial within 14 days
Investigation within 21 days and trial within 30 days
168.x: The Disha Bill, 2019 proposed completion of investigation within 7 days and trial within 14 days, making the total period 21 days.
168.tq: Separate the two time limits rather than treating 21 days as the investigation period.
xs: The **Disha Bill, 2019** sought **investigation in 7 days** and **trial in 14 days** — option **(3)**.
That makes **21 days** in total, so option (2) confuses the parts with the total.
xa: It worked by **amending the IPC and CrPC**.
AP Cabinet approved its **withdrawal** after the Centre advised reconsideration.
**BNS and BNSS** replaced IPC/CrPC from **1 July 2024**.

168.s: The Andhra Pradesh Disha Bill, 2019 proposed amendments primarily to which of the following laws?
o: The Indian Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and the Juvenile Justice Act
The Domestic Violence Act and the Dowry Prohibition Act
The Representation of the People Act and the Indian Evidence Act
168.x: The Disha Bill proposed amendments to the Indian Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure for dealing with sexual offences against women.
168.tq: Identify the exact statutes associated with the proposed legal amendment.
xs: The **Disha Bill** proposed amending the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** and the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)** — option **(1)**.
Aim: finish investigation (**7** days) and trial (**14** days) within **21 days**.
xa: Withdrawn because **BNS** and **BNSS** replaced IPC/CrPC from **1 July 2024**.
Delivery arms: **Disha SOS app** and **Disha police stations**.
**One Stop Centres** are a separate MWCD Mission Shakti mechanism.

168.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Disha Bill, 2019:
1. The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved its withdrawal after the Centre advised reconsideration.
2. The advice was connected with the replacement of the IPC and CrPC by the BNS and BNSS.
3. The BNS and BNSS replaced the IPC and CrPC with effect from 1 July 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All three statements are correct. The Bill was withdrawn after the Centre sought reconsideration in the context of the BNS and BNSS, which came into force on 1 July 2024.
168.tq: Check the linked sequence of withdrawal, legislative replacement and effective date.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **AP Cabinet** approved **withdrawal** after the Centre advised reconsideration.
Reason: **BNS** and **BNSS** replaced the IPC and CrPC from **1 July 2024**.
xa: The Bill had aimed at a **21-day** timeline (investigation **7** + trial **14** days).
Delivery arms: **Disha SOS app**, **Disha police stations**.
**Women Helpline 181** was universalised in **2019**.

168.s: A woman facing violence requires police assistance, medical aid, legal support, counselling and temporary shelter at a single location. Which facility is designed for this purpose?
168.x: One Stop Centres provide police, medical, legal, counselling and shelter support to women facing violence under one roof.
168.tq: Match the practical needs in the situation with the institution offering integrated support.
xs: A **One Stop Centre** gives **police, medical, legal, counselling and shelter** help under one roof — option **(1)**.
A **Disha police station** is only a police delivery arm; a **Village Secretariat** delivers general services.
xa: OSCs are part of MWCD's **Mission Shakti** with **Shakti Sadan**.
Backed by **Women Helpline 181** (universalised **2019**).
**Aasara** is SHG loan support, not a crisis centre.

168.s:
Consider the following statements about One Stop Centres (OSC):
1. They are part of the Ministry of Women and Child Development's Mission Shakti, along with Shakti Sadan.
2. They are backed by Women Helpline 181.
3. Women Helpline 181 was universalised in 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
168.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: OSCs are part of MWCD's Mission Shakti with Shakti Sadan, and are backed by Women Helpline 181. Statement 3 is wrong: Helpline 181 was universalised in 2019, not 2024. Hence '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options containing 3 are wrong.
168.tq: OSC = Mission Shakti; helpline 181 universalised 2019.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: OSCs are part of MWCD's **Mission Shakti**, with **Shakti Sadan**.
Statement 2: backed by **Women Helpline 181**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Helpline 181 was universalised in **2019**, not 2024.
xa: OSCs help women facing violence with **police, medical, legal, counselling and shelter** support.
The **Disha Bill, 2019** was withdrawn after **BNS/BNSS** took effect (**1 July 2024**).
SHG support comes through **Aasara**.

168.s:
Consider the following statements regarding YSR Kapu Nestham:
1. It covers Kapu, Balija, Telaga and Ontari women.
2. The eligible age group is 45–60 years.
3. The annual assistance is ₹15,000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: YSR Kapu Nestham covers Kapu, Balija, Telaga and Ontari women aged 45–60 years and provides ₹15,000 annually.
168.tq: Combine community, age and amount details in a single scheme-identification question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**YSR Kapu Nestham** covers **Kapu, Balija, Telaga and Ontari** women aged **45-60**.
It pays **₹15,000** a year.
xa: ⚠ **YSR Cheyutha** covers **BC/SC/ST/minority** women of the same age with **₹18,750**.
**Jagananna Chedodu**: **₹10,000** a year to tailors, rajakas, nayee brahmins with shops.
**Kapu** pensions via caste corporations: **6.84 lakh** (Dec 2025).

168.s: Jagananna Chedodu provides annual assistance to which of the following groups, subject to the stated eligibility of having shops?
o: Kapu, Balija, Telaga and Ontari women aged 45–60 years
Self-employed tailors, rajakas and nayee brahmins
Pregnant women and children below six years
Poor minority brides and their parents
168.x: Jagananna Chedodu provides ₹10,000 per year to self-employed tailors, rajakas and nayee brahmins with shops.
168.tq: Distinguish occupational beneficiaries from caste- or gender-based beneficiaries of nearby schemes.
xs: **Jagananna Chedodu** helps **self-employed tailors, rajakas and nayee brahmins** with shops — option **(2)**.
It paid **₹10,000** a year.
Kapu, Balija, Telaga, Ontari women = **YSR Kapu Nestham**; minority brides = **Dulhan/Shaadi Tohfa**.
xa: YSR Kapu Nestham: **₹15,000** a year to women aged **45-60**.
⚠ **₹10,000** a year was also **Vahana Mitra** (auto and taxi drivers).
Pregnant women and children get **Sampoorna Poshana**.

168.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Scheme)
a. Chandranna Pelli Kanuka
b. YSR Kalyanamasthu
c. Shaadi Tohfa
d. Dulhan

List-II (Description)
i. Muslim brides
 ii. SC, ST, BC, minorities and disabled
 iii. Same broad groups as Kalyanamasthu
 iv. Muslim brides, introduced in April 2015

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
168.x: Chandranna Pelli Kanuka covered SC, ST, BC, minorities and disabled persons; YSR Kalyanamasthu covered the same broad groups; Shaadi Tohfa was for Muslims; Dulhan was for Muslim brides and began in April 2015.
168.tq: Start with the sure Muslim-bride pair and then complete the community matching.
xs: Correct match: **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Chandranna Pelli Kanuka** (TDP, **2018**) → SC, ST, BC, minorities, disabled; **YSR Kalyanamasthu** (**2022**) → same broad groups.
**Shaadi Tohfa** → Muslim brides; **Dulhan** → Muslim brides, introduced **April 2015**.
xa: Dulhan paid **₹50,000** at marriage.
Dulhan was later renamed **YSR Shaadi Tohfa**.
Kalyanamasthu/Shaadi Tohfa are **YSRCP, 2022** schemes.

168.s: Dulhan scheme provided which benefit?
168.x: Dulhan was introduced in April 2015 and provided ₹50,000 to Muslim brides at marriage.
168.tq: Identify the exact beneficiary, occasion and amount of marriage assistance.
xs: **Dulhan** gave **₹50,000 to Muslim brides at marriage** — option **(3)**; introduced **April 2015**.
**₹24,000** = Nethanna Nestham; **₹18,750** = YSR Cheyutha; **₹15,000 per child** = Talliki Vandanam.
xa: Dulhan was later renamed **YSR Shaadi Tohfa**.
**Chandranna Pelli Kanuka** (TDP, **2018**) covered SC, ST, BC, minorities and disabled.
Minority welfare also includes **Haj and Jerusalem** pilgrimage aid.

168.s:
Consider the following statements regarding minority welfare in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Imams and Mouzams receive ₹5,000–10,000 per month.
2. The annual expenditure mentioned for this assistance is ₹180 crore.
3. Urdu is the second official language of the State.
4. Haj and Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance is provided.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
168.x: All four statements are correct: the monthly assistance is ₹5,000–10,000, the annual expenditure is ₹180 crore, Urdu is the second official language, and Haj and Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance is provided.
168.tq: Use an all-correct option when every listed community-welfare feature is supported.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Imams and Mouzams get **₹5,000-10,000** a month; **₹180 crore** a year.
**Urdu** is the second official language; **Haj and Jerusalem** pilgrimage aid is given.
xa: Minority allocation: **₹6,090 crore** (2026-27).
**Dulhan** (**April 2015**) gave **₹50,000** to Muslim brides.
Education support: post-matric scholarships, **RTF**, **Mega DSC** coaching.

168.s: The stated proposal regarding ration distribution in Andhra Pradesh is that rice should be provided at the rate of:
o: 10 kg for every adult male only
25 kg for every village household only
5 kg for every family, irrespective of family size
5 kg for every family member, treating the family as the unit
168.x: The proposal was to provide 5 kg of rice for every family member, with the family treated as the unit for distribution.
168.tq: Distinguish per-member entitlement from a per-family entitlement.
xs: The CM wants **5 kg rice for every family member**, treating the **family as the unit** — option **(4)** (12 Sep **2026**).
So it is per member, not a flat **5 kg** per family.
xa: Rice subsidy: **₹2,345 crore** in 2024-25 BE.
**Mee Mart** (Jul **2026**): PDS modernised with **NCCF**.
Family mapping is also required before new pensions.

168.s: Anna Canteens are primarily intended to provide:
o: Subsidised meals for the urban poor
168.x: Anna Canteens provide subsidised meals primarily for the urban poor.
168.tq: Match the scheme with its target population and service.
xs: **Anna Canteens** give **subsidised meals for the urban poor** — option **(4)**.
Bicycles = **Badikosta**; tribal nutrition = **Giri Gorumudda / Poshana Plus**; house sites = **Pedalandariki Illu**.
xa: Meal price: **₹5**.
**62 rural canteens** opened on 15 Apr **2026** at **Dharanikota (Palnadu)** → total **269**.
Ration: **5 kg rice** per family member.

168.s: A meal at an Anna Canteen in Andhra Pradesh is priced at:
168.x: Anna Canteens provide a meal priced at ₹5.
168.tq: Recall the flagship unit price associated with the programme.
xs: An **Anna Canteen** meal costs **₹5** — option **(3)**.
The canteens serve **subsidised meals for the urban poor**.
xa: **62 rural canteens** opened on 15 Apr **2026** at **Dharanikota (Palnadu)**.
Total canteens: **269**.
⚠ **5 kg** rice per family member is the ration plan — a different "5".

168.s: Pedalandariki Illu is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Providing house sites and houses for poor women
Providing cash assistance to self-employed barbers
Providing bicycles to Class IX girls
168.x: Pedalandariki Illu provides house sites and houses for poor women. It is linked with the broader Housing for All effort.
168.tq: Distinguish housing assistance from other welfare benefits with overlapping poor-beneficiary groups.
xs: **Pedalandariki Illu** gives **house sites/houses for poor women** — option **(1)**.
It was the housing pillar of **Navaratnalu** (YSR Jagananna housing).
xa: Houses in **Jagananna colonies** launched on **3 June 2021** (**G2-GS 2023** key).
BJP seeks a probe into alleged **fake house site pattas** (2019-24).
Current policy: **3 cents** (rural) / **2 cents** (urban) per homeless household by **2029**.

168.s: The AP State Housing Corporation is associated with which programme and motto?
o: Weaker Section Housing Programme — “Housing for All”
168.x: The AP State Housing Corporation, also referred to as APHCL, runs the Weaker Section Housing Programme with the motto “Housing for All”.
168.tq: Match the implementing agency with its programme and motto.
xs: The **AP State Housing Corporation** (**APHCL**) runs the **Weaker Section Housing Programme**, motto **"Housing for All"** — option **(3)**.
"Housing for All" is also the national goal behind **PMAY-U and PMAY-G**, which the State converges.
xa: Housing for All: **7.60 lakh** houses to be finished by **March 2026**.
**PMAY-U + PMAY-G** convergence, tracked on **CFMS**.
House sites: **3 cents** rural, **2 cents** urban.

168.s: Under the current housing policy, the house-site entitlement for an eligible homeless household is:
o: 3 cents in rural areas and 2 cents in urban areas
2 square metres in rural areas and 3 square metres in urban areas
3 acres in rural areas and 2 acres in urban areas
2 cents in rural areas and 3 cents in urban areas
168.x: The policy provides house sites of 3 cents in rural areas and 2 cents in urban areas for every eligible homeless household by 2029.
168.tq: Check the direction of a rural–urban size comparison.
xs: House sites: **3 cents rural, 2 cents urban** for every eligible homeless household — option **(1)**.
Option (4) reverses them; the unit is **cents**, not square metres or acres.
xa: Target year: **2029**.
Houses in progress: **7.60 lakh**, under **PMAY-U (BLC), PMAY-G, PM-JANMAN**.
Motto of AP State Housing Corporation: **"Housing for All"**.

168.s: YSR Jagananna housing under ‘Pedalandariki Illu’ is associated with which date for the launch of houses in Jagananna colonies?
168.x: Houses in Jagananna colonies under YSR Jagananna housing were launched on 3 June 2021.
168.tq: Test the exact date associated with a State housing initiative.
xs: Houses in **Jagananna colonies** were launched on **3 June 2021** — option **(1)** (**G2-GS 2023** key).
**11 April 2019** is the **Aasara** SHG loan cut-off date; **January 2020** is **Amma Vodi**.
xa: YSR Jagananna housing = Navaratnalu's **Pedalandariki Illu**.
BJP seeks a probe into alleged **fake house site pattas** (2019-24).
Current policy: sites by **2029**.

168.s: CLAP, or Clean Andhra Pradesh, primarily focuses on which of the following?
o: Free transport for mothers and newborns
Full fee reimbursement for post-matric students
Door-to-door segregated garbage collection and sanitation
168.x: CLAP focuses on door-to-door collection of segregated garbage and sanitation activities across Andhra Pradesh.
168.tq: Identify the core function rather than an associated environmental output.
xs: **CLAP** = **door-to-door segregated garbage collection and sanitation** — option **(4)**.
Launched **2 Oct 2021** (Gandhi Jayanti).
xa: Results (2024-25): segregation **96.07%**; **6,890 tonnes/day** processed.
**104 STPs** (**690.90 MLD**); **171** under construction.
**Swachh Andhra**: **500 ODF Plus villages** milestone (Jan **2026**).

168.s: The target mentioned for Jal Jeevan Mission coverage in rural Andhra Pradesh is to provide tap connections to all rural households by:
168.x: The stated target is coverage of all rural households by 2027.
168.tq: Distinguish the future target year from the current coverage statistic.
xs: JJM aims at tap connections for **all rural households by 2027** — option **(3)**.
So far **70.04 lakh** households (**73%**) have tap connections (2024-25).
